books: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants
Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries
meta.note: Rule rows (PWC25 shape): id, world, statement (paraphrased), locators, speaker, mechanism, seam (AB code), derives (blocked slugs a playable model exists for), default_dial_reason, licence. Proposals: a batched reader (gpt-6-luna) read the books in shards of about 8,000 words; nothing here was human-checked, and no source text is kept.

rules.statement: A prepared spell has one predetermined effect and lets its caster use full magical power; improvised magic is more flexible but generally weaker.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Glossary (ars-magica-core#000)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to fixed effects for stronger prepared magic; a world can widen improvised magic’s flexibility at the cost of lower power.

rules.statement: Especially powerful spells take hours to cast and require vis, but let the caster use full magical power.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Glossary (ars-magica-core#000)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to requiring hours and vis for peak spell power; a world can relax either cost, with vis scarcity and delay limiting use.

rules.statement: There is no fixed daily cap on spells, but casting many in quick succession is likely to exhaust the caster.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Glossary (ars-magica-core#000)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to unlimited daily casting with fatigue from rapid use; a world can tighten the limit, making magical exertion more costly.

rules.statement: All magi have an innate capacity for magic that enables them to use nearly any kind of magic after training, but makes people around them uneasy.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Glossary (ars-magica-core#000)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to granting broad magical potential alongside social unease; a world can reduce either, changing who can learn magic and how others react.

rules.statement: A ritual taught to every Hermetic magus at the end of apprenticeship enables resistance to magic.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Glossary (ars-magica-core#000)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a learned ritual that blocks magic; a world can vary its availability or strength, with training determining access.

rules.statement: Parma Magica protects a wizard from other magic and suppresses the hostile social effect that Gifted people normally have on one another.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: The Foundation of the Order (ars-magica-core#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default the protection blocks magic and Gift-based hostility; a world can narrow either defense, because the protection is a learned magical technique.

rules.statement: A Bjornaer magus can take the form of their heartbeast, but avoids other kinds of shapeshifting and cannot form the links needed to have a familiar.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: House Bjornaer (ars-magica-core#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default the heartbeast is the sole permitted animal form and familiars are unavailable; a world can loosen either limit, because Bjornaer training treats the heartbeast as central.

rules.statement: A character can belong to only one House at a time. True Lineage Houses cannot be joined after training, while Mystery Cult Houses admit members through initiation and the remaining Houses are comparatively open to trained magi.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: The Houses of Hermes (ars-magica-core#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default each character has one House and lineage membership is inherited through training; a world can allow transfers or additional affiliations, at the cost of weakening House identity and obligations.

rules.statement: Tremere hold their apprentices’ voting sigils until the apprentice defeats the parens in certamen or the parens dies. If the trainer does not hold their own sigil, the new sigil passes upward to the nearest ancestor who does.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: House Tremere (ars-magica-core#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default voting authority stays with the first ancestor in the chain who holds their sigil; a world can end this delegation earlier, at the cost of Tremere’s concentrated political control.

rules.statement: Verditius magi generally cannot cast Formulaic spells without casting tools, because most inherit their founder’s magical Flaw.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: House Verditius (ars-magica-core#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default the Flaw prevents unaided Formulaic casting; a world can reduce or remove the restriction, because it is an inherited magical weakness.

rules.statement: A declared Wizards’ War begins at the rise of the full moon after the declaration arrives on the next full moon night, and ends at the rise of the following full moon. During that period, the two participants may kill one another without violating the Code.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Wizards’ War (ars-magica-core#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a formally declared, month-bounded exception to the no-killing rule; a world can change its timing or scope, with the risk of Tribunal punishment for abusive use.

rules.statement: A legal Tribunal requires at least 12 magi from at least four covenants in attendance, plus a Quaesitor to oversee legality. The Quaesitor does not vote but counts toward the quorum; the Praeco may vote only to break a tie.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Tribunals (ars-magica-core#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to these attendance and voting thresholds; a world can alter them, trading procedural legitimacy for easier or more restrictive decision-making.

rules.statement: If a Praeco’s ejections leave a Tribunal without its quorum or its presiding Quaesitor, the gathering is invalid. The presiding Quaesitor must certify the Tribunal’s validity at its conclusion.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Tribunals (ars-magica-core#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to invalidating a meeting that loses required attendance or oversight; a world can relax certification, at the cost of weaker checks on abuse.

rules.statement: A regional Tribunal meets every seven years, while the Grand Tribunal meets every 33 years at Durenmar. The Grand Tribunal alone can decide disputes between Tribunals and make decisions binding across the whole Order.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Regional Tribunals; The Grand Tribunal (ars-magica-core#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the stated schedules and jurisdiction; a world can change meeting intervals or authority, with slower decisions or less unified law as the tradeoff.

rules.statement: A magus who refuses a Tribunal’s imposed punishment can be subjected to a Wizard’s March: he is expelled from the Order and loses the Code’s protection. By tradition, his possessions go to those who kill him.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: The Peripheral Code (ars-magica-core#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to expulsion and loss of legal protection for refusing punishment; a world can soften the sanction, at the cost of weaker Tribunal enforcement.

rules.statement: Magic sold directly to a non-member for mundane payment must eventually lose its power, either through limited charges or a limited duration. Trading for vis or other arcane items is an exception described in the passage.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Magical Items (ars-magica-core#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to making directly sold magic temporary or consumable; a world can permit permanent sales, risking uncontrolled magical goods among mundanes.

rules.statement: A character may spend Confidence after seeing a roll’s result to add +3 per point, up to the character’s Confidence Score. It cannot be spent on a botch or a season-long activity roll, and spent points never return.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Using Confidence (ars-magica-core#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a limited, permanently spent bonus after the roll; a world can allow recovery or broader use, reducing the cost of relying on Confidence.

rules.statement: A grog template can have up to three Minor Flaws, matched by the same number of Minor Virtues; companions and magi can have up to 10 points of Flaws, matched by the same number of Virtue points. Minor choices are worth 1 point and Major choices 3.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Detailed Character Creation Summary, step 3 (ars-magica-core#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the stated caps and matching points; a troupe can change the caps, trading character balance for a different campaign style.

rules.statement: Character creation assigns 75 experience points to Native Language and 45 points across a listed set of early-childhood Abilities. Later life grants 15 experience points per year, or 20 with Wealthy and 10 with Poor.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Detailed Character Creation Summary, steps 5–6 (ars-magica-core#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the listed age-based experience rates; a world can alter childhood or later-life training to reflect its education and wealth norms.

rules.statement: A Hermetic magus receives 240 apprenticeship experience points for Arts and eligible Abilities, and 120 spell levels. A spell taken at apprenticeship cannot exceed Technique + Form + Intelligence + Magic Theory + 3, after relevant Virtues and Flaws are applied.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Detailed Character Creation Summary, step 7 (ars-magica-core#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to these apprenticeship budgets and spell ceiling; a saga can adjust them to set how capable newly trained magi are.

rules.statement: After apprenticeship, a magus may optionally allocate 30 points per year among Arts, Abilities, and spell levels.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Detailed Character Creation Summary, step 8 (optional years after apprenticeship) (ars-magica-core#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to 30 points each year; a saga can alter the rate to make older magi more or less advanced.

rules.statement: Characters older than 35 must make aging rolls before play, and may die of old age; if death occurs, the group may instead return to the preceding year.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Starting Character Age (ars-magica-core#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to aging checks above 35 with the option to step back one year; a world can change the threshold or remove the rollback, trading longevity or player safety.

rules.statement: A listed spell entry gives its Technique and Form, spell level, and the character’s Casting Total with that spell; mastery information may also be noted. A Casting Total above the spell level allows easy casting, while a total substantially below it may cause difficulty.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Spells Known (ars-magica-core#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.mechanism: law: casting total versus spell level
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to comparing total against level as described; a setting can tune how forgiving casting is, affecting reliability and magical competence.

rules.statement: For children aged 6–7, reduce all Characteristics by 4 and Size by 2; at ages 8–9 the reductions are 3 and 2, at 10–11 they are 2 and 2, and at 12–13 they are 1 and 1. Characters aged 14 or older receive no adjustment.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Child Characters (ars-magica-core#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to applying the age adjustments exactly as listed; a setting could soften them to represent unusually mature children, at the cost of departing from the stated age-based model.

rules.statement: A Hermetic magus may belong to only one House. House membership grants its listed character-creation benefit; Merinita magi without a faerie-related Virtue or Flaw also receive one Warping Point to allow initiation into the Mystery.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Magi Only: Hermetic House — Hermetic Houses Summary (ars-magica-core#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one House and its listed benefit; a world could change which benefits Houses grant, with membership and initiation defining access.

rules.statement: Grogs may take at most three points of Flaws and an equal number of Virtue points, and may take only Minor Virtues and Flaws; they cannot take The Gift or Story Flaws. Companions and magi may each take up to ten Flaw points and an equal number of Virtue points, with Major traits worth three points and Minor traits one.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Virtues and Flaws (ars-magica-core#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the character-type limits and point values; a world could raise or lower those caps to make minor characters more or less exceptional.

rules.statement: Characters with a Might Score cannot take Virtues affiliating them with a different supernatural realm, including The Gift, True Faith, Faerie Blood, and Blood of the Nephilim. If multiple sources grant Magic Resistance, use only the highest total rather than adding them together.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Characters with Might Scores (ars-magica-core#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to forbidding cross-realm affiliations and taking only the strongest resistance; a world could allow mixed sources or stacking, at the cost of weakening realm boundaries or increasing protection.

rules.statement: A being with a Might Score is immune to Warping and to supernatural backlash from its own realm, such as Twilight, Hubris, or Vituperation. It may spend one point from its Might Pool to use an Ability or power that would normally cause Warping, but still suffers other consequences of a failed or botched roll.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Characters with Might Scores (ars-magica-core#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to immunity with a one-point Might expenditure for otherwise Warping-causing use; a world could make such use riskier, trading the supernatural immunity for a cost or backlash.

rules.statement: A Mythic Companion receives a free status Virtue and a free Minor Virtue; each Flaw point may provide two Virtue points, up to ten Flaw points. The resulting maximum is 21 Virtue points and 10 Flaw points, though required traits count against the stated limits.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Mythic Companions (ars-magica-core#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the stated bonus and caps; a world could reduce the extra Virtue allowance to make supernatural companions less powerful.

rules.statement: A Devil Child must take Devil Child, Demonic Blood, Demonic Might or Demonic Powers, Puissant Guile, and Tragic Life or an agreed substitute. It may take three additional Virtue points at no cost and up to seven additional Flaw points, each of which grants two Virtue points.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Mythic Companions — Devil Child (ars-magica-core#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the required demonic ancestry and tragic constraint; a world could loosen or tighten the creator’s hold, changing how much freedom the child has in exchange for its powers.

rules.statement: Major Virtues cost 3 points and Major Flaws grant 3; Minor ones cost or grant 1. Central characters may take at most 10 points of Flaws, including no more than 5 Minor Flaws.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Chapter 4: Virtues and Flaws (ars-magica-core#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the stated point values and caps; a troupe can tighten or relax them to tune character power and complexity.

rules.statement: Characters must take one Social Status, and normally may take a given Virtue or Flaw only once. A character should have no more than one Story Flaw or Major Personality Flaw; these limits can be waived by troupe agreement where specified.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Virtues and Flaws Rules and Guidelines (ars-magica-core#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to these limits to distribute story hooks; a troupe can turn the limits up or down to shape how often individual characters dominate stories.

rules.statement: A character with The Gift can be taught Supernatural Abilities without buying the matching Virtues, and may begin with one such Ability; learning further ones requires opportunities in play. A character without The Gift who gains an Ability from a Virtue cannot learn new Supernatural Abilities during the saga, though existing ones can improve.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Types of Virtue and Flaw — The Gift (ars-magica-core#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to Gift as the gateway to learning new powers; a world can loosen that restriction for easier supernatural training, at the cost of making the Gift less distinctive.

rules.statement: A character with a Supernatural Virtue or Flaw is immune to Warping caused by living in a high aura of the same realm as that Virtue or Flaw.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Supernatural (ars-magica-core#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to matching-realm immunity; a world can remove or broaden it to change how strongly supernatural origin protects inhabitants from aura exposure.

rules.statement: A tainted Virtue or Flaw is Infernal; supernatural abilities it grants are always Infernal. At most half of a character’s Virtues and Flaws may be tainted: no more than 5 points of Tainted Virtues, or 10 for a Mythic Companion, and no more than 5 points of Tainted Flaws.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Tainted Virtues and Flaws (ars-magica-core#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to Infernal-only tainted abilities and the listed caps; a troupe can allow more corruption to make infernal influence more pervasive, at a moral and social cost.

rules.statement: Atlantean Magic lets a caster use Water-way range to target something on or in the same connected waterway, provided caster and target meet the water-contact conditions; it has the level of Sight range. Storm duration is available for Aquam or Auram spells cast during a storm and lasts until that storm ends.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Virtues — Atlantean Magic (ars-magica-core#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to waterways and storms as bounded casting conditions; a world can broaden the connected region or duration, at the cost of less restrictive magic.

rules.statement: Sin-Eating takes the unforgiven sins of a dying or recently dead person, usually onto the practitioner; the sin’s magnitude is treated as a Minor, Serious, or Major Affliction. It prevents the dead person from becoming a ghost because of unrepented sins, but the effect on either soul’s ultimate fate is unknown.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Sin-Eating (ars-magica-core#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to transferring the burden to the sin-eater while preventing this cause of ghosthood; a world can make the soul outcome knowable, with consequences for the practitioner or deceased.

rules.statement: Storm Duration preserves a storm only for the lifetime it would naturally have had; it cannot make a storm last indefinitely. A Sun Duration effect can maintain or create a storm for a day, and repeated castings can extend its presence.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Possible Abuses of Storms (ars-magica-core#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the storm’s natural lifetime; a world can allow repeated day-long maintenance, at the cost of repeated castings.

rules.statement: A Body-of-water target covers an entire lake, river, or sea, with its boundaries determined as for Water-way. It has the same Target level as Structure, but very large bodies of water require an additional magnitude.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Body-of-water (Target) (ars-magica-core#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to Structure-level targeting of one defined body; a world can raise the magnitude for very large waters, reflecting their scale.

rules.statement: A Bee King can give any group of bees commands they can physically perform, including suicidal orders; standing instructions persist until countermanded, and simple commands can be spoken aloud. A touched bee can relay complex messages, while a Bee King can understand a hive and read a touched bee’s mind.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Bee King (ars-magica-core#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to command of physically possible bee actions; a world can limit long-running or suicidal orders, balancing control against the bees’ lives.

rules.statement: When a character takes or inflicts a wound, a stress die plus Angry must reach 9 to trigger berserk; deliberate attempts need 6 after a wound, or 9 otherwise. While berserk the character gains +2 Attack and Soak, loses 2 Defense, cannot retreat or spare enemies, and attacks friends if foes are gone; each round the character may try to calm down with a stress die + Perception − Angry against 6.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Berserk (ars-magica-core#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the stated triggers and combat modifiers; a world can make frustration trigger more often, at the cost of risking harm to allies.

rules.statement: When casting Formulaic spells, the caster may spend one pawn of vis per magnitude to increase Range, Duration, Target, or size by one magnitude, repeating this as needed. Casting success, Fatigue loss, and Penetration use the original spell level, but each pawn spent adds one botch die; this cannot reduce parameters or exceed Formulaic limits and does not apply to Spontaneous or Ritual spells.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Boosted Magic (ars-magica-core#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one vis pawn per parameter magnitude; a world can raise the botch risk or restrict which parameters can be boosted, trading flexibility for danger.

rules.statement: A character with Death Prophecy cannot die from wounds or old age until the prophecy’s stated condition is met, though serious injury remains possible. The storyguide must keep the condition in play and provide fair warning of relevant signs.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Death Prophecy (ars-magica-core#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to preventing death until the condition is fulfilled; a world can make the condition broader or more symbolic, at the cost of greater uncertainty.

rules.statement: A Demonic Blood character has up to 30 levels of Infernal Powers, each paid for with Might Points equal to half its magnitude, rounded down but never below 1. Constant powers use the usual design rules and permanently reduce the Might Pool by their cost; they cannot be switched off.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Demonic Blood (ars-magica-core#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a limited pool of purchased Infernal effects; a world can allow more power levels, with the cost of permanently reduced Might for constant effects.

rules.statement: With Diedne Magic, a Fatigue-free Spontaneous spell may use the usual division by 5 without a stress die, or division by 2 with a stress die and possible botch. When Fatigue is spent on a Spontaneous spell, double the lower applicable Art before dividing the total by two; the caster still rolls a stress die and can botch.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Diedne Magic (ars-magica-core#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the stated alternate calculations; a world can require the riskier stress-die method more often, exchanging stronger magic for danger.

rules.statement: A narrow supernatural focus has 25 points to divide between maximum effect level and Penetration: each level of effect costs 2 points and each point of Penetration costs 1. Activating an effect costs 1 Fatigue level at level 25 or below, 2 at levels 26–50, and 3 at levels 51–75.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Focus Power (ars-magica-core#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the 25-point budget and stated fatigue costs; a world can change the budget or thresholds to set how potent and tiring focused powers are.

rules.statement: Folk Magic permits spells only in one selected narrow category. Casting requires at least 15 minutes of uninterrupted preparation and a Fatigue level whether the attempt succeeds or fails; its Casting Total is half Stamina, Realm Lore, aura modifier, and stress die combined.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Folk Magic (ars-magica-core#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one category, 15 minutes, and one Fatigue level; a world can broaden the categories or alter the casting burden to reflect how accessible its folk magic is.

rules.statement: Kassalan Exorcism can ward against ghosts and the physical dead or strip their Might, but cannot affect other spirits or creatures. Each attempt costs one Fatigue level, five minutes of uninterrupted preparation, and a handful of Kassalan Dust, whether or not it succeeds.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Kassalan Exorcism (ars-magica-core#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the narrow undead target and three-part cost; a world can widen the targets or change the dust and fatigue costs to establish the reach of its exorcists.

rules.statement: A wielder of Harnessed Magic can end their own spells, and the enchantments in magic items they made, by concentrating; the attempt uses casting timing and concentration rules and can be retried in a later round after distraction. When the wielder dies, all their spells and magic items end.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Harnessed Magic (ars-magica-core#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to creator-only cancellation at any distance and automatic shutdown on death; a world can alter who may cancel effects or whether they survive their maker.

rules.statement: A Land Regio Network lets a traveler move between any two networked regiones in one Diameter, regardless of distance. Finding whether a local regio belongs to the network requires an Intelligence plus Area Lore roll against Ease Factor 9; access may be controlled by others.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: (Land) Regio Network (ars-magica-core#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one Diameter of travel and an Ease Factor of 9; a world can change travel time, discovery difficulty, or gatekeeping to shape access to the network.

rules.statement: A Leather Ripper destroys a group of leather objects with a level 30 effect and zero Penetration. It requires a moment of concentration and one Fatigue level, but no speech or gestures.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Leather Ripper (ars-magica-core#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to destroying a group of leather items at the stated cost; a world can vary the affected materials or fatigue cost to tune the power's usefulness.

rules.statement: A character with Greater Power can activate a supernatural effect of level 50 or lower, assigning its levels one-for-one to Penetration instead if desired. Activation costs one Fatigue level for effects up to level 50 and two for levels 51–100; Initiative is Quickness minus half the effect's magnitude, rounded down.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Greater Power (ars-magica-core#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one significant power per Virtue with the stated level, Penetration, fatigue, and Initiative rules; a world can change those limits to calibrate the strength and cost of at-will abilities.

rules.statement: A character using Flexible Formulaic Magic may shift one of Range, Duration, Target category, or Target size by one step by changing the spell's casting level by one magnitude, or swap one parameter for another at the same level. The change cannot break Formulaic magic limits, does not apply to Ritual magic, and final level determines success, Fatigue, and Penetration calculations.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Flexible Formulaic Magic (ars-magica-core#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one-parameter adjustments within normal limits and exclude Rituals; a world can widen the adjustments or include Rituals to change how adaptable known spells are.

rules.statement: A magus with the leprosy-linked legacy may turn a wound into vis for one magical activity: a Light Wound yields 3 pawns, Medium 6, Heavy 9, Incapacitating 12, and a Deadly Wound that kills him 15. The vis is personal, cannot be stored, and any amount unusable or surplus to the activity is lost; the wound cannot recover until the activity ends, and using the power more than three times in a year adds a winter Aging roll.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Leprosy-linked Virtue (opening passage) (ars-magica-core#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to these wound-to-vis amounts; a world can change the wound costs or annual limit, because the magic is fueled by bodily suffering.

rules.statement: Life Boost adds +5 to a Formulaic or Ritual casting total for each extra Fatigue level committed before the casting roll. Spending more Fatigue levels than the caster has requires soaking damage equal to 5 per extra level plus a stress die, without armor; the Fatigue and any resulting wound apply even if the spell fails.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Life Boost (ars-magica-core#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to +5 per committed Fatigue level; a world can alter the bonus or damage rate, with exhaustion and bodily injury as the price.

rules.statement: Life-Linked Spontaneous Magic lets the caster declare an effect level before rolling. If the divided casting result falls short, each 5 points or fraction of shortfall costs one additional Fatigue level; when Fatigue runs out, the remaining shortfall becomes damage against Soak and may kill the caster.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Life-Linked Spontaneous Magic (ars-magica-core#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one extra Fatigue per 5 points of shortfall; a world can change that conversion, trading life energy for a more predictable spell effect.

rules.statement: A lesser supernatural power can be activated at will and has a total power level of at most 25. It costs one Fatigue level at level 25 or lower, two at levels 26–50, and so on; its Initiative is Quickness minus twice its magnitude, and power levels may instead be assigned one-for-one to Penetration.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Lesser Power (ars-magica-core#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the stated level and Fatigue brackets; a world can raise the cap or reduce costs, but must decide how freely available powers are balanced.

rules.statement: A power from Lesser Purifying Touch cures one chosen illness, but not injury or other misfortune, and using it costs one Fatigue level. The illness should be relatively minor or commonly recoverable without supernatural help.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Lesser Purifying Touch (ars-magica-core#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one Fatigue per cure of a limited illness; a world can broaden eligible ailments, with stronger healing requiring a greater cost.

rules.statement: A Maker of Textured Vessels spends one Long-Term Fatigue level to make a vessel that grants +3 to one Ability when materials for the related task have been stored inside it. The first user becomes its owner, other users gain no bonus, and the vessel is an Arcane Connection to that owner; a user with Magic Resistance cannot be claimed or benefit.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Maker of Textured Vessels (ars-magica-core#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one owner-bound vessel and a +3 task bonus; a world can alter the bonus or ownership limits, while creation fatigue and personal binding constrain use.

rules.statement: A Maker of Water Vessels creates a vessel at the cost of one Long-Term Fatigue level; its drinker substitutes the crafter’s Potter skill at the time of creation for one Ability for one scene or three minutes, whichever is longer. The first drinker becomes owner; drinking from a vessel owned by someone else, or first claiming an unowned vessel, causes Warping unless the drinker has Supernatural Virtues, and Magic Resistance prevents claiming.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Maker of Water Vessels (ars-magica-core#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one temporary Ability substitution per vessel; a world can adjust duration or the Warping restriction, with ownership and magical exposure as costs.

rules.statement: A Major Magical Focus adds the lowest applicable Art score twice when it applies to a spell or Lab Total; a Minor Magical Focus uses the same calculation for a narrower field. A magus can have only one focus, and it can benefit laboratory work but cannot be specifically based on a laboratory activity.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Major Magical Focus; Minor Magical Focus (ars-magica-core#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to doubling the lowest relevant Art contribution in a defined specialty; a world can widen or narrow eligible fields, limiting the advantage through specialization.

rules.statement: A magus with Mythic Blood may invoke and cancel one designed non-Ritual magical feat at will; its level plus Penetration limit depends on whether it needs speech or gesture: 15 for neither, 20 for gesture, 25 for speech, and 30 for both. The feat takes the time and concentration of fast-casting a mastered Formulaic spell, and its Penetration is not increased by the caster’s Penetration score.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Mythic Blood (ars-magica-core#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one freely toggled feat within the speech-and-gesture caps; a world can change those caps, with casting attention and inherited supernatural nature constraining it.

rules.statement: A spell using Performance Duration lasts only while its caster actively performs the chosen verbal or physical Ability. Casting requires a Characteristic + Ability roll against Ease Factor 3; failure prevents the spell, a botch botches it, and no further rolls are needed while performing continues.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Performance Magic — Performance (Duration) (ars-magica-core#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to requiring continuous performance and an initial Ease Factor 3 check; a world can broaden eligible performances, at the cost of making spellcasting harder to recognize.

rules.statement: When the caster stops performing, a Performance Duration spell ends. Combat use of Brawl or Martial Abilities requires a stress die with three extra botch dice, with every nonbotch treated as zero.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Performance Magic — Performance Abilities (ars-magica-core#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to ending the effect as soon as performance stops and heavily limiting combat performance; a world can relax the combat restriction, at the cost of less risk while casting amid danger.

rules.statement: A personal supernatural power is an at-will effect equivalent to a Formulaic spell of level 25 or lower, and must have Personal Range or be constant. Activation costs one Fatigue level at level 50 or lower and two at levels 51–100; the user may trade levels one-for-one for Penetration, otherwise it is zero.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Personal Power (ars-magica-core#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to limiting each power to level 25 and charging Fatigue according to level; a world can allow stronger powers, at the cost of greater exhaustion.

rules.statement: A Potent spell adds the sum of the selected Casting Item bonuses to the caster’s Casting Score, without changing the spell’s level. The caster must touch every specified item to cast; the spell’s Potency cannot exceed the designer’s Magic Theory score, and only a magus with Potent Magic can design one from scratch.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Potent Magic — How Potent Magic Works (ars-magica-core#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to requiring all designed items and capping Potency at Magic Theory; a world can permit remote or substitute items, at the cost of weakening the item-based constraint.

rules.statement: A relic with True Faith score 3 has one agreed power, but ceases to function after its owner behaves impiously until suitable penance is completed. A basic relic has True Faith score 1 and no additional power.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Powerful Relic; Relic (ars-magica-core#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to suspending the powerful relic after impiety until penance; a world can make the relic’s response less strict, at the cost of weakening its moral enforcement.

rules.statement: A skinchanger transforms into the animal represented by a carried item while in physical contact with it; the change takes one full round, and clothing and possessions do not transform. If the item is stolen, its holder gains an Arcane Connection to the character and the character cannot transform until recovering it; a destroyed item can be replaced over a season.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Skinchanger (ars-magica-core#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to requiring contact with a vulnerable animal-token and leaving possessions behind; a world can make the token easier to replace, at the cost of reducing the bodily and security risks.

rules.statement: A Spiritual Pact lets its holder spend a Confidence Point and roll Presence + Magic Lore + a stress die to gain a pool of the spirit’s Might points, always fewer than the spirit currently has. The holder can spend the pool on the spirit’s powers; it does not replenish, and any remaining pool is replaced rather than added to if the pact is invoked again.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Spiritual Pact (ars-magica-core#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a finite borrowed pool paid for with Confidence and limited by the spirit’s current Might; a world can make the patron more generous, at the cost of giving up more of its own power.

rules.statement: When a Spiritual Pact holder spends the last point in the pool, all powers used through it end and the active connection to the spirit lapses. While the pool remains, the spirit can sense the servant’s location and health through an indefinite Arcane Connection.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Spiritual Pact (ars-magica-core#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to ending all borrowed effects when the pool is exhausted and letting the spirit track its servant meanwhile; a world can reduce the spirit’s access, at the cost of weakening the pact’s oversight.

rules.statement: A divine-blooded character has Divine Might (Corpus) equal to age divided by 20, gains Magic Resistance from it, and holds Corpus vis equal to Might divided by 10, rounded down to at least one pawn; that vis can be extracted only after death. The character cannot be warped or use powers from a non-Divine realm.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Angelic heritage (ars-magica-core#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to age-scaled Divine Might and death-only vis extraction; a world can change the scale or extraction condition because the power derives from divine ancestry.

rules.statement: A divine-blooded character can invoke up to 30 levels of holy powers, designed using Hermetic or Divine guidelines, by spending Might points equal to half the power's magnitude rounded down, with a minimum cost of 1. Power Initiative equals the character's Quickness; each further purchase adds 30 power levels but does not increase Might.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Angelic heritage (ars-magica-core#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a bounded power-level allotment and Might expenditure; a world can adjust the allotment or cost because divine effects draw on a finite reserve.

rules.statement: Strong Faerie Blood delays aging rolls until age 50 rather than 35 and adds –3 to those rolls, cumulative with other bonuses. It also grants Second Sight without cost and vision in total darkness or semi-darkness.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Strong Faerie Blood (ars-magica-core#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to delayed aging and enhanced dark vision; a world can vary the age threshold or penalty because the body and senses reflect faerie ancestry.

rules.statement: A character with Variable Power selects one power that grows according to age divided by 10, Might divided by 5, Warping, or an appropriate Ability score. Each point of variation generally adds five effect levels or a similar effect of the same level; the Virtue may be taken for different powers but applies only once to each.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Variable Power (ars-magica-core#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one chosen trait that scales a single power; a world can choose a different scaling trait or rate because the power develops alongside its source.

rules.statement: Tethered Magic lets the caster hand control of a non-Ritual spell to another person for its duration, or attach it to an object that transfers it to a suitable target entering range. Activating an effect in a magic item can also be tethered, but every spell and item effect the caster activates becomes an Arcane Connection to that caster.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Tethered Magic (ars-magica-core#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to delegated control or object-triggered transfer with a personal connection as the cost; a world can change the connection's duration because tethered magic leaves a trace linking it to its originator.

rules.statement: Tainted Treasure cannot naturally increase in value: when traded, its curse moves to the replacement goods, and investments or buildings bought with it eventually fail. Used for a nonsinful purpose, the treasure destroys itself; it can still pay for services, but its sinful-spending limitation makes dangerous or covetous recipients likely.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Tainted Treasure (ars-magica-core#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a curse that follows exchanged value and punishes benevolent use; a world can define what counts as sinful because the treasure's harm expresses its infernal origin.

rules.statement: Unaging prevents age-related characteristic loss, though aging still accumulates Decrepitude. Nonfatal crises cause no ill effects; potentially fatal terminal crises can still kill, and the character dies at five Decrepitude points, without becoming enfeebled at four.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Unaging (ars-magica-core#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to immunity from ordinary aging but not fatal illness or accumulated decrepitude; a world can change the death threshold because the trait suspends decline rather than granting invulnerability.

rules.statement: Withstand Casting reduces Fatigue loss from spellcasting by one level per Virtue level, but never below one level lost; it does nothing when the spell would cost no Fatigue. When the Fatigue powers an effect, withstanding the loss also removes the corresponding benefit, and Vulnerable Casting increases the loss before this reduction is applied.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Withstand Casting (ars-magica-core#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to reducing casting fatigue while preserving a minimum cost and diminishing any benefit fueled by that cost; a world can alter the reduction because power still requires exertion.

rules.statement: When a character rolls zero on a Stress Roll for a Supernatural Ability, Power, or spell, remove 5 experience points from the involved Ability or Art. If the roll also botches, remove enough experience to lower the score by one full level, or 5 experience points if that is greater.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Broken Vessel (ars-magica-core#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: power loss follows failed stress rolls; a world can change the loss amount or trigger, with the cost expressed as diminishing supernatural ability.

rules.statement: A spontaneous spell must name its intended level. If its actual level differs by more than one level, it still takes effect, but the storyguide determines what it does; levels assigned to Penetration count toward the target.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Chaotic Magic (ars-magica-core#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: substantial variance makes an effect uncontrolled; a world can widen or narrow the one-level tolerance, at the cost of reliability.

rules.statement: The Constant Expression continuously produces minor, non-fatiguing spontaneous effects. The character has one long-term Fatigue level that cannot be recovered through sleep; suppressing the effects requires a Stamina + Concentration simple roll against Ease Factor 3 + Warping Score, with another attempt every two minutes after failure.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: The Constant Expression (ars-magica-core#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: minor magic keeps occurring and costs a lasting Fatigue level; a world can change its range or suppression difficulty, with distraction and exhaustion as the price.

rules.statement: To attempt Ceremonial or Ritual magic while affected by the Constant Expression, make the same suppression Concentration roll; one success covers the whole casting, and the attempt may be repeated every 15 minutes. The character also takes extra botch dice equal to her Warping Score, and her laboratory has a free safety penalty of –3.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: The Constant Expression (ars-magica-core#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: focused or laboratory magic remains possible but is riskier; a world can adjust the penalty or retry interval, with botch risk and unsafe lab work as costs.

rules.statement: Use of a corrupted Ability, Art, or spell for a selfish or sinful purpose gains +3 to its roll or total; if that bonus turns failure into success, the character gains 5 experience points in the relevant trait. Neutral or selfless use instead takes –3, and failure caused by that penalty removes 5 experience points; corrupted magic or Ability use also appears unholy.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Corrupted Abilities; Corrupted Arts; Corrupted Spells (ars-magica-core#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: selfish use is rewarded and decent use impaired, with visible spiritual taint; a world can alter the bonus, penalty, or experience change, making moral compromise the cost.

rules.statement: Aiming rolls of zero automatically botch, and Finesse rolls take –3. Separately, a Careless Sorcerer rolls two additional botch dice when casting spells, except when the character would normally roll none.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Clumsy Magic; Careless Sorcerer (ars-magica-core#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: inaccurate or careless magic is more likely to go wrong; a world can change the penalty or extra dice, with failure risk as the cost.

rules.statement: All totals that include a selected Form are halved, except Magic Resistance and Advancement Totals; experience costs are calculated from the unhalved Technique score. A selected Technique instead halves every total that includes it, including Lab and Casting Totals, but not Advancement Totals.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Deficient Form; Deficient Technique (ars-magica-core#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: one magical field sharply reduces relevant totals without changing advancement costs; a world can change which totals are affected, with reduced effectiveness as the cost.

rules.statement: When the character stays in one place longer than a season, apply –1 to all rolls and totals until the scene changes; after a year without a change of scene, the penalty becomes –3.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Craving for Travel (ars-magica-core#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: remaining in one place creates a worsening penalty; a world can change the waiting period or severity, with travel or exposure to new experiences as the remedy.

rules.statement: A character’s Perdo effects cannot cause permanent destruction: ordinary spells temporarily disrupt their targets, which return to their natural state when the spell ends. Ritual Perdo spells work normally.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Harmless Magic (ars-magica-core#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to temporary disruption for non-ritual Perdo; a world can allow lasting destruction, trading the limitation for more potent magic.

rules.statement: When a character faces a specified provocation, they avoid uncontrollable rage on a stress-die result of 9 or higher; if rage begins, they can try again each round to calm down. While enraged, they gain +3 Damage but take –1 on other scores and rolls, and a botch makes them try to kill everyone nearby.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Fury (ars-magica-core#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a provocation-triggered rage with a repeated chance to recover; a world can soften or intensify the trigger and consequences to tune the danger of losing control.

rules.statement: A character dependent on a particular Form of vis must consume 1 pawn of that vis each season. Without it, the character loses one Long-Term Fatigue Level that cannot be recovered until the vis is consumed; after consuming it, one level returns after an hour.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Hunger for (Form) Magic (ars-magica-core#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one pawn per season and accumulating fatigue loss; a world can change the required Form or frequency, balancing access to vis against survival.

rules.statement: On full-moon nights, a cursed person takes a full round to become a non-magical predator of Size –1 to +2; clothes and belongings do not change. At dawn they return to human shape and heal wounds suffered while changed, but retain animal intelligence and no memory of their actions in that form.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Lycanthrope (ars-magica-core#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the monthly trigger and dawn restoration; a world can alter the trigger, animal limits, or recovery, changing the curse’s duration and danger.

rules.statement: A character’s past sin is perceptible to suitable supernatural senses and imposes –1 on social interaction rolls or totals. Spending a Faith Point hides the manifestation and suspends the penalty for Sun duration.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Manifest Sin (ars-magica-core#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a persistent detectable mark with a Faith Point escape lasting Sun duration; a world can change the cost or duration to set how difficult penitence or concealment is.

rules.statement: Magic that needs its caster’s ongoing guidance responds sluggishly; condition-triggered spells and devices take about two minutes to activate. Constant effects from items made by the character are interrupted at sunrise and sunset, and the character takes –3 on Finesse rolls.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Inconstant Magic (ars-magica-core#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to delayed activation and two daily interruptions; a world can shorten or extend these lapses, trading reliability for the character’s magical instability.

rules.statement: After using a stress die to cast a spell, the character must make an Intelligence + Concentration stress roll against half the spell’s level. On failure, their next action must be another Formulaic spell of at least the same level, or a spontaneous spell with Fatigue spent and no levels reserved for Penetration; a botch leads to continued casting until unconsciousness.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Magic Addiction (ars-magica-core#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a spell-level-based control check and forced further casting on failure; a world can adjust the check or the cost of further casting to set the addiction’s severity.

rules.statement: When chance selects who suffers a misfortune, a jinxed character is favored as the target; for a random event affecting a group, the storyguide should make the character its victim half the time and their companions the other half. The character does not cause the bad luck or take extra penalties.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Jinxed (ars-magica-core#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to assigning half of group misfortunes to the jinxed character; a world can change that share, making bad luck more or less concentrated.

rules.statement: When a night-terror check fails, the character wakes in panic and loses a Long-Term Fatigue Level. The losses accumulate; if they become unconscious, the character sleeps for a full day and night, wakes Winded, and the terrors end.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Night Terrors (ars-magica-core#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a failed check causing cumulative fatigue loss and eventual forced recovery sleep; a world can adjust the check or recovery threshold to control how debilitating the condition is.

rules.statement: A character with a restricted supernatural power can use it only after a required ceremony, against a specified class of targets, or in stated circumstances; this limitation may be taken separately for each power. A Hermetic Restriction instead prevents spellcasting and effects from items the character made under certain conditions, but spells already running continue.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Restricted Power; Restriction (ars-magica-core#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to blocking activation whenever the stated restriction applies; a world can narrow or broaden the trigger, with loss of access to the power as the price.

rules.statement: Short-Lived Magic reduces spell duration: Year becomes Moon, Moon becomes Sunrise or Sunset, and Sun becomes Diameter. Diameter, Concentration, Ring, and Momentary durations are unchanged.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Short-Lived Magic (ars-magica-core#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to stepping down only the three listed durations; a world can make the reduction harsher, at the cost of spells ending sooner.

rules.statement: With Short-Ranged Magic, halve Casting Totals when the caster is not touching the target, and halve Lab Totals when designing an effect or spell with a range beyond Touch, including Eye.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Short-Ranged Magic (ars-magica-core#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to halving both totals when the range exceeds Touch; a world can set a different distance threshold, trading reach for reduced effectiveness.

rules.statement: A character susceptible to Warping gains one extra point associated with each Realm from which they gained any Warping during that year. These added points accrue over the year and do not trigger Twilight or other events caused by acquiring Warping points.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Susceptibility to Warping (ars-magica-core#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one extra point per represented Realm each year; a world can alter the rate, with increased supernatural instability as the cost.

rules.statement: Unnatural Magic makes the caster’s Creo rituals temporary: magically closed wounds reopen when casting ends, and Creo cannot extract vis from an aura because the resulting physical form will not persist.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Unnatural Magic (ars-magica-core#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to ending Creo ritual results when casting ends; a world can allow persistence, but doing so removes the defining instability.

rules.statement: Vengeful Powers cause a harmful side effect whenever a character uses a covered non-Infernal power for a non-sinful purpose; more beneficial uses provoke worse consequences. Magic Resistance and protections that keep demons away block the retaliating forces, though not their ability to sense the good use.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Vengeful Powers (ars-magica-core#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a harmful, roughly contemporaneous consequence whose severity rises with the good achieved; a world can change its severity, with collateral harm as the cost.

rules.statement: A character with Susceptibility to Faerie Power must resist disorientation with a Stamina roll at least equal to the Faerie aura rating on entering one, and has half normal Magic Resistance against faerie effects. Another person’s Parma Magica protects them normally.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Susceptibility to Faerie Power (ars-magica-core#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the aura-rated resistance check and halved personal resistance; a world can change the trigger or reduction, at the cost of heightened exposure.

rules.statement: A character with Viaticarus cannot be affected by demons’ Obsession power. Traditional threshold wards and magical wards against Corpus- or Mentem-aligned beings keep them out unless the ward’s establisher or a resident invites them in.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Viaticarus (ars-magica-core#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to blocking demonic temptation and warded entry, with an invitation overriding exclusion; a world can change who may invite them, altering the boundary’s authority.

rules.statement: With Vulnerable Casting, a magus loses one additional Fatigue level whenever a spell would normally cause Fatigue loss; spells that would cause none still cause none. Each level of this Flaw adds another lost level.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Vulnerable Casting (ars-magica-core#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one extra Fatigue level per rank on fatiguing casts; a world can adjust the added loss, trading spellcasting endurance for power.

rules.statement: Vulnerable Casting adds extra Fatigue loss in the same category as the spell: short-term for Formulaic spells and long-term for Ritual spells. Extra short-term loss can cause unconsciousness, with each overflowing level adding an hour; extra long-term loss can cause wounds.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Vulnerable Casting (preceding Vulnerable Magic) (ars-magica-core#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to matching the spell’s Fatigue category; a world can increase the extra loss, at the cost of unconsciousness or wounds.

rules.statement: A character cannot begin play with both Vulnerable Casting and Withstand Casting. If acquired later, apply Vulnerable Casting’s increased loss first and then reduce it through Withstand Casting.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Vulnerable Casting (preceding Vulnerable Magic) (ars-magica-core#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to vulnerability before resistance; a world can permit both from the outset, but must choose which effect takes priority.

rules.statement: A specified uncommon circumstance immediately ends the duration of a spell on its target, or ends all of the affected character’s active spells. This flaw can be taken multiple times with different triggers, but not alongside an equivalent Restriction or Necessary Condition.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Vulnerable Magic (ars-magica-core#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a narrow, stated trigger; a world can make triggers more common, making active magic easier to dispel.

rules.statement: A target who knows the magus has just used magic may perform a folk remedy to gain Magic Resistance of 5 times their Magic Lore score against that magus’s magic, or 0 if they lack the Ability. A person with Magic Lore can also try to break a lasting enchantment with an Intelligence + Magic Lore roll against 9 plus the spell’s magnitude or higher.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Vulnerable to Folk Tradition (ars-magica-core#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to resistance only against the recent caster; a world can broaden the folk remedy’s protection, limited by the target’s lore and the difficulty of breaking lasting effects.

rules.statement: Wanderlust limits the character to two nonconsecutive seasons per year in one area; intervening seasons must be spent traveling to unfamiliar places. If travel is prevented, the resulting discomfort should generate stories.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Wanderlust (ars-magica-core#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a two-season annual limit; a world can tighten or relax it, with confinement or travel obligations as the cost.

rules.statement: A character warped by magic begins with five Warping Points, Warping Score 1, and a Minor Flaw reflecting the source of the Warping. With troupe permission, the source can be another Realm.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Warped by Magic (ars-magica-core#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to five points and a source-related Minor Flaw; a world can change the source, with the character carrying its lasting mark.

rules.statement: Waster of Vis loses one quarter, rounded up, of the raw vis used; the lost pawns do not contribute to the magical effect but do count toward botch dice and the per-use maximum. Ritual casting and studying raw vis require one third more pawns than usual.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Waster of Vis (ars-magica-core#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to losing a rounded-up quarter of the vis; a world can raise or lower the waste, trading extra materials for the same effect.

rules.statement: Weak Magic halves the normal Penetration Total for spells after subtracting spell level and adjusting for Arcane Connections; it also halves the benefit of instilled item Penetration. It does not halve the Casting Total.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Weak Magic (ars-magica-core#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to halving penetration only; a world can change the fraction, reducing the ability to overcome resistance or improve enchanted items.

rules.statement: Corpse Magic takes fifteen minutes of chanting to awaken a corpse, which must be relatively intact and have received no burial rites from a Divinely sanctioned religion. At Ease Factor 9 it can speak, 12 can compel truth or protect it from further use, 15 can animate it, and 18 can place it under direct mental control; three failed command rolls end its activity until the moon rises.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Corpse Magic (ars-magica-core#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to temporary animation with escalating difficulty for truth and control; a world can lengthen activity, at the cost of stronger ritual and command requirements.

rules.statement: A character without an Ability score may use an unasterisked Ability at zero with three extra botch dice; asterisked Abilities are unavailable. One experience point permits use at zero without those extra dice, while Supernatural Abilities always require at least one experience point.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Abilities With No Score (ars-magica-core#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the stated training gate and risk; a world can relax access, reducing the significance of training or Virtues.

rules.statement: A hex requires an outward expression of intent: speak the wish to the victim, write its specifics on or near the target, or act on a representation in a matching way; some physical act is always involved. The hex must have a stated delay, from immediate to a descendant's third generation, and longer delays generally increase potency.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Hex (ars-magica-core#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Require a visible or physical expression and a declared delay; a setting can loosen either condition, with clarity and greater eventual potency traded against immediacy.

rules.statement: Add the delay modifier to Intelligence + Hex + aura bonus when checking a hex against its effect's Ease Factor: moment −12, day −6, week −3, month 0, season +3, year +6, generation +9, and lifetime +12. Ease Factors 6, 12, 18, 24, and 30 correspond to minor, serious, major, critical, and terminal severity, respectively; a botch can cause unintended outcomes or harm to the caster.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Hex Delay Modifiers / Hex Effects (ars-magica-core#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Use the listed delay scale and severity thresholds; a world can shift the bonuses or consequences, balancing stronger delayed curses against the risk of unpredictable backlash.

rules.statement: A hex can be permanently undone for a target by absolution in a religious ceremony, or removed by other supernatural effects. For removal effects, treat the hex as a spell whose level is 10 times the number of botch dice represented by its severity; for example, serious is level 20 and critical is level 40.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Hex (ars-magica-core#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Allow religious absolution or sufficient supernatural countermeasures to end a hex; a world can restrict which traditions work, making access to cleansing a cost.

rules.statement: Induction creates an illusion only its target can perceive. It requires at least one minute of conversation and a Communication + Induction roll; a target who cannot hear the inducer is immune, and belief becomes harder as the imagined situation grows more dangerous, at Ease Factors 3, 6, 9, 12, and 15 from innocuous to potentially suicidal.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Induction (ars-magica-core#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Require audible, sustained interaction and scale resistance with danger; a world can shorten the conversation or change the risk scale, at the cost of easier or less credible influence.

rules.statement: After successfully inducing an illusion, the inducer may spend at least fifteen minutes and roll again to raise it one danger level, with the new Ease Factor reduced by 3; repeated attempts can escalate the target through the risk levels. The target later recognizes magical influence unless the successful roll exceeds the Ease Factor by the stated margin, which can be reduced by up to 3 using listed follow-up and realism factors.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Induction (ars-magica-core#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Permit gradual escalation and give targets a chance to recognize the effect afterward; a world can make escalation faster or recognition harder, trading time and subtlety.

rules.statement: Parma Magica is a roughly two-minute ritual that adds five times the user's score to Magic Resistance until the next sunrise or sunset. The user can suppress it by concentrating; with consent and touch, the user can also protect one other person per score point while they can see one another, but protecting others reduces the effective score by 3 for the user and each protected person, and the user can cancel their protection at any distance.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Parma Magica (ars-magica-core#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Grant a strong personal ward and limited, sight-linked protection for consenting allies; a world can change the protection capacity or penalty, with broader defense diluting the ward.

rules.statement: Persona changes appearance after one round of concentration and a Stamina + Persona roll against Ease Factor 9, and the same process restores the natural appearance. The change can alter visible traits and apparent identity but not characteristics, essential nature, or transferred virtues and flaws; the user has one identity per Persona point.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Persona (ars-magica-core#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Allow convincing changes in outward appearance while preserving underlying traits and a finite identity repertoire; a world can relax those limits, risking changes to identity or biology.

rules.statement: Shapeshifter changes the user into a mundane animal from robin size (−10) through bear size (+2), using one round of concentration and a Stamina + Shapeshifter roll against Ease Factor 9; returning to human form uses the same procedure. The user has one available shape per ability point.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Shapeshifter (ars-magica-core#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Use a fixed repertoire of mundane animal forms and a common transformation test; a world can widen the size range or repertoire, with greater flexibility increasing the potential scope.

rules.statement: Premonitions can be called upon when danger might be avoided: roll Perception + Premonitions against a difficulty that rises as danger becomes less severe or more distant. A success by at least 3 also gives some indication of the danger's nature, with more detail for larger margins.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Premonitions (ars-magica-core#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Give warnings whose clarity depends on success and whose difficulty reflects urgency; a world can provide more specific forecasts, at the cost of making danger easier to evade.

rules.statement: A Major Hook grants 3 points to spend on Boons and a Minor Hook grants 1; Hooks do not provide Build Points. Each Minor Boon costs 1 point and each Major Boon costs 3, and Boons must be funded by Hooks.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Hooks; Boons (ars-magica-core#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to balancing Boons with Hook points; a troupe can add more Hooks for more advantages, accepting the extra story obligations they bring.

rules.statement: Accessible covenant power sets a maximum level for a single Lab Text or enchanted-device effect: Low allows 25, Medium 40, and High or Legendary has no limit. Medium access requires a covenant at least 10 years old, High 50 years, and Legendary 100 years; Low has no minimum age.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Accessible Power Level (ars-magica-core#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the chosen power tier's level and age limits; a world can raise or lower access, with hierarchy or a young covenant limiting what magi may use.

rules.statement: An Art summa costs Build Points equal to level plus quality, has a maximum level of 20, and has a quality cap of the lower of 22 or 11 plus the amount its level is below 20. An Ability summa costs quality plus three times level, has a maximum level of 8, and has a quality cap of the lower of 22 or 11 plus three times the amount its level is below 8; a tractatus costs one point per quality and cannot exceed quality 11.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Library (ars-magica-core#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the listed costs and caps; a world can loosen the limits, making exceptional books available at greater covenant expense or through play.

rules.statement: Lab Texts cost 1 Build Point per 5 levels, while Casting Tablets cost 2 per 5 levels; both follow the accessible-power maximum level. A Casting Tablet lets a magus cast a Formulaic or Ritual spell they do not know.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Lab Texts; Casting Tablets (ars-magica-core#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the stated costs and level limits; a world can make spell references more or less accessible, with tablets costing more and carrying risk when used for Aegis of the Hearth.

rules.statement: A vis source costs 5 Build Points for each pawn it yields annually. Stored vis costs 1 point per 5 pawns, and is consumed when used rather than replenishing automatically.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Vis (ars-magica-core#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to yearly source production and one-use stocks; a world can make vis scarcer, forcing magi to find replacements in play.

rules.statement: A Minor Contested Resource means access requires a story; ordinarily, winning the contest makes that resource available for 5 years. A covenant may take this Hook more than once for separate resources.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Minor Hooks — Contested Resource (ars-magica-core#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a five-year period of access after a successful story; a world can shorten or lengthen it, changing how often the resource must be secured.

rules.statement: Prevailing Loyalty begins with the total Gift modifier for all covenant magi divided by the number of magi: Gentle Gift or no Gift contributes 0, the Gift −30, and Blatant Gift −105. Apply situation and event modifiers to loyalty points, then convert the total to a score using the Ability advancement table, ignoring the negative sign.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Calculating Prevailing Loyalty (ars-magica-core#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to averaging Gift effects and applying the listed modifiers; a world can make covenfolk more or less responsive to treatment, with loyalty reflecting morale and willingness to serve.

rules.statement: Covenant familiarity adds 2 loyalty points for each year the covenant exists, up to a maximum equal to the base loyalty points imposed by the magi's Gifts. This familiarity applies to the home covenant's magi, not foreign Gifted visitors.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Familiarity (ars-magica-core#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to 2 points per year up to the stated cap; a world can change how quickly familiarity grows, trading faster loyalty gains for a longer adjustment period.

rules.statement: A Minor Aura Boon raises the covenant's Magic aura by 1 and may be taken up to 7 times, to a maximum aura of 10; all covenfolk must live within that aura. A Major Aura Boon instead raises the aura of a limited area by 1 and is only worthwhile when the overall aura is already 5.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Minor Boons — Aura; Major Boons — Aura (ars-magica-core#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the stated aura increases and limits; a world can concentrate or spread the stronger aura, with covenfolk exposed to Warping if they live in level 6 or higher.

rules.statement: At year end, add sundry expenses to normal yearly costs, subtract total expenditure from income, and add any surplus to covenant stores or subtract a shortfall. Even a small spring covenant may spend 50 pounds yearly, with larger ones spending five or ten times as much.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Expenditure (ars-magica-core#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to settling the account once yearly; a world can vary exceptional spending, because travel and purchases can create extra costs.

rules.statement: For every 10 points of inhabitants other than laborers, servants, and teamsters, provide 2 servant points; then include those servants and subtract twice the number of laborers from the relevant inhabitant-point total to find teamsters, at 1 per 10 points. Laborers, craftsmen, and teamsters are subject to the stated staffing limits and cost-saving rules.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Covenfolk Categories (ars-magica-core#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the listed staffing formulas; a world can reduce staff through magic or emergency austerity, at the cost of poorer service or other consequences.

rules.statement: Regular upkeep is generally 1 pound per inhabitant point, plus 1 pound per 10 laboratory points, 1 per 320 weapons-and-armor points, and 1 per magus, scribe, bookbinder, or illuminator for writing materials. Relevant building Boons add 2 pounds for each Minor Boon or 5 for each Major Boon; other listed categories, tithes, and sundry expenses are added separately.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Yearly Expenditure Categories (ars-magica-core#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to charging the stated yearly rates; a world can change prices or obligations, because maintenance, supplies, and local dues vary.

rules.statement: Inflation starts at zero in the covenant’s first year and usually rises by 1 pound for every 100 pounds of expenditure each year. It may stay level in favorable years or rise more in bad years, and does not rise in a year when expenditure falls.
