locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Inflation (ars-magica-core#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the suggested annual increase; a world can tie the change to harvests and spending, since local economic conditions drive prices.

rules.statement: Each laborer saves 1 pound, but laborer savings are normally capped at half of Provisions costs. A common craftsman saves 1 plus half their Craft Ability, rounded down; a rare craftsman saves an amount equal to their Ability, with savings capped per craft at 20% or 50% of the relevant expenditure category.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Cost Saving (ars-magica-core#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the stated savings and per-category caps; a world can adjust the caps to fit its production, because staffing and demand constrain useful output.

rules.statement: A magical item saves 1 pound yearly per magnitude of effect, while each Ritual spell saves about 5 pounds per magnitude, subject to the storyguide’s judgment. Magic may also replace workers and thereby reduce staffing needs.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Magic (ars-magica-core#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the listed annual savings; a world can change the valuation of magical labor, because vis and other costs may outweigh money saved.

rules.statement: When a covenant loses a Boon, provide story opportunities to regain it and treat the loss as a Hook; when it gains a Boon, give it a corresponding Hook reflecting the world’s response. A removable minor Hook should take at least six stories to overcome, and a major one around twenty.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: The Covenant in Play (ars-magica-core#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to turning changes in fortune into Hooks and sustained stories; a world can make Hooks harder or impossible to remove, because they drive the saga.

rules.statement: The Gift makes people who notice its bearer suspicious and envious, imposing a –3 penalty on the Gifted person’s social rolls and totals, including training. The Blatant Gift intensifies the reaction and penalty to –6; avoiding notice can prevent the ordinary effect, while precautions only reduce the Blatant Gift to ordinary Gift reactions.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: The Gift (ars-magica-core#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to applying the relevant penalty when the Gifted person is noticed; a world can alter its intensity or the effectiveness of concealment, because social suspicion is the Gift’s cost.

rules.statement: The Gift causes ordinary people to react with distrust or hostility, with a Blatant Gift producing stronger rejection and monitoring. A Parma Magica prevents its bearer from being troubled by other magi’s Gifts, but does not prevent others from reacting to the bearer’s Gift.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: The Gift; First Impressions (ars-magica-core#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to social resistance keyed to Gift intensity; a world can soften or sharpen it, with the Gift’s unsettling presence as the cause.

rules.statement: A spell combines one Technique, which determines the kind of magical action, with one Form, which determines what kind of thing it affects. A Form score also adds one fifth of that score, rounded up, to resistance against relevant hazards; applicable bonuses do not stack, so use only the highest.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: The Hermetic Arts (ars-magica-core#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one action discipline paired with one target domain and a rounded-up defensive bonus; a world can change the pairings or bonus, reflecting magical aptitude.

rules.statement: Creo creates or heals things and can improve them only within the limits of their kind. Created things last only while the spell lasts, although consequences such as tracks or dirt left behind can remain; created food nourishes only for the spell’s duration.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Creo (Cr) “I Create” (ars-magica-core#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to temporary created matter with lasting mundane consequences; a world can permit lasting creation, at the cost of raw vis.

rules.statement: Muto grants or removes properties a target cannot naturally have, while Perdo destroys a thing or one of its properties and Rego moves a thing or changes it to a state it can naturally take. Changes that violate essential nature must be maintained and revert when magical power stops.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Muto (Mu) “I Transform”; Perdo (Pe) “I Destroy”; Rego (Re) “I Control”; The Limit of Essential Nature (ars-magica-core#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to transformation bounded by natural possibility, with unnatural changes requiring upkeep; a world can loosen that boundary, making lasting alteration a major cost or exception.

rules.statement: Hermetic magic cannot affect the Divine or change a thing’s essential nature. It also cannot permanently create without raw vis, reverse natural aging, restore physical energy, transfer skills or knowledge, raise the dead, alter time, or affect an unsensed target without an Arcane Connection.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Limits of Magic (ars-magica-core#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to hard limits on these effects; a world can open particular limits through another tradition or exceptional theory, with the risk and rarity that entails.

rules.statement: Raw vis is tied to a Technique or Form and is consumed when used, usually degrading the substance that held it. For spellcasting, each pawn spent can add 2 to Casting Score; no more pawns of either type may be used than the caster’s score in its corresponding Art, and each pawn adds one botch die when a stress roll comes up zero.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Raw Vis; Spellcasting Options: Using Raw Vis (ars-magica-core#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to vis as a limited, consumed power source with a matching Art and botch risk; a world can raise the limits, at the cost of scarce magical material.

rules.statement: A Ritual spell takes 15 minutes per magnitude and requires one matching pawn of vis per magnitude. Formulaic spells take seconds; when a Formulaic casting total is 1–10 below the spell level, the spell still works but costs one Fatigue level, while a shortfall of 11 or more causes failure and the same Fatigue loss.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Ritual Magic; Formulaic Magic (ars-magica-core#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to quick learned spells and slower, vis-consuming rituals, with fatigue for marginal Formulaic castings; a world can change those costs, trading speed or endurance for power.

rules.statement: A spell’s Penetration Total is its Casting Total plus Penetration Bonus minus spell level. A total at or below zero cannot overcome any Magic Resistance; otherwise the spell affects a target only if its Penetration Total exceeds that target’s resistance.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Penetration Total (ars-magica-core#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to excess casting power overcoming resistance only when it exceeds the defense; a world can shift the threshold, making stronger defense or penetration investment decisive.

rules.statement: Casting requires concentration, and a failed concentration roll makes the spell fail. A maintained spell requires another roll every two minutes during continuing distraction, while an undistracted caster can maintain concentration for 15 minutes per point of Concentration.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Concentration (ars-magica-core#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to concentration as a vulnerable upkeep condition with timed checks under ongoing distraction; a world can extend or shorten the interval, with attention and training as the limiting resource.

rules.statement: Casting words and gestures each modify the casting score: loud speech and exaggerated gestures each add 1, while quiet speech subtracts 5, silent speech subtracts 10, subtle gestures subtract 2, and no gestures subtracts 5. Voice range is 50 paces when loud, 15 when firm, 5 when quiet, and zero when silent; ritual casting requires loud speech and exaggerated gestures at the points its procedure calls for them.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Spellcasting options (ars-magica-core#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to firm speech and bold gestures with no modifier; a world can tune the score penalty or voice distance, reflecting the tradeoff between discretion and effective range.

rules.statement: A fast-cast spontaneous spell first tests Quickness + Finesse + a stress die against the situation’s Ease Factor, which in combat is the opponent’s Initiative Total. Each additional fast cast in the same round takes a cumulative –6 to this speed test; after one fails, no more can be cast that round. The spell’s Casting Score is reduced by 10 and it adds two botch dice; options that alter the spell itself, such as spending raw vis to boost it, cannot be used.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Spontaneous Spells — Fast Casting (ars-magica-core#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the listed penalties and one failed speed test ending further attempts; a world can adjust the cumulative penalty or per-round limit, reflecting how taxing rapid reactions are.

rules.statement: To defend quickly against a magical effect, the caster must know its governing Form; if it cannot be identified automatically, Perception + Awareness must meet 15 minus the effect’s magnitude. A defense at half the attacking spell’s level can protect the caster or one other person, while one matching or exceeding that level can neutralize it; mundane threats likewise require a sufficiently powerful defense.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Spontaneous Spells — Fast Casting (ars-magica-core#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to half-level protection and full-level neutralization; a world can change these thresholds, reflecting how much force is needed to deflect or cancel an attack.

rules.statement: Ceremonial casting takes 15 minutes per magnitude and adds Artes Liberales and Philosophiae to the Casting Score; the spell’s level cannot exceed one magnitude per 15 minutes spent. Props add from +1 for tiny items to +5 for room-sized items. A prepared casting space reduces casting time to 12, 9, 6, 3, or 1 minute per magnitude according to its suitability.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Spontaneous Spells — Ceremonial Casting (ars-magica-core#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the stated time, level cap, and bonuses; a world can alter space and prop benefits, reflecting the expense and effort of constructing an effective ritual setting.

rules.statement: An Arcane Connection lets a caster target something not currently sensed, provided the spell uses Arcane Connection range and the caster is aware of the link. Once separated, a connection fades according to its kind, from hours for local air or shed skin to decades for a body part and indefinitely for certain magical bonds; careless storage may cause it to link to a different person or place.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Arcane Connections (ars-magica-core#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the listed connection lifetimes and awareness requirement; a world can shorten or lengthen them, reflecting the stability of sympathetic links and the risk of mishandling them.

rules.statement: Magic affects a target with Magic Resistance only if its Penetration exceeds that resistance; targets without resistance are affected regardless of Penetration. A Penetration Ability user with an Arcane Connection can multiply the Ability by a bonus of +1 to +4 based on the connection’s lifetime, and further sympathetic links can stack, with no one link granting more than +2. Forceless casting sets Penetration to 0, so it cannot affect a target with resistance of 0 or higher.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Penetration; Forceless Casting (ars-magica-core#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to Penetration needing to exceed resistance and the stated connection multipliers; a world can tune the multipliers or available links, reflecting how strongly likeness and provenance focus a spell.

rules.statement: Parma Magica adds five times its Ability score to Form-based Magic Resistance, takes two minutes to perform, and lasts until sunrise or sunset. The caster can suppress both Parma and Form resistance while concentrating; with consent and a touch, the caster can protect one person per Parma point while they can see one another, but this reduces the effective Parma score by 3 for everyone protected.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Magic Resistance — Parma Magica (ars-magica-core#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the fivefold resistance, duration, and visibility-limited protection; a world can adjust those values or the bond condition, reflecting the focus required to maintain a magical ward.

rules.statement: Magic Resistance prevents magic from reaching the protected person, clothing, and nearby possessions rather than dispelling the effect. A spell directly targeting a resistant person fails against that person, but an area spell can still affect others; magically moved things can cross the resistance, but their magical motion cannot unless it penetrates. An indirect effect that is not resisted must be aimed with Perception + Finesse, using an attack-like comparison.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Magic Resistance — The Functioning of Magic Resistance; Aiming (ars-magica-core#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to resistance stopping magical influence at the person while leaving natural motion and other targets unaffected; a world can broaden or narrow what is protected, reflecting whether the defense blocks effects, substances, or both.

rules.statement: A botch on a spell roll makes the Casting Total zero but generally still causes an uncontrolled, altered effect. Each zero on the botch dice grants one Warping Point, and gaining at least two from a single event triggers a Twilight avoidance test; a successful test takes two minutes to regain control, while failure enters Twilight. In Twilight, elapsed real-world time depends on Warping Score, ranging from two minutes at score 1 to final, eternal Twilight at score 10 or higher.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Dangers — Botches; Wizard’s Twilight (ars-magica-core#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to botches producing uncontrolled effects, Warping, and the listed Twilight timing; a world can change thresholds and durations, reflecting the lasting danger of magical instability.

rules.statement: On a successful comprehension, compare Intelligence plus the already-rolled stress die, after subtracting Enigmatic Wisdom, against the Twilight result. A tie or lower score gives the base duration; each point of excess shortens the duration by one table step, and anything shorter than Diameter lasts only a moment in the real world.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Twilight Time (ars-magica-core#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the duration table and one-step-per-point shortening; a world can change how quickly excess success compresses time to make comprehension affect how long the maga is absent.

rules.statement: A comprehension botch adds one duration-table step for each zero rolled and causes a negative experience effect; a failed roll gives the base Twilight duration and a bad effect. A botch on the Twilight side means only a total above zero is needed to comprehend, with no other consequence.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Twilight Time (ars-magica-core#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to harsher experience and longer exposure on a comprehension botch; a world can soften or intensify that penalty, with the cost expressed as adverse Twilight consequences.

rules.statement: Every Twilight experience adds a simple-die roll of Warping Points beyond those that triggered it. Comprehension gives a minor magical neutral or beneficial scar and one reward: twice the new Warping Points in relevant experience, a minor or major Virtue at 7 or more points, or a spell whose magnitude equals the points gained.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Effects of Twilight (ars-magica-core#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a random 1–10 additional Warping Points and a beneficial reward; a world can reduce the reward or change its thresholds, balanced by the additional Warping burden.

rules.statement: Failure to comprehend gives an annoying magical scar and one penalty: lose two relevant experience points per Warping Point (not below zero), gain a minor Flaw at 7–10 or major at 10 or more, or lose spells with total magnitudes equal to the points gained. Flaws require at least 7 gained points.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Effects of Twilight (ars-magica-core#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a loss proportionate to Warping gained; a world can alter the loss menu or thresholds, with the cost being the lasting harm of an incomprehensible experience.

rules.statement: During Twilight, a maga may be unconscious, act without initiative and later remember nothing, or physically disappear and return near the same place. If her body stays in the world, it is immune to magic, damage, aging, and hunger, but cannot cast magic.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: During Twilight (ars-magica-core#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one of the described outward states and immunity while present; a world can make exposure more dangerous, at the cost of losing the protection during the absence.

rules.statement: Certamen attacks and defenses are rolled each round; a defense equal to or higher than the attack prevents effect. An attack advantage is added to Intelligence plus Penetration, then resistance (Stamina plus Parma) is subtracted; each remaining five points or fraction costs one Fatigue level.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Certamen (ars-magica-core#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to fatigue as the duel's only damage and five-point loss bands; a world can change the resistance or bands, with exhaustion limiting the duel's duration.

rules.statement: Certamen causes no wounds. Losing more Fatigue levels than available causes an extra hour of unconsciousness for each excess level; either participant may spend attuned raw vis, gaining +2 attack or defense per pawn for one round, capped by the relevant Art score.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Certamen (ars-magica-core#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a short-lived +2 per pawn boost capped by Art; a world can raise or lower the cap, with expendable vis as the resource cost.

rules.statement: Heartbeast transformation affects only the Bjornaer, takes a moment, and leaves possessions unchanged. The fixed creature-kind cannot be changed by Hermetic magic; while transformed, Animal magic affects the maga rather than Corpus or Mentem, and she may cast magic with a –15 penalty because she cannot speak or gesture.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Bjornaer — The Heartbeast (ars-magica-core#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to an instantaneous, self-only change with fixed animal kind and severe casting penalty; a world can ease the penalty or broaden forms, at the cost of weakening the mystery's limits.

rules.statement: Held effects stay dormant while the caster concentrates; on release they resolve as Momentary effects, with effect and Penetration assessed at release. If the target or other required parameters no longer fit, the effect fails.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Spell Timing (Minor Illusion Mystery) (ars-magica-core#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to holding an effect only while concentration continues; a world can extend or shorten that window, with interruption or loss of a valid target as the cost.

rules.statement: Midday/Midnight effects begin at the next dawn, dusk, noon, or midnight and last until the following such boundary; Season effects wait for the next equinox or solstice and last until the one after it, require a ritual, and are Moon-level. While (Condition) lasts as long as the built-in condition holds and is Concentration-level; Not (Condition) lasts while the condition is absent, is Sun-level, and cannot exceed a month.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Spell Timing (Minor Illusion Mystery) (ars-magica-core#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the printed celestial boundaries and target conditions; a setting can change the calendar or permitted conditions, trading flexibility against a clearly bounded duration.

rules.statement: If (Condition) effects trigger when their specified condition is met and then last for their separately chosen Duration; add four magnitudes to that Duration-based level and cast the spell as a ritual. The spell expires unused if the caster enters Twilight, dies, or a year passes.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Spell Timing (Minor Illusion Mystery) (ars-magica-core#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one trigger within a year; a world can lengthen the waiting period, at the cost of a more persistent prepared effect.

rules.statement: A recurring spell must be a ritual and cannot be an effect that requires ritual casting for an unusual effect or non-Hermetic origin. Its frequency adds +5 magnitudes per minute, +4 per day, +3 per month, +2 per year, or +1 per decade; it cannot recur more often than once per minute. A second activation in the same allowed interval has no effect, and each recurrence cancels the previous instance before restarting.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Recurring Spells (ars-magica-core#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the frequency table and non-stacking restart; a world can allow faster or overlapping recurrences, with greater magical complexity as the cost.

rules.statement: For Verditius enchantment, crafting is integrated into the item's first enchantment season; if mundane crafting normally takes longer than a season, the combined process takes at least that many whole seasons. Appropriate Craft adds its current score to that creator's Lab Totals for the item, at most one Craft Ability per season. Verditius details add Philosophiae to Shape and Material bonuses for enchantment, subject to the Magic Theory limit; crafting this way reduces opening vis by the Craft score, to a minimum of one pawn.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Verditius — Verditius Magic (ars-magica-core#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to craft and enchantment sharing the required seasons and to the stated bonus limits; a world can demand more time or materials for complex creations.

rules.statement: An enchanted casting tool takes a laboratory season and can be enchanted only once; it cannot hold other powers or serve as an enchanted-item base. Its Lab Total must be at least double the final effect level, and it costs one pawn of Technique or Form vis per 10 effect levels, rounded up. Added options include fast or quiet casting for +2 levels each, multiple casting for +2 per extra spell, a casting-roll bonus of X for +X, or summoning or dismissing the tool for +10 each.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Enchant Casting Tools — Minor House Mystery Virtue (ars-magica-core#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one tool property package, bounded by Lab Total and vis; a world can permit more properties, at greater resource and laboratory cost.

rules.statement: Embitterment makes a listener hostile to a chosen person after as little as one round of comprehensible conversation. The check is Communication + Embitterment + stress die against a base Ease Factor of 6, 9, 12, 15, or 18 according to the relationship; hatred adds 3 and a desire to harm without killing, while loathing adds 6 total and prompts an attempt to kill. Range is Voice, Target Individual, and Duration Sun, extendable to Moon by adding 3 to the Ease Factor; the affected person cannot choose to disobey.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Embitterment (ars-magica-core#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the relationship-based difficulty and specified emotional intensity; a world can weaken compulsion, allowing resistance but reducing the power's certainty.

rules.statement: Whistle Up The Wind creates a wind effect at Voice range on an Individual target, with Stamina + Ability checked against an Ease Factor from 6 to 18 based on strength. The wind continues after whistling stops; Music checks can change it to a similar-strength wind, weaken it, or end it, but cannot strengthen it. At each sunset it drops one strength grade until gone.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Whistle Up The Wind (ars-magica-core#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a wind that decays one grade every 24 hours at sunset; a world can make it last longer, at the cost of sustained control or additional effort.

rules.statement: A magus can make an active Arcane Connection permanent with one laboratory season and one pawn of Vim vis. Vis extraction yields one pawn of Vim vis per 10 points or part thereof in the Creo Vim Lab Total per season; raw vis transfer between physical containers takes a day, and use in any one season is capped at twice Magic Theory in pawns.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Fixing Arcane Connections; Vis (ars-magica-core#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the season, vis, and capacity limits stated; a world can make vis scarcer or connections harder to preserve, increasing the material cost of magical work.

rules.statement: An invested item accumulates one progress point per season for each point its Lab Total exceeds the effect’s modified level; it is complete when progress reaches that level. Its total effect-vis expenditure cannot exceed the vis used to prepare it, and effects cannot be removed to free capacity.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Instilling Effects; Invested Items (ars-magica-core#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to fixed capacity and irreversible effects; a world can raise or lower capacity, paid for in preparation vis and permanent commitment.

rules.statement: A lesser enchantment needs no preparation, holds one power, and must be completed in one season with a Lab Total at least twice the modified effect level. Its vis cost is one pawn per ten effect levels or fraction, and the object’s material and size limit how much vis it can hold.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Lesser Enchantments (ars-magica-core#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one quickly made, capacity-limited power; a world can relax the season or capacity limits, at the cost of making lesser enchantments less distinct.

rules.statement: A charged item costs no vis and takes one season to make. It yields one charge for every five points or fraction by which the Lab Total exceeds the effect level, including one charge when the totals are equal; it cannot be made if the Lab Total is lower.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Charged Items (ars-magica-core#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to power stored as finite charges; a world can alter charges per excess Lab Total, trading item longevity against crafting advantage.

rules.statement: A device effect normally has zero Penetration, uses range measured from the device, and needs concentration to persist if its model spell does. One trigger action may be performed per round; breaking the device ends all its powers.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Using Enchanted Devices (ars-magica-core#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to device-centered range and fragile, limited activation; a world can change those limits, with greater reach or resilience making devices more potent.

rules.statement: Effect modifications add to the effect level: maintaining concentration for the wielder costs +5, restricting use to a fixed list of people costs +3, an environmental trigger costs +3, and a fast trigger costs +5 while granting +3 Initiative. A linked trigger costs +3 to the triggered effect; each added level of Penetration grants +2 Penetration.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Effect Modifications (ars-magica-core#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to level surcharges for added convenience or access control; a world can change the surcharges, balancing flexibility against crafting effort.

rules.statement: A talisman must be prepared by its magus, who can have only one at a time and must destroy the old one before making another. While touching it, the magus treats it as part of their body for Personal effects and touch, and it has an Arcane Connection to them; it also grants its Form-based Magic Resistance when not touched.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Talisman Attunement (ars-magica-core#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one personal anchor with powerful access and a risk if captured; a world can weaken the bond or remove the one-talisman limit, at the cost of diminished identity and security.

rules.statement: A Longevity Ritual takes a season and costs one pawn of vis per five years of the subject’s age, rounded up. Its aging-roll bonus is +1 per five points or fraction of the Creo Corpus Lab Total; it ends at an aging crisis, and the anchor makes the magus permanently sterile.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Longevity Rituals (ars-magica-core#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a crisis-ended life-prolonging anchor with sterility as its body cost; a world can change duration or fertility consequences, balancing longevity against lasting sacrifice.

rules.statement: A magus with a Laboratory Text can reproduce its effect in one season if their Lab Total meets its level; multiple effects may be reproduced together if they share Technique and Form and their combined levels do not exceed that total. The reproduced design cannot be altered, and a charged-item text yields charges equal to one fifth of the user’s Lab Total, rounded up.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Laboratory Texts — Using Laboratory Texts (ars-magica-core#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to exact, faster reproduction gated by Lab Total; a world can permit modifications or change the threshold, at the cost of reducing fidelity or increasing research burden.

rules.statement: Casting a formulaic or ritual spell from a tablet uses Stamina + Technique + Form + Aura + a stress die, modified for Virtues, Flaws, and requisites. Subtract the spell level: a result of 0+ casts it at one Fatigue level lost; −1 to −10 costs two, −11 to −20 costs three, −21 to −30 costs four and gives one Warping point, and −31 or less costs five and gives Warping points equal to spell magnitude; gaining at least two Warping points also requires a Twilight check.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Casting from Tablets (ars-magica-core#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Resolve tablet casting by the stated bands; a world can increase the fatigue or Warping burden for greater danger, paid for in the caster's stamina and stability.

rules.statement: To decode another magus's Laboratory Text, spend seasons in a laboratory accumulating points equal to the relevant Technique-and-Form Lab Total; reaching the text's level makes it understood. Once a text is decoded, other texts by that author at or below that level can be translated without a lab, while a higher-level text needs separate decoding; translated texts cannot become Casting Tablets.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Translating Laboratory Texts (ars-magica-core#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Use Lab Total points as the decoding progress; a world can make unfamiliar notation harder by raising the required level, costing seasons and laboratory access.

rules.statement: In one season, a magus may perform multiple laboratory activities only if they are the same activity type and use the same Technique and Form. Add their levels together and compare the sum to the Lab Total; if their applicable Lab Totals differ, use the lowest, and experimentation results affect every activity that season.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Multiple Laboratory Activities (ars-magica-core#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Combine compatible work under one Lab Total; a world can allow more varied combinations, at the cost of spreading effort and sharing experimental consequences.

rules.statement: A qualified laboratory assistant adds Intelligence + Magic Theory to the researcher's Lab Total, with the assistant's Virtues and Flaws applying too; a negative contribution penalizes the total. The normal assistant limit is the researcher's Leadership score, with at least one allowed, and a familiar permits one additional assistant; helpers gain exposure experience but no other benefit from the activity.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Help in the Laboratory (ars-magica-core#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Add each eligible helper's contribution; a world can restrict assistance to preserve secrecy or coordination, with reduced laboratory output as the cost.

rules.statement: Missing up to ten days of a season causes no laboratory penalty. Missing 11–20 days reduces the Lab Total by 10 plus two for each day beyond ten, to a maximum reduction of 30; missing more than 20 days prevents laboratory work for that season.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Distractions from Lab Work (ars-magica-core#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Apply the stated lost-time penalty; a world can shorten the grace period because celestial timing is unforgiving, costing interrupted researchers their season's work.

rules.statement: A familiar bond requires a Lab Total of at least Magic Might + 25 + five times the animal's Size, and is completed in one season if the total is sufficient. It costs one pawn of matching Technique or Form vis per five points or fraction of the Lab Total; bonding makes each partner an Arcane Connection to the other, grants them a mutual True Friend relationship, and lets either affect the other without first overcoming the other's Magic Resistance.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: The Initial Bond; The Bound Familiar (ars-magica-core#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Require the stated Lab Total and vis to create a reciprocal bond; a world can make bonds more demanding, with scarce vis and mutual exposure as the price.

rules.statement: The bond's golden, silver, and bronze cords each range from 0 to +5. Allocate Lab Total points among them; scores 0–5 cost respectively 0, 5, 15, 30, 50, and 75 points, and no cord allocation may exceed the Lab Total. Golden reduces magic botch dice but cannot remove them all; silver adds to Personality and mental-resistance rolls and can attempt once per day to free an overcome partner on 9+; bronze adds to Soak, healing, deprivation, and aging rolls, but not Fatigue resistance.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: The Three Cords (ars-magica-core#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Set cord benefits by purchased strength; a world can limit the total allocation or cord maximum, requiring the partners to trade one kind of protection for another.

rules.statement: Powers invested in a familiar bond may target the magus, familiar, or both, with no limit on the number invested. Matching the binding Arts gives +5 Lab Total if either Art matches and +10 if both do; each power costs one pawn of matching vis per ten modified levels or fraction, and an invested constant effect does not cause Warping.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Empowering the Bond (ars-magica-core#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Permit bond powers only for the partners and charge vis by modified level; a world can narrow eligible targets or remove the constant-effect exception, at the cost of flexibility or safety.

rules.statement: Opening an apprentice's Arts takes a season and gives score 0 in all fifteen Arts. Existing supernatural abilities require an Intellego Vim Lab Total based on their levels and their Virtue category; meeting the requirement only removes them, while reaching twice the requirement lets the master choose to preserve or convert them into a Hermetic Virtue. An Art below 5 in the master's scores gives the apprentice a Deficiency in that Art.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Opening the Arts (ars-magica-core#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Use the Lab Total thresholds to decide whether prior supernatural gifts are lost or retained/converted; a world can raise the threshold to protect a child's existing abilities, costing laboratory effort.

rules.statement: At the start of each season, a magus may choose to experiment on a spell, enchantment, familiar enchantment, or item investigation. Experimentation adds a simple die to the Lab Total but requires a stress-die roll on the extraordinary-results table for every project season; results accumulate across seasons. A Laboratory Text cannot be used while experimenting.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Arcane Experimentation — The Experimental Premise (ars-magica-core#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a simple-die Lab Total bonus with a results-table risk each season; a world may turn risk up or down, trading certainty for a chance to exceed normal laboratory limits.

rules.statement: A chosen risk modifier of +1 to +3 is added to each extraordinary-results roll and adds the same number of botch dice. A zero on the stress die calls for one botch die plus the risk-modifier dice, and one more botch die for each point of laboratory supernatural aura.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Arcane Experimentation — Exceptional Risk; Extraordinary Results (ars-magica-core#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the selected modifier increasing both result severity and botch exposure; a world can make ambition more or less costly, with dangerous magic and aura magnifying mishaps.

rules.statement: If an experimental creation is flawed or hard to use, the magus can keep it or recreate it in another season using normal laboratory rules. Recreation adds the Magic Theory score from the experiment to the Lab Total, so that score is counted twice; no further experimentation is required.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Arcane Experimentation — Extraordinary Results (ars-magica-core#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to letting a near-miss be salvaged for a season and a doubled Magic Theory contribution; a world can make recovery easier or harder, with time as the price.

rules.statement: On an experimental spell project, if the Lab Total including the simple-die bonus remains below the spell level, the spell is not invented, but the extraordinary-results roll is still made. On an item project that cannot meet the invested effect level, all vis is lost and the extraordinary-results roll still applies; a flawed effect that does fit occupies device capacity.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Arcane Experimentation — Inventing a Spell by Experimentation; Enchanted Items Created by Experimentation (ars-magica-core#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to requiring the target level and preserving a flawed item's capacity use; a world can relax the threshold or capacity penalty, at the cost of diminishing the danger of experimental investment.

rules.statement: When an experiment produces a side effect, a simple-die result determines its scale: results 1–10 range from an exaggerated sigil, through minor or major flaws and side effects, to benefits and a fatal flaw. A modified-effect result instead reduces or increases parameters on 1–6, restricts use on 7–8, changes the effect on 9–10, or replaces it on 11+.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Extraordinary Results Chart — Side Effect; Modified Effect (ars-magica-core#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to anomalies modifying a creation's behavior or parameters according to the roll; a world can make anomalies gentler or harsher, with extraordinary power carrying unpredictable consequences.

rules.statement: A breakthrough needs about 30 points for a Minor, 45 for a Major, or 60 for a Hermetic advance. A Minor advance adds a useful feature within existing theory, a Major pushes but does not break limits, and a Hermetic advance breaks a Lesser Limit.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Arcane Discovery — The Breakthrough (ars-magica-core#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to escalating research thresholds as the proposed change approaches a magical limit; a world can vary the totals, making transformative theory require more or less accumulated work.

rules.statement: Original research requires an experimental Discovery result. A risk modifier of up to +3 is permitted according to Magic Theory, at one point per five points or fraction thereof; it modifies the results roll rather than the Lab Total, and some or all of it may be added or subtracted to obtain a Discovery alongside the ordinary result.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Arcane Discovery — Experimentation (ars-magica-core#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to using expertise to steer the chance of discovery without boosting production; a world can broaden or narrow that steering, with the danger and uncertainty of research remaining.

rules.statement: To stabilize a discovery, repeat the original experiment for the same number of seasons with the same Lab Total, risk modifier, and vis, and adjust the results roll in the same direction. Avoiding Disaster, No Benefit, and Complete Failure stabilizes it; success grants breakthrough points equal to effect magnitudes and creates a Laboratory Text. The attempt also gives Warping Points equal to magnitude minus a simple die, whether it succeeds or fails.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Arcane Discovery — Stabilizing the Unknown (ars-magica-core#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to requiring exact replication before a discovery becomes reliable, awarding magnitude-based progress but imposing Warping; a world can change the stability threshold or Warping cost.

rules.statement: Studying a non-Hermetic insight source takes a season and a stress roll of Intelligence + Magic Theory against 18; success grants one insight, failure grants none, and a botch creates a false insight. An insight specifies one exact effect; successfully making it while experimenting earns breakthrough points equal to its magnitude, but the effect's parameters cannot be varied.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Arcane Discovery — Integration; Creating the Effect (ars-magica-core#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to source-based insights enabling fixed experimental effects and magnitude-scaled progress; a world can make insight easier or more restrictive, with access to rare knowledge as the bottleneck.

rules.statement: A lab’s net Virtue capacity cannot exceed Size + Refinement. Occupied Size equals Virtue points minus Flaw points minus Refinement; when occupied Size is positive, subtract it from Refinement to calculate base Safety.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Laboratory Characteristics; Laboratory Virtues and Flaws (ars-magica-core#025)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the Size-plus-Refinement capacity and occupied-space Safety formula; a world can change how much room refinements create, reflecting the work and space needed to fit improvements.

rules.statement: Raising Refinement by one takes a season, requires familiarity and Magic Theory at least three higher than the desired score, and increases Safety by one or two points depending on occupied Size. Each season of work to improve it may also yield Highly Organized on an Intelligence + Magic Theory roll of 12, remove a Hidden Defect on 15, or acquire that defect on a botch.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Refinement (ars-magica-core#025)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one season per Refinement point and the stated skill thresholds; a world can vary the duration or checks to represent how difficult lab redesign is.

rules.statement: A lab’s General Quality adds to every Lab Total. Specializations add their scores to matching Lab Totals, and applicable Specialization bonuses accumulate; a lab may have at most two activity and four Art Specializations, with no more than two Techniques among the latter.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: General Quality; Laboratory Specializations (ars-magica-core#025)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to additive General Quality and Specialization bonuses within the stated caps; a world can change these caps to reflect how narrowly or broadly a lab can be optimized.

rules.statement: Safety subtracts from botch dice on lab activities. In an unsafe lab, each season requires a simple die roll; a result no greater than the absolute Safety score triggers a botch check, with at least one botch die, and a botch causes a lab accident.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Safety (ars-magica-core#025)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the seasonal accident chance and botch-die adjustment described; a world can make unsafe work more or less hazardous, with accidents as the cost.

rules.statement: For each season of labwork, a positive Warping score gives a chance equal to that score on a simple die of warping the season’s product. Odd results cause a side effect and even results a modified effect; the lab also receives Personality Traits totaling its Warping score.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Warping (ars-magica-core#025)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a per-season Warping check that alters the output; a world can change the trigger rate or outcome table, with unpredictable products as the price of a warped lab.

rules.statement: A lab’s Health modifies inhabitants’ Wound Recovery rolls, and half its score rounded down modifies Living Conditions for Aging if they spend at least half the year there. Each Aesthetics point, positive or negative, gives the owner five experience points in an appropriate Reputation over time.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Health; Aesthetics (ars-magica-core#025)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to Health bonuses only for residents and the stated Reputation experience per Aesthetics point; a world can alter the thresholds or rate to model local living conditions and gossip.

rules.statement: If maintenance is unaffordable, after two seasons of use without it the lab automatically gains a Flaw or loses a Virtue that reduces Upkeep; the process may repeat after another two seasons. Extensive Stores extend the initial grace period to six seasons, while No Stores removes it.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Upkeep; Structure Virtues and Flaws (ars-magica-core#025)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to deterioration after two neglected seasons, modified by storage conditions; a world can turn the grace period to reflect how quickly neglected equipment becomes unusable.

rules.statement: Minor lab Virtues generally require one season to install and Major ones two, with the worker needing Magic Theory at least three points above Refinement; Flaws take effect immediately. Improvements must fit available capacity or be balanced with Flaws.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Laboratory Virtues and Flaws (ars-magica-core#025)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to construction time, skill threshold, and space balancing; a world can change these costs to represent how labor-intensive laboratory improvements are.

rules.statement: A spell’s level is its base effect level plus adjustments for Range, Duration, Target, and size. Its magnitude is one fifth of its level, rounded up; each magnitude normally costs 5 levels, and a ritual spell requires that many pawns of vis.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Chapter 9: Spells — Levels; Magnitudes (ars-magica-core#026)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Use five-level magnitude steps and ritual vis costs by default; a world can change those rates to make magic more or less costly because its magical reserves differ.

rules.statement: Raising or lowering Range, Duration, or Target by one listed step changes a spell by one magnitude, or 5 levels; below level 5, each such step changes it by only 1 level. Spontaneous spells must use listed parameter categories, while designed Formulaic or Ritual spells may use other values at the troupe’s discretion.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Chapter 9: Spells — Changing Ranges, Durations, and Targets (ars-magica-core#026)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Use the listed parameter ladder and the reduced sub-level-5 adjustment; a world can permit custom parameter categories more freely because its magic theory is more flexible.

rules.statement: A continuing spell can persist after its caster moves out of range, but an effect that the caster controls can only be controlled while the caster is in range; control resumes if the caster returns. Momentary magic ends quickly even when its consequence remains, while longer durations sustain an effect, and a Momentary ritual creation normally lasts as an ordinary thing.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Chapter 9: Spells — Ranges; Durations (ars-magica-core#026)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Treat spell duration as governing active magic, not every lasting consequence; a world can make consequences expire with the spell because its magic sustains reality more directly.

rules.statement: A container-target spell can either lock onto valid targets present at casting, continuing to affect them after they leave, or affect valid targets while they are inside during the spell. The second mode stops affecting targets that leave, affects later entrants, and ends if its container ceases to exist; a Circle-target spell ends if its circle is broken.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Container Targets — Static and Dynamic Targets (ars-magica-core#026)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Use static targets unless the spell is designed as dynamic; a world can make container effects dynamic by default because its magic tracks changing occupants.

rules.statement: A magical-sense spell grants one kind of information through one of the recipient’s ordinary senses; several kinds require separate spells. The information inherits that sense’s limitations, and the magical sense must penetrate the resistance of both the sensed creature and the recipient, while the ordinary sense itself needs no penetration.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Magical Senses (ars-magica-core#026)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Require one spell per sense and penetration against both relevant resistances; a world can relax these limits because its supernatural senses bypass ordinary perception or resistance.

rules.statement: A Rego ward protects its target from things of the relevant Form, and its range is measured to the protected target. A Circle ward also prevents warded things on either side from crossing or acting across the circle, including damaging it; Hermetic wards still need to penetrate Magic Resistance.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Magical Wards (ars-magica-core#026)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Use the protected target as the ward’s target and require penetration; a world can let wards affect intruders directly because its protective magic can target threats.

rules.statement: Creo magic can create natural objects as sound examples of their kind, with Finesse used to control details. Creo-made artificial objects last only for the spell’s duration unless made by a Momentary ritual; Rego craft reshapes existing materials without creating or destroying matter, and a Perception + Finesse roll must meet the mundane craft difficulty plus 3, adjusted for the work time.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Magical Craft (ars-magica-core#026)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Use distinct Creo creation and Rego rearrangement rules, with Rego requiring mundane-material expertise; a world can allow matter creation through Rego because its magic does not conserve matter.

rules.statement: Creo craft uses Intelligence + Finesse: one basic property has Ease Factor 0, two or three properties or one precise property has Ease Factor 3, and elaborate changes use Rego craft difficulties. Spell designs may permit specified variations, generally at higher spell level, but each spell still makes only one type of thing.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Magical Craft — Creo craft magic (ars-magica-core#026)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Limit each design to one product type and charge for flexibility; a world can allow unrestricted custom outcomes because its craft magic is inherently adaptable.

rules.statement: A spirit-summoning spell brings the spirit instantly to the caster but provides no control over it; it may be directed into the summoner’s ward. A spirit in Mythic Europe can be called by a non-ritual spell, but a spirit in another realm requires a ritual.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Summoning Spirits (ars-magica-core#026)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Summoning moves a spirit without binding it and requires a ritual across realms; a world can grant control or remove the ritual cost because its summoning tradition is stronger.

rules.statement: A spell’s behavior is fixed when it is designed: a static container effect affects those present at casting and stays with them, while a dynamic effect affects whoever is inside during its duration, vanishes from them on exit, and returns on reentry. If the container ceases to exist, the dynamic effect ends; the two behaviors require separate spells, though knowledge of one helps invent the other.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Passage 28, before “Being Inside a Container” (ars-magica-core#027)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to fixed spell behavior and let a world turn the static/dynamic choice; dynamic coverage costs a separate spell and fails if its container ceases to exist.

rules.statement: A container remains a spell target while it is still the same thing, even if it moves or changes size; opening a door does not end a room, but packing away a tent does. A container that grows beyond the spell’s size limit ends the effect, and a marked circle changes identity if its size changes or it is moved to another surface; a boundary defined only by a marker is similarly fragile.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Persistence of Containers (ars-magica-core#027)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to intuitive continuity of the same container; a world can make marked borders more fragile, at the cost of allowing small physical changes to end their spells.

rules.statement: For most Forms, each added magnitude (five spell levels) multiplies the maximum target size by ten. Base sizes are Form-dependent for Individuals, a Part is at most a base Individual, a Group has the mass of about 10 standard Individuals, a Room fits about 100, a Structure contains 10 base Rooms, and a Boundary is 100 paces in diameter; Intellego and Circle targets ignore target-size adjustments.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Targets and Sizes (ars-magica-core#027)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to these approximate size bands; a world can turn toward precise measurement, with the cost of extra calculation and adjudication.

rules.statement: Changing a non-living target’s size at the base guideline can enlarge it by up to tenfold or shrink it by up to 100-fold. Each extra magnitude allows another tenfold enlargement or hundredfold shrinkage; original target size adds to those modifiers, and living-target size changes use their own guidelines, with roughly 3 Size points equaling a tenfold change.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Targets and Sizes (ars-magica-core#027)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the stated multiplicative limits; a world can turn size changes toward finer measurement, with larger transformations requiring higher spell levels.

rules.statement: A Creo spell that creates something targets the created Individual or Group, not a Room; creating a part is healing or Muto instead. A Momentary Creo spell that leaves a lasting creation must be a Ritual.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Targets and Creo; Ritual Spells (ars-magica-core#027)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to creation targeting the thing produced; a world can allow room-filling creation only through an appropriately sized Group, at the cost of meeting that spell’s size level.

rules.statement: Rituals take longer and require vis. Formulaic and Spontaneous spells cannot have Year duration, Boundary target, or levels above 50; Rituals are at least level 20, are mandatory when a guideline or lasting Momentary Creo creation requires one, and cannot be replicated by Spontaneous magic, even ceremonially.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Ritual Spells (ars-magica-core#027)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to rituals as costly access to effects unavailable to ordinary casting; a world can widen non-ritual limits, at the cost of weakening the distinction and vis requirement.

rules.statement: A requisite needed for an effect adds no spell levels, but one that adds a meaningful extra effect usually adds at least one magnitude; a purely cosmetic detail needs none. A caster’s effective score for each primary Art is capped by the lowest applicable requisite score, including multiple requisites and any relevant Deficiency.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Requisites (ars-magica-core#027)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to requisite Arts limiting casting ability and meaningful additions raising level; a world can relax either limit, at the cost of broader access to complex effects.

rules.statement: Animal magic affects natural nonhuman animals, animal-like minds and bodies, and animal products. Use Animal for a creature with Cunning and Mentem for one with Intelligence; an intelligent being’s animal-shaped body can still be affected by Animal, while Bjornaer in animal form is treated as an animal in both mind and body.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Animal Spells (ars-magica-core#027)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to targeting by the creature’s essential mind and body type; a world can treat shapechangers as animals more broadly, at the cost of making their altered forms easier to affect.

rules.statement: Repeated or prolonged Muto Animal transformations can warp an animal’s natural constitution or destroy it. Animals given new abilities may need a few minutes to adapt to them.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Muto Animal Guidelines (ars-magica-core#027)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to temporary adaptation with cumulative strain from excess transformation; a world can reduce the strain, at the cost of making repeated alterations safer.

rules.statement: Animal effects can calm, frighten, paralyze, passivate, or control animals at different power levels; control may require continued attention or touch, and some especially stubborn animals can resist each round against Ease Factor 12.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Rego Animal Spells (ars-magica-core#028)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to control that lasts only while maintained; a world can make commands more durable, with resistance and loss of control as the cost.

rules.statement: Aquam normally affects liquids outside living bodies; liquids inside a body require an effect designed for that purpose and an appropriate Animal or Corpus requisite. A base water Individual is about five paces wide and two deep; naturally occurring liquids use one-tenth that volume, processed liquids one-hundredth, dangerous liquids one-thousandth, and poison one dose.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Aquam Spells (ars-magica-core#028)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to these target categories and volumes; a world can broaden bodily targeting, at the cost of requiring specialized design and appropriate requisites.

rules.statement: Temporary created water can quench thirst but gives no lasting benefit; created poisons begin at Ease Factor 3, with each added magnitude increasing that factor by 3. More unnatural liquids require higher magnitude, and very unnatural liquids also need a Muto requisite.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Creo Aquam Guidelines (ars-magica-core#028)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to temporary water and escalating poison difficulty; a world can permit lasting nourishment or stronger poison, with greater spell investment.

rules.statement: A ward can prevent eligible supernatural beings from affecting targets inside its circle; the Rego Animal ward applies to beasts whose Magic Might is no higher than the spell level, while the Rego Aquam faerie ward also bars direct or indirect interference and ranged attacks across the boundary.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Rego Animal Spells — GENERAL; Rego Aquam Spells — GENERAL (ars-magica-core#028)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a bounded ward keyed to a power threshold; a world can allow higher-ranked beings through, or strengthen the ward, with a corresponding increase in spell level.

rules.statement: Rego Aquam can move liquid instantly up to 5 paces; each added magnitude raises the distance to 50 paces, 500 paces, one league, seven leagues, and then a destination known through an Arcane Connection. Slightly or very unnatural movement costs one or two magnitudes more.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Rego Aquam Guidelines (ars-magica-core#028)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the stated distance ladder and extra cost for unnatural movement; a world can extend travel further, requiring stronger magic or a connection to the destination.

rules.statement: Water can naturally be changed into ice or steam by Rego Aquam without requisites; controlling it in a slightly unnatural way adds one magnitude and a very unnatural way adds two. Rego Aquam botches can cause spectacular, dangerous loss of control.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Rego Aquam Guidelines (ars-magica-core#028)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to natural-state changes without extra requirements; a world can permit stranger transformations, but they cost power and risk loss of control.

rules.statement: Aquam and Auram effects can be maintained only for their stated duration; several spells end when concentration stops, and some effects explicitly persist or end in other ways, such as oil lasting until it dissipates or a ward lasting for its ring duration.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Creo Aquam Spells; Rego Aquam Spells; Creo Auram Spells (ars-magica-core#028)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the spell’s stated duration and concentration limits; a world can make effects persist longer, at the cost of greater power or a ritual.

rules.statement: Weather spells generally need Sight range to reach the upper air where weather forms; creating weather in unnatural circumstances adds one magnitude, very unnatural circumstances two, and an effect wholly detached from normal context four. A base Auram Individual covers a weather phenomenon across a standard Boundary.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Creo Auram Guidelines (ars-magica-core#028)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to naturally situated weather and standard area scale; a world can allow localized or context-free weather, but charges additional power for the departure from normal conditions.

rules.statement: The thorny-bush barrier grows from existing bushes or fertile soil and can extend 20 paces, stand 4 paces high, and be 1 pace thick. It has +15 Soak, can be cut only with edged weapons (requiring a Heavy Wound), and inflicts +15 damage on anyone trying to force through; climbing it requires a Dexterity + Athletics roll against 9 and inflicts +10 damage.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Before LEVEL 25, thorny-bush wall description (ars-magica-core#030)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a hazardous, impassable plant barrier; a world can turn down its size or damage because the thorns are unnaturally resilient.

rules.statement: The winter-solstice crop ritual must be performed at noon the day after the solstice, within the affected region. It protects the crops belonging to those present from ordinary blight and disease for a year, but does not control weather or prevent deliberate harm; its area can cover roughly six miles across.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: LEVEL 35, The Bountiful Feast (ars-magica-core#030)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a year-long crop-protection field; a world can narrow ownership or territory because the rite only covers fields of its participants.

rules.statement: A living tree made conscious can perceive its surroundings at a normal human level, but moves its branches only over hours. A ritual can instead make a small forest's trees conscious, cruel, and able to reach the ground with their branches over an hour or two; they cannot uproot themselves.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: LEVEL 25, Stir the Slumbering Tree; LEVEL 60, Curse of the Haunted Forest (ars-magica-core#030)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to awareness without quick movement; a world can grant greater mobility at the cost of ritual-scale magic and a dangerous disposition.

rules.statement: Plant transformations usually retain some plant nature; turning a plant into another kind of thing generally requires one magnitude above the most fitting guideline. Turning plants into worked goods also adds one magnitude, and changing plants into metal or stone requires Terram.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Muto Herbam Guidelines (ars-magica-core#030)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to requiring extra power for finished goods or nonplant forms; a world can relax the added magnitude because the transformation is more extensive.

rules.statement: Destroying living wood usually requires one magnitude more than destroying dead wood. Fire manipulation, transformation, or destruction becomes harder as intensity rises: for each five points of fire damage above +5, add one magnitude to the spell level.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Perdo Herbam Guidelines; Muto, Perdo, and Rego Ignem Guidelines (ars-magica-core#030)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a rising power surcharge for harder targets; a world can change the surcharge because stronger or living material resists more.

rules.statement: A spell that makes plants grab victims can require Strength rolls against 9 to escape; a botch can make escape impossible without outside help. When the caster stops concentrating, a victim held by Tangle of Wood and Thorns can escape against 6 instead.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Rego Herbam Spells, LEVELS 15 and 20 (ars-magica-core#030)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a binding that persists while concentration lasts; a world can make botches more or less severe because a failed escape attempt can worsen the bind.

rules.statement: Imaginem changes sensory impressions rather than making the represented objects real: an illusory bucket cannot hold water, and an illusory wall offers no resistance. Greater complexity, directed movement or sound, and intricate detail each increase the required spell level as described in the guidelines.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Imaginem; Creo Imaginem Guidelines (ars-magica-core#030)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to sensory-only effects with no physical force; a world can raise the complexity cost because detailed or directed illusions take more power.

rules.statement: To imitate a particular person or object, the caster makes a Perception + Finesse roll, modified from −3 for an unfamiliar subject to +3 for a very familiar one or an available model. Person-imitation difficulty is 6 for acquaintances, 9 for friends, and 12 for close friends or relatives; a botch makes the imitation obviously false in use.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Imaginem, paragraph on mimicking a specific object or person (ars-magica-core#030)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to familiarity-based accuracy; a world can shift the difficulty because close observers know the subject better.

rules.statement: Creo Imaginem creates images affecting one sense at level 1, adding another sense per level through all five senses at level 5. A commanded image needs the caster to concentrate and remain in range when directing it; otherwise it freezes.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Creo Imaginem Guidelines; Phantasmal Animal (ars-magica-core#031)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to images that affect only the senses the spell’s level permits; a world can raise the level to add senses, at the cost of greater magical effort.

rules.statement: Intellego Imaginem can perceive at a distance using one sense at level 1, with each additional sense adding one level. Intellego Imaginem can also discern illusions only when the detecting spell is at least one magnitude stronger than the illusion.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Intellego Imaginem Guidelines; Discern the Images of Truth and Falsehood (ars-magica-core#031)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the senses and illusion strength specified; a world can allow more distant or broader sensing, at the cost of higher spell level.

rules.statement: Muto Imaginem can alter an object’s sensed qualities: level 1 changes one sensation, rising to a complete change in appearance at level 5, but it cannot change solidity. Accurate imitation depends on the caster’s familiarity with the model.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Muto Imaginem Guidelines (ars-magica-core#031)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to altered sensory appearance without changing solidity; a world can require close familiarity for convincing copies, limiting what a caster can imitate.

rules.statement: Perdo Imaginem effects that remove an image last only while the spell lasts, since images arise again naturally. Momentary effects can therefore cause only a brief flicker; destroying a changing image requires one additional magnitude.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Perdo Imaginem Guidelines (ars-magica-core#031)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to sensory suppression lasting only for the spell’s duration; a world can make changing images harder to suppress, requiring an extra magnitude.

rules.statement: Rego Imaginem effects that shift changing images require one extra magnitude, and shifting an image along with its object requires another. Each additional sense affected also raises the guideline by one magnitude.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Rego Imaginem Guidelines (ars-magica-core#031)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to shifting a single sense of a static image; a world can extend the effect to changing images or more senses, at increased level.

rules.statement: Mentem magic affects intelligent minds, while beast minds are affected by Animal and elemental minds by the relevant elemental Form. Individual minds have no size modifier, but affecting a Group or an area uses size modifiers normally.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Mentem Spells (ars-magica-core#031)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to intelligent individual minds without a size adjustment; a world can expand effects to groups or areas, at the cost of size increases.

rules.statement: A Momentary Intellego Mentem effect can answer one question, even when its answer is complex, but it does not explain why. Obtaining extensive information takes time.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Intellego Mentem Guidelines (ars-magica-core#031)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one answer per momentary effect; a world can permit broader inquiry by allowing more time, exposing the caster to delay or interruption.

rules.statement: Removed memories do not naturally return, so a Momentary Perdo Mentem spell can erase them permanently. Removed emotions naturally return unless the spell has continuing duration; a continuing effect can also prevent relearning forgotten information.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Perdo Mentem Guidelines (ars-magica-core#031)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to permanent removal of memory but only temporary suppression of emotion; a world can require continuing magic to prevent emotional return or relearning, at ongoing cost.

rules.statement: The boundary ritual diverts casual travelers so they do not discover the place within it. Active searchers may try once per day with a Perception stress roll against Ease Factor 12; difficult terrain raises the target number, open terrain lowers it, and completely open terrain cannot be used. Ritual participants are exempt, and finding the place does not block later approach.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Boundary-concealment spell (passage opening) (ars-magica-core#032)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to diverting casual discovery while allowing daily active searches; tune the search difficulty to terrain because the concealment depends on natural cover.

rules.statement: A ritual switches two creatures’ minds but leaves their souls in place. Before the transfer, each makes a Stamina stress roll against Ease Factor 3; if both fail, both die, while one failure kills only that creature and makes the spell fail. Even a survivor needs a day to fully adjust to the new body.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Exchange of the Two Minds, Level 55 (ars-magica-core#032)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to exchanging minds without souls and requiring a pre-transfer survival test; a world can make the transfer safer or deadlier by changing its bodily shock and survival threshold.

rules.statement: Terram difficulty increases from earth through clay, stone, glass, metal, and gemstones, but each material step does not automatically add a full magnitude. A base Individual is about ten cubic paces for earth or clay, one cubic pace for stone, one cubic foot for base metal, one tenth cubic foot for precious metal, and one cubic inch for gemstones.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Terram Spells (ars-magica-core#032)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to progressively harder material targets with smaller metal and gem quantities; adjust material difficulty and base volume to set how costly precise fabrication or destruction is.

rules.statement: For Muto Terram changes, changing dirt to or from sand, mud, or clay uses the same magnitude, stone or glass adds one magnitude, and metal or gemstone adds two; the adjustment is applied once even when transforming between two materials in the same difficult class. The amount affected is limited by the guideline for each endpoint.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Muto Terram Guidelines (ars-magica-core#032)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to paying once for the harder material class and respecting both endpoint quantities; a world can raise these costs to make transmutation rarer and more resource-intensive.

rules.statement: Terram control generally costs one extra magnitude for stone or glass and two for metal or gemstones, except simple relocation. Instant relocation of a nonliving object is up to 5 paces at the base guideline, with successive increases reaching 50 paces, 500 paces, one league, seven leagues, and finally a place linked by an Arcane Connection.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Rego Terram Guidelines (ars-magica-core#032)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to escalating range by magnitude while making precise control and difficult materials costlier; tune the distance ladder to determine how accessible long-distance transport is.

rules.statement: Magic residues halve in magnitude as an effect ends, then lose one magnitude for each duration of the original spell. Once at zero, residues fade by one magnitude per month for non-ritual Momentary, Concentration, or Diameter effects and by one per year for other effects; at negative magnitude 10 they are gone.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Intellego Vim Guidelines (ars-magica-core#032)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to residue weakening on this schedule; a world can lengthen or shorten the evidence window to make magical investigation easier or less reliable.

rules.statement: Hermetic Muto Vim cannot alter Spontaneous spells and can only affect Hermetic magic.
