Casting it alongside the spell being changed requires an Intelligence + Concentration roll against Ease Factor 9; failure prevents both spells, while a botch causes both to botch. Altering another caster’s spell requires cooperation or fast casting, and the Muto Vim Penetration total must exceed the target spell’s unless cooperating.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Muto Vim Guidelines (ars-magica-core#032)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to limiting spell alteration to known Hermetic magic and imposing a timing and control check; relax cooperation or Penetration requirements to make counter-magic more accessible.

rules.statement: A Vim spell that detects or counters magic must be strong enough relative to its target, and parameter increases are deducted before calculating the strength available for that purpose. A single spell may target one magical effect or a person or object; targeting a person or object can include suitable magic affecting it, while dedicated detection spells do not automatically detect other categories such as items, effects, or creatures.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Vim Spells (ars-magica-core#032)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to category-specific detection and spending spell strength on range and target first; broaden categories or reduce parameter costs to make magical surveillance more powerful.

rules.statement: Muto Vim can alter a spell only while it is being cast, not after casting is complete. Its duration must cover the target spell’s casting time; a normally cast Formulaic spell needs only Momentary duration, while a practical Ritual can be covered by Sun duration.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Muto Vim Spells (ars-magica-core#033)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to effects that combine only during casting; a world could allow later alteration, at the cost of changing a rule the passage treats as impossible.

rules.statement: A Muto Vim effect must be tailored to a particular kind of alteration, and cannot raise a target spell above the Muto Vim spell’s level. Superficial changes can target spells up to twice the Vim spell’s level plus 1 magnitude; significant changes can target up to the Vim spell’s level plus 1 magnitude; total changes can target up to half that amount.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Muto Vim Guidelines (ars-magica-core#033)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to specific, level-bounded modifications; a world could broaden them, but would lose the constraint that prevents one spell from changing another arbitrarily.

rules.statement: If a modified spell’s resulting parameters would ordinarily require a Ritual, either the original spell or the Muto Vim spell must be a Ritual. A non-Ritual Muto Vim spell cannot turn a non-Ritual spell into an effect that requires a Ritual.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Muto Vim Spells (ars-magica-core#033)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to requiring at least one Ritual for Ritual-scale results; a world could relax this, at the cost of bypassing the usual ritual requirement.

rules.statement: A Muto Vim effect in a magical item may affect only another spell-like effect in that same item, never a spell chosen by the wielder. When the item’s effect is manipulated, cooperating or self-activating magi must make an Intelligence + Concentration roll against Ease Factor 9; without prior coordination, the caster must fast-cast, identify the effect’s Form, beat the activator’s Initiative with a fast-cast defense, and exceed the item’s Penetration.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Muto Vim Spells & Enchanted Devices (ars-magica-core#033)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to item-internal targeting and a timing check; a world could allow external targeting, but it would remove the item’s built-in limit and coordination cost.

rules.statement: A Muto Vim increase in spell power or parameters cannot raise the affected spell’s level above the Muto Vim spell’s level. A Muto Vim effect that increases power also cannot exceed the limits of its particular guideline.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Muto Vim Spells (ars-magica-core#033)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to capping the modified spell at the modifier’s level; a world could permit stronger results, at the cost of weakening the level-based limit.

rules.statement: Perdo Vim can dispel a specific type of effect up to the Vim spell’s level plus 4 magnitudes and a stress die, or an effect of one supernatural realm up to half the Vim spell’s level plus 4 magnitudes and a stress die. Some targets, including Hermetic enchantments and specified enchantment types, require a Ritual; effects protected by Magic Resistance require the dispelling spell to penetrate it.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Perdo Vim Guidelines (ars-magica-core#033)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to type- or realm-bounded dispelling with penetration and ritual limits; a world could allow universal dispelling, at the cost of removing target-specific knowledge and safeguards.

rules.statement: Rego Vim can sustain or suppress spells within its level limits. Sustaining cannot extend a spell beyond its natural possible duration, and suppression ends when the Rego Vim effect ends or the original spell expires.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Rego Vim Guidelines (ars-magica-core#033)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to temporary maintenance or suspension without extending the spell’s natural lifespan; a world could allow permanent extension, at the cost of bypassing duration limits.

rules.statement: The Aegis of the Hearth lasts a year and distinguishes natives from foreign beings and effects for each casting. Foreign creatures with Might cannot cross its boundary unless their Might exceeds its level; foreign effects crossing inward must penetrate its level, while foreign effects originating inside suffer a penalty of half its level to their Casting Total or Penetration.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Rego Vim Spells — Aegis of the Hearth (ars-magica-core#033)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a year-long boundary ward with distinct entry and inside penalties; a world could change its duration or strength, with greater protection demanding a stronger ward.

rules.statement: A student can use a summa only while their score in its subject is below the book’s level; a tractatus takes one season, benefits a student only once, and gives no benefit to its author. Studying a book also requires fluency at 4 or higher in its language and the ability to read its script; learning a supernatural Ability from a book additionally requires a score of at least 1 in that Ability.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Studying from Books; Reading Summae; Studying Tractatus (ars-magica-core#034)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to these access limits; a world can lower the language or prior-skill barriers to make learning more accessible, at the cost of weaker prerequisites.

rules.statement: Studying an Art from raw vis consumes one pawn for every five levels, or fraction thereof, already held in that Art, with a minimum of one pawn. The study’s source quality is a stress die plus aura bonus; a double botch can cause Wizard’s Twilight, and the number of botch dice equals the pawns spent.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Vis (ars-magica-core#034)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to consuming vis in proportion to existing skill; a world can reduce the cost or risk, making Art advancement less resource-intensive.

rules.statement: A summa’s author chooses its level up to half their score in the subject; lowering the level raises quality by one per level for an Art or three per level for an Ability, capped at the base quality. Writing progress each season equals Communication plus Language, and completion requires points equal to the level for an Art or five times the level for an Ability. A tractatus takes one season and has quality equal to Communication plus 6.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Writing Books — Summae; Tractatus (ars-magica-core#034)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a fixed writing rate and a quality-versus-level tradeoff; a world can make books quicker or more powerful, shifting the value of scholarship.

rules.statement: A supernatural Ability is initially learned through teaching or training and requires at least 5 experience points in the first season. Its source quality is reduced by the student’s total scores in other supernatural Abilities; if the student has had the Hermetic Arts opened, subtract the higher of 15 or the sum of their Art scores as well.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Learning Supernatural Abilities (ars-magica-core#034)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to increasing learning difficulty as mystical expertise accumulates; a world can waive some penalties, making broad supernatural training easier.

rules.statement: Taming requires consecutive seasons of daily interaction, with progress exceeding the creature’s Might; interrupted progress is lost and cannot be transferred between trainers. A mundane trainer gains Intelligence plus Animal Handling plus Animal Ken minus the creature’s Might each season, while a Hermetic magus uses a Rego-Form laboratory total minus the creature’s Might.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Training Creatures — Taming Animals; A Hermetic Tamer; A Mundane Trainer (ars-magica-core#034)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to taming as sustained relationship-building; a world can shorten the process or retain progress through interruptions, at the cost of less demanding creature bonds.

rules.statement: A tamed creature gains Loyalty +0 toward its tamer. A season of further training raises Loyalty by 1, to a maximum of +3, or transfers the loyalty to a present character; commands use Presence plus an appropriate handling Ability against a task-based difficulty, with Loyalty tests sometimes required for dangerous tasks.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Training Creatures — Loyalty; Commanding a Creature (ars-magica-core#034)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to loyalty as a limited bond that improves through time; a world can make obedience automatic or allow stronger loyalty, at the cost of reducing uncertainty and training effort.

rules.statement: A Mystery initiation succeeds automatically when the Mystagogue’s Presence, House Lore, and Script bonus meet the target: 15 for a known Minor Virtue, 21 for a known Major, 18 for a new Minor, or 30 for a new Major. Script elements can add bonuses, often by requiring a quest, sacrifice, or Ordeal; prior Ordeals reduce the target, but it cannot fall below 9.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Mystery Initiation; The Initiation Script (ars-magica-core#034)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a deterministic initiation whose difficulty is offset by costly script requirements; a world can change targets or rewards, trading easier advancement against greater sacrifice.

rules.statement: Warping points come from living in a supernatural aura of strength 6 or more, powerful or continuous supernatural effects, and botches when using supernatural abilities. A character needs five times their new Warping Score in additional points to raise it; the four realms’ points combine, while beings with Might are immune.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Warping; Gaining Warping Points; Warping and Non-Humans (ars-magica-core#034)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to accumulating a shared long-term supernatural consequence; a world can make particular sources count more or less, changing the cost of prolonged exposure.

rules.statement: Warping Point sources accumulate. A person continuously affected by a strong supernatural effect that was neither made for them nor cast by them gains points both for the effect's strength and for its ongoing influence.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Opening paragraph; Powerful Supernatural Effects (ars-magica-core#035)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to stacking every applicable source; a setting can reduce accumulation, at the cost of making prolonged supernatural exposure less consequential.

rules.statement: Living in an aura stronger than 5 can cause Warping: at strength 6, always being there gives 1 point per year; at strength 8 it gives 2 per year, while strength 10 gives 1 per month. Half-time and frequent-visit rates are lower; people whose supernatural abilities come from the aura's realm gain no points for living there.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Living in Strong Auras (ars-magica-core#035)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the stated aura-and-time table; a world can alter the rates, with the in-world consequence of making residence in potent places more or less hazardous.

rules.statement: A powerful supernatural effect gives its target 1 Warping Point unless the target cast it or it was specifically designed for them; Hermetic spells of magnitude 6 or higher count as powerful. A continuous powerful effect not designed for the target gives 1 point when applied and 5 per year thereafter, while a momentary ritual gives a point only when first applied if neither exception applies.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Powerful Supernatural Effects; Constant Supernatural Effects (ars-magica-core#035)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the stated power, duration, and target-design tests; a world can broaden what counts as powerful, increasing the risk of exposure.

rules.statement: Being personally under an active supernatural effect for at least half the time counts as constant influence and gives 1 Warping Point per year for each effect; if different effects provide the influence, they still count. A directly affected person counts, but someone merely living in a magically affected structure does not; familiar and Talisman bonds and their imbued powers are exceptions.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Constant Supernatural Effects (ars-magica-core#035)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to personal influence lasting at least half the time; a world can count indirect or intermittent exposure too, at the cost of faster Warping.

rules.statement: A botched attempt to invoke a supernatural effect adds 1 Warping Point for each zero on the botch dice.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Supernatural Botches (ars-magica-core#035)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one point per botch-die zero; a world can soften this penalty, reducing the lasting cost of failed supernatural control.

rules.statement: For mundane characters, Warping Score 1 grants a Minor Flaw, score 3 grants another Minor Flaw, score 5 grants a source-attuned supernatural Minor Virtue that stops further points from living in a strong aura of that same type, and score 6 and each later score grants a Major Flaw. The flaws reflect the main source of the Warping.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Effects of Warping (ars-magica-core#035)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the stated thresholds and source-matching consequences; a world can change them, making accumulated supernatural exposure more or less transformative.

rules.statement: Aging rolls begin in the Winter after a character turns 35 and occur yearly; the total is a stress die without botch plus age divided by 10 rounded up, minus living-condition and Longevity Ritual modifiers. Aging points accrue in Characteristics, and a Characteristic drops by 1 once its points exceed its absolute value, then its accumulated points reset.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Aging (ars-magica-core#035)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to annual aging from 35 with modifiers and characteristic loss; a world can delay onset or ease modifiers, reducing the pressure of age.

rules.statement: A Longevity Ritual lasts until a crisis: it ensures survival of that crisis, but its power is spent and must be renewed. A crisis raises Decrepitude before its roll, and a survivor—even one saved by magic—needs the rest of the season to recover; a Longevity Ritual also makes pre-35 aging-table results of 10 or more count as 9.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Aging; Crisis (ars-magica-core#035)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the ritual being consumed by crisis and recovery costing the season; a world can make it reusable, reducing the cost of surviving a crisis.

rules.statement: In a grapple, an attacker with positive Attack Advantage establishes Grapple Strength equal to that advantage. Later successful attacks add to it; the captive can attack to subtract their advantage, and reaching zero or less frees them while giving the grappler a Light Wound. The captive cannot take other actions involving movement while held.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Combat Options — Non-Lethal Combat (ars-magica-core#035)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to advantage-based restraint that can be strengthened or escaped; a world can make holds easier to escape, reducing the danger of being immobilized.

rules.statement: Add the Load of carried heavy or bulky items, then find the Burden threshold reached: for example, Load 9 gives Burden 3. With Strength 0 or less, Encumbrance equals Burden; otherwise subtract Strength from Burden, to a minimum of 0. Subtract Encumbrance from relevant rolls, including athletic actions and spellcasting, but not combat Attack or Defense when the load is mostly weapons and armor.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Encumbrance (ars-magica-core#036)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the stated load thresholds and Strength reduction; a world can change the burden curve to make carrying gear more or less costly, reflecting its expectations of travel and equipment.

rules.statement: Characters generally have six shared Fatigue levels, from Fresh through Winded, Weary, Tired, Dazed, and Unconscious. Weary, Tired, and Dazed impose cumulative penalties of –1, –3, and –5 to rolls, including Fatigue tests but excluding Soak; brief strenuous actions call for a Stamina – Encumbrance stress roll against 6, with failure costing one Short-Term level and a botch costing two. Short-Term levels recover with quiet rest, from two minutes at Winded up to two hours at Unconscious, while each Long-Term level requires a good night's rest.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Fatigue (ars-magica-core#036)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to separate short- and long-term fatigue sharing one track; a world can speed or slow recovery, reflecting how punishing exertion and rest are.

rules.statement: Damage exceeding Soak determines wound severity by Size and the Damage Table; each further 5 points of excess damage raises the wound one level. Wound penalties accumulate without a maximum (Light –1, Medium –3, Heavy –5), and an Incapacitated character cannot act; nonfatal wounds do not immediately kill, though wounds can worsen into Incapacitation.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Wounds; Damage Table; Wound Table (ars-magica-core#036)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to cumulative penalties and escalating severity; a world can make wounds more or less lethal, reflecting its desired danger and resilience.

rules.statement: For each wound, make Recovery rolls at its severity's interval: weekly for Light, monthly for Medium, and once per season for Heavy. Meeting the Improvement Ease Factor (10, 12, or 15 respectively) improves it one level; meeting only the Stable Ease Factor (4, 6, or 9) leaves it unchanged and adds a cumulative +3 to future rolls, while failing that threshold worsens it one level. Recovery totals use Stamina, Chirurgy or Medicine, magical aid, and a stress die, without wound penalties.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Recovering From Wounds (ars-magica-core#036)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to gradual, interval-based healing with infection risk; a world can adjust intervals or thresholds to make medical care and recovery more or less consequential.

rules.statement: An Incapacitated character makes two Recovery rolls each day, at sunrise and sunset: a result of 0 or less kills them, while 9 or more improves all Incapacitating Wounds to Heavy. Any other result worsens the condition and applies a cumulative –1 to later Recovery rolls until improvement or death; an attending medic adds the relevant Ability score.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Recovery from Incapacitation (ars-magica-core#036)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to two daily death checks and worsening penalties; a world can make the crisis more forgiving or harsher, reflecting the availability and effectiveness of care.

rules.statement: A disease or poison requires an exposed character to pass a Stamina check against its Ease Factor; success means only minor discomfort, while failure inflicts a wound of the agent's severity, which then follows ordinary recovery rules. Diseases and poisons use Medicine rather than Chirurgy; diseases should not inflict fatal wounds upon first contraction, but poisons may do so.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Other Perils; Debilitation; Diseases; Poisons (ars-magica-core#036)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one resistance check followed by ordinary wound recovery; a world can tune agent difficulty and severity, reflecting local hazards and medical knowledge.

rules.statement: Food, water, and air deprivation require Stamina checks after 3 days, 1 day, and 30 seconds respectively. Checks begin at Ease Factor 3 and rise by one each further period; failure costs a Fatigue level, and after unconsciousness further failures cause a Light Wound that worsens one step each time. Food- and water-caused Fatigue is Long-Term and only returns after eating or drinking; air-caused Fatigue is Short-Term.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Deprivation (ars-magica-core#036)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to escalating checks at the listed intervals; a world can change intervals or consequences to represent different survival conditions.

rules.statement: Auras rated 1–10 modify supernatural activity according to the interaction table: for example, a Divine aura subtracts three times its rating from Magic activity and four times its rating from Faerie activity, while it does not hinder Divine power. In a foreign aura, supernatural acts also gain one extra botch die per aura rating, using the original rating; Divine powers receive neither penalties nor extra botch dice from other realms' auras.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Realm Auras; Realm Interaction (ars-magica-core#036)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one locally dominant aura modifying supernatural acts and botch risk; a world can change realm multipliers or aura strength, reflecting which powers its places favor.

rules.statement: A creature's Might score supplies its Magic Resistance, its starting Might pool, and the maximum strength of that pool. Powers spend their listed Might-point cost; if the pool is short, the power cannot be used, and the pool normally refills to the Might score over a day, at a constant rate unless specified otherwise.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Chapter 13: Bestiary — Creature Might (ars-magica-core#037)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a pool equal to Might that refreshes over a day; a world can alter the refresh rate or method, reflecting the creature's nature.

rules.statement: Creature-power Penetration equals Might score minus five times the power's Might-point cost, plus any Penetration bonus. A continuing creature power can be dispelled at an effective level equal to the creature's Might score.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Chapter 13: Bestiary — Creature Powers (ars-magica-core#037)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to cost reducing penetration by five per point and Might setting dispelling level; a world can tune power cost and strength to constrain supernatural creatures.

rules.statement: An Infernal aura can grow from especially vile individual sins, repeated sins in one place, or infernal creatures and powers. A particularly vile act can create a level 1 aura; repeated wrongdoing can raise it over time, and decades of repeated human sacrifice may produce a level 5 aura.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Infernal Auras — Sources of Infernal Auras (ars-magica-core#037)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to aura strength accumulating from repeated or extreme wrongdoing; a world can change the threshold and rate, with local evil leaving a lasting stain.

rules.statement: A Divine aura generally strengthens on Sundays and holy days and weakens at night and on evil days. A blessed person, place, or object can carry a fragile Divine aura, but exposure to the sinful world makes it vanish; an aura carried into another realm is swallowed by that realm's aura.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Divine Auras (ars-magica-core#037)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a calendar-driven strength cycle and fragile blessings; a world can change which days amplify it or how quickly exposure erases it, reflecting local faith and holiness.

rules.statement: True Faith grants Magic Resistance equal to ten times the character's True Faith Score. At each dawn, the character regains Faith Points up to that Score, but gains none if already holding more points than the Score; spending requires acting in accordance with God's will, and a character without a Score can spend only one point at a time.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: True Faith (ars-magica-core#037)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to resistance and daily point recovery based on the Faith Score; a world can change the recovery or permitted uses, with faithful conduct as the condition.

rules.statement: A relic gives its bearer Faith Points usable like Confidence and Magic Resistance equal to ten times its Faith Score, but a person benefits from only one relic at once; trying to benefit from more is sinful and cancels all relic benefits. Its Divine Might equals ten times its applicable Faith Score, limits use of its powers, protects the relic against direct supernatural effects, and refreshes its Might Pool at sunrise.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Relics (ars-magica-core#037)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one active relic per bearer and a sunrise-refreshed power limit; a world can alter the limit or refresh, with devotion and restraint shaping access.

rules.statement: A relic repels Infernal creatures within a distance in feet equal to its Divine Might: an Infernal creature whose Might does not exceed the relic's cannot enter. If it does enter, it takes damage equal to the relic's Might each round until it leaves; ordinary Soak reduces that damage.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Relics — Scourging the Infernal (ars-magica-core#037)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a Might-sized exclusion radius and recurring damage to stronger intruders; a world can change radius or damage, with relic holiness defining the boundary.

rules.statement: Entering a regio shifts a character out of the normal world and into a supernatural level. Entry can happen by being led by an affiliated native, by seeing into a level and crossing its boundary, by following a path or ritual, or accidentally when lost near the boundary; the sight roll's Ease Factor is 5 plus twice the aura difference, with relevant aura ratings added when the character is in a different aura.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Regiones — Entering and Leaving Regiones (ars-magica-core#037)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to at least one defined entry route per regio and an aura-difference sight threshold; a world can make access easier or more restrictive, with paths, natives, or special abilities as gates.

rules.statement: A supernatural creature’s Might score sets how hard magic can affect it: 20 challenges starting magi, 40 troubles a middle-aged magus, 60 challenges even powerful magi, and 75 makes it nearly immune to Hermetic magic. High Might can keep lethal spells from ending a climactic fight quickly and can encourage magi to improve Penetration with Arcane Connections, horoscopes, or images.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Might (ars-magica-core#038)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the listed Might benchmarks; a world can raise or lower them to tune magical resistance and battle duration, at the cost of requiring more preparation or making the creature easier to affect.

rules.statement: A power’s Might cost governs its Penetration and frequency of use, rather than directly measuring its strength. A creature could use devastating fire with no Might cost as often as desired, while a healing power costing 25 Might could be used only once or twice per day.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Powers (ars-magica-core#038)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to costs that trade more uses and Penetration against each other; a world can loosen that tradeoff, at the cost of making powerful effects more routinely available.

rules.statement: A beast normally makes only one weapon attack in a round, even if it has several natural weapons. Its secondary weapons are less effective than the primary weapon listed first.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Beasts in Combat (ars-magica-core#038)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one natural weapon attack per round; a world can allow multiple attacks, at the cost of making multi-weapon beasts substantially more dangerous.

rules.statement: A successful ambush by a beast with the Ambush Predator quality automatically gives it Initiative in the first combat round and +3 to its Attack total for that round only.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Qualities — Ambush Predator (ars-magica-core#038)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the automatic first-round advantage; a world can reduce it when warning or terrain weakens the ambush, at the cost of diminishing the predator’s surprise.

rules.statement: A constrictor can grapple a target smaller than itself; while it holds the grapple, the target is deprived of air and checks Stamina every 30 seconds, or five rounds, against the normal deprivation effects. After securing the grapple, the creature may continue constricting and attack with another weapon on later rounds.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Qualities — Constriction (ars-magica-core#038)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the stated size limit and five-round checks; a world can make escape easier or harder, at the cost of changing how quickly restraint becomes life-threatening.

rules.statement: When a charged, exerted attack by an Overrun creature hits, the target tests Dexterity + Athletics against an Ease Factor based on pre-Soak damage plus the Size difference. Failure knocks the target down and away, inflicts falling damage, and costs its next action to stand; a prone target cannot parry.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Qualities — Overrun (ars-magica-core#038)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the damage-and-size test; a world can alter the Ease Factor or consequences to tune the impact of charges, at the cost of making knockdowns more or less likely.

rules.statement: Once a creature has bitten a foe, it may roll on the following round to inflict +6 damage or, if able, drag the victim underwater. The victim resists either result as a successful grapple with Attack Advantage 10, and a drowning victim may try to break free each round against that same advantage.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Qualities — Roll Attack (ars-magica-core#038)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to Attack Advantage 10 for both outcomes; a world can make the follow-up harder or easier to resist, at the cost of changing the danger of a successful bite.

rules.statement: A creature with Swallow Whole can swallow a target at least four Size points smaller. The victim can use only Brawl inside the gullet, cannot breathe, and reaches the stomach after three rounds; stomach acid then inflicts +9 damage each round, or +36 if fully immersed, with a Strength + Athletics roll determining reduced immersion.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Qualities — Swallow Whole (ars-magica-core#038)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the four-Size gap, three-round transit, and listed acid damage; a world can change those thresholds, at the cost of making engulfment more or less survivable.

rules.statement: A creature with Spiny inflicts its normal damage when struck by a bite, claw, or fist, and the attacker also suffers +5 damage. If the spines are venomous, the attacker’s own Attack Advantage is used to test whether the venom takes effect against it.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Qualities — Spiny (ars-magica-core#038)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to +5 retaliatory damage and the attacker’s own advantage for venom; a world can strengthen or weaken the retaliation, at the cost of changing how risky close combat is.

rules.statement: A creature’s venom takes effect when its Attack Advantage exceeds the target’s Protection, even if the attack causes no wound. Choose either a Light Wound avoided with a Stamina roll against Ease Factor 12, or a Medium Wound avoided against Ease Factor 9; each additional purchase increases severity or raises the avoidance Ease Factor by 3.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Venomous (ars-magica-core#039)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default venom is a single wound check; a setting can turn up severity or avoidance difficulty, at the cost of a more dangerous creature.

rules.statement: For an animal with average lifespan 10 years, aging begins at age 7, the aging roll gains 1 for every 2 years of age, and the animal makes 5 aging rolls per year. Spread multiple yearly rolls across the four seasons, placing any extra rolls in Winter.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Aging (ars-magica-core#039)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default aging scales the human schedule by lifespan; a world can alter lifespan assumptions, changing how quickly its animals age.

rules.statement: When combining human and animal Characteristics, use the lower value if both are negative and the higher value if both are positive; otherwise add them. Shapechangers usually retain human Intelligence, but lycanthropes use Cunning instead; wounds carry between forms, except lycanthropes heal animal-form wounds when returning to human form.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Statistics of Shapechangers (ars-magica-core#039)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default transformations retain shared injuries and combine traits by sign; a world can make curses or species exceptions change mind or wound carryover.

rules.statement: A Daimon can create or dismiss an Aspect by thought without spending Might. Each Aspect has its own Might pool, cannot recover spent Might, and vanishes if its pool reaches zero, it suffers an Incapacitating wound, or it loses consciousness; the parent Daimon is unaffected and can discard an Aspect to escape a binding.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Daimons (ars-magica-core#039)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default Aspects are expendable agents independent of their source; a setting can make their loss affect the Daimon, at the cost of weakening its remote safety.

rules.statement: An Aspect cannot be within several miles of another Aspect from the same Daimon, and it cannot return to a location it has left for one day. An Aspect is also an indefinite-duration Arcane Connection in constant mental contact with its Daimon.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Daimons (ars-magica-core#039)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default placement limits prevent Aspect clustering and immediate reuse of a site; a world can relax these limits, allowing denser or faster manifestations.

rules.statement: A True Name costs 5 experience points to learn and functions as an indefinite-duration Arcane Connection to its being; a Daimon’s True Name also connects to all its Aspects, but a spell must identify which Aspect it targets. Knowing a being’s True Name adds 5 to research totals for that being’s synthemata.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: True Names and Synthemata (ars-magica-core#039)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default names provide a durable targeting link and a research bonus; a world can make names less reliable or more costly to learn.

rules.statement: An elemental only regains Might by resting for an entire season in a Magic aura of strength at least one-fifth its Might score; consuming vis instead restores 5 Might per pawn of matching Form or 2 per pawn of another Art. Wounds also reduce its Might pool by the wound penalty, and reaching zero leaves it inert until it regains a point.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Elementals and Might; Elemental Combat (ars-magica-core#039)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default elemental power is slow to recover and can be spent through injury; a world can accelerate recovery, at the cost of making elementals harder to exhaust.

rules.statement: Elementals do not suffer ordinary wounds: each wound reduces their Might pool by the wound penalty, while an Incapacitating Wound removes 5 points. Combat fragments contain vis according to cumulative wound penalties, but destroying the elemental’s matter also destroys that vis.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Elemental Combat (ars-magica-core#039)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default damage converts physical injury into lost animating power and harvestable fragments; a world can make the vis harder to collect or destroy it more readily.

rules.statement: A power with no point cost can be used without spending Might; a paid power spends its listed amount, while variable spell-copying powers charge 1 Might per magnitude. The listed power’s range, duration, target, and initiative constrain its use.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Earth Elemental Sample Powers (ars-magica-core#040)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the stated Might costs and spell parameters; a world can raise or lower those costs to tune power use, with Might expenditure limiting repeated effects.

rules.statement: Elemental bodies admit different kinds of harm: earth elementals are harmed by bludgeoning tools and digging implements, while piercing and slashing attacks are ineffective; water and air bodies let most weapons pass through, and fire bodies let weapons pass through but may ignite them. Fire can extinguish water elementals only when its damage exceeds their Might, and water can quench fire elementals according to the source’s Size and damage.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: An Earth Elemental; Water Elementals; Air Elementals; Fire Elementals (ars-magica-core#040)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the listed material interactions; a world can alter which attacks work, because an elemental’s substance determines its vulnerabilities.

rules.statement: An earth elemental’s successful Crush can pin a target no larger than itself; its grapple strength gains its Might divided by 5, rounded up. A successful grapple also damages carried items: fragile items are destroyed, robust items break and are destroyed on another hit, and metal items are damaged and break on another hit.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Earth Elemental Sample Powers (ars-magica-core#040)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the stated size and item-damage thresholds; a world can vary them to make grappling more or less hazardous, with equipment at risk.

rules.statement: The air elemental’s Dissolution temporarily melts one Terram Individual for the round, then it resolidifies in a changed shape. Against enchanted items, its Penetration must exceed five times the vis pawns invested; against living targets, it instead deals +15 damage to bones and other listed hard tissues, ignoring armor.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Air Elemental Sample Powers (ars-magica-core#040)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a one-round reshaping with the specified resistance and damage limits; a world can widen the affected materials, at the cost of making the effect more destructive.

rules.statement: A fire elemental’s Fascination makes a viewer who fails an Intelligence roll against Ease Factor 9 unable to act; the viewer may retry once each round. Burn deals a stress die plus the elemental’s current Might pool to anyone touching it, and ignites flammable material.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Fire Elemental Sample Powers (ars-magica-core#040)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the stated resistance roll and contact damage; a world can alter the difficulty or retry rate, with helplessness and fire damage as the stakes.

rules.statement: A fire spirit can spend 6 Might to create an elemental from enough raw elemental matter, with Might below its own, and automatically control it. It can instead seize control of another elemental if the power penetrates that elemental’s Might; when control ends, the created elemental remains.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: A Fire Elemental — Enliven the Gross Fire (ars-magica-core#040)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to automatic control of creations and a Might-penetration test for others; a world can change the cost or control limit, with an independent creature left behind when control lapses.

rules.statement: Adranus can manifest through touched animals, spending 4 Might for a plant of the stated scale or 5 for one Size +1 creature; an extra 2 Might controls ten standard creatures, and each further 2 multiplies the controlled mass by ten. It cannot control humans or other sentient beings, and cannot spend more than its Might magnitude on one use.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Adranus, the Spirit of Mount Etna — Manifestation (ars-magica-core#040)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the explicit creature, mass, and spending caps; a world can change the scale per cost, with Might and exclusion of sentient targets limiting control.

rules.statement: Adranus can make a target acquire one of three listed Flaws for 5 Might. A temporary grant ties up those Might points until the spirit removes the Flaw; a permanent grant reduces its Might Score by 5.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Adranus, the Spirit of Mount Etna — Grant Visions, Grant Simple-Minded, Grant Wrathful (ars-magica-core#040)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the listed temporary or permanent cost; a world can alter duration or price, with lasting changes carrying a permanent reduction in the spirit’s Might.

rules.statement: A ghost can move one object for 5 Might and keeps moving that same object until it puts it down. A revenant’s body can be destroyed without destroying its animating spirit; if expelled or left without a body, the spirit cannot return to that or another corpse unless it has a specific power.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Ghostly Warder — Kinesis; Fighting the Walking Dead (ars-magica-core#040)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one held object per expenditure and a separate spirit/body state; a world can allow or forbid re-entry, with bodily destruction not itself ending the spirit.

rules.statement: A faerie is constrained to its story-role; ordinary faeries cannot depart from it even when that leads to death. Highly cognizant faeries can alter their roles by taking in human emotional energy.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Creatures of Faerie (ars-magica-core#041)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default faeries to role-bound; a world can allow role changes for highly cognizant ones, paid for with human emotional energy.

rules.statement: Faerie bodies recover from damage automatically, keeping only injuries needed to make their roles believable, and faeries do not suffer fatigue. Their glamour-made gear also increases their Touch range.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: New Virtues and Flaws (ars-magica-core#041)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default faerie injury and fatigue to recover or not apply; a world can make lasting injuries matter when its stories require them.

rules.statement: A traditional ward prevents a faerie from touching the protected thing with its glamour and prevents Might recovery nearby; forced contact damages its body as though exposed to a +6 damage source. A sovereign ward prevents that faerie from harming its bearer, including indirectly, and direct contact destroys the faerie's body for the scenario.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: New Virtues and Flaws (ars-magica-core#041)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default wards to enforce limited taboos; a world can make a sovereign taboo absolute, at the cost of the faerie's presence.

rules.statement: A Stag of Virtue can heal one of its own Heavy or lesser wounds for 3 points, but only after eating dittany. It can delay poison in its body until the next sunrise or sunset at no cost, then permanently neutralize poison already inside it for 1 point after drinking water.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Stag of Virtue — Powers (ars-magica-core#041)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default healing and poison protection to require their listed bodily ingredients; a world can remove those requirements by making the powers freely available.

rules.statement: Faerie hound weapons can gain +5 Damage for two minutes; their howl can cause panic or intensify an existing emotion, overcome by a suitable Personality stress roll against Ease Factor 9. A hound can control one human's mind for a day through eye contact, paralyze a human who meets its gaze, or sense the direction and distance to its human quarry.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Faerie Hounds — Powers (ars-magica-core#041)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default hound powers to short-lived or single-target effects; a world can make the hunt more coercive by increasing its duration or removing the resistance roll.

rules.statement: A faerie whose flight power is active can fly, but cannot fight while flying incredibly fast; heavy encumbrance or carrying a passenger at least its own Size prevents flight unless another faerie shares the load.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Faerie Hounds — Powers (ars-magica-core#041)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default flight to be available subject to load and combat limits; a world can relax those limits if the faerie can share the burden.

rules.statement: A faerie can speak any language previously used to address it, without needing to penetrate the listener's resistance, because the effect acts only on the faerie.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: New Virtues and Flaws (ars-magica-core#041)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default language mimicry to cover only languages heard before; a world can grant universal speech at the cost of requiring an effect that reaches others.

rules.statement: A demon can discard its physical form on its action and become a spirit. While bodiless it cannot physically attack or be attacked, can move as quickly as it likes, and passes through physical barriers while remaining aware of its surroundings.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Infernal Creatures (ars-magica-core#041)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default demons to switch forms on their action; a world can make the spiritual form safer and faster, but it gives up physical combat.

rules.statement: A demon can spend 1 point per 10 Infernal Might, or fraction thereof, to form its specified solid body; taking one round per Might point. It can end the effect in one round of concentration, but its body and statistics otherwise remain unchanged, and it cannot use its physical Characteristics while spiritual.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Coagulation (ars-magica-core#042)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one specified physical shape and slow manifestation; worlds can change the allowed form or speed, with greater Might taking longer to gather and solidify.

rules.statement: When a mortal indulges in a venial sin, a demon may spend 1–3 Might points to impose its associated Personality Trait, provided it penetrates Magic Resistance; the imposed score equals points spent, up to 3. At the next chance to act on it, a failed resistance check makes the Trait permanent at +1, while success makes the imposed Trait disappear.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Obsession (ars-magica-core#042)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a sinful opening, penetration, and a later test before the influence becomes permanent; worlds can tune the trigger or trait increase, with the victim’s vice providing the opening.

rules.statement: A demon can enter a sleeping target’s dream for 1 point, or impose a waking vision for 5; dream changes must be gradual. A waking vision can stun the victim for a round, and the victim must roll against Ease Factor 9 or suffer an extreme reaction.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Envisioning (ars-magica-core#042)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to dream access at low cost and forceful waking hallucinations at higher cost; worlds can adjust intensity, with waking intrusion risking shock.

rules.statement: A demon can place any number of its Might points into a human as a possession pool; those points do not regenerate until possession ends, and reaching zero ends the possession. The demon controls the host, but must spend pool points to force actions contrary to the host’s nature or use the host’s supernatural abilities; spending all its Might also places its spiritual form in the host.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Possession (ars-magica-core#042)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a finite, non-regenerating pool that both sustains possession and pays for exertions; worlds can alter costs or control, with power committed to the host unavailable elsewhere.

rules.statement: Hermetic magic cannot detect demonic lies, illusions, Infernal Might, or the Infernal character of a demon’s powers; non-Divine Second Sight cannot pierce demonic illusions. Divine Second Sight uses Ease Factor 6 plus the demon’s Might magnitude, while ordinary Second Sight against naturally invisible things normally uses 9, increased by that magnitude for demons.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Demons and Magic (ars-magica-core#042)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to broad concealment from Hermetic detection and a tougher but possible Divine route; worlds can vary which senses pierce it, preserving demonic deception as its protection.

rules.statement: A successful Perdo Vim attack reduces a demon’s Infernal Might and removes any Might Pool exceeding its new Might. Reducing Infernal Might to zero destroys the demon without a corpse or vis.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Demons and Magic (ars-magica-core#042)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to attacks that erode Might and can ultimately destroy the demon; worlds can change the loss rate or endpoint, making the demon’s power reserve its measure of survival.

rules.statement: In an Infernal aura, a demon restores all spent Might over 24 minus twice the aura’s level hours, at an even hourly rate; outside such auras it restores all Might in 24 hours, and in a Divine aura it restores none.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Demons, Auras and Regiones (ars-magica-core#042)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to faster recovery in Infernal places and no recovery in Divine places; worlds can tune the rate, making the surrounding aura a source or denial of power.

rules.statement: In Christian lands, demons must abandon physical form at dawn on Holy Saturday and cannot spend Might until dusk on Easter Day. A Jewish household whose adult members atone for the previous year’s sins during the five days between Yom Kippur and Sukkot forces demons affecting it to flee for a year; demons cannot use Infernal Might directly against a Muslim who properly completed the hajj within the last year.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Religious Limitations on Demons (ars-magica-core#042)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to these faith-specific calendars and acts blocking or ending demonic effects; worlds can alter the qualifying observance, making religious practice the source of protection.

rules.statement: Build a corrupt beast from a mundane animal and give it the Corrupted Beast Flaw; balance each Flaw with a Virtue from the listed options. A beast corrupted for a long time or born corrupt may take additional Flaws to gain more Virtues.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Virtues and Flaws for Corrupted Beasts (ars-magica-core#043)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to requiring a listed Flaw for each Virtue; a world can permit other combinations if corruption is rare or costly.

rules.statement: A Corrupted Beast starts with Infernal Might 5, a sinful Personality Trait at +6, Presence –6 (or +6 when trying to intimidate), and the Tainted with Evil Flaw. Its deformity is difficult, but not always impossible, to disguise as natural.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Corrupted Beast (ars-magica-core#043)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the fixed traits and social reaction penalty; a world can tune how conspicuous corruption is, with concealment making detection harder.

rules.statement: A beast’s corpse typically yields one pawn of vis for every five points of its Might.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Virtues and Flaws for Corrupted Beasts (ars-magica-core#043)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one pawn per five Might; a world can vary the yield according to how much power remains in the corpse.

rules.statement: Greater Infernal Power adds 5 Might and grants a distinct power whose effect level cannot exceed Infernal Might + 10. It usually costs Might equal to its magnitude to activate, has an Initiative bonus of Quickness + magnitude, and requires Penetration; a beast may take it repeatedly for different powers, gaining more Might each time.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Greater Infernal Power (ars-magica-core#043)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the stated level cap and activation cost; a world can raise or lower the cost to change how often a beast uses its power.

rules.statement: Lesser Infernal Power adds 2 Might and grants a constant or activated effect capped at the beast’s Infernal Might. Activation usually costs 0–2 Might and its Initiative bonus equals magnitude; it cannot require Penetration, and a power that must overcome resistance is instead Greater.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Lesser Infernal Power (ars-magica-core#043)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a lower-cost, lower-cap power without Penetration; a world can make effects constant or activated to trade reliability against resource cost.

rules.statement: Divine-Might creatures use the normal rules for Magic Resistance, Penetration, and dispelling, are not omnipotent, cannot have True Faith, and are unaffected by The Gift. Certain flaws that mimic its effects can still provoke a negative reaction.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Creatures of the Divine (ars-magica-core#043)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to ordinary resistance rules and no Gift reaction; a world can decide whether specific supernatural flaws still offend Divine creatures.

rules.statement: An angel can spend 2 Might to manifest a flesh-like form that obeys mundane laws and can be wounded or killed. If that form is killed, the angel returns to spiritual form and may manifest again immediately if it has enough Might.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Angelic Powers — Angelic Mantle (ars-magica-core#043)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a vulnerable physical manifestation with a 2-Might cost; a world can alter the cost or consequences of losing the form.

rules.statement: Enfolding costs 2 Might to protect a target’s soul and mind from all supernatural targeting for a few moments; for 10 Might it instead makes the target’s body wholly immune to magic, pain, injury, fatigue, wounds, and death for at most one combat round. Envisioning costs 1 Might for a dream message or 5 for a waking vision, and can reach a target at any distance.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Angelic Powers (ars-magica-core#043)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to brief protection and distance-independent messages at the listed costs; a world can restrict range or duration to make angelic intervention less decisive.

rules.statement: Hermetic and other magic cannot affect the consecrated Host in any way.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Opening examples (ars-magica-core#044)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default magic cannot alter the Host; a world could broaden or narrow the immunity to other sacred things, because its explanation is the Host’s divine status.

rules.statement: Saints have no power of their own, but God may heed their intercession for the living; petitions are more effective in a saint’s area of interest and when made near that saint’s relics.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Saints (ars-magica-core#044)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default saintly intervention is mediated by God and favored by relevant relics; a world could make particular saints more or less responsive, reflecting their interests and standing.

rules.statement: A miracle may heal injuries, disease, or inherited afflictions, and may raise the dead—normally within about a week, though God may raise someone dead longer.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Miracles (ars-magica-core#044)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default miracles can heal and revive without a fixed magical procedure; a world could restrict revival to the first week or allow longer intervals, depending on divine purpose.

rules.statement: Punishment miracles inflict usually nonfatal, debilitating infirmities on people who have seriously disrespected God or his agents, as a call to repent.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Miracles (ars-magica-core#044)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default punishment is debilitating but rarely fatal and invites repentance; a world could make it harsher or gentler, according to the intended warning.

rules.statement: A miracle is more likely when a pious person sincerely asks, the affliction was wholly innocent, and an appropriate saint joins the request; God may still grant one to someone impious.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Miracles (ars-magica-core#044)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default likelihood rises with sincerity, innocence, and saintly support but is never guaranteed; a world could change how strongly these factors matter because divine choice remains free.

rules.statement: Monks and nuns vow poverty, chastity, stability, and obedience: they own no personal property, have no sexual relations, stay at one house, and obey its head.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Monasteries (ars-magica-core#044)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default vows constrain possessions, sex, travel, and conduct; a world could vary enforcement or permitted exceptions, with breach risking religious and institutional consequences.

rules.statement: The Church is entitled to one tenth of agricultural increase, and failure to pay is a serious sin commonly punished with heavy penance.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Resources (ars-magica-core#044)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default tithe is one tenth of agricultural produce; a world could change the rate or enforcement, with nonpayment carrying spiritual penance.

rules.statement: Markets usually meet weekly and draw people from roughly twelve miles around; fairs generally occur yearly for several days and can attract traders from much farther away.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Markets and Fairs (ars-magica-core#044)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default markets are weekly and local while fairs are annual and regional; a world could vary frequency and reach to reflect local trade and authority.

rules.statement: A widow may generally retain the profit, but not the income, from a third of her husband’s land until she remarries. If she owned land before marriage and has no adult sons, she is likely to regain full ownership of it.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Passage 46, opening section on widows (ars-magica-core#045)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a one-third profit share until remarriage; a setting can change the share or term to reflect local inheritance customs and family circumstances.

rules.statement: In some regions a widow may administer her son’s land as his guardian until he reaches adulthood, but stewardship may need to be purchased from the overlord, who may choose the steward. By convention, a lord may not arrange a woman’s marriage for a third time.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Passage 46, opening section on widows (ars-magica-core#045)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to guardian administration ending at adulthood, with the overlord controlling stewardship; a setting can relax those limits to shift authority toward families or local lords.

rules.statement: Nuns are generally protected as wards of the bishop: they cannot usually be compelled to marry and are not subject to their fathers or other local lords. Their lands are not divided through inheritance.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Passage 46, Nuns (ars-magica-core#045)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to ecclesiastical protection and undivided estate ownership; a setting can weaken these protections to make local political power more intrusive.

rules.statement: A woman may take temporary vows to withdraw into a nunnery while secular events unfold. A sufficiently influential nobleman can sometimes force her to leave and marry, but this is rare.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Passage 46, Nuns (ars-magica-core#045)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to vows providing a temporary refuge; a setting can make the refuge harder or easier to break depending on the noble’s influence and the Church’s protection.

rules.statement: The default historical setting assumes that magic has neither noticeably strengthened nor weakened since the Order was founded, though a troupe may instead decide it is rising or declining.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Chapter 16, The Fate of Magic (ars-magica-core#045)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.mechanism: law: magical strength may be set by the saga
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to stable magical strength; a saga can turn the dial toward growth or decline to change the availability of auras, vis, and supernatural opposition.

rules.statement: Renewable vis sources replenish, whereas vis finds are exhausted through use; early in a saga, finds let the group track consumption before deciding how much renewable supply to introduce. Suggested supply levels are up to 5 pawns per magus each year for low-vis play, about 10 for moderate play, and about 20 for high-vis play.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Resources (opening passage) (ars-magica-core#046)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to finite finds and modest supply; turn the dial toward renewable sources or higher annual amounts when the saga needs more magical capacity, accepting that withdrawing a source may frustrate players.

rules.statement: A tractatus can be studied only once by a particular character, making its advancement impact predictable. To slow advancement, limit the covenant’s summae and unstudied tractatus, and stop supplying books when a magus’s Arts reach the desired ceiling; the magus can still invent spells or study other Arts.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Resources (opening passage) (ars-magica-core#046)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to finite access to study books; increase supply for faster advancement, or cut it off at a chosen power level, trading broader progress for continued spell invention and other study.

rules.statement: Saga speed is determined by how many seasons of game time pass per session: a slow saga averages two or more sessions per season, a medium saga one to four seasons per session, and a fast saga more than one year per session. In a pulsed saga, long stretches of downtime alternate with intensive play; story arcs need explanations for why unresolved matters can wait through the quiet years.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Saga Speed (ars-magica-core#046)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a medium pace; slow or accelerate the passage of seasons to tune advancement and aging, with faster play making characters change and age more rapidly.

rules.statement: When a player runs a guest story while the regular storyguide participates, use isolated locations or rare-entry regiones to reduce clashes with long-term plans. The guest storyguide should agree with the regular guide on suitable rewards and risks beforehand.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Troupe-Style Roleplaying — Guest Storyguiding (ars-magica-core#046)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to self-contained stories; relax the isolation or entry limits when the story should affect the wider saga, at the cost of greater risk to established plans.

rules.statement: The alpha storyguide has final veto over additions to the saga, while beta storyguides may freely run the parts assigned to their locations. All guides should agree on tone and reward level.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Troupe-Style Roleplaying — Alpha and Beta Storyguides (ars-magica-core#046)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to an alpha guide’s final decision and bounded beta domains; broaden beta authority if the troupe wants more shared control, accepting increased coordination needs.

rules.statement: One point of Confidence may be awarded at session end for each listed achievement: meeting a personal goal, contributing to a group goal, succeeding at a difficult task, entertaining roleplay, or a guide-approved bonus. The bonus category is limited to one point per character per session.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Reference Guide — Confidence — Gaining Confidence Points (ars-magica-core#046)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the listed end-of-session awards and the one-point bonus cap; the group can tighten or broaden awards to adjust how quickly Confidence accumulates.

rules.statement: After seeing a roll’s result, a character may spend 1 to their full Confidence Score in points, adding +3 per point; Confidence cannot be spent on a botched roll.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Reference Guide — Confidence — Spending Confidence (ars-magica-core#046)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to post-roll spending with a +3 benefit per point and no use on botches; changing the cap or bonus alters how much stored Confidence can rescue a result.

rules.statement: For non-combat damage, add a stress die to the damage bonus and separately to the target’s Soak total. Compare the totals using the size-based wound ranges; each 5 points, or fraction group as specified by the table, by which damage exceeds Soak raises the wound level by one, and each additional size point expands every wound range by one.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Reference Guide — Non-Combat Damage — Non-Combat Damage Rolls and Damage Table (ars-magica-core#046)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the listed damage and soak totals and size ranges; adjust damage intensity or coverage to make hazards more or less dangerous, with greater exposure increasing the damage bonus.

rules.statement: A formulaic spell succeeds without fatigue loss when the casting total meets its level; being 1–10 points short still casts it but costs one fatigue level, while a larger shortfall fails and costs one level. The target is affected only if penetration exceeds its Magic Resistance.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Magic Rules — Formulaic Spellcasting Sequence (ars-magica-core#047)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to allowing a narrow shortfall to produce a costly cast; a world can tighten the success margin, with fatigue as the caster’s price.

rules.statement: A ritual takes 15 minutes and one pawn of vis per spell magnitude. Meeting the spell level casts it at a cost of one long-term fatigue level; shortfalls of 1–5, 6–10, and 11–15 still cast at costs of two, three, and four fatigue levels, while a shortfall of 16 or more fails and costs five; unmet fatigue costs convert to wounds.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Magic Rules — Ritual Spellcasting Sequence (ars-magica-core#047)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to slow, vis-consuming rituals with escalating fatigue costs; a world can change the time or vis requirement, trading access to powerful effects against resources and bodily harm.

rules.statement: A spontaneous spell cast with fatigue uses half the casting score plus a stress die and costs one fatigue level; a non-fatiguing attempt uses one fifth of the casting score. An effect is produced only when the resulting total meets its requirement.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Magic Rules — Spontaneous Spellcasting Sequence (ars-magica-core#047)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to making improvised magic more effective when the caster accepts fatigue; a world can increase or reduce the divisor, balancing safe flexibility against bodily cost.

rules.statement: A spell’s penetration must be greater than the target’s Magic Resistance to affect it. Sympathetic connections increase the penetration multiplier, while arcane connections add multiplier bonuses according to how long they last, from +1 for hours or days to +4 for indefinite connections.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Magic Rules — Penetration (ars-magica-core#047)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to resistance blocking effects unless penetration exceeds it; a world can strengthen the benefit of personal links, at the cost of obtaining or maintaining those links.

rules.statement: A foreign supernatural aura modifies powers according to the realm-interaction table: for example, magic power gains the aura rating in a Magic aura, has no effect in a Divine aura, gains half the rating in a Faerie aura, and loses the rating in an Infernal aura. Casting in a foreign aura adds one botch die per aura level, or two per level in a foreign regio.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Magic Rules — Realm Interaction Table (ars-magica-core#047)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to realm auras changing both power and risk; a world can intensify or soften cross-realm penalties, making location a meaningful magical cost.

rules.statement: A spell maintained by concentration requires checks against the listed difficulty for interruptions; for concentration spells, those difficulties are reduced by three. Maintaining additional spells is difficult, with the listed check set at 12 and increased by 3 for each spell beyond the second.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Magic Rules — Concentration (ars-magica-core#047)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to ongoing effects ending when concentration fails; a world can make concentration easier or harder, trading sustained magic against attention and vulnerability.

rules.statement: Each increase in spell size multiplies the affected volume by ten and adds one magnitude. The listed spell sizes define the base scale for targets such as individuals, groups, rooms, structures, and boundaries.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Magic Rules — Spell Sizes; Volumes and Targets (ars-magica-core#047)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a tenfold scale increase per added magnitude; a world can change the scale ladder, making broad effects cheaper or more demanding.

rules.statement: An enchanted effect can gain +2 penetration per added level; maintaining concentration adds 5 levels, restricted use adds 3, an environmental trigger adds 3, fast activation adds 5 and grants +3 Initiative, and a linked trigger adds 3. Use frequency raises the required modifier from 0 for once daily to +10 for unlimited uses.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Definitive Edition: Laboratory Rules — Enchanted Items, Effect Modifiers; Number of Uses (ars-magica-core#047)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to paying effect levels for enhanced penetration, triggers, and repeated use; a world can alter those surcharges, trading item capacity for convenience and power.

rules.statement: A wizard outside the Order should be offered the opportunity to join before the Order attacks; the passage describes this as the usual policy, with Flambeau making an exception for the sahirs he regarded as enemies.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Chapter One: House Flambeau — Join or Die (ars-magica-houses#000)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to requiring an offer before attacking outsiders; a world can make recruitment more coercive because rulers fear rival magical groups.

rules.statement: Members of the milites swear brotherhood and mutual-defense oaths. Their war-bands generally include at least three or four wizards, use scouts and guarded flanks and rear, and are accompanied by grogs.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Chapter One: House Flambeau — The Rise of the Milites (ars-magica-houses#000)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to mutual aid among oath-takers; a world can make the oath enforceable or costly because the band relies on trust in battle.

rules.statement: The Alarm effect can be used once per day and reaches everyone in a target Group, at any distance, if the user has an Arcane Connection to each person; its Penetration is +70. Hearing it prompts volunteer defenders to lower their Parmae Magicae and wait for the summons.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: The Horn of the Champions — Sounding the Alarm (ars-magica-houses#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to once daily and require a personal Arcane Connection for each recipient; a world could change the reach or frequency, with reliable long-distance warning limited by those connections.

rules.statement: The Summoning effect can be used once per day to transport each member of a target Group instantly to the horn, if the user has an Arcane Connection to that person. It has no Penetration, so a summoned magus can resist it.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: The Horn of the Champions — Summoning the Champions (ars-magica-houses#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to instant transport once daily, gated by an Arcane Connection and subject to resistance; a world could make it harder to resist or remove the connection requirement, at the cost of making forced travel more reliable.

rules.statement: A candidate to House Flambeau needs a sponsor, who arranges a combat-focused Gauntlet and decides whether the candidate passes. A candidate who fails an apprentice Gauntlet three times receives a fourth from a Quaesitor; passing then allows entry to the Order, but not to House Flambeau.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Joining House Flambeau (ars-magica-houses#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to sponsor-led testing with the sponsor as final judge; a world could set fixed tests or transfer judgment to an official, trading personal discretion for consistent admission.

rules.statement: Publicly swearing to the Code of Garus grants a new Story Flaw; taking the oath seriously may also count as a separate Personality Flaw. The Code includes duties to serve the Order, obey the House Primus, defend the innocent, and keep one’s pledged word.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: The Code of Garus (ars-magica-houses#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to an oath that adds a Story Flaw when publicly sworn; a world could make the oath magically enforceable, with the added obligation and its consequences serving as the cost.

rules.statement: Flambeau volunteers defending Castra Solis exchange fixed Arcane Connections with the castellan: each gives one to the castellan and receives one in return. The Alarm and Summoning effects use the user’s Arcane Connections to reach those volunteers.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: The Horn of the Champions (ars-magica-houses#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a reciprocal connection for each volunteer; a world could allow one-way or temporary links, with reduced trust or reliability as the tradeoff.
