rules.statement: A caster may limit a spell’s Penetration Total to 0 without extra skill or effort, by casting with only the effort needed to avoid fatigue and not using Penetration. Assuming the caster does not botch, this prevents the spell from affecting a target with Magic Resistance of 0 or more.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Forceless Casting (ars-magica-houses#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to allowing deliberate zero Penetration; a world can require a special procedure instead, because the choice represents intentionally withholding force.

rules.statement: In dimicatio, competitors cast real spells using forceless casting and each may fast-cast a defense against the other’s spell. The first spell to reach the opponent’s Parma wins; aimed spells that bypass Magic Resistance are forbidden, and a spell that penetrates Parma counts as foul play.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Dimicatio (ars-magica-houses#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a contest decided by the first spell reaching Parma; a world can ban or loosen the contest’s restrictions, trading safety and legality for greater danger.

rules.statement: In the detailed dimicatio procedure, contestants begin at Voice range, roll Initiative, and the winner casts first; if the defender’s fast-cast defense succeeds, that defender can cast on their turn and the exchange repeats. A defense around half the incoming spell’s level is usually sufficient, and contestants may spend vis.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Dimicatio in Detail (ars-magica-houses#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to alternating attacks and fast-cast defenses, with a half-level defense as a guideline; a world can set stricter defense requirements, making contests more hazardous.

rules.statement: A Wizard’s War must be declared on a full-moon night, begins at the rise of the next full moon, and lasts until the rise of the third full moon. It is legally a conflict between exactly two wizards and does not authorize attacks on, theft from, or scrying on other magi.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Wizard’s War and the Order (ars-magica-houses#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a fixed two-lunar-month conflict with legal protection for uninvolved magi; a world can change the term or scope, with the risk of wider conflict and legal disputes.

rules.statement: A new Wizard’s War cannot be declared until the previous one ends. Repeated declarations therefore create alternating periods of one month at war and one month at peace.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Wizard’s War and the Order (ars-magica-houses#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to requiring a month of peace between wars; a world can permit consecutive wars, at the cost of removing the opponent’s respite.

rules.statement: A combatant may hide in a friendly covenant and benefit from its Aegis and members’ refusal of entry; the opponent may not use the war as license to violate the rights of magi who are not combatants. A combatant can separately declare wars against multiple allies, though those opponents may unite against them.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Wizard’s War and the Order (ars-magica-houses#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to protecting noncombatants and allowing covenant refuge; a world can narrow these protections, but doing so raises the likelihood of escalation and retaliation.

rules.statement: A spell that does not penetrate Magic Resistance cannot affect a protected target; scrying spells likewise fail to detect a magus unless they penetrate that resistance. Arcane Connections can help a caster reach a target at a distance and improve Penetration, while sympathetic links can increase its multiplier.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Waging Wizard’s War (ars-magica-houses#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to requiring penetration for magical effects and detection against Magic Resistance; a world can weaken that barrier, making magi easier to locate and affect.

rules.statement: A Rego attack that supplies all the projectile’s motion is stopped by Magic Resistance and need not be aimed. If magic only lifts an object before releasing it to fall naturally, or gives it a brief launch and then releases it, the attack bypasses Magic Resistance but must be aimed; specially designed launched projectiles have a 20-pace range increment and cannot travel farther than a powerful mundane launcher could send them.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Projectiles and Rego Magic (ars-magica-houses#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to letting naturally moving or released projectiles bypass Magic Resistance; a world can require magical propulsion for every attack, because its natural philosophy may not support motion after release.

rules.statement: An invisible character cannot be targeted by attacks or spells until an observer locates her to within about half a pace; locating her usually takes a round and an opposed Perception + Awareness roll against Dexterity + Stealth – Encumbrance plus the applicable Stealth bonus. Once located, the observer tracks her until her signs change or she moves away for two or three rounds; visibility clues also set the invisible character’s attack, defense, and Stealth bonuses, from +1/+3/+3 for obvious signs to +9/+9/+12 when there are no signs.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Fighting Invisibly; Locating an Invisible Character; Effects of Invisibility (ars-magica-houses#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to concealment that blocks targeting until the location is found; a world can make sound, scent, or other cues more or less reliable, because invisibility does not suppress noise and may leave physical traces.

rules.statement: An invisible combatant’s first surprise attack automatically goes first and gets +3 to attack; after that, combat proceeds normally, and another surprise attack is possible after disengaging if the opponent still lacks the character’s exact location. Invisible combatants cannot fight as a trained group, and each invisible member of an untrained group adds one botch die to everyone in it.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Fighting Invisibly; Invisibility and Group Combat (ars-magica-houses#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to granting a one-round surprise advantage but making invisible allies harder to coordinate; a world can reduce the group penalty if allies have a reliable way to track one another.

rules.statement: Fast Trigger adds +3 to an enchanted effect’s Initiative modifier and increases that effect’s level by 5. Imperturbable Casting adds the caster’s Mastery score to Concentration rolls for the spell, while Precise Casting adds +1 to Finesse rolls and removes one botch die, to a minimum of one.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Effect Modification for Enchanted Items; Spell Mastery Special Abilities (ars-magica-houses#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to allowing faster item activation and improved casting at the listed level or Mastery costs; a world can restrict these refinements, because greater speed and precision demand specialized enchantment or spell practice.

rules.statement: House Acclaim is a free Reputation for each Flambeau magus, potentially known throughout the Order. Credible witnesses must see a deed for it to earn points; it can also lose points, including one point for each year without a gain, but it cannot fall below zero, and ignoble acts at zero can create a bad Reputation.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: House Acclaim (ars-magica-houses#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to public deeds raising a reputation that decays by one point per inactive year; a world can change decay or witness requirements, because prestige depends on continuing visible accomplishment.

rules.statement: A miles publicly swears to uphold an honor code, begins with 5 House Acclaim experience points, and can rely on other milites for assistance; relying on them too often may cost respect. The miles must obey the House Primus’s direct orders, though orders cannot dictate the magus’s vote or Tribunal speech, and fulfilling an order earns Acclaim experience.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: New Flaws: Miles (ars-magica-houses#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a public oath that grants standing and support while binding the character to orders; a world can widen or narrow the oath’s demands, because obligations are enforced through the House’s respect and authority.

rules.statement: A spell that creates a creature under magical control may still be resisted when the creature attacks: the summoned asp has no Might of its own, but Magic Resistance protects against its bite using the caster’s Penetration Total. A weapon wielded by an animated corpse can instead bypass Magic Resistance when the weapon itself is nonmagical.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Summoning the Creeping Death; Indirect Spells from ArM5 (ars-magica-houses#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to checking resistance against magically delivered creature attacks but not against a separate mundane weapon; a world can treat all attacks by controlled beings as magical, because the attack’s source may be considered the controlling effect.

rules.statement: A natural or nonmagical hazard can affect a target despite its Magic Resistance even when magic caused the hazard indirectly, such as a fire spreading, a tree falling, or a pit opening beneath someone. A magical effect that directly harms or touches the target still requires penetration.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Indirect Spells from ArM5; Projectiles and Rego Magic (ars-magica-houses#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to allowing indirect physical consequences through Magic Resistance while blocking direct magical harm; a world can let resistance protect against all magic-caused consequences, because it may treat causal magic as equivalent to contact.

rules.statement: A sling-sized stone can be launched at a target within range. The caster must succeed at an aiming roll; on a hit, Magic Resistance does not protect the target, and the stone deals +5 damage with a 20-pace range increment.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Opening spell description (ars-magica-houses#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a physical projectile that bypasses Magic Resistance only after a successful aim; a world could make magical resistance apply, at the cost of weakening the spell’s unusual penetration.

rules.statement: A magus using family members as agents may spend Bond Maintenance points on them, with the available points equal to the Adventure experience received for that story. The player must connect the story’s events plausibly to the family members’ fortunes; a tenuous connection may limit spending to 1 point.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Nepotism (ars-magica-houses#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to family agents gaining investment from story-linked Bond Maintenance; a world could require a stronger connection or lower the limit, reflecting how hard it is to turn an adventure into a relative’s advantage.

rules.statement: A family has a Reputation that can be changed by the actions of its members. A character may use that Reputation with people who do not personally know the character; family membership can be concealed to avoid an unwanted family Reputation.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Family Reputation (ars-magica-houses#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to family Reputation standing in for personal Reputation only with strangers; a world could make kinship easier to discover, at the cost of losing the option to avoid inherited reputation.

rules.statement: A charm worn by an apprentice can suppress the negative thoughts caused by the Gift, and a magus can instead shelter the apprentice within Parma Magica. Neither measure prevents negative reactions from ordinary people to the group.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: The Itinerarium (ars-magica-houses#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to suppressing Gift-driven mistrust without changing mundane reactions; a world could extend the protection to bystanders’ reactions, at the cost of making social concealment much easier.

rules.statement: Reading or writing paradoxographia takes no time away from laboratory work and grants no experience points.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Paradoxography (ars-magica-houses#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to treating the activity as leisure with no time or experience benefit; a world could award practice or require downtime, trading free flavor for mechanical advancement or a real time cost.

rules.statement: At an event, an individual may use Etiquette to seek the most memorable performance; the host sets the target from 6 to 21. The best successful result earns experience toward a fitting Reputation, and the performer may instead give the result to another person.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Etiquette — Individual (ars-magica-houses#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a host-set target of 6–21; turn the target upward when the host wants stricter conduct, because social control of the event determines the standard.

rules.statement: In an etiquette duel, each participant chooses a penalty no greater than their Etiquette score. Add the two chosen penalties and subtract that sum from both participants’ usual rolls; failures can make the participants look foolish or boorish and may lead to poor Reputations.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Etiquette — Competitive (ars-magica-houses#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to applying both declared penalties to both rolls; turn the dial through each participant’s Etiquette score, with greater willingness to risk rudeness worsening both performances.

rules.statement: For a collaborative event, add all participants’ scores and compare the total with similar past events; each botch subtracts 10. Hosts can improve their social standing through a successful event, while attendance can create useful contacts.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Etiquette — Collaborative (ars-magica-houses#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to summing the group’s results and subtracting 10 per botch; a troupe can raise or lower the event benchmark, with hosting effort and botches shaping the outcome.

rules.statement: A mundane character can spend money on suitable materials to gain +1 per amount equal to the weekly income of all guests, capped by the character’s Etiquette score. Gathering suitable items takes time: a city resident may spend at most one pound per day, while someone outside a city must travel to one or hire a skilled procurer; a magus’s rare, relevant gift can instead add +1 to +5.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Money and Good Manners (ars-magica-houses#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the stated spending rate and Etiquette cap; a world can make suitable goods scarcer, increasing the time or procurement cost of a stronger social performance.

rules.statement: A lacuna is a patch in a city where the Dominion does not dominate. It lets a magus cast without Dominion realm-interaction penalties only when the spell does not target something inside the Dominion; lacunae can move or vanish and may have a Magical, Infernal, Faerie, or no aura.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Urban Magic — Lacunae (ars-magica-houses#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to removing Dominion interaction penalties only for eligible casting from the lacuna; turn its size, stability, and access into dials, since useful sites may be small, transient, or costly to use.

rules.statement: A character who searches for lacunae spends a season and rolls Intelligence + Area Lore against 9; the first search reveals obvious public sites. A character familiar with the area knows three small lacunae per Area Lore level, and a site offering extra resources must carry a limitation unless it came from specified character or story sources.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Finding New Lacunae (ars-magica-houses#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one season, target 9, and three known sites per Area Lore level; the troupe can make extra resources costly through access restrictions, inhabitants, exposure, or an Infernal aura.

rules.statement: A muse may grant one nearby character the Free Expression Virtue, or double that character’s existing Free Expression benefit, while the muse is with them. The artist is typically driven to improve their craft and character to remain worthy of the muse.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: New Virtues — Muse (ars-magica-houses#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to helping only one character while the muse is present; a world can make the benefit conditional on proximity and the artist’s ongoing effort to improve.

rules.statement: Mystical Choreography reduces ceremonial magic to five minutes per magnitude, or one minute per magnitude when performed in a prepared space, however temporary.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: New Virtues — Mystical Choreography (ars-magica-houses#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to five minutes per magnitude and one in a prepared space; a world can make preparation the dial, trading setup for faster ceremonial casting.

rules.statement: Once per story, a character with Supernatural Beauty may ask the storyguide to add a fortunate coincidence to a scene; the storyguide chooses it, and the troupe may veto use where supernatural aid is profoundly unlikely. The character must have positive Presence.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: New Virtues — Supernatural Beauty (ars-magica-houses#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one coincidence request per story subject to storyguide choice and troupe veto; a world can narrow eligible scenes, with the aid justified by beauty’s ability to attract help.

rules.statement: Performance Magic requires a separate Minor Virtue for each activity and linked Ability used to disguise casting; the activity must be performed each time. Activities can replace words, gestures, or both, while props may be required to replace both.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Performance Magic, in Brief (ars-magica-houses#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to requiring the chosen activity and any necessary props for concealment; a world can loosen that requirement, at the cost of making covert casting easier.

rules.statement: A Performance Duration spell lasts only while the caster performs, and the caster automatically succeeds at Concentration rolls to maintain it. Casting requires a roll of die + the Ability’s Characteristic + Ability against Ease Factor 3; failure or a botch makes the spell fail.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Performance Magic, in Brief (ars-magica-houses#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to ending the effect when the performance stops; a world can let it persist longer, at the cost of weakening the link between spell and performance.

rules.statement: Ceremonial props add to Casting Score according to size: +1 for tiny, +2 small, +3 medium, +4 large, and +5 for props too large to move from their room. Using props slows ceremonial casting, and they are aids rather than magical items.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Ceremonial Magic (ars-magica-houses#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to granting the listed bonus while requiring a suitable physical prop and slower casting; a world can make props portable or faster to use, at the cost of reduced bonus.

rules.statement: Prepared ceremonial spaces determine casting time per magnitude: 12 minutes for a temporary space, 9 for a naturally suitable one, 6 for a deliberately designed one, 3 for a laboratory or contemplative place, and 1 for a dedicated casting room. Mystical Choreography also permits one-minute casting regardless of how temporary the prepared space is.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Ceremonial Magic (ars-magica-houses#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to setting casting time by the quality of the prepared place; a world can allow rapid casting in ordinary locations, at the cost of diminishing the value of preparation.

rules.statement: If a saint grants the Civic Patron’s requested miracle, the Dominion’s penalties for Realm interaction fall to zero for one scene or story, as the troupe decides; the character’s magic must be used virtuously to defend the city from harm.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Invocation of the Civic Patron (ars-magica-houses#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to removing Dominion penalties only for virtuous city defense and only for the granted duration; a world can broaden the protection, at the cost of stricter service or divine conditions.

rules.statement: Creo magic produces a functional natural object unless the spell botches. An Intelligence + Finesse roll can add detail; for artificial objects, achieving detail requires the same Finesse as Rego crafting from raw materials.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Creo Magic (ars-magica-houses#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a functional but not specially tailored result unless the caster succeeds at Finesse; a world can allow more precise creation without a roll, at the cost of reduced uniqueness.

rules.statement: Rego magic can perform work a mundane artist could do with tools; its Finesse Ease Factor is 3 higher than the mundane task’s, with a further +3 for work that takes a month, +6 for a season, or +9 for a year. A day’s work adds nothing.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Rego Magic (ars-magica-houses#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to applying the time-based difficulty increases as stated; a world can remove them for magically accelerated work, at the cost of making intricate long-term craft easier.

rules.statement: A granted emotion can supply an artificial +5 Personality Trait. Extreme emotions can be resisted with an opposed Personality Trait roll against Ease Factor 9; milder emotions use Ease Factor 4 plus the artificial Trait’s score, despite having the same level as stronger effects.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Created Emotional Bias (ars-magica-houses#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a +5 emotional bias that can be resisted by the stated roll; a world can make emotions harder to resist, at the cost of increasing their coercive impact.

rules.statement: Directly created sensory species are resisted by Parma Magica. A convincing detailed image requires a Finesse roll, while simply overwhelming sight or producing a basic effect does not necessarily require one.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Opening passage before An Enemy Awash in the Pure Sigil of the Magus (ars-magica-houses#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default direct sensory creations to being resisted by Parma; a world can turn resistance off for effects without a magical medium, because the defense counters magical targeting.

rules.statement: Magic can create, understand, control, change, or destroy thoughts; it can also alter how sensations are categorized or impair a specific cognitive capacity. A spell that suppresses a capacity only temporarily restores it when the spell ends.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Altering Thoughts (ars-magica-houses#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default cognitive impairments to ending with their spell; a world can make them persistent, at the cost of departing from the described temporary-capacity model.

rules.statement: Magic can create episodic memories, but cannot create procedural or inscribed memories that grant Abilities. A single created memory uses base level 5; episodic memories may provide a fact or, at the troupe’s discretion, automatic success on a particular Lore check.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Memory; Inscribed Memories; Procedural Memories; Episodic Memories (ars-magica-houses#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default magic to creating episodic memories but not learned Abilities; a world can permit magical skill creation, at the cost of changing the stated limit of Hermetic understanding.

rules.statement: Creating an episodic memory requires an Intelligence + Finesse roll against Ease Factor 6. Success margins of 3, 6, and 9 allow progressively more caster-known detail; failure produces an unbelievable memory, while a botch leaves a conspicuously false element.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Episodic Memories (ars-magica-houses#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default memory detail to depend on the roll and margin; a world can fix detail regardless of skill, at the cost of removing the passage’s reliability limits.

rules.statement: Episodic memories damaged or distorted by magic can mend through inference and related reasoning. Loss of autobiographical memory does not remove other abilities, though the person may not know which abilities they can use or understand the details of actions performed instinctively.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Episodic Memories (ars-magica-houses#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default episodic-memory damage to self-repair and leave other abilities intact; a world can make damage permanent or ability-blocking, at the cost of the described recovery and separation between memory and skill.

rules.statement: Thoughts and memories created by a spell fade when it expires. A target can preserve an impression by actively using or reproducing it for an hour per image or significant cluster of facts, but the reconstructed version is imprecise and errors accumulate in complex material.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: The Memorization of Created Knowledge (ars-magica-houses#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default created knowledge to fade with its spell and require an hour of use to reconstruct; a world can allow instant or exact retention, at the cost of bypassing the described effort and loss of precision.

rules.statement: A Rego Mentem inclination can make someone more receptive to belief or less interested in what they perceive. Lack of interest makes the person less likely to remember what was seen, but does not itself destroy memories.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Other Tricks of Memory — Inclinations (ars-magica-houses#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default inclinations to affect response rather than erase memory; a world can let them directly remove memories, at the cost of expanding this effect beyond the stated limit.

rules.statement: A formally declared rivalry between two magi continues for both of their lifetimes, ending only when either one dies. The rivals may hinder one another and endanger each other, while others are expected not to interfere.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Beloved Rivals (ars-magica-houses#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a rivalry that lasts until one rival dies; a world could make it shorter or allow outsiders to intervene, at the cost of weakening the relationship’s lasting force.

rules.statement: An eristic moot requires at least five attendees: two participants and three witnesses. Participants agree beforehand which forms of contest are allowed; in a subtle contest, magic is prohibited.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Eristic Moots (ars-magica-houses#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to five attendees and agreed contest methods; a world could change the minimum or permit magic in subtle contests, at the cost of changing public scrutiny and risk.

rules.statement: In a magical moot, participants may publicly disclaim intent to kill and allow each other to use scrying magic; with these declarations, only an opponent’s death leads to prosecution under the Code of Hermes.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Eristic Moots (ars-magica-houses#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to prosecution only if a participant dies under these declared terms; a world could impose stricter limits, at the cost of making magical contests less permissive.

rules.statement: Tytalan apprenticeship lasts 15 seasons before instruction ends, but the apprentice does not thereby become a magus. The apprentice must force the master to accept them as an equal; if the apprentice does not bring magic into the challenge, the master will.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: The Apprentice’s Gauntlet (ars-magica-houses#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to 15 seasons followed by a challenge for recognition; a world could shorten training or remove the challenge, at the cost of changing what qualifies an apprentice to join.

rules.statement: An apprentice who kills their master becomes a magus immediately, regardless of how much training is complete. Passing the Gauntlet before completing 15 seasons can leave the apprentice with the Weak Parens Flaw.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: The Apprentice’s Gauntlet (ars-magica-houses#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to immediate status on the master’s death and a flaw for premature success; a world could require completed training, at the cost of removing this dangerous shortcut.

rules.statement: An apprentice who fails the Gauntlet three times is usually advised to ask a Quaesitor to administer it; this route is considered ignoble and often results in the Tormenting Master Flaw.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: The Apprentice’s Gauntlet (ars-magica-houses#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to advice after three failures and a likely flaw for the outside-administered route; a world could change the threshold or consequences, at the cost of changing the pressure to succeed unaided.

rules.statement: The Book of Instruction assigns punishments for specific apprentice behaviors, with arbitrary conditions and durations; examples include collecting 144 pinecones for obduracy and wearing vinegar-soaked clothes for one week for intransigence.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Excerpts from the Book of Instruction (ars-magica-houses#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to behavior-triggered, text-specified punishments; a world could replace the penalties or make them predictable, at the cost of changing the regime’s arbitrary pressure.

rules.statement: A magus can join House Tytalus by accepting its philosophy and forcing a Tytalus of similar or greater age to recognize them as worthy, using a challenge like the Apprentice’s Gauntlet. A magus who abandons the House has one year to join another House before being punished for vagrancy.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Joining House Tytalus (ars-magica-houses#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to earned entry and a one-year deadline after departure; a world could relax either condition, at the cost of changing how exclusive membership is.

rules.statement: A character with Persona changes into or out of an identity with one round of concentration and a Stamina + Persona roll against Ease Factor 9. Each Persona Ability point provides one identity; gaining another point requires creating a new identity.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: New Supernatural Ability: Persona (ars-magica-houses#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one identity per Ability point and a target of 9; a world can raise the target or restrict identities because maintaining multiple convincing selves is demanding.

rules.statement: A deep-cover identity begins with Reputation 1 after a witnessed act establishes it. Actions that support the role give 1 experience point, and living in a community for a season usually gives 2; gaining more than 2 per season risks suspicion. After dormancy lasting years equal to its Reputation, the Reputation loses 1 point each year.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Deep Cover Disguises (ars-magica-houses#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the stated Reputation gains and decay; a world can accelerate decay because communities forget an absent identity.

rules.statement: A Persona transformation is detectable as a Muto Corpus effect of level 10 at first, then drops by one magnitude for each sunrise or sunset after the change. For equivalent spell effects, use a level equal to five times the Persona Ability score.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Personae (ars-magica-houses#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a detectable level-10 trace that fades twice daily; a world can make traces persist longer because magical scrutiny is stronger.

rules.statement: A Leper Magus can accept wounds to generate vis for one current magical working: a Light Wound gives 3 pawns, Medium 6, Heavy 9, Incapacitating 12, and Deadly 15. The vis cannot be stored or used by anyone else, excess is lost, the wound must heal fully before reuse, and use more than three times in a year adds an Aging roll in winter.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: New Virtues: Leper Magus (ars-magica-houses#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to wound severity setting the vis amount and self-only use; a world can increase the wound cost because this power draws on diseased flesh.

rules.statement: In a debate, an attacker’s choice of Folk Ken, Intrigue, or Artes Liberales interacts with the opponent’s Charm, Guile, or Leadership defense: the matching table gives +3, 0, or −3 to the attack. A debate ends at its preset round limit, or when a position loses at least 5 Fatigue Levels.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Resolving Differences (ars-magica-houses#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the printed modifier table and a typical 5–10 round limit; a world can shorten debates because its arbiter wants a quicker decision.

rules.statement: In a debate with observers, Argument Strength converts into votes: at strengths 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, and 7+, respectively, the winner gains 10%, 20%, 30%, 40%, 50%, and 60% of neutral votes; at strengths 5, 6, and 7+, the winner also takes 10%, 20%, and 30% of hostile votes. Unassigned neutral votes abstain.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Winning Arguments (ars-magica-houses#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the stated vote percentages; a world can make observers harder to sway because factional loyalties outweigh persuasion.

rules.statement: In a case debate, each testimony can be used once: written or mundane testimony gives +1, testimony from a social inferior gives +2, and a peer’s gives +3; Quaesitorial examination adds a cumulative +3. A praeco typically ends the debate after 10 rounds.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Case Rulings (ars-magica-houses#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one use per testimony and the stated bonuses; a world can restrict testimony because formal review is tightly controlled.

rules.statement: When an agent’s Resistance reaches zero during recruitment by a rival, the agent becomes a double agent and favors the principal with the higher Bond Strength. The original principal can retain the agent as a triple agent by discovering the subordination and feeding false information.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Double Agents and Hostile Takeovers (ars-magica-houses#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to loyalty following the higher Bond Strength at zero Resistance; a world can make loyalty harder to shift because agents fear betrayal or punishment.

rules.statement: A supernatural ability succeeds when a die roll plus the relevant Characteristic, ability score, and aura modifier meets the task’s Ease Factor; it normally costs no Fatigue unless that ability says otherwise. When penetration is needed, calculate it as Casting Total minus Ease Factor plus Penetration Bonus; use five times the ability score as its equivalent spell level.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Supernatural Abilities — The Basics (ars-magica-houses#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to no Fatigue cost and the stated total; a setting can make particular abilities tiring, with exhaustion as the cost.

rules.statement: A character may spend raw vis to raise a supernatural ability’s Casting Total by 1 per pawn, but may spend no more pawns than the ability score and gains an extra botch die for the expenditure. The vis must be appropriate to that ability.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Supernatural Abilities — The Basics (ars-magica-houses#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a one-point boost per pawn capped by ability score; a world can loosen the cap, risking more botches and consuming scarce vis.

rules.statement: An accelerated supernatural ability uses the Art experience scale and has no character-creation level cap; its equivalent spell level is its Casting Total, rather than five times its score. It still functions as an ability in totals and follows the usual supernatural-ability restrictions, including the vis rules.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Accelerated Abilities (ars-magica-houses#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the accelerated advancement scale and Casting Total equivalence; a world can restrict accelerated abilities to keep high-magnitude effects rare.

rules.statement: When designing a supernatural ability, fix three of Range, Duration, Target, and base guideline, allowing only one to vary with ability score or Casting Total. Prefer ability score for breadth with little impact on others, and Casting Total for effects imposed on others; every use requires the tradition’s stated practices.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Designing a Supernatural Ability (ars-magica-houses#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to three fixed parameters, one variable parameter, and mandatory practices; a world can loosen these limits at the cost of making abilities broader or easier to impose.

rules.statement: Summon Animals requires an audible call and a suitable habitat within one day’s journey; on a Communication plus ability roll against Ease Factor 9, it brings the score-dependent number or equivalent mass of animals within an hour. Exceeding the Ease Factor by 3 reduces arrival to two minutes, and by 6 to one round; the animals are friendly but not directly communicative, and their departure is set by the storyguide.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Example Supernatural Abilities — Summon Animals (ars-magica-houses#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the listed animal limits and arrival times; a world can shorten the range or arrival window, with suitable habitats and a successful call as constraints.

rules.statement: Whistle Up the Wind creates a wind at its rolled strength, using the table’s Ease Factors from 6 for a light breeze to 18 for hurricane force. The wind persists after the whistle stops, but each sunset weakens it by one strength step; changing it, weakening it, or ending it requires a Communication plus Music concentration roll, and a new roll is needed to increase strength.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Example Supernatural Abilities — Whistle Up the Wind (ars-magica-houses#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to sunset-driven weakening and no strengthening without a fresh roll; a world can extend the duration, with weather remaining in place as the consequence.

rules.statement: Control Fertility affects one human, one animal of Size +2 or equivalent mass, or one tree or equivalent vegetation, and requires physically marking the target. A Presence plus ability roll against Ease Factor 9 lasts one month, plus one month for each full 3 points above the factor; a target cannot be affected again until the next spring, and the ability score sets the permitted effect.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Example Supernatural Abilities — Control Fertility (ars-magica-houses#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the stated target, duration, score-based effects, and spring reuse limit; a world can broaden targets or remove the seasonal restriction, at the cost of greater reach.

rules.statement: A Columbae ward requires drawing a circle and inscribing symbols that define a category within one Hermetic Form; it can be narrowed by properties or an Arcane Connection. Completing the circle enchants its perimeter and always costs one Fatigue level; the Warding Total is a stress die plus Stamina, Warding, aura, and other applicable modifiers.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Columbae — Major Supernatural Virtue: Warding (ars-magica-houses#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a marked circle, a single-Form category, and one Fatigue level per ward; a world can allow broader wards, requiring more stringent definitions or higher costs.

rules.statement: For a ward against a natural object or material, compare the Warding Total with the Hermetic spell level needed for that target; mundane animals require 5, while wood requires 30. Against a supernatural target with Might, calculate Penetration as though the spell were level 0 and use the full Penetration Total as the ward’s effective level.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Wards and Penetration (ars-magica-houses#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the stated target thresholds and use full Penetration against Might; a setting can raise or lower these thresholds to tune ward reliability, with greater resistance making protection harder to establish.

rules.statement: A Columba’s Warding cannot affect creatures that have Magic Resistance but no Might, leaving such beings immune. Hermetic wards instead must penetrate Magic Resistance, and ordinarily cannot use an Arcane Connection to a supernatural target unless it is inside the circle when the ward is cast.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Wards and Penetration (ars-magica-houses#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to immunity for Might-less resistant targets under Warding and the stated Arcane Connection restriction for Hermetic wards; a world can broaden these interactions, at the cost of weakening the distinction between warding traditions.

rules.statement: A Columba with Ring/Circle Magic draws circles at twice normal speed, rolls to maintain concentration only if the circle breaks while casting, and reduces the Ease Factor for concentration during casting by 3. The benefit applies only to Hermetic spells with Touch range, Ring duration, and Circle target; damaging or erasing any required boundary mark immediately ends the effect.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Minor Hermetic Virtue: Ring/Circle Magic (ars-magica-houses#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the specified casting benefits and immediate ending when a mark is damaged; a world can relax the boundary or parameter requirements, at the cost of making the warding tradition’s special technique less limiting.

rules.statement: When using Ring/Circle Magic, a Columba may mark the perimeter of a well-defined enclosed space or natural boundary and treat it as a Circle; natural boundaries must be traversed at the circle-drawing speed, with a symbol visible from every direction. Alternatively, she can use Warding symbols to target or exclude specified shapes or materials and incorporate an Arcane Connection to improve Penetration against a particular being, but then forgoes the faster drawing and simple boundary-marking benefits.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Minor Hermetic Virtue: Ring/Circle Magic (ars-magica-houses#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the described marking procedures and trade-off; a world can allow simpler or faster boundary marking, at the cost of reducing the effort and precision required to define who or what an effect affects.

rules.statement: Every Columba must visibly mark each spell’s target in a definite way while casting, commonly with a removable chalk symbol. A model, representation, or Arcane Connection can stand in for the target when the caster needs to affect it beyond Touch range.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Major Hermetic Flaw: Necessary Condition (ars-magica-houses#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to requiring a deliberate target mark, with representations or Arcane Connections as substitutes at greater range; a world can permit unmarked casting, at the cost of removing a practical constraint on targeting.

rules.statement: Banishing requires a loud command naming the target realm and area, plus one Fatigue level; omitting or misidentifying the target’s Might source makes the attempt fail. The total is a stress die plus Presence, Banishing, and aura, and the excess over the area’s Ease Factor is Penetration; the Ease Factors are 3 for Near (within 10 paces), 6 for a Structure, and 9 for a Boundary.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: New Virtue: Banishing (ars-magica-houses#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the listed costs, total, and area difficulties; a world can change the Fatigue cost or area thresholds, with greater cost or difficulty representing the strain of expelling more distant or widespread threats.

rules.statement: On a penetrating success, Banishing expels all creatures of the chosen realm from the area for Sun duration, whether or not the user knew they were present. Affected creatures must leave by their quickest means; to return they must pass a Stamina plus the Ability’s originating Realm Lore roll against 12, and their Might is then reduced by half the Banishing score while they remain in the area; leaving restores it.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: New Virtue: Banishing (ars-magica-houses#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to area-wide expulsion for Sun and the stated return test and Might reduction; a world can shorten the duration or make return easier, at the cost of reducing the respite the power provides.

rules.statement: Donatores cannot cast spells on consecrated ground. Banishing aligned with a realm is harder to use against creatures of that same realm, and Divine beings fulfilling God’s plans are immune to its effects.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Favored Virtues and Flaws; New Virtue: Banishing (ars-magica-houses#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the ground restriction and aligned-realm limits; a world can waive either constraint, at the cost of removing religious or metaphysical boundaries on the tradition’s magic.

rules.statement: The rumored rite requires Ease Factor 78, Momentary duration, an individual target, dozens of pawns of vis, several magi, and Wizard’s Communion. Its leader faces Hades in an Underworld-like realm; even success and passing the test do not ensure a genuine return, and it cannot work on someone buried on holy ground or ascended to Heaven.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: The Path of Orpheus (ars-magica-houses#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a costly, uncertain route for retrieving a soul; a world can change the test or exclusions, with vis, coordination, and the risk of a deceiving demon as the price.

rules.statement: Sanguine Humor’s Blessing grants +1 to relevant Ability rolls for a Minor Story Flaw or +3 for a Major one; Hermetic spellcasting bonuses are +3 and +5 respectively. The qualifying Flaw must express a true feeling, only the first qualifying Flaw gained counts, and losing it removes the benefit until another is gained.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Major General Virtue, Sanguine Humor’s Blessing (ars-magica-houses#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to converting an emotional tie into a situational bonus; a world can alter bonus size or eligible ties, while losing the tie removes the benefit.

rules.statement: Adelphixis lets an Orphic magus target people connected to them through an emotional Story Flaw, and counts like an Arcane Connection when calculating spell level. A character with no Virtue or Flaw reflecting a strong emotional bond cannot use magic until such a bond arises again.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Minor Hermetic Virtue: Orphic Magic; Major Hermetic Flaw: Restriction (True Feeling) (ars-magica-houses#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to using emotional relationships as both targeting links and a condition for magic; a world can broaden eligible bonds, while loss of feeling can shut magic off.

rules.statement: Mythic Herbalism concoctions take one day per three Ease Factor points to brew, with +1 Ease Factor per extra dose; a failed Intelligence plus Ability roll makes them useless, and a botch may poison someone. Unused doses expire after one season; physical-bonus potions last for Sun duration and their benefits do not stack, while curatives last a month and only the largest Recovery bonus applies alongside a spell.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Major Supernatural Virtue: Mythic Herbalism (ars-magica-houses#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to making brewed remedies with selected strength and batch size; a world can tune expiry and stacking, while time, ingredients, and failure risk limit production.

rules.statement: A Root-Cutter can reduce the vis required for a healing Ritual by their Mythic Herbalism score, but never by more than half the original cost.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Minor Hermetic Virtue: Root-Cutter (ars-magica-houses#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to converting prepared natural materials into partial ritual-cost savings; a world can change the cap, while the skill score limits the saving.

rules.statement: Comprehend Magic uses Perception, its Ability score, and a stress die against an Ease Factor based on the magic’s source. Success identifies magic; continued study for one, two, and three rounds reveals its type, approximate function, and magnitude, and after three rounds the observer can add twice the Ability score to certain Vim spell Casting Totals against that specific subject.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: New Supernatural Ability: Comprehend Magic (ars-magica-houses#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to staged magical analysis that also improves targeted counter-magic; a world can vary the information or bonus, with observation time and possible resistance penetration as limits.

rules.statement: Opening a hedge wizard’s Arts requires an Intellego Vim Lab Total equal to five times the sum of the wizard’s Supernatural Ability scores. Reaching that level opens the Arts but removes all those Abilities; reaching twice that level can convert some or all into Hermetic Virtues instead, while a lower total fails.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Opening the Arts of a Hedge Wizard (ars-magica-houses#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to making conversion a high-threshold exchange between magical systems; a world can adjust the threshold or conversion choices, with lost native abilities as the cost.

rules.statement: A spell for suppressing a specific kind of magic can affect spells of that type up to its level plus two magnitudes; it can target either the spell or its caster. The listed counter-spells also use comparisons against the foreign spell’s level or the relevant Supernatural Ability score multiplied by five.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: New Spell Guideline; Other Magical Interests (ars-magica-houses#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to type-specific interference rather than universal cancellation; a world can change the power ceiling or eligible magic types, with specialization limiting coverage.

rules.statement: A craft worker can replace the words, gestures, or other actions normally used to produce a power with making an object; completing the object casts the effect when it is brought within range of its target. Making it takes normal craft time and at least as long as a Ritual of that level, requires concentration, allows work on only one object at a time, and still requires a botch check when one would normally be rolled; the object is not magical afterward.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Characters — Major Supernatural Virtue: Craft Magic (ars-magica-houses#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one effect per finished object, with workshop time and concentration as costs; a world can shorten crafting time, but risks making concealed casting too easy.

rules.statement: A craft worker may add one applicable shape, material, design, or inscription bonus to a crafted effect, but the total bonus cannot exceed the relevant Craft score. Elsewhere, designs and inscriptions can augment laboratory objects, with the total bonus capped by Magic Theory or an applicable Craft score.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Characters — Major Supernatural Virtue: Craft Magic; Design and Inscription Bonuses (ars-magica-houses#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to applicable bonuses capped by the craft or Magic Theory score; a world can raise the cap, but then powerful effects depend more heavily on specialized craft skill.

rules.statement: A character can make charged items without spending a season: crafting time is multiplied by the number of items. The Casting Total or Supernatural Ability roll substitutes for a Lab Total to determine effect level and charges; a self-only power can be made usable by others if it requires the item to operate, and a power with no activation roll uses a Craft roll and has base level 5.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Characters — Major Supernatural Virtue: Craft Magic (ars-magica-houses#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to time scaling with each item and to the roll determining charges; a world can ease batch production, but makes portable powers more widely available.

rules.statement: An object containing raw vis can be crafted into a lesser enchanted device without a season. The effect level must be no greater than five times the pawns of vis in the object; for a Supernatural Ability effect the roll need only meet its level, while a spell effect uses the ordinary Lab Total substitution.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Characters — Major Supernatural Virtue: Craft Magic (ars-magica-houses#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to vis physically incorporated in the device and a five-level-per-pawn ceiling; a world can loosen that limit, but makes vis less of a constraint on enchanted goods.

rules.statement: A spell focus contributes one applicable shape-or-material bonus to a spell’s Casting Total, limited by Magic Theory or, for a crafted spell, the relevant Craft score. Only one focus and one property can apply; a spell designed with a focus cannot be cast without that object, and an irrelevant property gives no bonus.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Minor Hermetic Virtue: Spell Foci (ars-magica-houses#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one required focus and one capped bonus; a world can allow foci to be optional, but loses the cost of carrying and protecting the required object.

rules.statement: Rustic magi cannot spend fatigue to strengthen spontaneous magic. Outside seasonal laboratory work, they divide their Casting Score by 5 to determine the Casting Total, making prepared and formulaic effects more dependable than improvised magic.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Major Hermetic Flaw: Weak Spontaneous Magic (ars-magica-houses#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to no fatigue-powered boost and the stated division by 5; a world can permit exertion, but trades the tradition’s preparation constraint for greater flexibility.

rules.statement: A sahir’s summons uses Presence + Sihr + Aura + a stress die against the jinni’s Might, and must penetrate its resistance. Each additional 15 minutes adds +2 to penetration but costs one Fatigue level afterward and adds a botch die; the basic rite takes at least 15 minutes and spends appropriate vis, normally one pawn per Might magnitude, with 1 pawn minimum and the Sihr score as the maximum.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Major Supernatural Virtue: Sihr — Summoning Jinn (ars-magica-houses#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a Might-based threshold, vis expenditure, and a fatigue-for-penetration trade; a world can reduce the vis cost, but makes summoning powerful spirits less resource-intensive.

rules.statement: A successful bargain binds a jinni to the sahir for the agreed duration, but the pact ends if the jinni spends its last Might point in service. Breaking the sahir’s terms ends the pact and makes the jinni an enemy; a sahir may keep at most a number of jinn equal to Leadership, with a minimum capacity of one.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Major Supernatural Virtue: Sihr — Bargaining with the Jinni (ars-magica-houses#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to magically enforced terms, Might expenditure as an early end condition, and Leadership-limited capacity; a world can loosen the capacity, but increases the number of bound spirits one sahir can command.

rules.statement: A Seirene must sing every spell and cannot cast silently; this requirement does not force the spell to have Voice range, and she cannot take Quiet Magic.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Characters (ars-magica-houses#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Require audible singing for all spells; a world can relax the requirement, while keeping it preserves the tradition’s dependence on voice.

rules.statement: To control listeners, roll Communication + Music against each target’s Stamina. A successful command lasts only while the performer continues making music; a new roll is needed to change or issue another command. The target’s resistance bonus is +0 for innocuous commands, +3 for questionable ones, +6 for dangerous ones, +9 for heinous ones, and +12 for suicidal ones.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Siren Song (ars-magica-houses#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Let successful music impose a command while it continues; increase resistance for more harmful orders, with the cost of maintaining the music.

rules.statement: When musicians perform together, at most two assistants can add their Music scores to the singer’s roll, and each assistant’s contribution cannot exceed the singer’s Music score.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Siren Song (ars-magica-houses#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Allow up to two capped helpers; a world can change the group size, balancing greater reach against dependence on coordinated performers.

rules.statement: Siren Song can reinforce an initial command with an emotion created by Enchanting Music, allowing the influence to continue after the music stops. Both rolls must beat the target’s Stamina, and accompanying Seirenes may add their Enchanting Music scores to the leader’s roll.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Siren Song (ars-magica-houses#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Permit the two musical powers to combine only after both succeed; a world can forbid the combination, while the dual success requirement limits persistent control.

rules.statement: A principal can directly manage at most twice Presence plus the higher of Intrigue or Leadership, minus the Gift’s social penalty, with a minimum of one agent. Exceeding this limit causes management problems and stories unless the principal releases agents or hires a factor; player characters are excluded from the count.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Agents are Directly Controlled (ars-magica-houses#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Use the formula as the default management limit; a world can raise or lower capacity, with excess agents bringing complications and lost control.

rules.statement: At character creation, the player has 12 agency points to recruit agents. Each costs the desired Bond Strength plus Resistance Strength, with a minimum cost of 1 and a minimum Bond of +1. During play, agency experience reduces Resistance by its current value per point of reduction; at zero Resistance the person becomes an agent, but needs a Bond of at least +1 before being used.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Recruiting Agents at Character Creation; Recruited Agents as Story Rewards (ars-magica-houses#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Require investment to overcome reluctance and establish a usable Bond; a world can change the points available or recruitment pace, with stronger or more resistant recruits costing more.

rules.statement: An agent can be assigned a task only if the agent has the needed ability and opportunity and has a Bond of at least +1. The principal rolls Communication + Charm, Intrigue, or Leadership, plus Bond Strength and minus the Gift’s social penalty; the task’s difficulty and urgency or risk modify the target.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Using Agents; Tasks for Agents; Modifiers to Persuasion Roll Ease Factors (ars-magica-houses#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Require agreement before an agent undertakes a task; a world can make demands easier or harder, with urgency and personal danger making compliance less likely.

rules.statement: Bond Strength can decline through events, and an agent whose Bond falls below zero stops serving. A principal can raise Bonds through stories and agency experience; money can substitute at 1 Mythic Pound per 5 points or 4 shillings per point, but money alone cannot raise a Bond above +3.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Maintaining Agents (ars-magica-houses#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Make loyalty maintainable through active support or payment, but cap purely purchased loyalty at +3; a world can alter upkeep or exchange rates, with neglected relationships risking departure.

rules.statement: Magical resistance can stop incoming spells: Trianoma and Viea’s incantations and enchanted arrows failed against Bonisagus’s protection. The passage gives no numeric resistance or penetration procedure.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: The Founder Trianoma (ars-magica-houses#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to resistance blocking effects that cannot overcome it; a setting can tune how often it succeeds, with magical safety balanced against attackers’ ability to penetrate it.

rules.statement: A spell that reveals a ghost lets its caster see the ghost if the spell overcomes its magic resistance, but does not make the ghost visible to anyone else. Its listed parameters are personal range, concentration duration, vision target, and level 30.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: New Intellego Mentem Spell — Reveal the Lingering Spirit (ars-magica-houses#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to perception being limited to the caster and dependent on overcoming resistance; a setting can widen who can see the target, at the cost of stronger or longer effects.

rules.statement: A magical staff can perform spontaneous magic and add its magical ability to the wielder’s, producing unusually strong results. No numeric limit or cost is specified.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Story Seed: A Pair in Isolation (ars-magica-houses#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the staff augmenting its wielder while held; a setting can cap the boost or make it consume stored power, because exceptional results need a limiting cost.

rules.statement: The Lancea Magica was described as an attack that bypasses a magus’s Parma Magica and delivers a lethal effect without resistance. The Colentes ordered its destruction, and its inventor burned the Laboratory Texts and promised not to pursue a similar effect.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Story Seed: The Lost Lance (ars-magica-houses#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the attack overcoming magical protection and being lethal; a setting can restrict access or impose a severe cost because the discovery is considered too dangerous to circulate.

rules.statement: Hermetic apprenticeship lasts 15 years, with at least one season of instruction each year; the apprentice must then pass a branch-specific gauntlet. A Bonisagus Theoretical Interview is a day-long oral examination of Magic Theory and the Arts, with a failed candidate repeating a personal interview with their parens until passing.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Magi Bonisagi apprentices / Theoretical Interview (ars-magica-houses#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to 15 years and annual instruction; a world can shorten or lengthen training, trading speed for the depth of magical education.

rules.statement: A Bonisagus magus may take another Hermetic magus’s apprentice, but suggested limits are one such apprentice at a time, no more than one from any one magus, never as a replacement for an unsatisfactory apprentice, and no more often than once every three years. Abuse can bring a low-crime charge or a Wizard War declaration.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Another Magus's Apprentice (ars-magica-houses#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the four suggested limits; a Tribunal can enforce them more or less strictly, with political punishment or violent retaliation as the cost.

rules.statement: A magus may have up to four apprentices while meeting the rule of teaching each one for a season per year, since Arts instruction is one-on-one. Bonisagus magi can also use one more laboratory assistant than normally allowed, including apprentices and familiars.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Multiple Apprentices / Working Together (ars-magica-houses#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to four apprentices and one extra assistant; a world can reduce either capacity, at the cost of fewer teaching or laboratory benefits.

rules.statement: With Continuous Research, each uninterrupted season on one laboratory project adds one point to a running modifier; at five points the modifier is +1 to Lab Total, and after 15 seasons it becomes +2. It continues growing only while the researcher neither changes subject nor interrupts seasonal laboratory work.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Optional Rule: Continuous Research (ars-magica-houses#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to +1 at five seasons and +2 at 15; a world can raise or lower the thresholds, with uninterrupted dedication limiting other activities.

rules.statement: Research made public earns House Acclaim: listed projects award their specified points, while inclusion in a folio doubles those points; reputation normally takes a year per point to spread. Acclaim scores are reached at 5, 15, 30, and 50 total points, corresponding to ranks 1 through 4.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: House Acclaim: Status in House Bonisagus / House Acclaim Points and Score (ars-magica-houses#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the stated point awards and slow reputation; a world can speed or slow recognition, with public disclosure of research as the price.

rules.statement: A Bonisagus magus’s Acclaim score adds to relevant Presence-based social rolls with House members, to rolls resisting Trianomae influence, and to apprentice-finding rolls. On a failed apprentice-finding roll the magus still gets an apprentice from another magus; failure by 5 or more antagonizes that magus, while a botch gives the finder the Major Story Flaw: Enemies.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: House Acclaim Points and Score (ars-magica-houses#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the score bonus and stated failure consequences; a world can narrow which social dealings count, with inter-house resentment as the cost.

rules.statement: Trianomae influence and information-gathering use Presence + Intrigue or Communication + Intrigue, respectively, with Gift penalties of –3 or –6 for Blatant Gift, waived when both parties have Parma Magica protection. Against an active opponent, Intrigue is contested; the winner’s margin determines effects, from identifying allies at 3 points to forcing action against a House’s interests at 15.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Intrigue (Trianomae) (ars-magica-houses#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the stated rolls, penalties, and margin thresholds; a world can make influence easier or harder, with suspicion and the Gift’s social penalty shaping access.

rules.statement: A Trianomae cipher note takes a day to decode: roll Intelligence + Latin + stress die above 6 plus the author’s Communication and Intrigue. Decoding one cipher before adds 3 to later decoding rolls; a Lab Text in the cipher can instead be handled using the ordinary Lab Text translation procedure.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: The Cipher of Trianoma (ars-magica-houses#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the stated threshold and one-day effort; a world can make ciphers more or less difficult, with time and access to an example determining the cost.

rules.statement: A magus can pursue original research without minimum Art or Ability scores; a Minor Breakthrough is usable within existing Hermetic magic, a Major one stretches its theory without breaking its limits, and a Hermetic Breakthrough creates an Arcane Ability or breaks a Lesser Limit. A Breakthrough’s scope and consequences should be agreed with the troupe.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Original Research / Breakthroughs (ars-magica-houses#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the three levels of discovery and group approval; a world can restrict reachable breakthroughs, with major changes to magical practice as the cost.

rules.statement: For original research, choose a risk modifier from +1 to +3: each 5 points or fraction of Magic Theory allows +1, so +2 requires Magic Theory 6 and +3 requires 11. Do not add it to the Lab Total; instead add or subtract up to that modifier from the Extraordinary Results Chart roll to seek a Discovery, and use the same adjustment throughout a multi-season experiment.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Original research (ars-magica-houses#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to allowing the Magic Theory-limited adjustment to seek a Discovery; a world can narrow the permitted adjustments, since pushing for a result means accepting the experiment’s other chart effects.

rules.statement: A Discovery must be followed immediately by stabilization through an exact repeat: use the same number of seasons, Lab Total, risk modifier, and vis, and adjust the chart roll in the same direction. Stabilization succeeds unless the result is Disaster, No Benefit, or Complete Failure; on success, gain points equal to the effect’s magnitude and create a Laboratory Text.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Stabilizing the Unknown (ars-magica-houses#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to requiring the exact repeat and a non-harmful chart result; a world can change which results count as harmful, with the cost being less predictable research.

rules.statement: A stabilized Discovery grants points equal to its magnitude, while stabilization also gives Warping Points equal to the magnitude minus a simple die, whether it succeeds or fails. At 2 or more Warping Points, the researcher must check for Wizard’s Twilight; failed stabilization may be retried in consecutive seasons.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Stabilizing the Unknown (ars-magica-houses#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the magnitude-linked progress and risk; a world can raise or lower Warping exposure, trading safety against the speed of reaching a Breakthrough.

rules.statement: Approximate Breakthrough targets are 30 points for Minor, 45 for Major, and 60 for Hermetic, but the storyguide sets the actual hidden target. Stabilized research texts on the same Breakthrough can contribute points after a season of decoding and study in a Hermetic laboratory; the reader gains points from Lab Total until reaching the experiment’s level, then adds its magnitude, without gaining Warping Points.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Surpassing the Limits; Multiple Laboratory Texts (ars-magica-houses#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a concealed, adjustable target and text-based contributions; a world can set a fixed public target, at the cost of losing uncertainty and storyguide flexibility.

rules.statement: A magus can know as many Parma folds as their Parma Magica score; the first is always the ability to extend protection to another. A fold generally takes two minutes and lasts until sunrise or sunset, cannot normally be switched while active, and modifies the Parma score before it is multiplied by 5 for resistance; reductions round up and cannot take the score below 0.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Arma Magica — Parma Magica Folds (ars-magica-houses#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a fixed fold for each ritual and a capacity based on Parma score; a world can allow fold switching, at the cost of weakening the commitment to a chosen defense.

rules.statement: A Parmula is a lesser enchanted object that grants its wearer Magic Resistance 30, but lasts only one year and cannot be made to provide a different resistance level. Its effect has level 44, takes a season to create, and costs five pawns of Rego or Vim vis.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Parmulae (ars-magica-houses#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the fixed 30 resistance and one-year lifespan; a world can permit stronger or longer-lasting versions, requiring a further breakthrough.

rules.statement: Figurines are made for a specific recipient and can hold Hermetic spells or eligible Minor Virtues; spells must have Touch range, Individual target, and Sun duration. Wax takes a month and holds magic for six months, while wood takes two months and holds it for a year; damage ends the magic immediately, and figurine effects have zero Penetration.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Figurine Magic (ars-magica-houses#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to recipient-specific, temporary figures whose magic ends on damage; a world can extend duration or broaden eligibility, paying with more time or research.

rules.statement: A realm-aligned spell is invented with Magic Theory limited to the caster’s relevant Realm Lore score, reducing the Lab Total. In its aligned realm it avoids that realm’s ordinary influence and reduces botch dice by the relevant Lore score; its interaction with other auras follows the special realm-aligned table.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Realm-Aligned Spells (ars-magica-houses#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to alignment with Magic, Faerie, or Infernal realms and Lore-based botch reduction; a world can permit Divine alignment, which would alter the stated limit.

rules.statement: A magus normally has legal protection against attacks, but protection is lost in a degree proportionate to committing, preparing, or recently having committed a crime; another magus may then act against them, but the response must be proportionate.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Forfeit Immunity (ars-magica-houses#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to partial, proportionate loss of legal protection; a world can broaden or narrow the circumstances because Tribunals judge the conduct and response.
