rules.statement: A declared Wizard War gives the recipient one lunar month to prepare, followed by one lunar month of open conflict. During the war, the combatants may attack each other’s lives and property without prosecution, but collateral harm to others can forfeit protection, and shared property is not a legal target.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Wizard War (ars-magica-houses#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the two one-month periods and immunity only between the combatants; a world can change declaration procedures or the scope of immunity, at the cost of legal certainty.

rules.statement: A high crime allows the prosecution to request a Wizard’s March; a Tribunal still chooses an appropriate penalty, and a magus who refuses to obey a Tribunal’s punishment can be charged with a high crime. Lesser offenses do not by themselves permit a March.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: High and Low Crimes (ars-magica-houses#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to March being available only for listed high crimes; a world can change the offense list or penalties, risking inconsistent judgments.

rules.statement: A regional Tribunal’s rulings ordinarily bind its residents and visitors, while First and Grand Tribunal rulings can apply throughout the Order. A regional Tribunal may revise its own earlier rulings but cannot contradict higher Tribunal rulings.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Abide by Tribunal Decisions (ars-magica-houses#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to hierarchical, territorially limited rulings; a world can give local Tribunals more latitude, at the cost of uniformity.

rules.statement: A Quaesitor who kills another magus outside Wizard War must face Tribunal judgment. Being inside a magus’s sanctum automatically removes legal protection against that sanctum’s owner, though a lethal response to a minor provocation is not justified merely by that provocation.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Slaying (ars-magica-houses#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to mandatory review of a killing and a sanctum-based exception to immunity; a world can broaden or narrow that exception, trading security for protection against abuse.

rules.statement: For two hours before sunrise on Good Friday, a strong Divine aura covers Magvillus and suppresses its Aegis of the Hearth. The loss of that defense is confined to this interval and place.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: The Imperfect Defense (ars-magica-houses#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a predictable two-hour annual gap in the fortress defense; a world can change its duration or remove it, for religious or tactical reasons.

rules.statement: An enchanted council device can transport an outer-council member and companions to the reception house, signal that a meeting is called, and destroy itself; the Primus can remotely trigger the signal and destruction. The device also serves as a casting token for Magvillus’s Aegis.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: The Magvillus Council (ars-magica-houses#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a device with transport, alert, and remote self-destruction effects; a world can limit its range or access to protect the fortress and its council.

rules.statement: A magus’s magical power includes their ability to use, practice, or study magic, as well as protected magical property such as vis, sites, devices, familiars, apprentices, books, and laboratory equipment. Deliberately harming these interests is illegal, while attacks on mundane covenant resources are generally treated less severely.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Deprivation of Magical Power (ars-magica-houses#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to broad protection for magical capacity and assets, with lesser treatment for mundane resources; a world can expand or contract the protected interests, affecting what counts as a serious offense.

rules.statement: A magus may give an attending magus their sigil to vote as a proxy at the owner’s residential Tribunal or the Grand Tribunal. A directed proxy must follow the owner’s instructions; disregarding them is a high crime, while an owner using a free proxy may disown unwanted decisions, relieving the owner of legal responsibility but insulting the proxy.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Proxy Voting (ars-magica-houses#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to allowing instructed or freely delegated votes only at the two authorized Tribunals; a world can tighten proxy rules to prevent accumulated votes, because misuse threatens the legitimacy of decisions.

rules.statement: A magus who loses or renounces House membership has one year to join another House; after that, they may be charged with low-crime vagrancy and ordered to find a House before the next Tribunal. Ignoring that judgment is a high crime that can lead to a Wizard’s March.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Vagrancy (ars-magica-houses#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a one-year period to secure House membership; a world can shorten it or ease admission, because House affiliation is the Order’s legal means of belonging.

rules.statement: A magus must have one residential Tribunal. If found delinquent under that Tribunal’s residency requirements, they have seven years to comply or change Tribunals before they can be charged with vagrancy; residency may be changed by appearing before the Presiding Quaesitor, who must be satisfied the move is genuine.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Voting Rights (ars-magica-houses#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one official residence and a seven-year cure period; a world can make residency stricter or looser, because reliable notice of cases is needed.

rules.statement: Knowingly agreeing with an infernal agent is forbidden, even if the agreement seems harmless or is only to avoid contact; conviction will almost certainly bring a Wizard’s March. Ignorance that the creature was a demon is the only stated possible defense.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Deals with Devils (ars-magica-houses#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to treating any knowing agreement with a demon as a severe offense; a world can vary the penalty, because infernal bargains are considered a danger to the Order.

rules.statement: To establish an offense for molesting the fay, prosecution must show that other magi were endangered, using an actual attack as evidence or otherwise showing an attack was likely. Reasonable defense of life or property is a defense, while culpable provocation can support conviction.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Molesting the Fay (ars-magica-houses#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to requiring a credible threat to other magi and allowing reasonable self-defense; a world can lower the evidence threshold, because retaliation may spread danger beyond the original dispute.

rules.statement: Magic used to spy into another magus’s legal affairs is an offense, and penalties depend on harm done or intended. Reasonable effects within a covenant may detect magical spying, but should not significantly or deliberately invade visitors’ privacy; unintentionally catching a Redcap can still lead to damages if secrets were revealed.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Scrying (ars-magica-houses#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to permitting detection of magical spying while protecting visitors from deliberate intrusion; a world can broaden privacy protections, because Redcaps and covenants handle sensitive information.

rules.statement: Certamen cannot legally be used to defy a Tribunal judgment, force a magus to break the Code, or ignore a Code violation. A mutually accepted challenge cannot be appealed to a Tribunal; a challenge over a genuinely disputed, non-criminal matter may be enforced if the Tribunal upholds its legality.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: The Legality of Certamen (ars-magica-houses#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to barring magical duels from overriding legal protections while allowing them to settle genuine non-criminal disputes; a world can narrow that scope, because dueling must not replace Tribunal justice.

rules.statement: A proposal for a new Tribunal ruling must be published at least two years before the meeting by sending it to the Tribunal’s covenants. The Tribunal may adopt it, but traditionalists require rulings to clarify, expand, or embellish the Oath rather than create wholly new provisions.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Proposal Rulings (ars-magica-houses#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to two years’ notice and a requirement that rulings relate to the Oath; a world can permit shorter notice or broader lawmaking, because debate and prior notice support orderly decisions.

rules.statement: A witness may request a Quaesitor’s magical verification; the witness must lower Parma and dispel other spell or item effects, and the Quaesitor first checks for magic that could manipulate the verification. A senior or peer Quaesitor then uses truth-testing magic and questions the witness; endorsement normally prevails in a perjury case, but infernal aid can defeat it.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Endorsing Testimony (ars-magica-houses#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to treating an endorsed account as true after the witness drops protections; a world can make verification less conclusive, with infernal interference as the reason.

rules.statement: No magus can be compelled to undergo truth-detection. If one side’s testimony is endorsed, that side normally wins the perjury case; if neither side submits, the Tribunal judges the evidence, while two verified opposing accounts trigger suspicion of infernal involvement and suspend related cases for investigation.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Passage 22 (ars-magica-houses#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to voluntary testing and the stated case outcomes; a world can change the evidentiary weight, with mistrust or infernal deception as the cost.

rules.statement: Conflicting indirect testimony can only be resolved by Quaesitorial investigation, which normally delays the case until the next Tribunal so absent witnesses can be interviewed.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Passage 22 (ars-magica-houses#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to requiring investigation and a Tribunal delay; a world can allow faster resolution, at the cost of weaker evidence.

rules.statement: For a Wizard’s March, a victim normally receives one quarter of the outcast’s estate as damages; the prosecutor receives one quarter, or one half if also the victim, and the remaining half goes to the inheritor. Tribunal coffers receive no share from calling the March.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Penalties — Damages; Fines (ars-magica-houses#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the stated estate shares; a world can alter the distribution, with reduced compensation or inheritance as the consequence.

rules.statement: A convicted magus may accept a penalty, negotiate different terms, or refuse it; if no settlement is reached, the default is a Wizard’s March. Refusing a lesser penalty three times causes the Quaesitor to declare the magus Marched.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Penalties — Determining Penalties (ars-magica-houses#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to negotiation followed by a March if unresolved; a world can offer more chances, with prolonged enforcement and risk to victims as the cost.

rules.statement: Damages, fines, or services should normally be completed by the next Tribunal, and apprentice surrender is immediate. Failure to comply is a high crime; unforeseen inability to pay can earn an extension, though the fine may increase.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Penalties — Determining Penalties (ars-magica-houses#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to next-Tribunal completion and immediate apprentice surrender; a world can grant more time, at the cost of increased fines.

rules.statement: Cutting the cords between a magus and familiar causes extreme pain and lasting emotional harm to both; afterward they cannot bear each other’s presence, the familiar usually flees, and they normally cannot be bonded again. The Quaesitor’s ritual requires the convicted magus to provide the vis, or the separation can be done in a season of laboratory work and checked at the next Tribunal.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Punishments — Loss of Familiar (ars-magica-houses#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to permanent, painful separation with vis or a season of work as the cost; a world can permit recovery or rebonding, weakening the punishment.

rules.statement: Investigation immunity permits a Quaesitor to use reasonable magical inquiry during a justified investigation, including entry into a suspect’s sanctum; it does not authorize Mentem magic on magi or their servants without permission. Inside the sanctum the investigator and agents have forfeited immunity, which returns upon leaving.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Investigation Immunity; Sanctum Invasions (ars-magica-houses#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to limited investigative immunity with Mentem and sanctum exceptions; a world can broaden the protection, at the cost of exposing private secrets.

rules.statement: A Presiding Quaesitor may veto a ruling only for a clear, direct conflict with the Code or a higher-Tribunal ruling, or to prevent a miscarriage of justice; the legality judgment calls for an Int + Code of Hermes result of 6 or more. Advisers are consulted, and a veto can be reviewed or appealed.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: The Presiding Quaesitor; The Veto (ars-magica-houses#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a narrow veto requiring the stated result and review; a world can widen the veto, risking abuse and loss of Quaesitorial authority.

rules.statement: A Quaesitor may grant a non-Quaesitor a letter that provides investigation immunity and lets the recipient demand cooperation; when events prevent advance approval, the authority may be granted afterward, usually for a successful investigation.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Opening section (ars-magica-houses#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: written authority grants limited investigative privileges; a world can broaden or narrow them, with misuse risking legal consequences.

rules.statement: A sanctum mark on a text protects it from unwelcome readers even outside the sanctum, and reading it is a low crime. A House symbol likewise marks a book or scroll-case as secret to the House; another magus who reads it commits a low crime.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Sanctum Law (ars-magica-houses#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: marked writing is legally restricted rather than physically inaccessible; a world can make marks detectable or enforce stronger penalties, at the cost of access to knowledge.

rules.statement: A Quaesitor-trained magus can use Acute Sense with enhanced magical sense spells to notice altered, hidden, or destroyed magical traces. Detection succeeds on Perception + Penetration + a stress die against 6 plus the responsible creature's Might magnitude or Hermetic spell magnitude; taking the ability twice adds Mastery to the roll.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Acute Sense (ars-magica-houses#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: trained investigators can notice deceptive traces but must beat a magnitude-based threshold; a world can make detection more reliable or subtler, balanced by training and specialized senses.

rules.statement: When magic ends, its trace's magnitude is halved, then falls by one each time the spell's duration passes; Momentary traces fall each round. Once at zero, non-ritual Momentary, Concentration, and Diameter traces decay monthly, while other traces decay yearly; traces disappear at magnitude –10.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Spell Traces and Sigils (ars-magica-houses#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: evidence fades at a duration-linked then calendar-based rate; a world can speed or slow that loss, changing how long investigators have before the evidence is gone.

rules.statement: A trace examined with an appropriate Intellego Vim effect reveals its caster's distinctive sigil. If magic expires under Shroud Magic, its trace instead bears a false sigil, and no known Hermetic method can reveal the true one; each Shroud Magic design produces a fixed alternative.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Spell Traces and Sigils — Shroud Magic (ars-magica-houses#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: traces identify their caster unless specifically masked; a world can make masking harder or allow countermeasures, at the cost of leaving evidence of the masking magic.

rules.statement: Forceless casting limits a spell's Penetration to 0 without requiring special skill or effort. It will not affect most magi whose Magic Resistance is at least 0 unless the caster botches, but can still affect Redcaps, companions, or grogs and cause legal trouble.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Forceless Casting (ars-magica-houses#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a caster may avoid penetrating magi's resistance while still risking effects on unprotected people; a world can make this safeguard stricter or looser, with botches and collateral harm remaining costly.

rules.statement: Fenicil's rituals require a group to prepare Wizard's Vigil spells whose combined magnitude equals the ritual's Ease Factor. The leader rolls Stamina + participants' summed Ability scores + aura modifier + die; failure to meet the Ease Factor fails the ritual, and an unstressed, undisrupted casting has no botch dice. Each ritual costs vis equal to its Ease Factor, though up to half may be replaced by prepared materials costing one pound of silver per pawn.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Fenicil's Rituals (ars-magica-houses#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: powerful effects demand coordinated casters, preparation, time, and costly materials; a world can adjust group size or costs, trading accessibility against the risk of failure and resource depletion.

rules.statement: Mercere Portals link fixed places and are restricted to House members and magi serving the Order; a guardian may admit other travelers who seem harmless and pay one pawn of vis. The House's known method works only for Portal devices, not portable storage or other linked-place items.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Mercere's Portals (ars-magica-houses#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: authorized travelers can move between linked Portal sites, while outsiders need permission and pay one pawn of vis; a world can widen access or add destinations, at the cost of security.

rules.statement: Mercere's House may admit unGifted followers as members with the Oath's rights and duties; they must swear the Oath and serve the Order. This is a special privilege of that House, not a general permission for other Houses to admit unGifted members.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: “Redcaps” and “Merceres” (ars-magica-houses#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to allowing only Mercere this exception; a world can broaden or revoke it, at the cost of changing who may join the Order.

rules.statement: A covenant registers by giving directions to a nearby Mercer House, accompanying a Redcap to verify the route, and signing a promise to shelter any Order member who requests it for at least three days each year. Redcaps keep covenant addresses rather than lists of individual magi, and undertake to visit each registered address at least once before Tribunal.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Messengers and Heralds (ars-magica-houses#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to registration carrying a three-day annual hospitality obligation; a world can remove or lengthen the stay, with less reliable access to Redcap visits as the likely cost.

rules.statement: Messages between covenants usually arrive within a year, or within a season for nearby destinations. Messages for another Tribunal are commonly routed through Harco using the Mercere's Portals.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Messengers and Heralds (ars-magica-houses#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to delivery on the stated seasonal or yearly scale; a world can make routes faster or less dependable, trading convenience against distance, danger, or network access.

rules.statement: Redcaps commonly exchange one unit of vis for two, with one pawn of Technique-associated vis valued like two pawns of Form-associated vis. The listed rates include 1 pawn of Technique vis for 1 pawn of Form vis, 2 pawns of Form vis for 1 pawn of Form vis, 2 pawns of Technique vis for 1 pawn of Technique vis, and 4 pawns of Form vis for 1 pawn of Technique vis; local supply and demand can alter the rates.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Merchants and Bankers — Vis Notation (ars-magica-houses#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the stated exchange schedule; a world can vary prices by region and demand, making access to particular vis types costly or advantageous.

rules.statement: A customary vis loan charges and pays 20% interest per year, with repayment currency fixed when the loan is made; a typical magus can borrow up to 10 pawns. A lien instead grants the lender a vis source's yield until repayment, with the loan usually set at 20% of that source's annual yield as principal—for example, a source yielding 4 pawns yearly can support a 20-pawn loan.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Merchants and Bankers (ars-magica-houses#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to 20% yearly interest or a lien priced from source yield; a world can raise rates or collateral demands, at the cost of greater debt and risk for borrowers.

rules.statement: A Redcap who pawns a magic item receives about half its assessed value and normally has a year to buy it back at that price. Until redemption, the Redcap may use the item; if the deadline passes, ownership transfers to the Redcap.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Merchants and Bankers (ars-magica-houses#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a one-year redemption window and a loan of half the item's value; a world can shorten the window or change the advance, increasing the chance of losing a useful device.

rules.statement: A custodian guarding a Mercere's Portal checks travelers, opens it for those permitted to pass, and may destroy it if danger is imminent. The guard may collect one pawn of vis per use, keep 10% of tolls, and decide whether to charge; Redcaps and other magi serving the Order traditionally pass free.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Mercenaries and Guardians (ars-magica-houses#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a guarded, selectively opened portal with an optional toll; a world can require tolls or deny access more strictly, trading convenience for security and revenue.

rules.statement: In the Stonehenge Tribunal, no covenant may circulate more than two pounds of magically created silver per resident per year. This restriction was adopted after magical silver caused inflation and halved silver's value over a few decades.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Merchants and Bankers — Magical Silver (ars-magica-houses#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the two-pound annual cap in Stonehenge; a world can change the cap or apply it elsewhere, balancing magical wealth against economic disruption.

rules.statement: A Redcap depositing vis into the Mercer House treasury is credited with 10% of the amount, while Redcaps generally carry no more than about 10 pawns at once. A Redcap's ordinary running allowance grows by about 1 pawn each year; other legitimate vis may be added, and withdrawals are permitted.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Merchants and Bankers (ars-magica-houses#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a 10% delivery credit and roughly 1 pawn of yearly allowance; a world can adjust the credit or carry limit, changing incentives and the risk of loss.

rules.statement: A Bloodcap with the greater malediction loses teeth and nails when exposed to a cross or scripture, taking a light wound each round. With the lesser malediction, either stimulus causes pain and stressful actions require a concentration roll of 9+.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Societas Merceris: the Bloodcaps — Requirements (ars-magica-houses#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the greater version for a severe, escalating vulnerability; a world can turn the dial to the lesser version, trading physical injury for impaired concentration.

rules.statement: Redcaps who report to their Tribunal’s senior Redcap and perform their duties can receive magic items and longevity potions; those who do not keep in touch lose peer respect and these rewards. A missed season or two can be made up the following year, and excused circumstances or other major service may mean no penalty.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Errant Redcaps (ars-magica-houses#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to rewards and informal penalties rather than compulsory service; a world can make reporting stricter, with the risk of House sanctions for persistent neglect.

rules.statement: For continual, deliberate neglect of responsibilities, a senior Redcap may seek a warning from the Mercere Primus; the final sanction is expulsion from the House. If the expelled Redcap is not accepted back within a year, the result is formal expulsion from the Order.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Errant Redcaps (ars-magica-houses#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to escalating warnings before expulsion; a world can shorten the process, making loss of House and Order membership the cost of disobedience.

rules.statement: Mercere magi may borrow up to 10 pawns of vis from the House without interest, exchange vis without an extra fee, and pass through Mercere’s Portals for free. They receive priority for item and longevity-potion commissions and purchases, and Redcaps generally help them even when doing so displaces other duties.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Magical Merceres (ars-magica-houses#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to House privileges with a 10-pawn interest-free borrowing ceiling; a world can reduce access or raise the cost to reflect scarce House resources.

rules.statement: Every Mercere magus spends at least one season in every seven traveling and carrying messages like a Redcap, as a practice meant to maintain humility and perspective.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Magical Merceres (ars-magica-houses#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one service season per seven-year cycle; a world can increase the required service, at the cost of laboratory or other personal work.

rules.statement: A Mutante may spend one pawn of vis per increase to raise a spell’s Range, Duration, Target, or size by one magnitude, and may apply several such increases. The spell’s casting success, fatigue loss, and penetration remain based on its original level, but each pawn adds one botch die; parameters cannot be reduced, and Formulaic magic limits still apply unless the spell is a Ritual.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Mutantes — Boosting (ars-magica-houses#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one magnitude of enhancement per pawn, with one added botch die each time; a world can raise the vis price or botch risk to curb amplified effects.

rules.statement: A caster may end a harnessed spell before its duration expires by concentrating on it, wherever the caster is; this takes roughly the time and concentration of casting the spell. If distracted, the caster can try again.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Mutantes — Harnessing (ars-magica-houses#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to caster-controlled early termination at a casting-like concentration cost; a world can make distraction harder to recover from or restrict the distance.

rules.statement: A tethered effect can pass its control to a person within the caster’s range, who then treats it as the caster, or can be attached to an object that triggers it automatically when a suitable target comes into range. The tether lasts only as long as the spell and cannot be used with Ritual spells.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Mutantes — Tethering (ars-magica-houses#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to temporary delegation or an object-triggered effect; a world can restrict eligible recipients or triggers, while duration and the Ritual exclusion limit use.

rules.statement: Adaptive Casting lets a magus apply a mastered spell’s mastery score and special abilities to a similar spell. If multiple mastered spells qualify, the caster must choose one mastery and use only its score and associated abilities for that casting.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Laboratory Rules — Mastered Spell Special Abilities: Adaptive Casting (ars-magica-houses#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one applicable mastery package per casting; a world can broaden which spells count as similar, risking more powerful combinations.

rules.statement: For an effect designed to accept boosting, spending one pawn of vis raises its Range, Duration, Target, or size by one magnitude; each pawn adds one botch die. Casting success, Fatigue loss, and Penetration use the effect’s original level, and parameters cannot be reduced or pushed beyond the limits of Formulaic magic unless the effect is already a Ritual.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Mutantum Magic — Boosting (ars-magica-houses#025)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to allowing one-magnitude increases per pawn; worlds can tighten the permitted parameters, since feeding vis makes magic larger but increases botch risk.

rules.statement: A harnessed effect can be ended early by its caster concentrating for roughly the time and effort of casting; this can be done over any distance, and a distracted caster may try again. A Harnessed Magic user can also cancel effects in items they created, but when that user dies, their spells and magic items cease to function.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Mutantum Magic — Harnessing; Virtues — Harnessed Magic (ars-magica-houses#025)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to allowing remote cancellation after casting-like concentration; worlds can make the cancellation harder, while the user’s death may end their maintained magic.

rules.statement: A tether lets its caster hand control of an effect to a person within range, who then acts as caster, or attach it to an object that casts it when a suitable target comes into range. The tether lasts only as long as the effect, and Ritual spells cannot be tethered; Tethered Magic also makes the user’s spells and activated item effects arcane connections to them.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Mutantum Magic — Tethering; Virtues — Tethered Magic (ars-magica-houses#025)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to transferring control or triggering an effect through a tether; worlds can restrict eligible recipients or triggers, while the tether’s duration and personal arcane connection constrain use.

rules.statement: Mercere’s Portals are paired invested archways, each requiring a Rego Terram effect of level 65, including unlimited uses. Each archway must contain an arcane connection to the other; the pair only works after a simultaneous connecting ceremony, and moving either portal thereafter permanently destroys the effect.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Mercere’s Portals (ars-magica-houses#025)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to fixed, paired gateways activated by a linking ceremony; worlds can restrict who may activate them with passwords or House-linked triggers, and relocation destroys the connection.

rules.statement: Stalwart Casting halves the Fatigue levels lost for a Ritual, rounding up and imposing a minimum loss of one, and substitutes normal Fatigue for long-term Fatigue. For a Formulaic spell, it prevents Fatigue loss caused by a low casting total, even when the spell fails.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Stalwart Casting (ars-magica-houses#025)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to reducing casting exhaustion as specified; worlds can narrow the benefit to one spell type, since the rule trades ordinary fatigue costs for greater endurance.

rules.statement: A harnessed effect can be ended early by concentrating, and the caster can try again later if distracted. A target controlling a harnessed and tethered effect can end it at will; the effect otherwise follows its stated duration.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Mutantum Spells — Harnessed; Mutantum Magic — Harnessing (ars-magica-houses#025)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to allowing the designated controller to end the effect early; worlds can limit who controls it, with concentration and duration setting the cost.

rules.statement: The two Cult of Heroes physical-characteristic rituals each permanently add 1 to a chosen physical Characteristic: the Followers version cannot raise it above 0, while the Heroes version cannot raise it above +5. Their mental-characteristic counterparts have the same limits for a chosen mental Characteristic.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Other Spells — Creo Corpus and Creo Mentem Spells (ars-magica-houses#025)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to permanent improvement by one up to the stated cap; worlds can change the cap, since these are powerful Ritual benefits.

rules.statement: Invisible to Magic can prevent magical detection and direct-target spells from affecting the user, but does not stop area effects. For each spell each round, the user rolls Stamina plus Concentration against an Ease Factor of 3 plus three times the spell’s magnitude; other actions require additional Concentration rolls.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Virtues — Invisible to Magic (ars-magica-houses#025)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to blocking detection and direct targeting while concentration succeeds; worlds can adjust the roll difficulty, but area effects remain a bypass.

rules.statement: The House provides material support according to rank: a young magus may have one listed aid at a time, and changing it takes a full season outside a House covenant; skilled magi may hold two support types, and experienced magi three. Seniority expands the kinds and amounts available, while the supply is limited and higher-priority members may take precedence.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: The Role of Young Magi; The Role of Skilled Magi; The Role of Experienced Magi (ars-magica-houses#026)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default aid to rank-based slots and seasonal changes; turn generosity and availability up or down; scarce House resources and competing priorities are the cost.

rules.statement: Young Tremere magi generally spend a season each year on House work, with less time lost if duties are completed quickly. In a crisis they are expected to muster; a magus who knowingly fails to answer the call is hunted by fellow Tremere.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: The Role of Young Magi (ars-magica-houses#026)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default one season of service per year and mandatory crisis muster; vary the workload and enforcement; time, obedience, and the risk of pursuit are the costs.

rules.statement: An experienced magus can use three support choices without repaying money or vis, but must show a sustained record of success to justify the expense. A support slot spent on a House gift can be recovered by returning equal-value goods or after superiors judge the service repaid.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: The Role of Experienced Magi (ars-magica-houses#026)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default three accountable support slots; vary the number and repayment standard; successful service or equivalent goods justify continued access.

rules.statement: A young magus may challenge once for a returned sigil, then may challenge again at each Decennial; winning gives the magus their own sigil and experienced-mag us standing for aid, though assigned work is usually suited to their abilities. A magus who holds a sigil may vote independently on matters the House leadership classifies as trivial.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Claiming the Sigil, to Move to the Role of Experienced Magus by Force (ars-magica-houses#026)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default one initial challenge and later chances every ten years; change the timing or the privileges; advancement risks disrupting House command and projects.

rules.statement: A Tremere apprentice can win the title of magus through the Gauntlet duel and then claim their sigil immediately; if they lose, they receive a new name instead. The most senior Tremere present decides whether the apprentice graduates.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Claiming the Name, to Move to the Role of Magus by Force (ars-magica-houses#026)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default a witnessed duel with senior approval; turn the challenge’s accessibility or oversight up or down; failure delays advancement and may change the apprentice’s name.

rules.statement: When dueling other Tremere, using vis is considered dishonorable. A sigil challenge may be made once at the magus’s chosen time, then only at Decennial meetings; a successful challenger is usually given their talisman as their sigil.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Promotion by Force; Claiming the Sigil, to Move to the Role of Experienced Magus by Force (ars-magica-houses#026)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default forbid vis in intra-House duels and restrict repeat challenges to ten-year meetings; a world can relax either restriction; reputation and access to advancement are at stake.

rules.statement: The Primus appoints a successor and rules for life; exarchs oversee House operations across one or more Tribunals. The Primus’s council of sigil-holding magi meets every ten years, but has lacked formal authority since the Schism.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Structure (ars-magica-houses#026)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default lifetime leadership with appointed succession and a decade-based advisory council; turn council authority or succession rules; central control trades local autonomy for coordination.

rules.statement: At Coeris, the Gate of Eurydice is said to lead toward the underworld, but using it causes Warping; many Tremere instead regard it as a regio reflecting a quester’s own thoughts and dreams. Its visions may encourage self-absorption and detachment from reality.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Coeris (ars-magica-houses#026)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default the Gate to dream-reflecting visions with Warping as the price of use; make the underworld access more literal or the visions more reliable; the cost is magical distortion and potential detachment.

rules.statement: A single ritual restored sight to more than a thousand blinded Bulgars. The eyes that grew were amber, matching the caster’s sigil, and this trait can be inherited by descendants; Warping deepens the color.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Amber Eyes (ars-magica-houses#026)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default mass restoration also leaves a hereditary, caster-marked trait; alter inheritance or the Warping link; magical healing carries a lasting visible consequence.

rules.statement: A Tremere magus may challenge an exarch to certamen over House policy or the office, but can challenge for the office only once and not while the House faces outside rivals. A defeated exarch cannot challenge again and must assist the successor.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Claiming the Sigil of Tremere (preceding Dissent) (ars-magica-houses#027)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one office challenge and a required handover; a world could relax either limit, at the cost of greater House instability.

rules.statement: During dissent, the exarch can disregard the Primus while publicly acting as though she obeys. The Primus’s support to dissenters and dissenters’ manpower and items to loyalists are lost; both sides temporarily set aside their conflict when facing enemies.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Dissent (ars-magica-houses#027)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to reciprocal loss of aid and a temporary truce against external threats; a world could make support continue or the truce fail, risking weakened factions.

rules.statement: When the Primus dies or retires, his legatus takes the office and chooses a replacement legatus. At each Decennial, consiliari duel for the right to assess the Primus; the victor may challenge him until the next Decennial, and other magi can qualify by defeating that victor in certamen.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Claiming the Sigil of Tremere, to Move to the Pole of Primus by Force (ars-magica-houses#027)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to succession through the legatus and a Decennial challenge cycle; a world could change the succession or challenge window, with consequences for leadership legitimacy.

rules.statement: A certamen follower of a school can use that school’s strongest techniques but cannot switch schools during the duel. A duelist using varied styles may switch at the beginning of a round, before attack and defense, but cannot use any school’s strongest techniques.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Styles of Certamen (ars-magica-houses#027)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a choice between depth and flexibility; a world could permit switching with full techniques, at the cost of making specialist training less distinctive.

rules.statement: A Tremere magus has a Minor Magical Focus in Certamen, improving dueling specialization but leaving them less powerful, age for age, than comparably focused magi in other areas.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Virtues and Flaws (ars-magica-houses#027)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a certamen-specific advantage paired with a broader opportunity cost; a world could reduce the cost, making Tremere duelists stronger outside their specialty.

rules.statement: A Wili’s gaze can make a young man forget warnings about her; an Intelligence roll of 9 or more lets him recall the warning. After he kisses her, he remains compelled to seek another meeting unless he succeeds at an Intelligence roll of 9 or more; friends can end this charm with a priest’s help.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Wili — Powers (ars-magica-houses#027)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a difficult but possible resistance and priest-assisted release; a world could alter the roll or remove outside help, increasing or reducing the victim’s vulnerability.

rules.statement: A Wili that kisses a willing or gaze-compliant victim permanently takes one fatigue level and restores all its Might points. It can feed on a given victim only once per day; a pack can kill through repeated kisses in one round.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Wili — Powers (ars-magica-houses#027)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to permanent fatigue loss exchanged for a full Might refill, limited to once daily per Wili; a world could make the loss temporary, reducing the danger and the creature’s gain.

rules.statement: A Moro can change between infant and death’s-head-moth forms at will. In moth form, it can bite a sleeping victim to take one fatigue level for a week and restore its Might; it feeds on a victim at most once per day, and repeated feeding can kill an adult over a week.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Moro — Powers (ars-magica-houses#027)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to at-will form change and once-daily feeding with week-long fatigue loss; a world could shorten the loss, reducing the risk of cumulative death.

rules.statement: In certamen, a specialist may trade attack, defense, initiative, or resistance for another combat advantage; the exchange is bounded by the relevant Finesse score unless the technique says otherwise. Some techniques require foregoing damage or an attack, and their benefits may last one or several rounds.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Andabatus–Velitus (ars-magica-houses#028)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to allowing only the stated score-bounded exchanges; a setting can make them broader or narrower to represent how specialized and costly its duel traditions are.

rules.statement: A successful strike can instead impose a lasting or temporary disadvantage: a laquerius can reduce an opponent’s Defense for the rest of the duel by the penalty accepted that round, while a velitus can lower Resistance by half its Finesse, rounded down. The generalist-style versions last one round for the Defense reduction and cap the Resistance reduction at Finesse divided by three, rounded down, with Resistance never below zero.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Laquerius; Velitus (ars-magica-houses#028)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the duration and score-based caps described; a world can shorten or strengthen these weakening effects, with duel balance as the cost.

rules.statement: An essedarius or Pumilius can turn a successful attack into a psychological effect instead of damage. The target risks surrender or losing an action if they fail the specified check; the essedarius’s target number depends on fatigue the attacker has forgone, while Pumilius uses a target of 12 modified by personality and research, or 9 for a less potent generalist imitation.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Essedarius; Pumilius (ars-magica-houses#028)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to requiring a failed check and giving up damage; a world can make the effect easier or harder by changing the target numbers and the social plausibility of the illusion.

rules.statement: A Charon trick requires a silent, gestureless spell to be prepared with an Intelligence + Concentration result of 15 or more, then maintained with a result of 12 or more each round until the predicted final round. If the prediction is right, the prepared spell follows the duel’s arcane connection, as does a spell cast after the duel ends.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Charon (ars-magica-houses#028)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the stated preparation and upkeep checks; a world can forbid or permit this exploit, with legal and reputational consequences as its cost.

rules.statement: For initiation, the Mystagogue’s total is Presence + House Lore + Script bonus, with no die roll. Targets are 15 for a known Minor Virtue, 21 for a known Major, 18 for a new Minor, and 30 for a new Major; prior ordeals can lower the target over three later initiations, but never below 9.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Introduction: The Mechanics of Initiation (ars-magica-houses#028)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to automatic success when the total meets the target; a setting can alter target levels or ordeal discounts to tune access to its Mysteries and the price of advancement.

rules.statement: An Initiation Script grants its listed bonus only when followed as written and can require an ordeal, quest, or sacrifice. A Mystagogue can add a Script component on an Ease Factor of 9 or change one on 12, but cannot change which Virtue the Script grants; that needs a different Script.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: The Initiation Script; Varying a Script (ars-magica-houses#028)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to enforcing the Script’s stated components and costs; a world can allow more flexible changes, balanced by greater difficulty or a more demanding sacrifice.

rules.statement: A Mystagogue can test only one alteration to an Initiation Script per attempt. If the alteration test fails, that Initiation attempt fails; if it succeeds, the modified Script determines the Initiation Total, and meeting or exceeding the Target Level completes the Initiation without another roll. The Initiate avoids the Script’s sacrifices if the Script proves unable to succeed, and the Mystagogue notices before those costs are imposed.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Initiation Script variation (opening passage) (ars-magica-houses#029)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one alteration per attempt and no sacrifice for a doomed Script; a world can allow more changes per season, at the cost of Mystagogue study or more complex rites.

rules.statement: Common Script elements award +3 for a required special place and time or a specific Quest, +1 for service or meaningful wealth sacrificed, and +3 to +6 for a great symbolic sacrifice. Ordeals award +3 for imposing a Minor Flaw or removing a Minor Virtue, +6 for worsening a Minor Flaw to Major, and +9 for imposing a Major Flaw or removing a Major Virtue.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Example Elements of an Initiation Script (ars-magica-houses#029)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the listed bonuses as a measure of the burden imposed; a world can change the scale, with larger rewards requiring more consequential loss or hardship.

rules.statement: Potent Magic adds +3 to Lab Totals and Casting Scores for a Minor version, or +6 for a Major version, within its narrow or wider field respectively. It can coexist with a Magical Focus, but only one Potent Magic area applies to an activity.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Potent Magic — Description (ars-magica-houses#029)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one applicable Potent Magic bonus per activity; a world can permit stacking, at the cost of sharply increasing specialization and power.

rules.statement: A Potent spell’s Potency is the sum of the selected Shape or Material bonuses from its Casting Items, and adds to Casting Score without changing spell level. The caster must touch every specified item or cannot cast the spell, and a spell’s Potency cannot exceed the designer’s Magic Theory score.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Potent Spells (ars-magica-houses#029)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a fixed item list and a Magic Theory cap; a world can allow improvised or remote items, at the cost of reducing the spell’s bonus or reliability.

rules.statement: A magus with Potent Magic can design Potent spells in the relevant field and can devise a variant of a known spell by changing its Casting Items; when that is the only change, the variant takes one season to invent. Any magus may learn and cast a Potent spell from a Lab Text or teacher, but only a Potent Magic holder can design one from scratch.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Potent Magic and Potent Spells (ars-magica-houses#029)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to access through training or a Lab Text, while original design requires the Virtue; a world can open design to all magi, at the cost of slower research or lower potency.

rules.statement: For library Build Point accounting, add a Potent spell’s Potency to its spell level and record its required Casting Items.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Designing Covenant Libraries (ars-magica-houses#029)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to counting the bonus as extra library value and listing required items; a world can waive the surcharge, at the cost of making potent texts more common.

rules.statement: At character creation, an older character may acquire a Mystery Virtue in place of a season of laboratory work, subtracting 10 experience points; all required Ordeals, Quests, and Sacrifices still apply.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Character Creation & the Mysteries (ars-magica-houses#029)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a 10-point experience cost plus the full Script burden; a world can reduce the experience cost, but should retain the in-world sacrifice that grants the Mystery.

rules.statement: The Ritual of Twelve Years is the sole way to gain the Heartbeast Virtue and join House Bjornaer. It brings the human soul and ancestral spirit into balance: the magus can become human or their heartbeast, and initiation also makes their parens and sept relatives mystical kin; they cannot leave the House.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: The Heartbeast (ars-magica-houses#030)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to an irreversible initiation that grants a true animal form and kinship; a world could make membership voluntary to loosen the bond, at the cost of the House’s mystical unity.

rules.statement: A heartbeast transformation takes one full round after a moment’s concentration, normally with no roll. During that round the magus can act using abilities from either form, but cannot perform complex tasks such as spellcasting; clothing and possessions do not change, and the magus cannot cast spells while fully animal.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: The Heartbeast in Play — Changing Form (ars-magica-houses#030)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a one-round change with no ordinary roll; a world could make changing faster or slower, trading tactical flexibility for the distinctive cost of transformation time.

rules.statement: A transformation can overcome a shapechanging spell or a spell that suppresses magic only with a Stamina + Heartbeast roll against an Ease Factor of 3 plus the spell’s magnitude; success against a shapechanging spell cancels it. A heartbeast cannot partially transform without a spell or the Theriomorphy Mystery.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: The Heartbeast in Play — Changing Form (ars-magica-houses#030)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the stated resistance roll and bar partial changes; a world could allow partial transformation more readily, at the cost of weakening the boundary between human and animal form.

rules.statement: A spell or enchanted item that changes a human’s shape leaves the target fundamentally human: Animal, Corpus, and Mentem magic can affect them, and the ongoing effect can be detected with Intellego Vim. An innate shapeshifter has an effect only at the moment of changing, but remains human in animal shape; a lycanthrope in animal form cannot be affected by Mentem.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Ringing the Changes (ars-magica-houses#030)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.mechanism: law: shapechanging magic and target nature
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to keeping spell-based and innate changes distinct from true heartbeast transformation; a world could treat all animal forms alike, at the cost of losing different magical vulnerabilities.

rules.statement: A heartbeast form is a real animal rather than a human under an animal appearance: Corpus and Mentem magic do not affect the magus in that form, though effects already active before the change remain active. Animal effects cast on the magus in animal form continue after returning to human form, and the transformation itself has no continuing magical effect.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Ringing the Changes (ars-magica-houses#030)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to treating heartbeast as an actual change of nature with no ongoing effect; a world could make it a sustained magical disguise, at the cost of exposing it to detection and dispelling.

rules.statement: When changing shape, use the higher of two positive or the lower of two negative values for each Characteristic other than Intelligence/Cunning; otherwise add the human and animal values. Retain human Intelligence except for lycanthropes, who use the animal’s Cunning. Animal-form Virtues and Flaws apply alongside human ones, wounds normally carry across forms, and lycanthropes heal animal-form wounds when returning to human form.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: The Heartbeast in Play — Statistics of Shapechangers (ars-magica-houses#030)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to carrying most traits and wounds across forms while combining Characteristics by the stated rule; a world could make injuries form-specific, at the cost of reducing the danger of changing shape.

rules.statement: A Bjornaer magus’s pregnancy must remain in one form from when it becomes visible until birth, or the child will not come to term. A child born to an animal mother is an animal; a child with an animal father is reported to lack a soul and have animal Cunning rather than human Intelligence.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: The Heartbeast (ars-magica-houses#030)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to preventing form changes during visible pregnancy; a world could permit them without consequence, at the cost of removing the stated bodily risk.

rules.statement: At Final Twilight, a Bjornaer always takes heartbeast form and flees human contact. One who knows only the Outer Mystery becomes a mundane beast; one with any Inner Mystery becomes an inner-heartbeast Great Beast with Magic Might equal to five times their Heartbeast Ability.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: The Heartbeast in Play — Heartbeasts and Wizard’s Twilight (ars-magica-houses#030)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to an irreversible animal outcome at Final Twilight, with Inner Mysteries determining whether Might remains; a world could let the magus retain human agency, at the cost of this dramatic final transformation.

rules.statement: The Heartbeast initiation has Ease Factor 15 and a Script Bonus of +6, plus one for each witness sharing the initiate’s temperament and minus one for each opposing witness; the Mystagogue counts. Success is possible only once for an initiate, and failure permanently bars entry into House Bjornaer; success immediately grants the Heartbeast Virtue and Ability at level 1 and changes the initiate into the heartbeast.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Initiation of Heartbeast (The Ritual of Twelve Years) (ars-magica-houses#031)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the stated one-attempt initiation, with witness temperament changing its bonus; a world could allow retries, but the irreversible failure protects the clan’s sacred rite.

rules.statement: Secret Name initiation has Ease Factor 15 and Script Bonus +8. It ends all pre-existing Arcane Connections and invalidates all sympathetic connections; thereafter, sympathetic connections never work against the initiate, while anyone who knows the secret name can cast against them without subtracting spell level from Penetration, and the initiate needs that name to use Personal Range.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Secret Name (Minor House Mystery) (ars-magica-houses#031)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to old connections ending and the secret name granting both protection and a bypass; a world could make the name less potent, but secrecy is the protection’s cost.

rules.statement: Theriomorphy lets the magus add one Quality or Virtue of the heartbeast to human form with a Stamina + Heartbeast roll against Ease Factor 9, taking a full round; another such roll removes it. The change visibly alters the body, causes a constant mystical effect for Warping, is not protected by Hidden Shape, and may require observers to make a Brave roll.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Theriomorphy (Minor House Mystery) (ars-magica-houses#031)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one feature at a time and a visible, Warping-producing change; a world could permit subtler or longer-lasting changes, but animal traits remain a conspicuous cost.

rules.statement: Sensory Magic spells have Personal Range and affect beings in the spell’s area who perceive the caster through its chosen sensory medium; targets can be acquired throughout the duration, but all effects end when the spell expires. The caster must keep producing the medium, cannot affect nonliving things or use Intellego, and the spell must penetrate a target’s Magic Resistance.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Sensory Magic (Minor House Mystery) (ars-magica-houses#031)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to ongoing acquisition of perceivers within the sense-defined area; a world could widen the media or targets, but continued sensory emission and penetration constrain the effect.

rules.statement: To assume an inner-heartbeast, the magus first takes outer-heartbeast form, then rolls Stamina + Heartbeast against Ease Factor 9; the change takes a full round during which the magus can only defend using outer-form statistics. Returning to outer form is automatic, and all inner-form features operate together only while in that form.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: The Inner Heartbeast in Play (ars-magica-houses#031)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a full-round, all-or-nothing change with automatic return; a world could make changes quicker, but vulnerability during transformation limits tactical use.

rules.statement: Inner-heartbeast refinements apply only to that form. The embryonic initiation takes at least one season at an ancestor site, consumes one pawn of appropriate vis per three Ease Factor points, causes one Warping Point, and gives a +3 bonus because the acquired Virtue works only in inner form; the heartbeast type grants a further +3 for its favored refinement categories.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Embryonic Initiation of a Refinement Mystery (ars-magica-houses#031)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the listed vis, time, Warping, and form restriction; a world could reduce these costs, but refinement consumes scarce vis and risks mystical distortion.

rules.statement: An inner-heartbeast supernatural Power is initiated as if it were an invested-item effect, with Uses per Day and Penetration specified; the magus’s relevant Lab Total must exceed its level. Minor Powers affect only the magus or provide magical senses and may be constant, while Major Powers can affect others and cannot be constant; their Ease Factors are 21 and 30 respectively.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Acquiring Powers (ars-magica-houses#031)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the Minor/Major division and stated Lab Total and initiation thresholds; a world could loosen them, but external effects and constant use are deliberately restricted.

rules.statement: A Great Beast’s inner-heartbeast initiation requires the magus to earn 10 Adventure experience points through trials, then takes a season and imposes a Hermetic or Supernatural Major Flaw. Its Ease Factor is 21 and Script Bonus +13; success grants the chosen inner-heartbeast mystery.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Initiation to the Mystery of the Inner Heartbeast (ars-magica-houses#031)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to mentor-set trials, a season-long rite, and a lasting Major Flaw; a world could vary the ordeal, but the mentor’s teaching carries a permanent cost.

rules.statement: A spell that affects a heartbeast of Size +2 or larger must include a Size modifier, making it at least one magnitude higher.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: The Magic of House Bjornaer (ars-magica-houses#032)
rules.speaker: rulebook

rules.statement: Only one Form of the (Temperament) Heartbeast spell may affect a character at a time, because the spells influence bodily humors and only one humor can be influenced this way at once. Casting requires animal form; afterward the caster may return to human form without losing the effect.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Form of the (Temperament) Heartbeast Spell (ars-magica-houses#032)
rules.speaker: rulebook

rules.statement: Facilitate the Stifled Form is cast at the same time as a formulaic spell whose level is less than twice its own. If successful, the target spell avoids penalties from reduced or absent voice or gestures; for a Voice-range target spell, the volume used for this spell sets its range.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Facilitate the Stifled (Form) Spell (ars-magica-houses#032)
rules.speaker: rulebook

rules.statement: For every point of Size removed from a creature, reduce Strength by 2, raise Quickness by 1, and reduce each wound level’s damage range by 1, to a minimum of 1; increasing Size applies the reverse changes. Each Size point also halves or doubles mass, respectively.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Creatures of Non-Standard Size (ars-magica-houses#032)
rules.speaker: rulebook

rules.statement: A creature with Ferocity has 3 confidence points and a confidence score of 1, usable only in a described situation that triggers its natural ferocity. Herd animals temporarily gain this Virtue when forced to fight as a group, but do not have it when alone unless they possess it as a Virtue.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Ferocity; Herd Animal (ars-magica-houses#032)
rules.speaker: rulebook

rules.statement: A venomous attack affects its victim if the creature’s Attack Advantage exceeds the victim’s Protection; this can happen even if the attack causes no wound. The avoidance Ease Factor ranges from 3 to 15.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Qualities: Venomous (ars-magica-houses#032)
rules.speaker: rulebook

rules.statement: Apt conduct is treated as a condition of effective magic: most Criamon magi find their powers diminished when they fail to live morally, and the degree of spiritual pollution is considered measurable.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: What the House Believes; Apt Action (ars-magica-houses#033)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to weakening a magus’s powers after inapt conduct; a setting can tune how strongly particular acts count, with spiritual pollution as the in-world cause.

rules.statement: A tattoo can be enchanted as a personal magical item without causing Warping. Its base material score is 2, multiplied by size: tiny 1, palm- or forehead-sized 2, limb- or scalp-covering 3, and torso-covering 4; unusual inks or resonant designs may add material bonuses.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Body Modification Rules — Tattoos; Enchanting Tattoos (ars-magica-houses#033)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to allowing personal enchantments on tattoos using the stated size-based scores; a world can vary bonus materials and designs, paid for through their scarcity or preparation.

rules.statement: Changing a child’s skull shape through binding gives an aptitude for one symbolically matching path, providing +3 to the Initiation Script for that path’s first station. Other bodily alterations can give similar effects.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Body Modification Rules — Other Modifications (ars-magica-houses#033)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a single path-linked +3 first-station bonus from childhood alteration; a world can allow other procedures or path matches, at the cost of disfigurement and objectionable treatment.

rules.statement: A magus whose stigmata are burned away grows them back or has them migrate so the damaged area becomes part of the pattern; a changed body shape retains its stigmata. The marks cannot be removed by magic.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Stigmata (ars-magica-houses#033)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to persistent, honest marks that adapt to bodily changes and resist magical removal; a world can decide how much of the pattern migrates, while destruction of skin does not erase it.

rules.statement: A magus may study Enigmatic Wisdom for a year under a Criamon magus or Cave ghost and gain the Ability at score 1; the Prima may then offer House membership. A magus without a House for a year ordinarily faces death under Hermetic law, so the House sometimes arranges adoption before renouncing a leaver.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Practices & Beliefs — Enigmatic Wisdom For Magi From Other Houses; The Gorgiastics (ars-magica-houses#033)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to granting the Ability after one year and making membership optional; a world can tighten access or adoption, with the danger of the year-without-a-House penalty.

rules.statement: For composing or answering a riddle, a player may roll Intelligence + Enigmatic Wisdom against an Ease Factor from 3 to 25. The shallow answer is immediately apparent; the deep meaning of an answer takes about a year of occasional consideration.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Riddles — Rolls for Riddles (ars-magica-houses#033)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to immediate shallow insight and a year for deep understanding; a world can shorten or lengthen reflection, trading speed for less considered insight.

rules.statement: A completed riddle is followed by a new one when the magus has exhausted its usefulness, represented by gaining a Mystery Virtue station or increasing Enigmatic Wisdom. Novel answers are sent to the Central Clutch, and accumulated answers lower future roll Ease Factors.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Riddles — Rolls for Riddles (ars-magica-houses#033)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to tying new riddles to advancement and letting accumulated lore ease later rolls; a world can make the communal archive more or less helpful, depending on how much new insight it contains.

rules.statement: A magus fading into a path’s repose may compress wisdom into a place or object that others can learn from through contemplation. Niobe’s spring permits a magus with Enigmatic Wisdom to study one Art per season, provided the magus’s score in it is below 5; multiple students may use it together but must study the same Art, and its aura is 1.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Final Transmission; Perfect Transmission Site Example (ars-magica-houses#033)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to wisdom stored for contemplative study, with Niobe’s example limited by Art score and shared seasonal focus; a world can change the site’s teaching scope, at the cost of time spent there.

rules.statement: An adulteration is solidified psychic detritus associated with unresolved issues, commonly arising at Final Twilight or from uncontrolled Twilight, trauma, an apprentice’s death, or a familiar’s loss. Resolving the creator’s adulteration releases its burden; exceptionally, resolving a major one grants a fitting positive Twilight benefit.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Adulterations: Lingering Problems (ars-magica-houses#033)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a creature-like manifestation tied to its creator’s unresolved issue, removable by addressing that issue; a world can make major resolutions rewarding, with the benefit dependent on the experience.

rules.statement: Adulterations created by a magus in Twilight can range from minor attention-getting beings or events to severe monsters and deathtraps. They may merge and grow stronger as more spiritually transgressive magi enter Twilight; a creature usually has Magical Might 10–45, knows its creator’s location, and can pass its creator’s Aegis without invitation or trigger wards that ignore that creator.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Designing Adulterations (ars-magica-houses#034)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to creator-linked entities that can locate their source and bypass source-specific defenses; a setting can make them weaker, stronger, or amalgamated according to the creator’s transgression and the number of such events.

rules.statement: A magus who creates an adulterous place is fated to return until resolving its central issue; the regio usually disappears after resolution, returning its contents to ambient magic or placing them in the mundane world. Some Final Twilight adulterations instead leave permanent regiones or auras.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Designing Adulterations (ars-magica-houses#034)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a creator-bound place that closes when its issue is resolved; a world can make the resulting site permanent, with the aftermath determined by the source of the adulteration.

rules.statement: Resolving an adulteration usually marks progress rather than instantly removing the represented flaw: in the example, confronting the embodied aggression removes one point from the Angry Personality Trait, with further change left to later roleplay.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Example: Introducing an Adulteration (ars-magica-houses#034)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to resolution reducing a represented flaw incrementally; a world can set the amount of change, requiring ongoing effort because spiritual development takes time.

rules.statement: The Carnal Wolf’s physical form can be destroyed by magic, but the adulteration reforms elsewhere. It instead ends when descendants of its creator confront it; they can soothe it into non-existence or familiarhood.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: The Carnal Wolf (ars-magica-houses#034)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to bodily destruction failing to remove the underlying entity; a world can permit resolution or conversion only through the creator’s descendants, tying the cost to lineage and reconciliation.

rules.statement: A living Primus may, according to House belief, draw the Axis Magica into his body and carry it elsewhere; entering Twilight re-establishes it and shifts Mythic Europe’s aura pattern. While this is happening, no other magus can return from Twilight or shelter there from magical harm.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: The Spectral Primi (ars-magica-houses#034)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the Primus serving as a costly living anchor that relocates the Axis and disrupts Twilight refuge; a world can decide whether the reputed ability is real, at the risk of others dying without shelter.

rules.statement: A magus may follow only one path at a time. Leaving a path removes access to all its stations except Enigmatic Wisdom; returning restores prior understanding, while Primi retain prior stations when taking the Path of the Mirror.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: The Paths (ars-magica-houses#034)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to incompatible path frameworks that suspend learned station benefits when changing paths; a world can allow exceptions, with the usual cost being the loss of access until return.

rules.statement: To gain a station, a magus needs House Criamon Lore at least one point above the station’s position, a trial or ritual investiture, and insight in a story; the fifth station therefore requires Lore 6. A magus living inaptly loses the powers associated with spiritual purification until purity is restored, and failure to follow a Pious path slowly reduces those abilities.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Stations; To Do Is to Be. to Be Is to Do (ars-magica-houses#034)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to station powers requiring qualifying Lore, ordeal, and insight, with conduct maintaining access; a world can make the behavioral restriction stricter because spiritual impurity undermines the powers.
