rules.statement: A labyrinth meditation grants, for one hour, a bonus equal to half Enigmatic Wisdom on one qualifying roll: an Enigmatic Wisdom or Lore roll, or a physical action lasting at most one minute. The relevant Ability must already be at least 1; scores 3 and 6 remove the need for a physical maze and walking, respectively, and the bonus cannot be stacked.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Labyrinth Meditations (ars-magica-houses#034)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one short-lived, nonstacking focus bonus after meditation; a world can reduce preparation requirements for higher wisdom, while the time spent meditating limits repeated use.

rules.statement: Mystically nourished magi do not age and need not eat, drink, breathe, or sleep in magical or mundane regions, but gain one Warping Point each year and must meditate six hours daily. The effect fails without sufficient magical energy, in certain hostile realms, or after inapt conduct; Dominion or Infernal influence restores one bodily need per day and aging after Enigmatic Wisdom + 1 days.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: The Avenue of Drinking the Winds of Inspiration and the Station of Spiritual Nourishment (ars-magica-houses#034)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to replacing bodily needs and aging with daily meditation and yearly Warping; a world can vary which realms suppress it, charging the character lost nourishment and renewed aging for spiritual incompatibility.

rules.statement: After labyrinth meditation, a follower of Perfect Economy of Movement automatically succeeds once per day on one Dexterity-related Ability roll with Ease Factor 21 or less.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: The Avenue of the Tiniest Seed and the Station of Perfect Economy of Movement (ars-magica-houses#034)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one prepared, guaranteed precise action per day up to the stated difficulty; a world can narrow eligible actions, with the daily limit reflecting the power’s exceptional precision.

rules.statement: The Microcosm station lets a magus cast as if holding an Arcane Connection to any mundane place previously visited or mundane thing previously touched that is currently in a mundane place; people cannot be targeted this way.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: The Avenue of the Spherical Mirror and the Station of the Microcosm (ars-magica-houses#034)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to treating prior contact with mundane places or objects as an Arcane Connection, but not with people; a world can broaden the eligible targets, at the risk of making remote targeting easier.

rules.statement: To use a remembered connection to a place or thing, the magus must distinctly recall it: regularly visited places have Ease Factor 6, yearly visits 9, and places visited long ago 12. An evocative object or mark adds up to 3; a botch recalls a wholly wrong place without the magus realizing it.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Passage 36, opening limitation (ars-magica-houses#035)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to these recall difficulties and the +3 memory aid; a world can make rare or poorly remembered connections harder because memory weakens with distance and time.

rules.statement: A magus who has reached the Body’s final station but remains in the world regains aging-lost attributes, stops using Aging Points, and raises negative physical Characteristics to 0. Unless killed, bodily damage heals completely at full moonrise; stigmata and Warping continue.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: The Avenue of Repose in the Body and the Threshold of Corporeal Repose (ars-magica-houses#035)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to full healing only at full moonrise and no protection from death; a world can alter the interval because the body is purified but not immortal.

rules.statement: A spirit traveler finds familiar places on a total of 6, previously visited places on 12, unknown places with a strong connection on 15, and especially distant places on 18 or more. Journeys take about an hour; a failed search wastes an hour and grants +1 on a retry, while the unmoved body can always be found.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: The Avenue That Is a Crossroad — Passing Through Rules (ars-magica-houses#035)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the listed destination thresholds, hour-long trips, and cumulative retry bonus; a world can make remote destinations harder because the traveler must navigate magical space.

rules.statement: After a round of preparation and a Stamina + Concentration roll against Ease Factor 6, a magus can treat a solid mundane object as spectral for minutes equal to Enigmatic Wisdom. Each additional object raises the Ease Factor by 1, groups raise it by 3, and people cannot be affected; the power works on as many objects as the magus can concentrate on.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: The Avenue That Leads to Transcendence and the Station from Which to Ignore the Real (ars-magica-houses#035)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to brief, concentration-limited passage through objects and exclude people; a world can raise the difficulty because souls are not mundane matter.

rules.statement: A Strife adept’s meditation can reduce an unresisted object to powder, or kill mundane things in an area no wider than 500 feet per Enigmatic Wisdom level, but not humans. Weapon strikes have four times the usual Attack Total and Penetration of Enigmatic Wisdom × 5; Divine-aligned beings and matter without exploitable flaws are immune.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: The Avenue That Splinters and the Station of Blood and Bronze (ars-magica-houses#035)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to powerful destruction bounded by area, target type, and exploitable flaws; a world can broaden or narrow targets because this power exploits decay rather than simply dealing force.

rules.statement: A Strife adept can attract or repel one Form at a time, switching targets or Forms once per round without fatigue or concentration. The combined weight cannot exceed three times the adept’s weight; the adept must be aware of targets, and the power fails against warded objects.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Avenue of Charm and Scorn, and the Station That Repels and Attracts Elements (ars-magica-houses#035)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a weight cap, one Form at a time, and no effect through wards; a world can change the weight limit because the adept’s own body anchors the force.

rules.statement: Golden Cider requires prior meditation on the victim’s weaknesses, Enigmatic Wisdom at least one-fifth of the victim’s Magic Resistance, bare-hand contact for three uninterrupted minutes, and the victim to remain partly immobile. It makes magical items mundane, turns some supernatural beings into symbolic things or removes their assumed bodies, but cannot affect the Divine; it also cannot sever the Gift without its bearer’s knowing cooperation.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Avenue of Death and the Station of Golden Cider (ars-magica-houses#035)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to demanding preparation and sustained contact, with Divine immunity and cooperation protecting the Gift; a world can change eligible targets because the power strips away supernatural strife.

rules.statement: A Walking Backwards healer can restore non-human objects, plants, and animals by meditation, generally only up to 10 yards across; human-made damage cannot be undone and the dead cannot be revived. Around a dying person, meditation can hold death off for Enigmatic Wisdom hours, plus positive Stamina hours at the cost of a Twilight experience; the healer cannot choose to harm.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: The Avenue of Healing and the Station of Rice and Honey (ars-magica-houses#035)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to restoring non-human things and delaying, not curing, human death; a world can change the size or duration because healing draws on harmony and prolonged effort risks Twilight.

rules.statement: At the final station of the Path of Walking Backward, a magus permanently gives up using Perdo with every Form except Vim and Imaginem, because the magus will no longer destroy the harmony perceived in things.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Avenue of Silencing Discordant Whispers and the Threshold of Repose (ars-magica-houses#036)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to making the restriction permanent; a world can loosen which combinations are forbidden; the sacrifice reflects the magus’s refusal to use destructive power.

rules.statement: A magus at this station can change age, gender, and species in the time of a breath, but wounds remain across forms. Human appearances are consistently related: there is only one appearance for each age-and-sex combination, and younger forms look like younger versions of older ones.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Avenue of Silencing Discordant Whispers and the Threshold of Repose (ars-magica-houses#036)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to near-instant changes with persistent wounds; a world can limit available forms or slow transformation; continuity of injury prevents a change of appearance from healing the body.

rules.statement: A magus of this station can choose when to die, but pride or fear of death prevents reaching the state. Taking risks remains a choice that may result in death.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Avenue of Silencing Discordant Whispers and the Threshold of Repose (ars-magica-houses#036)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to voluntary control over the time of death, not immunity to death; a world can narrow when the choice can be made; fear or pride blocks access to the ability.

rules.statement: Ascending to the Spharios joins the magus to the universe’s mind; the magus may bring along worthy people or creatures, or evil traits of people and places, for the sphere to absorb and nullify. A magus who does not ascend remains alive in perfect harmony.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Avenue of Silencing Discordant Whispers and the Threshold of Repose (ars-magica-houses#036)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to ascent as a voluntary, integrating departure; a world can restrict who or what may accompany the magus; joining the sphere means surrendering individual existence.

rules.statement: The threshold grants no immunity to Twilight. A magus abstaining from magic and avoiding powerful supernatural auras can avoid Twilight by avoiding the gain of two or more Warping Points at once.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Twilight and Walking Backwards (ars-magica-houses#036)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the stated avoidance conditions and the two-point threshold; a world can alter the threshold or eligible auras; abstinence and avoiding powerful supernatural places are the price of safety.

rules.statement: An Arcadian Travel Initiation has Ease Factor 18 and a script bonus of +14. Its candidate must alone map every entrance at every level of a faerie regio whose highest level is at least 5, then travel to its center and back before dawn without magic, aid, food, drink, or contact with inhabitants; the ordeal grants Fear, and the starting landmark becomes a permanent Arcane Connection.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Sample Wayfarers Initiation: Arcadian Travel (ars-magica-houses#036)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the listed test, bonus, and prohibitions; a world can change the regio requirement or ordeal; the candidate earns the secret through an unsupported and frightening journey.

rules.statement: In Arcadia, travelers may be unable to return to the exact place they left, and actions there may affect or be reflected in the mundane world. Some accounts instead describe the realm as changing in response to desires, which it absorbs; attaining a desire without a strong reason to leave can strand a traveler.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: The Search for Arcadia (ars-magica-houses#036)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to consequential travel and desire-shaped surroundings; a world can decide which account governs a journey; the realm’s shifting nature and absorbed desires make return uncertain.

rules.statement: A maga with Arcadian Travel can use a sleep-inducing charm to open a trod through dreams and travel to Arcadia in spirit. Travelers do not age or suffer harm from lack of food or water while away, but can die by other means; a dead traveler's spirit remains in Faerie.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Faerie and Dreams (ars-magica-houses#037)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to spirit-only travel with no aging or hunger costs; a world can make death or other hazards more consequential because travelers remain vulnerable to them.

rules.statement: A temporary charm takes about ten minutes to make and must be used immediately, usually with spontaneous magic; a permanent charm takes several hours, requires a special object, and must be remade if that object is damaged. With Faerie Magic and an Arcane Connection to the target, a successful charm increases the Penetration multiplier by two; the roll must reach 6 for a temporary charm or 9 for a permanent one, and only one charm can be used in a spell.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Charms (ars-magica-houses#037)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one charm per spell and the stated preparation and roll thresholds; a world can loosen these limits, at the cost of weaker or less durable sympathetic links.

rules.statement: When a faerie is bound as a familiar, the maga may spend Fatigue Levels to use its powers, each level providing Might Points equal to its Might divided by 5. The familiar can recover that many Might Points by resting, and can spend Might Points to spare the maga Fatigue loss, at a cost based on the Fatigue Level she would have reached.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Enchanting a Faerie Familiar (ars-magica-houses#037)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to shared powers and fatigue at one fifth of the familiar's Might per Fatigue Level; a world can change the exchange rate to make the bond more or less taxing.

rules.statement: A faerie familiar's three ordinary bond cords weaken over time: one cord gains an Aging Point each year, normally the highest-valued one. When all three reach 0, the bond breaks at the year's end, releasing the familiar and destroying powers invested in the bond.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Enchanting a Faerie Familiar (ars-magica-houses#037)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one cord degrading each year and complete release at zero; a world can slow or prevent decay, reducing the special instability associated with faerie bonds.

rules.statement: Faerie Chains of the Familiar Slave binds a supernatural creature as a familiar until a stated condition occurs. Its ritual level must be at least the creature's Might plus 15, it cannot affect a creature already bonded to another, and an unwilling target may require overcoming its resistance; its cords start at 0.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Faerie Chains of the Familiar Slave (ars-magica-houses#037)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a condition-bounded bond with the Might-plus-15 minimum and zeroed cords; a world can permit lower-cost bonds, at the risk of weaker control or shorter service.

rules.statement: The three negative faerie cords prevent decay when their total value balances or exceeds the total of the positive cords; if one side has the greater total, its highest-valued cord gains an Aging Point each year. Each negative cord also imposes its own penalties on the maga and familiar.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: The Three Faerie Cords (ars-magica-houses#037)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to balancing positive and negative cord totals to halt decay; a world can require a larger negative total, making stability costlier in personal drawbacks.

rules.statement: A character with Harmless Magic cannot permanently destroy things with Perdo spells: the target is disrupted only for the spell's duration and returns to its natural state afterward. Ritual Perdo spells are exempt.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Harmless Magic (ars-magica-houses#037)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to temporary disruption for non-ritual Perdo effects; a world can make the limitation apply to rituals too, trading away lasting destruction for a more universal rule.

rules.statement: Vulnerable Magic causes a spell's duration to end when its specified unusual circumstance affects its target, or ends all of the caster's active spells if the circumstance affects the caster. The flaw can be taken multiple times with a different trigger each time.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Vulnerable Magic (ars-magica-houses#037)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one defined trigger per instance that immediately ends affected magic; a world can make triggers rarer or more common, adjusting how often the weakness matters.

rules.statement: Outside any supernatural aura, subtract the Tin Cord’s value from the bound character’s Personality Trait, natural resistance, healing, deprivation, Aging, and Soak results. A faerie familiar bound by negative cords may grow increasingly distressed and may try to escape, act spitefully, or die to break free.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: The Tin Cord (ars-magica-houses#038)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: apply the full penalty outside a supernatural aura; a world can lessen it if the bond is less restrictive, because the faerie’s resentment stems from being fettered.

rules.statement: A familiar inherits the magus’s Gift-related social effects, including protections or additional drawbacks. For cord effects, use only the applicable cord with the greatest value; when positive and negative cords both apply, add the bonus and subtract the penalty.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Binding the Gift (Minor House Mystery) (ars-magica-houses#038)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: share the Gift’s social effect and resolve competing cords by strongest value; a world can weaken inheritance or change cord strength, because the familiar shares the magus’s supernatural social influence.

rules.statement: To open a trod, the maga needs a destination charm, must perceive it and touch its associated object if prepared in advance, then concentrate for about ten minutes and roll stress die + Perception + the charm-making Ability + Aura against the destination’s Ease Factor. The factors are 3 times the regio level to reach a regio level, 3 times the current level to leave a regio, 3 times (13 − current aura modifier) to reach Arcadia, and 3 times (13 − destination aura modifier) to leave Arcadia; an Arcane Connection reduces the factor by 6. A mundane destination requires first reaching a regio above it, and up to a number of willing participants equal to the maga’s Faerie Magic score can travel with her.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Arcadian Travel (Minor Arcadian Mystery) (ars-magica-houses#038)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: allow charm-opened routes with the listed difficulty and participant cap; a world can make routes rarer or harder to open, because trods connect levels of Faerie and the mortal world.

rules.statement: Animae magic uses Creo to summon a faerie associated with a Form, with little control over its identity, or Muto to turn a mundane thing into an appropriate faerie. The spell’s level must exceed the listed guideline by the faerie’s Might; for example, a Might 1 insect requires base 11, while turning a pool into a Might 10 water faerie requires base 20.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Animae Guidelines (ars-magica-houses#038)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: summoned or transformed animae have Might added to the guideline level; a world can restrict which Forms produce them, because their nature is tied to the thing or Form involved.

rules.statement: Becoming requires three separate seasonal laboratory transformations of body, mind, and spirit, in any order; each Lab Total must meet its ritual level. Until the spirit transformation grants Might, the Lab Total is capped at Warping Score × Faerie Magic score. The body ritual’s level is age − 35 + 5 × Decrepitude; the mind ritual’s is total Ability scores; the spirit ritual’s is total Arts scores.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Becoming (Major Arcadian Mystery) (ars-magica-houses#038)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: require all three costly seasonal transformations and use the stated formulas; a world can change the prerequisites or ritual burden, because becoming fae fundamentally changes body, mind, and magic.

rules.statement: The body transformation stops aging and removes Fatigue, but prevents ordinary exertion and spontaneous-casting fatigue unless the character spends a Confidence Point to simulate it. The mind transformation removes the need for sleep and grants two extra non-laboratory seasons yearly, but bars learning new Abilities and inventing spells not similar to known spells. The spirit transformation removes the Gift, grants Faerie Might equal to half the Becoming Lab Total and immunity to Warping, but makes casting or laboratory work cost one Might Point per magnitude.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Transforming the Body; Transforming the Mind; Transforming the Spirit (ars-magica-houses#038)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: transformations grant their benefits with the stated restrictions and costs; a world can tune the tradeoffs, because the change exchanges human capacities for faerie nature.

rules.statement: Charm Magic gives +1 to Casting Total per charm and +1 per represented category, up to the maga’s Faerie Magic score in charms. With an Arcane Connection, Penetration Multiplier gains +1 per category beyond the first, in addition to the normal +2 symbolic bonus; a combined charm gains +3 Ease Factor for each added concept.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Charm Magic (Minor Folk Mystery) (ars-magica-houses#038)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: grant bonuses only when charms fit the spell and target; a world can limit broad or unsuitable symbols, because the benefit comes from a specific sympathetic match.

rules.statement: Activating a Story Magic charm costs a Confidence Point and causes its idea to enter the session, with the actual event decided by the storyguide. If a clear numeric benefit is needed, use +3 to related rolls for the scene; a story charm can also substitute for a Charm Magic charm in its category, still at the Confidence Point cost.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Story Magic (Major Folk Mystery) (ars-magica-houses#038)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: spend Confidence to introduce a relevant story element, with the guide controlling its form; a world can require narrower applicability, because the effect is narrative influence rather than a guaranteed outcome.

rules.statement: Held effects remain dormant while the caster concentrates; on release, they resolve as Momentary effects, with range and target parameters checked at release. Midday/Midnight effects wait for the next named time and last until the following one; Season effects wait for the next equinox or solstice and end at the one after that, require a ritual, and have Moon-level duration.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Illusion Mysteries — Spell Timing (ars-magica-houses#039)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to delayed effects that recheck their target when released; a world can extend the wait using seasonal or daily triggers, at the cost of ritual work for Season effects.

rules.statement: While (Condition) effects last while a specified activity or temporary physical state continues; Not (Condition) effects last while a specified common physical condition is absent, up to one month. If (Condition) effects add four magnitudes, require a ritual, and expire untriggered if the caster dies, enters Twilight, or a year passes.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Illusion Mysteries — Spell Timing (ars-magica-houses#039)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to ending conditional effects when their condition changes; a world can allow a single delayed trigger, but it costs four magnitudes and a ritual and risks expiry.

rules.statement: A recurring spell must be a ritual and cannot be an effect that requires a ritual for an unusual effect or non-Hermetic origin. It cannot trigger more than once per minute; the frequency surcharge is +5 magnitudes per minute, +4 per day, +3 per month, +2 per year, or +1 per decade, and a second daily trigger has no effect. Each recurrence cancels the prior instance before restarting, so recurrences do not stack.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Illusion Mysteries — Recurring Spells (ars-magica-houses#039)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one active instance that restarts on its schedule; a world can make effects recur more often only by paying higher magnitudes, with a hard one-minute minimum.

rules.statement: Glamours created by Creo or Muto Imaginem behave materially like the thing represented for the spell’s duration and can leave lasting changes to their surroundings. Intricate or complex glamours add one magnitude; mentally directed movement or turning an animate target into an inanimate object adds two, and an ignored animate target gradually regains mobility.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Illusion Mysteries — Glamour (ars-magica-houses#039)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to materially effective illusions whose environmental consequences persist; a world can make elaborate or directed forms easier, while the target’s nature and neglect can undo a transformation.

rules.statement: A spell glamour can alter another caster’s spell only if it is fast-cast, targets a spell as it is cast, specifies its Form and magic tradition, and penetrates that spell’s Penetration Total; it cannot affect spontaneous magic. The example turns a formulaic Ignem spell into harmless color and sound.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Illusion Mysteries — Spell Glamours (ars-magica-houses#039)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to spell alteration only when the countering effect overcomes the target spell; a world can permit transformation into a different effect, but limits it to prepared fast-casting against another caster.

rules.statement: Nature Lore is associated with a chosen natural domain, works as local Area Lore, and counts as three points lower beyond the home region. At score 2 it detects nearby supernatural elements and regio boundaries; at 3 it can locate vis once per season; at 7 it permits mental communication and summoning help by concentration; at 8 it grants an Arcane Connection to any part of the area; at 9 its denizens are compelled to obey.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Nature Mysteries — Nature Lore (ars-magica-houses#039)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to local knowledge and increasingly strong rapport as the score rises; a world can extend the influence to other regions, but applies a three-point penalty outside the familiar area.

rules.statement: Awakening takes at least a season and uses a representative natural subject; its required level is 25 plus Might plus five times Size, or five times aura plus the area Size modifier. It costs one pawn of suitable vis per five levels or fraction; an awakened being gains Might equal to aura times five if it lacked Might, and an animal gains Intelligence.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Nature Mysteries — Awakening (ars-magica-houses#039)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to creating one intelligent guardian-like being from a representative subject; a world can allow additional beings only in distinct auras, with seasonal labor and vis as the cost.

rules.statement: Powers invested in an awakened being have a combined level limit of ten times the pawns spent awakening it. Each power costs the being one Might Point per ten levels or fraction; five pawns of relevant Art vis spent when installing it reduce that activation cost by one Might Point, and once power investment begins the being can never become a familiar.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Nature Mysteries — Awakening (ars-magica-houses#039)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a fixed capacity bought through the awakening cost, with Might spent for each activation; a world can lower that running cost by consuming vis at installation, but forfeits familiar-bonding.

rules.statement: A Guardian of Nature ritual costs a Fatigue Level and vis equal to the aura level, requires at least an hour, and merges the maga with a fluent, magical-aura locus. She becomes invisible and intangible, can sense and control nature there, and can leave for her living body after at least an hour of concentration, ending the effect; annual exposure grants one Warping Point, and complete destruction of the locus kills her.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Nature Mysteries — Guardian of Nature (ars-magica-houses#039)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a spirit-like presence bound to a natural region, powerful within it but unable to interact directly with the physical world; a world can enlarge the locus, at the cost of more vis and greater vulnerability to damage to its essential place.

rules.statement: The Embrace of Boethius permanently damages a probationer’s Gift, removing the ability to cast formulaic spells without casting tools. The target gains 7 Warping Points and must check for temporary Twilight; the initiation also brings Proud 1 and an avaricious fixation on wealth.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Embrace of Boethius (ars-magica-houses#041)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to permanent loss of tool-free formulaic casting; a world can soften or remove the restriction, but the ritual’s lasting damage is the price of admission.

rules.statement: A Mystagogue needs Verditius Cult Lore 1 for basic cult knowledge, 2 to initiate an apprentice while opening that apprentice’s Arts, 3 to receive Minor Inner Mysteries, and 5 for Major Inner Mysteries and master-level Contest entry. Self-initiation raises the target level because the Initiate cannot use a Mystagogue’s Lore score.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Learning the Inner Mysteries (ars-magica-houses#041)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to Lore-gated initiation and a higher difficulty for self-initiation; a world can lower the thresholds, trading institutional oversight for easier access.

rules.statement: A magus’s Hubris score adds to Lab Totals for making a talisman, enchanting casting tools, binding magical animals, making automata, and creating attuned items. It grows through listed rewards and achievements, such as 1 point for selling a lesser enchanted device, 3 for a greater one, and 6 for an attuned item.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Hubris (ars-magica-houses#041)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to pride increasing both crafting ability and temptation; a world can reduce the bonus or the listed gains, at the cost of weakening the link between success and corruption.

rules.statement: A magus’s first Inner Mystery initiation always gives the Minor Flaw Hubris. Later Ordeals can impose lasting costs: for example, Sever the Ties That Bind prevents renewed family attachments, while Self-Mutilation causes wounds that cannot be healed.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Ordeals (ars-magica-houses#041)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to an enduring personal cost for initiation; a world can allow less severe Ordeals, but then the sacrifice that helps make initiation possible is reduced.

rules.statement: An enchanted casting tool takes a season to make, can receive only one enchantment, and cannot hold other magical powers or serve as the basis for another enchanted item. Its final effect level must be no more than half the maker’s Lab Total, and it costs one pawn of appropriate Technique or Form vis per 10 effect levels, rounded up.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Enchant Casting Tools (Minor House Mystery) (ars-magica-houses#041)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a permanent, limited spell-linked tool with seasonal work and vis costs; a world can ease the capacity or cost limits, making these tools more common.

rules.statement: An item of quality takes a season and one pawn of Vim vis to create, and brings one appropriate Shape and Material bonus to its surface. The bonus applies to relevant rolls but cannot exceed the maker’s Philosophiae score; the item is not a magical device and is not detected by simple magic detection.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Items of Quality (Minor House Mystery) (ars-magica-houses#041)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one capped, narrow bonus without ordinary magic-device detection; a world can allow multiple bonuses or easier detection, changing the item’s value and concealment.

rules.statement: Reforging a device takes at least a season and compares a Creo or Rego Vim Lab Total plus a stress die against each power’s level. Successful reforging can add capacity equal to the maker’s Philosophiae score, but costs that many pawns of Vim vis and raises each power’s future reforging level by five times that score.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Reforging Enchanted Items (Minor House Mystery) (ars-magica-houses#041)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to recoverable extra capacity that makes later reforging harder; a world can remove the escalating difficulty, at the cost of allowing repeated easy expansion.

rules.statement: An elder rune linked to an Art can be inscribed during item creation and doubles the enchanter’s score in that Art for enchanting the item. Each rune is tied to a particular Art and tree, so this benefit is not freely reassigned.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Verditius Elder Runes (ars-magica-houses#041)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a rune providing a double Art score only for the Art it represents; a world can let runes apply more broadly, weakening the limits imposed by their associations.

rules.statement: An eligible enchanted device may receive up to two elder runes when it is opened for enchantment; each rune raises every effect’s final level by 5 and costs one pawn of vis for its associated Art. For an effect governed by a rune, the enchanter may double the corresponding Art score; an existing applicable Focus can also add the lowest Art again.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Elder Runes (ars-magica-houses#042)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to allowing one or two runes on eligible devices; a world can limit which Arts have runes, since adapting another rune is a Minor Breakthrough, and the cost is vis plus harder enchantment.

rules.statement: When a rune is inscribed on a device made from its sympathetically linked tree, the enchanter gains +2 to the Lab Total, in addition to the device’s Shape and Material bonuses. Enchanting-item seasons can use vis up to Magic Theory multiplied by Philosophiae when the second rune mystery is known.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Elder Runes (ars-magica-houses#042)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the +2 bonus and the multiplied seasonal vis limit; a world can make matching wood or expanded vis capacity scarce, with material and vis costs as the constraint.

rules.statement: An automaton’s Magic Might is 10 plus its Size and Material Base Points; this also sets its Magic Resistance and the maximum pawns of vis it can hold. Its maker must spend a season constructing it, then spend Vim vis equal to its Might in one season to prepare it for enchantment.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Automata — Creating an Automaton; Preparing an Automaton for Enchantment (ars-magica-houses#042)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to Might controlling both resistance and enchantment capacity; a world can alter base materials or construction prices, with seasons, money, and Vim vis as costs.

rules.statement: Automaton powers are item enchantments with Personal Range and Part Target; they cannot cast effects on others or maintain Concentration Duration effects. Each power uses vis equal to one pawn per 10 final levels, rounded up, and must have a trigger and a daily frequency; the special stop command adds 3 levels.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Automata — Enchanting an Automaton (ars-magica-houses#042)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to restricted personal, part-based powers and command triggers; a world can vary permitted triggers or frequency, while vis and restricted capabilities limit the device.

rules.statement: An automaton’s installed Ability score cannot exceed its maker’s score in that Ability. The base effect of 25 grants Ability 1, and each added magnitude raises that score by 1; its shape must suit the task.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Automata — Enchanting an Automaton (ars-magica-houses#042)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a maker-skill ceiling and one Ability per suitable form; a world can permit broader tasks, at the cost of higher effect levels and appropriate construction.

rules.statement: At each year’s end, an automaton is undamaged if a stress die meets or exceeds its Magic Might; otherwise it loses 1 Might. Each 2 points lost imposes a cumulative –1 to Ability rolls, a botch removes 5 Might per botch, and Might 0 means it no longer works.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Automata in Play (ars-magica-houses#042)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to annual deterioration and cumulative penalties; a world can change the check interval or severity, with ongoing maintenance and risk of total failure as the cost.

rules.statement: An item-bound Curse imposes a Minor or Major Flaw: a Minor one lasts seasons equal to the creator’s Magic Theory at enchantment, while a Major one lasts that many years. Their base effect levels are 25 and 50 respectively, and conditional triggers add 3 levels, or 6 if keyed to a specified number of uses of another power.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Bind Curse (ars-magica-houses#042)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the stated duration, severity, and trigger surcharges; a world can limit available Curses, with high effect levels, vis, and the victim’s lasting impairment as costs.

rules.statement: A magical creature’s Might can be drained during an enchantment: for each point the enchanter’s Rego Vim Lab Total plus Hubris exceeds the creature’s Might, the device receives one pawn of usable vis, up to the creature’s Might. The energy cannot be stored; unused excess is wasted, and drained Might is permanently lost.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Bind Magical Creatures (ars-magica-houses#042)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to converting the Lab Total surplus into immediate, non-specific vis; a world can cap or forbid the conversion, with permanent loss to the creature and waste of excess as costs.

rules.statement: Spontaneous spellcasting requires the magus to use casting tools, with 15 individual tools available—one for each Art—and tools used in different combinations.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Passage 44, immediately before “Consumed Casting Tools” (ars-magica-houses#043)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to requiring Art-specific tools for spontaneous casting; a world can make tools optional or alter the number required, trading away this component of casting preparation.

rules.statement: A consumed casting tool is magically used up after casting, and making its replacement takes one hour. A regular tool cannot be copied for stockpiling; making another for a spell that already has one erases the existing tool’s magical link to that spell. No laboratory is needed to make tools.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Passage 44, “Consumed Casting Tools” (ars-magica-houses#043)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to consuming each tool on use and replacing it in an hour; a world can relax consumption or replacement time, at the cost of making spell preparation less restrictive.

rules.statement: A magus’s personal casting tools remain connected to him as Arcane Connections for years, while ordinary tools retain that connection for only a few weeks.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Passage 44, “Bound Casting Tools” (ars-magica-houses#043)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to years of connection for personal tools and weeks for ordinary ones; a world can shorten or extend these periods, affecting how long the connection can be exploited.

rules.statement: A character with severely damaged legs cannot walk without crutches or other aids, and even then moves only half a mile per hour. Rolls requiring quick movement take –9; Dodge and other combat rolls take –6, and combat uses twice the usual botch dice.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Passage 44, “Hobbled” (ars-magica-houses#043)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the stated movement limits and penalties; a world can vary the penalties or mobility, with the in-world consequence reflecting the severity of the injury.

rules.statement: A covenant’s Boons and Hooks must have equal total point costs at creation; Major choices are worth three points and Minor choices one, while Free Choices have no cost. Hooks provide the points for Boons, and the Unknown Hook is Major and adds a surprising Minor Hook selected by one player.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Chapter Two, “Paying for Choices” (ars-magica-houses#043)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to equal creation costs and the stated point values; a world can loosen the balance, accepting a covenant whose advantages are not offset by story complications.

rules.statement: A Minor Healthy Feature gives inhabitants with access to it +1 on aging rolls, and can be selected up to three times.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Chapter Two, “Minor Site Boons,” Healthy Feature (ars-magica-houses#043)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a +1 aging-roll bonus per selection, to a maximum of three; a world can change the bonus or cap, representing a weaker or stronger health-giving site.

rules.statement: A Minor Immunity protects people and objects within the covenant’s aura from one specified kind of damage or influence. The protection may suspend an illness rather than cure it, so its effects can return when someone leaves the aura.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Chapter Two, “Minor Site Boons,” Immunity (ars-magica-houses#043)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to blocking one selected harm inside the aura; a world can broaden the protection or make it permanent, at the cost of changing the effect on people who leave.

rules.statement: In a Time Dilation or Contraction site, residents and outsiders experience different rates of time: dilation lets residents live longer relative to outsiders but develop more slowly, while contraction lets them study and develop faster but makes them age rapidly from an outsider’s perspective. Vis sources usually replenish according to mundane time; local-time replenishment is a separately paid-for exception.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Chapter Two, “Major Site Boons,” Time Dilation or Contraction (ars-magica-houses#043)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the stated different rates and mundane-time vis refresh; a world can set the rate and whether sources refresh locally, with faster development balanced by accelerated aging.

rules.statement: A supernatural curse can overcome the covenant’s Aegis of the Hearth. One example makes wine cause fatal burns when tasted; it turns into green vitriol, and the curse had killed one magus.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Minor Site Hooks — Cursed (ars-magica-houses#044)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default curses can bypass ordinary site protection; a world can change what protections they overcome, with the cost of an enemy able to harm the covenant.

rules.statement: If the covenant fails a simple annual task, its aura falls by one point for the rest of that year. Symbolically reliving or repairing the event behind the damage can prevent the decline.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Minor Site Hooks — Flickering Aura (ars-magica-houses#044)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default the aura to lose one point for a year after a missed task; a world can change the task or decline, with recurring labor or a rite as the cost.

rules.statement: At one regio, the site sends members’ secret desires into the world, where they may take form and be harmed; the result can be mistaken for something another person wished to happen.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Minor Site Hooks — Regio (ars-magica-houses#044)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default the regio to manifest a member’s desire; a world can limit whose desires appear or how literally, at the cost of unpredictable consequences.

rules.statement: A recurring environmental hazard imposes a –1 penalty on exposed people’s Aging rolls. The Hook can be taken up to three times, and does not affect people with Hermetic longevity enchantments.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Minor Site Hooks — Unhealthy Environment (ars-magica-houses#044)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default each instance to a –1 Aging-roll penalty, stacking up to three times; a world can vary the hazard, while remediation costs magic or labor.

rules.statement: A covenant aura can twist people and structures toward a recurring theme; in one example, it reshapes the site into an ancient Egyptian village. Those changed gradually lose memories of their former identities and assume new roles.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Minor Site Hooks — Warping to a Pattern (ars-magica-houses#044)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default patterned warping to change people and buildings while eroding their old memories; a world can change the theme or pace, with loss of identity as the cost.

rules.statement: A resource with this Hook loses 10% of its original value each year and is exhausted within ten years unless action halts the decline.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Minor Resources Hooks — Dwindling Resource (ars-magica-houses#044)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default the resource to lose 10% of its original value each year; a world can alter the pace, with a story or other intervention needed to stop the loss.

rules.statement: A contested resource is available for five years after one story resolves the contest; the Hook can apply to multiple resources.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Minor Resources Hooks — Contested Resource (ars-magica-houses#044)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default one successful story to secure five years of access; a world can change the interval or contest, with repeated effort required to retain the resource.

rules.statement: Exposure to a castle puts people or interests within ten miles on notice of its presence; a supported knightly force can travel about twenty miles per day, allowing raids up to ten miles away and return before nightfall.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Fortifications — Castle (Major Hook) (ars-magica-houses#044)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default a castle to project military reach ten miles and become known to nearby interests; a world can change the reach, with political attention as the cost.

rules.statement: If loyalty is tracked separately for factions, a gain given to one faction reduces the loyalty points of every other faction by half the amount gained. When the gap between any factions’ Prevailing Loyalty reaches 3 or more points, a story arises from their conflict.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Divided Loyalty (ars-magica-houses#045)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to reducing rival factions’ loyalty by half the favored faction’s gain; a world can change the penalty or trigger threshold, reflecting how sharply favoritism breeds conflict.

rules.statement: A covenant with Loyal Covenfolk adds enough loyalty points to bring its Prevailing Loyalty to +3, or 30 loyalty points total. Rebellious Covenfolk instead subtracts enough points to reach −5, or −75 points, and disloyalty stories continue until morale improves.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Loyal Covenfolk; Rebellious Covenfolk (ars-magica-houses#045)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to setting loyalty at +30 or −75 points as specified; a world can change the target, with the in-world result being unusually dependable service or recurring disloyalty.

rules.statement: Diabolists whose minds have been clouded by their demon master appear normal under scrying and may temporarily forget their Infernal service. Rites have admitted the master and its minions through the Aegis, although the Aegis still restricts their supernatural abilities.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Diabolic Corruption (ars-magica-houses#045)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to hiding the servants and their master from scrying and bypassing the Aegis’s entry barrier while leaving its ability restrictions in force; a world can tune the concealment or bypass, at the cost of greater detection risk.

rules.statement: A curse can involuntarily make affected people live as wolves for years while retaining human intelligence and the ability to understand speech. Their altered bodies make them useful as guards and watchers on expeditions.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Useful Curse (ars-magica-houses#045)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a wolf form lasting years while preserving intelligence and speech comprehension; a world can vary the form or duration, with involuntariness and discomfort as the cost.

rules.statement: The covenant’s aura can alter its next generation along a shared theme: examples include every child being a twin, children being rare, or children having unusual traits or skills. Such changes can cause deaths in childbirth, population pressure, or dependence on immigration and remedies.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Infants (ars-magica-houses#045)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one consistent aura-driven pattern in children; a world can choose the pattern and its severity, with demographic and social consequences as the cost.

rules.statement: A powerful demon may cross the Aegis hidden inside a possessed covenfolk member, then use that host to harm people and recruit them to its service.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Possession Victim (ars-magica-houses#045)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to allowing the demon to enter concealed within its host; a world can limit what the host permits or what powers cross, while the demon’s presence creates a threat inside the covenant.

rules.statement: Some local forces hinder mundane intruders: fog can confuse attackers and warn residents, trails can misdirect tax collectors, and winds or storms can defend islands. These forces are generally ineffective against saints.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Defensive Environment (ars-magica-houses#045)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a local environmental defense that confounds ordinary intruders and can alert locals; a world can change its area or which threats it affects, with saints remaining an exception.

rules.statement: In a tithing miracle, goods sold after a tithe may weigh more than expected, up to the weight of the untithed material; some reported miracles increase the goods beyond even that amount.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Tithing Miracles (ars-magica-houses#045)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to restoring the tithe’s weight when goods are sold; a world can cap or exceed that increase, with the resulting wealth also strengthening the Church.

rules.statement: A covenant may use democracy, autocracy, hierarchy, bureaucracy, or anarchy, and can combine features of these models. Democracy gives magi equal standing and decides resource matters by consensus; autocracy leaves final decisions to one magus; hierarchy gives higher tiers greater rights and decision power; bureaucracy assigns areas of governance to offices; anarchy has no formal decision process, with nearby magi handling issues as they arise.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Chapter Three: Governance — Forms of Governance (ars-magica-houses#046)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one of the five governance templates; a world can tune how concentrated or distributed authority is, with the in-world tradeoff between efficient decisions and equal standing.

rules.statement: A covenant may require a quorum before a meeting can decide matters; more than half its members is a commonly reasonable threshold. Emergency meetings may use looser attendance and decision procedures, but should still avoid placing covenant safety entirely in one magus’s hands.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: The Council Meeting (ars-magica-houses#046)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a quorum above half for ordinary decisions; a world can lower the emergency threshold, at the cost of more decisions being made without broad consent.

rules.statement: A charter can specify who may vote and how votes count, including one vote per magus, weighted votes, officers’ extra or casting votes on matters in their remit, and how ties are resolved. It may also require a majority, a set threshold, or unanimity; abstentions and absences count differently under the stated majority procedures.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: The Charter of Covenant — Method of Governance; Examples of Vote-Taking (ars-magica-houses#046)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one vote per member and a simple majority of votes cast; a world can require higher thresholds or weight votes, at the cost of slower decisions or unequal influence.

rules.statement: A covenant oath commits members to support and maintain one another. A charter may define members’ entitlements, duties, and consequences for failure; if a Quaesitor notarizes it, the charter is enforceable under the Tribunal’s Peripheral Code.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: The Charter of Covenant (ars-magica-houses#046)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to an oath treated as binding by covenant custom; a world can make a notarized charter legally enforceable, with breach risking Tribunal-backed consequences.

rules.statement: A charter may reserve covenant vis for collective needs, distribute the remainder to members, require members to petition for shares, or leave vis with individuals. It may also require a yearly vis tithe, including to cover the Aegis of the Hearth.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Covenant Resources — Member Rights (ars-magica-houses#046)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to collective collection followed by distribution after covenant needs; a world can make shares need-based or individual, trading predictable communal supply against members’ personal control.

rules.statement: A powerful aura can benefit a covenant but expose covenfolk living within it to Warping; the Powerful Location example says almost all of them suffer it.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Covenant Situations — Powerful Location (ars-magica-houses#046)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a strong aura that provides useful power while warping most resident covenfolk; a world can soften or intensify the cost, with exposure to the aura as the cause.

rules.statement: The Hermetic Market’s truth effect has Penetration 15, though many believe it is higher: broken oaths make liars’ tongues bleed, forged items reveal themselves by chance, and false measures fail or refuse to weigh.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Covenant Situations — Hermetic Market (ars-magica-houses#046)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the listed truth effects at Penetration 15; a world can raise the effective strength, at the cost of making the site’s law harder to evade.

rules.statement: At the Worshipful covenant, the season remains fixed at harvest, keeping peasants busy and producing a great agricultural surplus, which is used to supply the Blackberry God with beer.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Covenant Situations — Worshipful (ars-magica-houses#046)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to an unchanging harvest season and surplus; a world can alter the scope or yield of the seasonal rule, with the surplus directed toward the god’s demands.

rules.statement: A covenant may let members keep vis found on adventures, but renewable vis sources usually belong to the covenant; a different allocation policy can encourage secrecy and cheating. The charter may also reserve access to shared resources for senior members or set limits on individual requests for covenant-funded purchases.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Covenant charter discussion (ars-magica-houses#047)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to personal ownership of adventure finds and communal ownership of renewable sources; a world can extend communal claims to all finds, at the cost of increased secrecy and disputes.

rules.statement: A charter can reward work for the covenant with a fixed reward per task or a portion of yearly resource income; members may also be assigned recurring or ad hoc duties. The council's power to compel such duties, and how obligations are distributed, should be specified.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Member Obligations (ars-magica-houses#047)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to duties and rewards defined by charter; a world can let councils assign extra tasks, at the cost of member consent and possible legal conflict.

rules.statement: In the sample service scheme, one share is an equal portion of half the covenant's vis stores on the day after the Winter Solstice, or its money equivalent. One Standard Service is one season at low risk, one month at moderate risk, or one day at high risk; service within the previous eight seasons earns one annual share, an equivalent Additional Service earns at most one extra share annually, and delinquent members receive no share until arrears are made up.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: The Carrot and the Stick (ars-magica-houses#047)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the stated service thresholds and annual share cap; a world can alter service periods or the half-store pool, balancing covenant needs against members' time and resources.

rules.statement: A covenant cannot change a member's charter obligations without that member's agreement under the stated Tribunal policy; doing so can constitute a High Crime. Censure for charter breach may include expulsion or withholding common resources, but withholding a member's own property may violate the Oath of Hermes.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Obligations and the Code of Hermes; Censure (ars-magica-houses#047)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to enforce only agreed charter terms and withhold communal property; a world can permit stricter enforcement, at the cost of legal sanctions or loss of trust.

rules.statement: In the sample council, four regular meetings occur each year, on the first day of each stellar season, and more than half the council must attend for a quorum; without a quorum, only ordinary matters may be enacted. Significant matters need a majority by member, consequential matters a majority by vote, ordinary matters need two votes, and the leader breaks ties.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Example of a Complex Method of Governance (ars-magica-houses#047)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the sample meeting and voting thresholds; a world can change quorum or voting rules, trading decision speed against member representation.

rules.statement: Prevailing Loyalty starts with the sum of magi's Gift modifiers divided by the number of magi: no Gift and Gentle Gift are 0, standard Gift is –30, and Blatant Gift is –105. Add situational loyalty points, then convert the total using the advancement table; each individual may differ from the covenant average by up to three points either way, apart from stated exceptions.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Calculating Prevailing Loyalty (ars-magica-houses#047)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to averaged Gift modifiers plus situational points; a world can weight particular groups or circumstances differently, with loyalty reflecting social treatment and familiarity.

rules.statement: Familiarity adds two loyalty points for each year a covenant exists, up to the amount needed to offset its negative Base Loyalty; newly recruited covenfolk dilute these points in proportion to their share of the population. A bad local Reputation costs five points per Reputation level, while a good one adds five if covenfolk know of or benefit from it.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Familiarity; Reputation (ars-magica-houses#047)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to yearly familiarity gains capped at the Gift penalty and five points per Reputation level; a world can change the rate or cap, making loyalty more or less resistant to time and public standing.

rules.statement: A magus's direct wound to a covenfolk member loses loyalty points according to wound severity; magical wounds count as one category worse, and an accidental wound in covenant defense halves the loss after that adjustment. Personally healing a wound gains the equivalent penalty back, increased by one level if magic is conspicuously used.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Wounds; Altruism (ars-magica-houses#047)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to severity-based loyalty changes with the magical-wound adjustment; a world can soften or intensify these consequences, reflecting how covenfolk judge magi's actions.

rules.statement: A Mentem ritual can affect a group of up to 100 people for a year, setting each person's Loyal to Covenant trait to +4 and overriding normal Prevailing Loyalty effects. Each affected person immediately gains 1 Warping Point, then 5 over the year and 5 more for every later year maintained; after the first year each has Warping Score 1 and gains Simple-Minded or Short Attention Span as a first Minor Flaw.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Instant Loyalty of the Rebellious Turb (ars-magica-houses#047)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the listed group size, duration, loyalty, and escalating Warping cost; a world can lower the cost or strengthen the effect, risking lasting mental harm and flaws.

rules.statement: Rego craft rearranges only supplied material, so every component of the finished object must be present; it cannot create matter or perform changes that are destruction or magical inspection. A Finesse check is required, with a target at least 3 above the equivalent mundane craft task; failure produces unusable work, while a botch can leave a hidden defect.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Rego Craft Magic (ars-magica-houses#048)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to requiring source materials and a Finesse check at mundane difficulty +3; a world can raise the target for speed or processing complexity, because rushed or intricate magical workmanship is riskier.

rules.statement: For Rego craft, reducing a month's work to an instant adds +3 to the Finesse target, a season adds +6, and a year adds +9; temporary processing materials can add +3 or more. Extending the spell's duration generally repeats the same operation on the original materials instead of continuing useful work.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Rego Craft Magic (ars-magica-houses#048)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one operation on the materials; turn the time-compression and processing-material modifiers upward for faster or more elaborate work, with increased failure risk as the cost.

rules.statement: A Rego craft spell or device can perform only a craft-like rearrangement, not create matter, kill living things, or inspect an object's history. Creo can move material toward an ideal form, while Perdo makes things more flawed rather than selectively removing imperfections.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Rego Craft Magic (ars-magica-houses#048)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.mechanism: law: craft magic rearranges supplied material
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to separating rearrangement, creation, destruction, and inspection by magical technique; a world can broaden craft effects, but would need to pay for the extra capability through a different magical method.

rules.statement: The cattle-milking spell uses the caster's Perception plus Finesse instead of a farmer's Animal Handling. Its target is at least 6 for familiar, undisturbed cattle, but starts at 15 or higher for cattle unused to magical milking and drops through 12 and 9 to 6 as successful milking accustoms them; a failed check may frighten them.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: A Spell to Milk Cattle (ars-magica-houses#048)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to substituting Finesse for animal-handling skill and setting the target by familiarity; a world can make animals adapt faster or slower, with disturbance and fear as the practical cost.

rules.statement: Rego craft devices let users make objects through a Finesse check, usually at a target 3 above the comparable craft task; weak results can be poor, and botches may hide flaws. Devices can be reused, but require time and vis to create, and their users may lack the specialist skill to operate them well.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Magical Alternatives to Covenfolk (ars-magica-houses#048)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a fixed, repeatable device effect with a user check when workmanship matters; a world can add more uses or user flexibility, at the expense of creation resources or poorer control.

rules.statement: The enchanted porter moves an inanimate object while its glove remains against it and the user moves; when contact ends, the object settles to the ground. The device can be used 24 times per day and maintains concentration itself.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: The Enchanted Porter (ars-magica-houses#048)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to moving one touched object only while the user maintains contact; a world can extend duration or uses, with greater device investment as the cost.

rules.statement: The provision chest prevents stored food from decaying while its door is closed; taking the food out ends the preservation, leaving it as fresh as when stored.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: The Vitalizer of Provisions (ars-magica-houses#048)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to preserving only contents inside a closed container; a world can permit preservation after removal, but should charge for a longer-lasting or portable effect.

rules.statement: The raven skinchanger can change into a raven form whose Intelligence remains human while the other characteristics are those of a raven; the form has size –3 and receives a +3 Soak bonus from the Skinchanger trait.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Spouse with a Secret (Skinchanger) — Raven Form (ars-magica-houses#048)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a fixed animal form with human Intelligence and the specified form statistics; a world can allow other forms, with their own traits and balancing costs.

rules.statement: Once the hound has a creature’s scent, it can track that creature without being misled by ordinary trail tricks; if the target has Magic Resistance, the effect must penetrate it.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: The Inexorable Hunter (ars-magica-houses#049)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to flawless scent-tracking once a target is scented; a world can make supernatural resistance defeat it, requiring the hunter to overcome Magic Resistance.

rules.statement: The collar continuously transforms a normal hound into an upright servant with hands and grog-level intellect while preserving its houndlike appearance and loyalty; the constant effect causes Warping over time.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Lesser Device: The Marvelous Hound (ars-magica-houses#049)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a lasting device transformation; a world can make continuous magic accumulate Warping, with the cost falling on the transformed creature.

rules.statement: The portal can be activated only from within the covenant and transports a group of people seen by its operators from as far as 500 paces; it has 24 uses per day, requires no Arcane Connection, and targets with Magic Resistance may resist.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Fantastical Device: The Remote Entrance Portal (ars-magica-houses#049)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to controlled one-way access for observed visitors; a world can allow resistance or limit access to 24 daily activations to preserve security and constrain use.

rules.statement: A ghost can become fully invisible or remain insubstantial, passing freely through physical objects; its physical combat statistics apply against other ghosts, while its touch can affect corporeal targets without being stopped by armor or parrying.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Ghostly Warden — Powers (ars-magica-houses#049)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to ghosts being physically intangible and able to conceal themselves; a world can limit their ability to affect the living or make such contact costly.

rules.statement: A covenant begins with one Typical income source, or may instead take two Lesser sources; annual income benchmarks are 40 pounds for Lesser, 100 for Typical, 250 for Greater, and 1,000 for Legendary, while no source yields zero.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Baseline; Source of Income Categories (ars-magica-houses#049)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to category-based annual income; a world can change source categories or starting reserves to reflect the covenant’s prosperity.

rules.statement: Each year, a source’s income is multiplied by the selected result: Slump 0.5, Contraction 0.8, Stagnation 0.95, Status Quo 1, Growth 1.05, Expansion 1.2, or Boom 1.5; changes are usually permanent, though some last only one year.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Improvement; Income Modification (ars-magica-houses#049)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to stable income unless the storyguide selects a change; a world can make effects temporary or permanent according to whether they reflect a passing event or lasting change.

rules.statement: A covenant may create at most 2 pounds of silver per magus per year under the described Tribunal limits, even if a spell creates much more at once; magical wealth creation also takes seasons and vis and can attract scrutiny or inflation.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Magical Improvement (ars-magica-houses#049)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a per-magus annual cap of 2 pounds of created silver; a world can impose the limit to curb inflation and reduce unwanted attention.

rules.statement: The coin spell makes its target forget having paid a coin, so a person who still has a reason to pay may offer another; the described toll arrangement uses this to collect payment twice.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: The Twice-Gifted Coin (ars-magica-houses#049)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to erasing the memory of a specific payment; a world can restrict the effect to that transaction, leaving the target’s other memories intact.

rules.statement: At year-end, add one-off purchases and other sundry costs to the covenant’s regular yearly expenditure, subtract the total from its income, and adjust its stores by the resulting surplus or shortfall.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Expenditure (ars-magica-houses#050)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to settling the budget yearly; a world can change the accounting period, reflecting how often its covenant reckons income and expenses.

rules.statement: For inhabitants’ upkeep, a magus or noble counts as 5 points in Spring or Winter and 10 in Summer or Autumn; a companion counts as 3 or 5, respectively. Other resident categories have listed values, while magi may reduce their cost to 3 by accepting poorer conditions or to 2 by living like standard covenfolk.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Points of Inhabitants (ars-magica-houses#050)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the listed seasonal point costs; a world can lower them for austere living, at the cost of privilege and potentially social standing.

rules.statement: A covenant needs 2 servants per 10 points of inhabitants, counting neither laborers, servants, nor teamsters in the initial total. It then needs 1 teamster per 10 points of the total excluding laborers and teamsters, after subtracting twice the number of laborers.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Covenfolk Categories (ars-magica-houses#050)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the stated staffing formulas; a world can allow fewer staff, at the cost of overwork or reduced services.

rules.statement: Laboratory points depend on Upkeep: a laboratory at 0 is worth 10 points, one at +2 is worth 30, and one at +3 is worth 60; above +2, each increase adds 10 times the new Upkeep score. For maintenance, multiply costs by 0.5 for light use, 1 for typical use, or 1.5 for heavy use.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Points of Laboratories (ars-magica-houses#050)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to Upkeep-based points and use multipliers; a world can simplify the scale, trading precision for easier covenant accounting.

rules.statement: Each laborer reduces Provisions expenditure by 1 pound, but laborers’ savings cannot exceed half of the Provisions total. They also reduce the teamster requirement by one for every five laborers.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Cost Saving — Laborers (ars-magica-houses#050)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the stated savings and caps; a world can raise the cap when a covenant relies more heavily on local food production.

rules.statement: A common craftsman saves 1 pound plus half their Craft Ability, rounded down; a rare craftsman saves a number of pounds equal to their Craft Ability. Each craft is separately limited to saving either 20% or 50% of the relevant expenditure category, as listed for that craft.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Cost Saving — Craftsmen (ars-magica-houses#050)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the listed craft savings and percentage caps; a world can adjust caps to match actual demand for a craft.

rules.statement: Each magnitude of effect in a magical item can save about 1 pound yearly, while a Ritual spell can save about 5 pounds per magnitude. Magical items may replace labor or craft work, and the required servant or teamster minimums may be reduced accordingly.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Cost Saving — Magic (ars-magica-houses#050)
rules.speaker: rulebook
