rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the stated annual savings estimates; a world can change the value per magnitude, reflecting the expense or scarcity of effective magic.

rules.statement: Inflation begins at 0 in a covenant’s first year and is suggested to rise by 1 pound per 100 pounds of expenditure each year. It may stay level in favorable years, rise faster in bad years, and should not rise in a year when expenditure falls.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Yearly Expenditure Categories — Inflation (ars-magica-houses#050)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the suggested annual increase; a world can make inflation fluctuate with conditions, reflecting local economic pressures.

rules.statement: When a covenant is short of money, it may cut wages, lay off staff, or neglect upkeep and provisions; reduced wages or neglect can damage Loyalty, while falling below minimum staffing can cause operational problems.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Emergency Savings (ars-magica-houses#050)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to allowing emergency cuts with consequences; a world can soften or intensify those consequences, reflecting how resilient or dependent the community is.

rules.statement: The golden apple tree yields six apples yearly, but three must be left to decay at its roots. Each missing apple adds one botch die to the stress roll, and every botch permanently lowers the tree’s annual yield by one apple.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Golden apple tree (opening passage) (ars-magica-houses#051)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to leaving three apples unharvested; the covenant can turn the harvest dial, but taking more risks permanently reducing future yield.

rules.statement: A single apple’s flesh sustains a person for a week and gives +6 to rolls to resist illness; each apple also contains Creo vis.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Golden apple tree (opening passage) (ars-magica-houses#051)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to treating each apple as a week of food and illness protection; a world can alter potency, with the limited yearly crop as the cost.

rules.statement: The Crone menstruates only once every two lunar cycles, and her menstrual blood contains Creo vis. Her blood is a powerful Arcane Connection to her; she may trade it for magical services benefiting her village, but will not deal with hostile magi.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: The Crone’s Blood (ars-magica-houses#051)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a two-lunar-cycle supply and a non-hostile exchange; the world can change access, with the Crone’s safety and village welfare at stake.

rules.statement: Golden maggots from the meadow’s corpses contain Creo vis; about six can be collected each summer. They live about a day unless kept with rotting flesh.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: A Foul Gift from a Festering Meadow (ars-magica-houses#051)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to roughly six maggots per summer and a one-day lifespan; a world can increase preservation, at the cost of keeping them with carrion.

rules.statement: The Lens of Wisdom can create one parchment page each year when noon solstice sunlight is focused through it onto blank parchment; the page contains Intellego vis, and removing the vis makes its writing fade.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Intellego — The Lens of Wisdom (ars-magica-houses#051)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one vis-bearing page per year; a world can change the rate, while each extraction destroys the writing.

rules.statement: Following the standing stones alone, away from the covenant, from dawn on the Autumnal Equinox reveals an additional stone and puts Intellego vis in the follower’s shoes; this can be done yearly.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Intellego — The Waystones (ars-magica-houses#051)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the solitary equinox route and annual yield; a world can vary the path, with isolation and exact timing limiting collection.

rules.statement: The Tree of Truth’s fruit clears the mind and helps its eater perceive the truth in a situation; the fruit also yields Intellego vis.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Intellego — The Tree of Truth (ars-magica-houses#051)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to clearer judgment after eating the bitter fruit; a world can deepen the insight, with the fruit’s availability and possible effects on the soul as limits.

rules.statement: Unhatched metallic-looking cocoons contain one pawn of Muto vis each and must be collected before sunset on the butterflies’ synchronized hatching day, July 20, or their power dissipates.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Muto — The Chrysalis of Rebirth (ars-magica-houses#051)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one pawn per intact cocoon collected by sunset; a world can extend the window, while a crowded field and rapid dissipation make gathering costly.

rules.statement: In the workshop, scraps from ordinary craftwork provide Muto vis; collecting more than half the annual amount requires magi to assist so much that grogs ask for spells, which reduce next year’s scraps. Deliberate breakage can add a stress die, but a botch causes a serious mishap or exposes the manipulation.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Muto — Covenant Workshop (ars-magica-houses#051)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to ordinary craft scraps and leave the yield at half or less; the world can reward extra maintenance or sabotage, risking worker resentment and damage.

rules.statement: At the lake’s first-snowfall storm, water collected as it turns to ice contains Muto vis; Snow and Wind may play tricks on collectors but do not object to their presence.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Muto — First Freeze of the Winter Spirits (ars-magica-houses#051)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to gathering during the few hours of the first-snowfall storm; a world can broaden the window, but exposure to cold and spirits’ pranks remains the cost.

rules.statement: A person remaining in the fetid meadow for more than a few moments must make a Stamina roll against Ease Factor 6 to avoid retching.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: A Foul Gift from a Festering Meadow (ars-magica-houses#051)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to requiring the EF 6 check after a short stay; a world can raise or lower the threshold, with the odor creating the hazard.

rules.statement: The butterflies hatch together at dawn on July 20; intact unhatched cocoons may contain Muto vis, but the vis dissipates after sunset unless harvested.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Muto — The Chrysalis of Rebirth (ars-magica-houses#051)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a sunset deadline; a world can shift it, while the synchronized hatch creates a short, labor-intensive harvest period.

rules.statement: Complete silence in the echo cave produces Imaginem vis, but magically silencing the cave prevents that production; merely blocking incoming sounds does not. Echoes take at least eight hours to fade, and the vis can be gathered with Rego Imaginem only while the cave is completely silent; gathering it causes noise that takes days to fade.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: The Sound of Silence (ars-magica-houses#052)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to requiring genuine silence and allowing vis to form only after echoes fade; a world could change the eight-hour and days-long periods, with silence and disruptive noise as the costs.

rules.statement: The silver coffer turns nearby stray thoughts into coins, each holding one pawn of Mentem vis; intense thoughts may also create an Arcane Connection to their thinker. It stops collecting when full and must be emptied before it can collect more.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: The Box of Unguarded Thoughts (ars-magica-houses#052)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to storing thoughts as one-pawn coins until the coffer fills; a world could set its capacity or allow thought extraction, risking magical spying and Arcane Connections.

rules.statement: Only women who have children and no man present can hear the nymph's sobbing. Listening causes overwhelming sorrow and regret, and tears collected in the purest vials contain Mentem vis.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Howling of the Winds (ars-magica-houses#052)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to restricting the sound to the stated listeners and making sorrow the cost; a world could broaden who hears it or alter the emotion and vis yield.

rules.statement: The goblin's stalagmite grows upward by a hand's breadth each season, and each season's growth can be ground into Terram vis. If left unbroken, it reaches the ceiling in three score years; it is narrow enough to snap off at its base.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: The Cave of the Nameless Goblin (ars-magica-houses#052)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to seasonal growth that can be harvested for vis; a world could change the rate or make breaking the stalagmite harder, affecting the goblin's eventual release.

rules.statement: At dawn, passing through the surviving doorway stones from outside to inside admits anyone to a level 1 Magical regio; crossing is possible only during the sun's rising. Visitors without another exit must stay overnight, and the villa gradually restores itself during their stay, reaching full glory after a month.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: The Auberge (ars-magica-houses#052)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a dawn-only doorway with overnight confinement; a world could widen the crossing window or provide another exit, changing the risk and duration of a visit.

rules.statement: Leaving one pawn each of Creo, Perdo, Rego, Muto, and Intellego vis around the cave's inscribed circle for a full season produces Vim vis at its center. At season's end both the invested Technique vis and the Vim vis can be recovered, or the Technique vis can remain to generate more Vim vis.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: The Cave of Magic (ars-magica-houses#052)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to requiring all five Technique pawns and a full season for Vim vis; a world could alter the inputs or duration, with the invested vis tied up until harvest.

rules.statement: A book gains one quality point from purchased resonant materials and two from story-acquired rare materials; clarifying it can add one more point. Clarification requires a relevant Art score of at least 15 or mastery of a relevant spell, and the book must spend 12 divided by aura strength years in a Magical aura; it crumbles if removed from one.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Extended Suggestions on the Quality of Books — Resonances (ars-magica-houses#052)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a maximum three-point resonance bonus and aura-dependent years of clarification; a world could change the prerequisites or bonus, with the book's survival bound to a Magical aura.

rules.statement: Casting tablets let a magus cast a spell whose intricacies he has not learned through laboratory research, but the method is dangerous because he cannot control the borrowed power accurately and is inflexible.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Opus Types — Casting Tablets (ars-magica-houses#052)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to permitting only the tablet's specified spell while imposing danger from poor control; a world could make tablet casting safer or more flexible, at the cost of weakening its limitation.

rules.statement: A casting tablet fixes the spell’s Range, Duration, Target, size, vis amount and Arts, and any Arcane Connection type when it is written; the caster cannot change these choices. Tablet spells gain no Penetration bonus unless the author built it into the spell’s level, though rituals can be cast from tablets.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Casting tablets (ars-magica-houses#053)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to tablets enforcing every written choice; a setting can loosen this for adaptable casting, at the cost of departing from the author’s design.

rules.statement: When a tablet user leads a Wizard’s Communion, a botch by any participant also makes the leader botch. The writer’s sigil remains visible alongside the caster’s.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Casting tablets (ars-magica-houses#053)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to shared botch consequences for a tablet-led Communion; a world could remove the leader’s exposure, reducing the danger of coordinating group magic.

rules.statement: For Formulaic and Ritual spells, subtract spell level from the Casting Total to determine the result. A result of 0 or better casts the spell at a cost of one Fatigue level; −1 to −10 costs two, −11 to −20 costs three, and −21 to −30 casts it, gives one Warping Point, and costs four. At −31 or below the spell fails, costs five Fatigue levels, and gives Warping Points equal to its magnitude; gaining at least two Warping Points also requires a Twilight check. Formulaic Fatigue loss is short-term and Ritual loss is long-term.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Casting Total table (ars-magica-houses#053)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the stated escalating Fatigue and Warping costs; a world could soften or steepen the thresholds, trading accessibility against the danger of magical strain.

rules.statement: Only a magus who has mastered a spell may author its casting tablet, but magi may copy tablets written by others. Tablet production does not teach a spell; at covenant creation, tablets cost two Build Points per five spell levels.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Casting tablets (ars-magica-houses#053)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to mastery being required to author, but not to copy or cast; a world could restrict copying to protect secret spells, at the cost of wider access.

rules.statement: A student must study a summa for at least one season before studying its commentary. A commentary has a +1 quality bonus that does not increase its Build Point cost.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Other Opus Types — Commentaries (ars-magica-houses#053)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to requiring prior study and granting the fixed bonus; a world could remove the prerequisite for easier scholarship, weakening the special role of commentaries.

rules.statement: A magus gains experience from only one correspondence each season, and only if its theme relates to the magus’s research or reading, the previous letter was read before replying, and at least one letter arrived that season. Useful correspondence grants one extra experience point that season.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Other Opus Types — Correspondences (ars-magica-houses#053)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one eligible correspondence and one bonus experience point per season; a world could allow several, accelerating learning in exchange for greater scholarly obligations.

rules.statement: A florilegium’s editor can include no more tractatus than half the editor’s Ability score or one fifth of the editor’s Art score, and needs at least twice that many source tractatus plus an Ability score of 6 or an Art score of 20. Eligible books gain +1 quality; an editor with an Ability score of 10 or Art score of 35, working from at least five times as many source tractatus, grants +2 instead. Each collection takes a season to assemble.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Other Opus Types — Florilegia (ars-magica-houses#053)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the stated expertise and source-library thresholds; a world could lower them for easier compilation, making unusually resonant collections more common.

rules.statement: A qualified reader can gloss a book during a season and raise its quality by 1, but repeated glossing cannot add further quality. An author can spend a season annotating a summa to raise its level by one third of the difference between the author’s current Art score and the score when the summa was written.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Other Opus Types — Glossed books and inspeximus (ars-magica-houses#053)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one quality point from glossing and a one-third level increase from authorial revision; a world could permit further revisions, at the cost of making old books improve indefinitely.

rules.statement: A library catalog acts as an arcane connection to the collection and its books. Only the newest accurate copy works as the library’s proxy; binding the library to its catalog takes a season and one pawn of Vim vis, and must be repeated if every catalog copy is destroyed.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Accession — Catalog as Proxy (ars-magica-houses#054)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to allowing magic aimed through the catalog while books are in the library; a world can require a current, accurate catalog, because the proxy is the collection’s protective link.

rules.statement: Poor reading conditions can impose a quality penalty of up to –6, at the storyguide’s discretion; magical comforts provide no bonus over the assumed optimal conditions. Research uses an Intelligence + Ability roll, with a library bonus from +1 for a few relevant books to +5 for a peerless collection; a significant magical item can add its own bonus, such as +3 to medical research.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Use — Study; Use — Research (ars-magica-houses#054)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the listed research bonuses and a maximum –6 study penalty; a world can make conditions or unusual items more consequential, because comfort and specialized holdings affect access to knowledge.

rules.statement: A mystical event can substitute for study from a number of pawns of vis equal to one-fifth of the highest Might among the creatures involved, rounded up. The magus must spend an entire season studying the event’s lessons, even if the event itself is brief.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Alternatives to Books — Phenomena — Significatos (ars-magica-houses#054)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one season of study and the rounded-up Might-based limit; a world can vary which events qualify, because mystical insight depends on the phenomenon and its participants.

rules.statement: A realia collection is studied like a tractatus: its quality depends on its unique, informative specimens, and it can be studied as many times as its quality. A quality-6 collection requires 32 excellent specimens; splitting it for simultaneous study creates smaller collections, and each study still counts against the complete collection’s use limit.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Alternatives to Books — Phenomena — Realia (ars-magica-houses#054)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one permitted study per quality level; a world can allow more or fewer uses, because the value lies in a finite set of distinctive specimens.

rules.statement: Great Works function as summae or tractatus, but cost at least 100 Mythic Pounds or equivalent magical resources to build. They cannot gain quality bonuses from scribing, binding, or illumination, but receive triple the usual bonus from resonant materials and clarification.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Alternatives to Books — Information — Great Works (ars-magica-houses#054)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the stated minimum cost and triple resonance and clarification benefits; a world can change the investment, because large-scale learning structures trade resources for unusual teaching forms.

rules.statement: A magus may have only one sanctum at a time; it must be marked with a square, circle, diagonal lines, and the owner’s name. The Code permits the owner to slay a magus trespassing there without penalty, and some Tribunals limit how often the sanctum may be changed.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Chapter Eight: Sanctum (ars-magica-houses#054)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one legally marked sanctum and the stated protection against penalty for killing a trespassing magus; a world can impose stricter change limits, because Tribunal law controls the privilege.

rules.statement: Ring-and-circle wards can bar mundane people, pests, or fire without vis; wards at entrances do not warp those inside. Defacing the circle can break the ward, so durable versions are carved into stone or fixed in metal.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Chapter Eight: Sanctum — Ring and Circle Wards (ars-magica-houses#054)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a ward that blocks its specified mundane target until its circle is defaced; a world can make the circle more or less durable, because the ward’s boundary is its vulnerability.

rules.statement: A standard laboratory has one 500-square-foot chamber with a ten-foot ceiling, sturdy walls and roof, and equipment costing five Mythic Pounds. A worker with Magic Theory 3 or higher needs two seasons to set it up: after the first season and three pounds it functions with a –3 penalty to Lab Totals, and the second season and remaining two pounds remove that penalty.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Chapter Nine: Laboratories — The Standard Hermetic Laboratory (ars-magica-houses#054)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the stated two-season, five-pound setup and temporary –3 penalty; a world can penalize nonstandard spaces or low skill further, because a functioning lab depends on space, materials, and expertise.

rules.statement: A standard season assumes ten hours of laboratory work per day, six days each week, leaving about ten rest days. Up to ten missed workdays can be made up on rest days without penalty; more than ten days away reduces the Lab Total, and working fewer than ten hours daily reduces the season’s Lab or Advancement Total by 10% per missing hour.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Life in the Laboratory (ars-magica-houses#055)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the stated work schedule and absence limits; a world can make lab work more or less forgiving, with lost research time or reduced output as the cost.

rules.statement: Non-standard schedules can raise a season’s Lab Total, but their fatigue, health, Warping, and botch consequences apply as specified for each routine. Multiple routines stack, except that Overtime, Double Overtime, and Triple Overtime cannot combine with one another, nor can Early Riser combine with Nocturnal; disruption removes the bonus but not the penalties.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Non-Standard Laboratory Routines (ars-magica-houses#055)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to cumulative bonuses and costs with the stated incompatibilities; a world can tune the reward and strain, paid for with fatigue, danger, or deterioration.

rules.statement: A lab’s Virtue points minus Flaw points cannot exceed Size plus Refinement. Each point of Size or Refinement raises that limit by one; positive occupied Size reduces base Safety, and every full two points of unused excess Size requires an Empty Flaw.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Laboratory Characteristics — Size (ars-magica-houses#055)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the point-capacity and Safety formulas; a world can change how much space supports improvements, at the cost of greater hazards or unused-room drawbacks.

rules.statement: Increasing Refinement by one requires a season of work, familiarity with the lab, and Magic Theory at least three points higher than the desired Refinement. Each increase makes one more point available for Virtues, lowers occupied Size by one, and improves Safety by one or two points.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Laboratory Characteristics — Refinement (ars-magica-houses#055)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one season per improvement and the stated prerequisites; a world can make optimization faster or slower, with the time and expertise invested as the cost.

rules.statement: Safety is subtracted from botch dice on laboratory activities. If Safety is negative, each work season has an accident check: a simple die result no greater than its absolute value triggers a botch roll with at least one die, and a resulting botch causes a disaster with its risk modifier increased by that absolute value, to a maximum of +3.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Laboratory Characteristics — Safety (ars-magica-houses#055)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the seasonal accident check for unsafe labs; a world can soften or intensify the hazard, with risk to the magus and covenant as the cost.

rules.statement: For each season of work in a lab with positive Warping, roll a simple die; a result no greater than the Warping score warps that season’s product. An odd result produces a side effect and an even result a modified effect, chosen to fit the source of the Warping.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Laboratory Characteristics — Warping (ars-magica-houses#055)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a per-season chance of source-themed alteration; a world can change the threshold or severity, with unpredictable products as the price.

rules.statement: A lab’s General Quality modifies all Lab Totals, while each applicable Specialization adds its rating to relevant Lab Totals; Specialization bonuses stack. A lab may have at most two activity Specializations and four Art Specializations, including no more than two Techniques.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Laboratory Characteristics — General Quality; Laboratory Specializations (ars-magica-houses#055)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to additive bonuses within the listed specialization caps; a world can broaden or narrow supported work, at the cost of lab space and specialization choices.

rules.statement: A Minor Virtue normally takes one season to install and a Major Virtue two seasons; the worker needs Magic Theory at least three higher than the lab’s Refinement. If maintenance is unaffordable, after two seasons of use a lab gains a Flaw or loses a Virtue that lowers Upkeep; this repeats after each further two seasons if needed.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Laboratory Virtues and Flaws — Virtues; Laboratory Characteristics — Upkeep (ars-magica-houses#055)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the listed construction time, skill threshold, and two-season neglect interval; a world can make improvements or upkeep more demanding, paid for with seasons, money, or lost benefits.

rules.statement: For an experienced magus, subtract the Build Point value of a lab’s Virtues from the magus’s experience points, not the covenant’s Build Points. Each Minor Virtue takes one season and costs 10 points; each Major Virtue takes two seasons and costs 20 points.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Laboratory Build Points (opening paragraphs) (ars-magica-houses#056)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to charging the magus for improvements they personally made; a world can change the season and point costs to reflect how long laboratory construction takes.

rules.statement: When a new owner takes over a unique lab with positive Refinement, they must spend a season rearranging and exploring it before use. Its resulting Refinement is the lower of its old score and the new owner’s Magic Theory minus 3; if that leaves too many Virtues, some are lost. A failed secret Perception + Magic Theory check against three times the old Refinement adds Predecessor, and a botch adds Hidden Defect as well.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Taking Over a Laboratory (ars-magica-houses#056)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to requiring a season and limiting inherited refinement by the new owner’s skill; a world can make old labs easier or harder to adapt to explain how idiosyncratic their prior owner’s methods were.

rules.statement: A lab with one central Feature improves activities connected to it but makes unrelated activities less effective; it can have only one such focus. Building a Lesser Feature takes one season and a Greater Feature takes two; they provide one and three Specialization points, respectively.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Laboratory Features (ars-magica-houses#056)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one specialized focus that trades general usefulness for stronger focused work; a world can adjust the construction time and bonuses to make specialized facilities common or exceptional.

rules.statement: A magic item or enchantment that duplicates an existing laboratory Virtue or Flaw grants it immediately without using space. Otherwise, each 10 effect levels adds one Specialization point or each 20 levels adds one Characteristic point; a powerful effect across the whole lab may also increase Warping at the storyguide’s discretion.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Magic Items for Laboratories (ars-magica-houses#056)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to converting effect levels into lab improvements at the stated rates; a world can make powerful whole-lab enchantments riskier by assigning them Warping.

rules.statement: Moving a lab without magic takes one season to pack it, transport costs equal to two years of maintenance and may cause breakage, and reassembly takes two seasons. Magic can avoid the mundane move’s breakage and expense; the process is time-consuming enough that magi often abandon or donate old labs instead.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Moving a Laboratory (ars-magica-houses#056)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the stated time and maintenance cost for mundane relocation; a world can reduce those costs with magic, while treating breakage and labor as the price of ordinary transport.

rules.statement: If the lab lacks ingredients for a particular Technique or two particular Forms, the relevant Lab Totals are halved. A lack of equipment can instead make one selected activity category, or two non-Items/Spells/Texts categories, impossible; that equipment flaw can be taken no more than twice.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Free Outfittings Flaws: Missing Ingredients and Minor Outfittings Flaws: Missing Equipment (ars-magica-houses#056)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to halving work hindered by missing ingredients and forbidding work without essential equipment; a world can broaden or narrow these shortages to reflect local supply and laboratory technology.

rules.statement: Taking over a positive-Refinement lab designed for transient use, or a lab with Refinement zero or less, requires no change to its statistics and allows work to begin immediately.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Taking Over a Laboratory (ars-magica-houses#056)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to immediate use for adaptable or unrefined labs; a world can require a settling-in period if even temporary facilities are culturally or magically unfamiliar.

rules.statement: A Mental Construct lab cannot exceed the magus’s Intelligence in Size. Without sophisticated magic, it cannot be used to bond with a familiar, enchant items, make Longevity Rituals, teach, or probably extract vis, though spell invention, Laboratory Text work, and Art study remain possible.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Major Supernatural Flaws: Mental Construct (ars-magica-houses#056)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to limiting an imagined lab by the owner’s Intelligence and excluding listed activities; a world can permit further uses through sophisticated magic, at the cost of that special capability.

rules.statement: Each regularly used non-Ritual laboratory spell adds 1 Warping to the lab or subtracts 1 from its Safety. Spells whose Arts match the Arts being used for a Lab Total cannot add a bonus to that total through General Quality or a Specialization; effects from vis, magic items, external sources, or nonmagical objects may do so.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Spells for Laboratories (ars-magica-houses#057)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one Warping or one Safety loss per regularly used spell; a setting can relax the matching-Arts restriction for easier laboratory enhancement, at the cost of greater magical side effects or reduced balance.

rules.statement: A spell can fix a target’s mind resolutely on its current task and keep it from wavering. Daily use calls for the Addled laboratory routine, and magi may regard the effect as mentally warping and dependency-forming.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Example Laboratory Spells — The Resolute Mind of the Tireless Researcher (ars-magica-houses#057)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to task-fixation for the spell’s duration; a world can make repeated use more damaging, with dependence and weakened will as the cost.

rules.statement: A ritual can furnish an empty chamber with a fully equipped laboratory, granting the listed characteristics, virtues, flaws, and specializations. Unless the lab receives rigorous higher-level upkeep, its virtues are quickly lost and it declines to a more ordinary standard.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Example Laboratory Spells — The Laboratory of Bonisagus (ars-magica-houses#057)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a complete lab appearing in a suitable empty room; a world can demand sustained intensive upkeep to preserve its superior qualities.

rules.statement: A spell can keep a lab’s equipment and tools immaculately clean, granting the Spotless Virtue if recast every lunar month. While active it raises the lab’s Warping by 1; if the spell stops and ordinary cleaning does not maintain the condition, the Virtue is lost.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Example Laboratory Spells — Gleam of the Freshly-Polished Glass (ars-magica-houses#057)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to monthly recasting and +1 Warping while active; a world can make the cleanliness permanent through mundane labor instead, trading magical cost for upkeep effort.

rules.statement: A spell can move all movable contents of a chamber to a room reachable by the caster’s Arcane Connection, retaining their arrangement and relative positions; the destination must fit the occupied area. For a lab, a Perception + Finesse roll faces Ease Factor 9 + 3 times Refinement, modified by organization and room-shape differences; failure gives Disorganized or removes Highly Organized, while a botch gives Hidden Defect.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Example Laboratory Spells — The Ambulatory Laboratory (ars-magica-houses#057)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to transporting the contents intact when the destination fits; a world can increase mishap risk for refined, organized, or differently shaped labs, with disorder or hidden defects as the cost.

rules.statement: A variant using Arcane Connection Range can bring the contents of a remote laboratory into the caster’s room, allowing an entire lab to be stolen.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: Example Laboratory Spells — The Ambulatory Laboratory (ars-magica-houses#057)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to remote retrieval only through an Arcane Connection; a world can permit theft of distant labs, balanced by the need for that connection.

rules.statement: A covenant council meets four times yearly, and a quorum is valid only when more than half of its current members attend. Ordinary motions need a second and pass by majority of those present; charter changes, expulsions, and admission of probationary members require unanimity.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: The Oath of Covenant — Governance of this Covenant (ars-magica-houses#057)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to majority rule with unanimity for the listed high-stakes decisions; a world can change thresholds to make governance faster or more protective of dissenters.

rules.statement: A probationary member serves for seven seasons, has half a full member’s vote and half share of surplus resources, and must complete at least one assigned remunerated task during probation without requiring payment. Completion normally allows elevation to full membership unless evidence shows the magus unfit to swear the covenant oath.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: The Oath of Covenant — Membership; Rights of the Members; Responsibilities of the Members (ars-magica-houses#057)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a seven-season probation with half shares and one mandatory task; a world can make admission more or less demanding, at the cost of time, service, and restricted standing.

rules.statement: A member may leave by renouncing the covenant oath before at least two council members, ending that member’s rights and duties. Censure can reduce a full member to probationary status or a probationary member to Protected Guest; expulsion requires unanimous approval of the remaining council.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Houses of Hermes and Covenants: The Oath of Covenant — Membership; Censure of the Members (ars-magica-houses#057)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to witnessed renunciation for voluntary release and council action for penalties; a world can make exit or expulsion harder, binding members more tightly to the covenant.

rules.statement: To integrate an ancient magical tradition, a researcher gathers breakthrough points toward a threshold that is typically 30 for a Minor, 45 for a Major, or 60 for a Hermetic breakthrough. A successful experimental effect based on an Insight adds points equal to its magnitude; the researcher must find a different Insight source before repeating this process.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Introduction — Hermetic Integration of Ancient Magic; The Breakthrough; Creating the Effect (ars-magica-magic#000)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the typical 30/45/60-point thresholds; a troupe can vary them, since the research is meant to make rediscovery uncertain and consequential.

rules.statement: A season investigating an ancient-magic source requires a stress roll of Intelligence + Magic Theory against Ease Factor 18. Success grants an Insight, failure grants none that season, and a botch produces a false Insight; a source generally yields only one Insight, shared by everyone who studies it.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Introduction — Hermetic Integration of Ancient Magic; Insight (ars-magica-magic#000)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one Insight per source after a successful seasonal roll; a world can make rare sources richer, because some exceptional lore may contain several distinct discoveries.

rules.statement: An Insight specifies one fixed effect, which the researcher must invent without changing its Range, Duration, Target, or other parameters. A successfully created effect grants breakthrough points equal to its magnitude; another magus can reproduce it only from its Lab Text and cannot vary it.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Introduction — Hermetic Integration of Ancient Magic; Creating the Effect (ars-magica-magic#000)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to an exact, non-variable effect; a troupe can relax that restriction after integration, because the fixed version represents incomplete understanding.

rules.statement: A fluent speaker of Adamic (Dead Language score 5) can name a target within voice range and thereby gain a lasting Arcane Connection to it; the speaker also has such a connection to any mundane thing whose name they know. A character with some Adamic knowledge gains a +1 Penetration multiplier when naming a target with Magic Resistance in a spoken ritual, and a non-fluent speaker must already have an Arcane Connection; the examples give a total multiplier of +2 at Adamic 1 with an hours-long connection and +5 at Adamic 5.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Chapter One — The Language of Adam (ars-magica-magic#000)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to voice-range naming and lasting connections only for a fluent speaker; a world can require additional ritual constraints, because the language is exceptionally difficult to recover.

rules.statement: When a fluent Adamic speaker names something for the first time, the name subtly changes its destiny to fit the speaker’s idea of it. The speaker chooses the associated concept but cannot directly control how the change unfolds.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Chapter One — The Language of Adam (ars-magica-magic#000)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to an indirect, story-level destiny change; a troupe can make the consequence stronger or weaker, because the effect is intentionally outside the speaker’s direct control.

rules.statement: A character can reconstruct an ancient language by spending a season comparing two derivative languages, but must be fluent in both and have Area Lore 5 for the common language’s birthplace. The season provides 2 Exposure experience points in the common language Ability.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Chapter One — The Tower of Babel; Linguistic Research (ars-magica-magic#000)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the two-language and Area Lore 5 prerequisites; a world can ease or heighten them, because access to historical knowledge and cultural context varies.

rules.statement: When experimenting on a lost language as if researching a Breakthrough, each 2 points or fraction above 5 in the related languages allows a +1 or −1 adjustment to the experimentation result, to a maximum of +3 or −3; a result of 0 still requires a botch check. A Discovery grants 15 experience points in the common language, while a botch grants no seasonal experience and removes 15 experience points from the shared Ability.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Before “Seeking Lost Babylon” (ars-magica-magic#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the stated adjustment cap and botch risk; a world can raise or lower the cap, changing how much linguistic expertise can offset the danger of rushed research.

rules.statement: Eden’s regio has a mundane underwater level, a flooded first level, and higher levels at 5 and 10; its highest described level has a guarded entrance. Humans and reptiles are barred, and the guardians immediately send intruders who bypass the boundary down to a lower level.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: The Garden of Eden (ars-magica-magic#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to level-based access with guardians enforcing entry limits; a world can change which levels exist or who is barred, with the guardians’ intervention as the cost of trespass.

rules.statement: Humans can pass the guardians by completely taking a non-reptilian animal form, but must keep that form throughout their stay; the guardians expel anyone who adopts a forbidden form. Non-corporeal humans, faeries, and demons are also denied entry, while beings with Divine Might may come and go freely.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: The Garden of Eden — after “Other Edens” (ars-magica-magic#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the listed categories and a complete, maintained animal form as the entry condition; a world can broaden or narrow eligibility, with failed disguise or forbidden nature causing expulsion.

rules.statement: Inside Eden, inhabitants do not hunger or thirst, need no sleep, and do not experience seasonal change; animals can speak Adamic but gain no Intelligence score or supernatural powers. Magi in animal form lose access to The Gift and cannot cast spells or activate devices that require their use, though existing effects and continual device effects remain.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: The Animals (ars-magica-magic#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to Eden’s restrictions applying throughout the regio; a world can tune which needs or abilities are suspended, with the price being loss of ordinary magical agency for visiting magi.

rules.statement: Eating fruit from either central tree immediately removes the eater from Eden and bars future entry; the eater permanently becomes the animal form they had when eating it, and all animals of that species are expelled too. The Knowledge fruit grants Intelligence to a formerly Cunning creature or The Gift to an already intelligent one, and gives at least 1 Warping Point plus enough to raise Warping Score by 1; the Life fruit instead causes deep sleep, requiring a successful Aging roll without an Aging Point to wake, then grants Magical Might equal to 10 minus Size if the eater had no Might.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: The Fruits (ars-magica-magic#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the fruit’s fixed transformation and removal effects; a world can alter the gifts or their costs, trading lasting changes in form and access for knowledge or supernatural ability.

rules.statement: A shaman can readily summon a suitable Faerie, Magical, or Infernal spirit of Might 30 or less and bargain for its aid; it may be assigned a task or bound to a weapon. Each shaman also has a personal familiar spirit that follows and assists them.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Mongol Spirit Shaman (ars-magica-magic#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to spirits of Might 30 or less and aid secured by bargaining; a world can change the Might ceiling or required bargain, with the spirit’s terms limiting the service.

rules.statement: A Mongolian blunt arrow deals non-lethal damage; an armor-piercing arrow has a +2 damage modifier and reduces range by 15, while a flaming arrow has a +1 damage modifier and reduces range by 15. A signal arrow has a −3 damage modifier and adds 10 range.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Mongolian Bows — Mongolian Bow, Continued (ars-magica-magic#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the listed arrow-specific modifiers; a world can change the tradeoff between damage, range, and non-lethal or signal use, at the cost of reduced performance in other areas.

rules.statement: A fluent Adamic writer with Artes Liberales 1 or higher can inscribe a being’s or object’s name as a symbol on it, creating an Arcane Connection for later targeting. The mark can also associate the target with Cain and his destiny.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Adamic Writing (ars-magica-magic#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: written names create a lasting targeting connection; a world can make the Cain association stronger or weaker because the mark may impose an unwanted magical destiny.

rules.statement: Anyone who kills Cain inherits his curse: they become deformed, are driven from the Dominion by trembling and groaning, and become a shadow of themselves after death. Cain eventually rises again, with the delay ranging from days to generations.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Finding Cain (ars-magica-magic#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: killing Cain transfers his curse and he returns eventually; a world can vary the delay because vengeance is passed on only after the killer’s suffering has been answered.

rules.statement: Cain can split off a shadow for no points, but each separation costs him 10 Might and one +3 Personality Trait. A shadow acts independently and lacks awareness of the others; shadows recombine when they meet, restoring their shared whole, whose maximum Might is 70.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Cain, the Fugitive — Shadow of Cain (ars-magica-magic#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: splitting redistributes Cain’s Might and traits among independent selves; a world can change the number or cost of shadows because each represents a fragment of his curse.

rules.statement: Cain recovers Might by sleeping more than six hours, at 1 point per hour, or by killing and eating a living creature, gaining about 1 point per 2 points of the creature’s Size above −15. If diminished from his default Might, he also regains 1 point each night; when incapacitated, he heals all wounds as if they were Light Wounds.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Cain, the Fugitive (ars-magica-magic#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: sleep, predation, and nightly recovery restore Might, while incapacitation heals rapidly; a world can make recovery depend more heavily on feeding because Cain’s curse drives him to consume life.

rules.statement: A Canaanite necromancer can attempt to reproduce a Hermetic Corpus or Mentem effect that communicates with, commands, or summons the dead. Success requires a stress roll of Communication + the Ability against an Ease Factor of three times the effect’s magnitude.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Major Supernatural Virtue: Canaanite Necromancy (ars-magica-magic#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: eligible dead-related effects use the stated roll and magnitude-based target; a world can narrow eligible effects because the tradition is limited to dealing with the dead.

rules.statement: A magus integrating the tradition gains breakthrough points equal to each invented effect’s magnitude and needs 45 points to complete the integration. Until completion, Veil of Death is available only for effects invented from Insight Lab Texts; afterwards the magus gains the permanent virtue and its benefits.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Hermetic Integration (ars-magica-magic#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: 45 accumulated points complete integration; a world can alter the research threshold because adopting the tradition changes Hermetic practice.

rules.statement: Veil of Death targets any dead mortal human who has not entered Heaven, regardless of distance, if the caster can sense the target or has an Arcane Connection. It is equivalent to Sight range for magnitude; supernatural creatures and dead animals are excluded, and Heaven is beyond reach.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: New Range: Veil of Death (ars-magica-magic#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the range reaches eligible human dead at any distance but requires a connection; a world can expand eligible targets because the boundary reflects the tradition’s limits.

rules.statement: A magus with Canaanite Magic is permanently connected to the dead and gains a +4 Penetration multiplier bonus against them. In return, dead spirits detect the magus within seven miles and can locate him with a Perception roll against Ease Factor 6; the dead also gain a permanent connection to him and a +4 Penetration multiplier bonus when attacking him.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Minor Hermetic Virtue: Canaanite Magic (ars-magica-magic#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: enhanced access and penetration come with reciprocal exposure and vulnerability; a world can adjust the radius or bonuses because the dead are always aware of the magus’s presence.

rules.statement: When a character botches an attempt to summon or speak with the dead, a demon may impersonate the intended spirit and subtly corrupt what it communicates. Hermetic magic cannot directly see through the deception, though the demon may reveal itself by making mistakes.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Opening passage on Canaanite necromancy (ars-magica-magic#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a deceptive spirit appearing after a botch; a world can vary the demon’s power and how readily it slips up, at the cost of reliable information.

rules.statement: Drinking from En-Dor’s stream every day sustains a character and grants an effect like a +5 Longevity Ritual while the character remains in the regio. On leaving, the drinker must immediately make an Aging roll, even if younger than 35; a Hermetic laboratory can extract 2 pawns of Aquam vis per season, tainted by the Divine.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: En-Dor Regio Level One (ars-magica-magic#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to sustenance and longevity only within the regio; a world can change the benefit or departure cost, with aging risk and tainted vis as the price.

rules.statement: While incorporeal, Zephaniah can become invisible at will, pass through walls, and ignore physical attacks, fatigue, and wounds. She has a permanent connection to the dead that gives her a +4 Penetration multiplier when interacting with them.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Zephaniah — Powers: Dead Canaanite Necromancer (ars-magica-magic#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to an incorporeal ghost with these protections and access to the dead; a world can narrow the protections or connection, balancing ghostly freedom against limited interaction.

rules.statement: Zephaniah can spend 10 points to become physically present for one day. A wound or fatigue requires a Concentration roll to remain manifested; incapacitation, death, or unconsciousness ends the manifestation, and she cannot end it voluntarily before its duration expires.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Zephaniah — Powers: Return to Flesh (ars-magica-magic#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a one-day bodily manifestation with the stated interruptions; a world can tune its duration or point cost, trading temporary life for vulnerability.

rules.statement: A ghostly necromancer can spend 5 points to push one person’s limbs for a Diameter. The push is weak: a conscious target automatically resists it, but doing anything else at the same time requires an Intelligence + Concentration roll against Ease Factor 9 minus the target’s Size.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Ghosts of Necromancers — Powers: Marionette (ars-magica-magic#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to weak, short-lived limb control that a conscious target can resist; a world can strengthen or extend control, at the cost of greater resistance or power expenditure.

rules.statement: A defixio can channel a chosen spell or Supernatural Ability against a described target without sensing them or possessing an Arcane Connection; it does not itself supply power or improve Penetration. Preparing one takes a day and costs one pawn of appropriate vis per magnitude, and success is checked against an Ease Factor increased by one per magnitude; the creator’s roll excess determines Defixio Lore Penetration.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Defixio Lore (ars-magica-magic#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a prepared device that targets by description without a connection; a world can alter its cost or targeting difficulty, with vis expenditure and weak descriptions limiting use.

rules.statement: Event Duration is available only to Rituals: the spell waits until its fully specified trigger occurs, possibly forever. It requires Intellego and, when identifying a person, place, or thing, the relevant Form requisite; the trigger must occur within range, and the spell adds +1 magnitude in addition to the underlying effect’s duration cost.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: New Duration: Event (ars-magica-magic#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a ritual held until a specified event within its range; a world can broaden triggers or range, with requisite, penetration, and magnitude costs constraining it.

rules.statement: Unlimited Range is available only to Rituals and requires one sympathetic connection or a combination totaling at least +2 on the Sympathetic Connections table; an Arcane Connection is unnecessary. It adds +6 magnitudes, or +2 to the base for guidelines that require an Arcane Connection.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: New Range: Unlimited (ars-magica-magic#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to remote ritual targeting with sufficient sympathetic links; a world can lower the link threshold or magnitude surcharge, trading broad reach against setup and ritual cost.

rules.statement: A ritual can move its caster to the place shown in a picture they make during casting. The caster must succeed at Dexterity + Craft against Ease Factor 9 and cast successfully; a botch may send them into a wall, to a merely similar place, or to a Faerie regio.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Passage to the Place Pictured (ars-magica-magic#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to travel to the depicted site only after a successful craft roll; a world may restrict distant or unknown destinations because inaccurate images can cause dangerous misplacement.

rules.statement: In defixio magic and Unlimited Range spells, nicknames, birth names, and bynames can identify a target, but religious names such as baptismal, religious laqab, or rabbinical names cannot. If only a religious name is used, the spell fails; including one alongside an allowed name has no effect, and where birth and religious names coincide only a nickname or byname works.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Religious Names in Defixio Magic (ars-magica-magic#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to excluding religious names as valid sympathetic links; a world could relax this restriction, at the cost of changing the cultural and magical protection attached to sacred names.

rules.statement: An Event-duration spell can wait until a written, fully specified event occurs, potentially years after casting; the caster should record the trigger and relevant spell totals. A zero Penetration Total reduces some risk of violating the Code but means creatures with Might never trigger it, and magi may still be vulnerable when Parma expires at sunrise and sunset.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Using Duration Event (ars-magica-magic#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a fixed written trigger that activates once its conditions occur; a world can broaden triggers or penetration, but risks mistaken activation and legal violations.

rules.statement: An Unlimited Range spell can use a symbolic representation as a sympathetic connection, but the caster must create it and an inaccurate or inadequate representation can fail with disastrous results. A storyguide may limit this range, for example to continental Europe or 49 leagues.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Using Range Unlimited (ars-magica-magic#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.mechanism: law: symbolic connection and range limit
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to allowing travel to any represented place; a world can cap distance or require familiarity to avoid hazardous destinations and overly broad travel.

rules.statement: Only defixiones whose magic has not yet been released can be studied; suitable discoveries should generally be limited to one or two for each season spent searching.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Finding Defixiones (ars-magica-magic#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to making unspent devices studyable and spent ones ineligible; a world could increase availability, at the cost of making magical research and acquisition easier.

rules.statement: A sanctuary’s layered defixiones can curse male entrants in succession, while women may enter and leave freely. Removing a defixio does not end its protection while it remains intact, but destroying it does and makes it unsuitable for study.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Protective Defixiones (ars-magica-magic#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to intact devices continuing to protect the site wherever moved; a world could make removal deactivate them, trading recoverable research materials for simpler disarming.

rules.statement: Fertility Lore permits visual inspection taking about five minutes: Ease Factor 3 detects pregnancy and estimates natural due date within 10% of remaining time, or identifies relationship, with +1 per generation and +3 for exact relation; Ease Factor 12 assesses fertility. Surreptitious inspection raises the relevant Ease Factor by 3, and the Ability alone cannot assess an unborn child.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Arcane Ability Fertility Lore (ars-magica-magic#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to visual, nonmagical inspection with the listed difficulties; a world could let the skill identify unborn-child traits, at the cost of removing the need for specialized magic.

rules.statement: The Unborn Child Target treats a fetus from conception to birth as an Individual, but the caster must sense the mother and her Magic Resistance also protects the fetus. The related integration breakthroughs require 15 points for Fertility Lore and 35 for Fertility Ritual Magic.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: New Target: Unborn Child; Integrating Fertility Magic into Hermetic Theory (ars-magica-magic#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to targeting the fetus only through a sensed mother and her resistance; a world could permit direct targeting, at the cost of bypassing maternal protection.

rules.statement: A Fertility Ritual is performed at conception and can assign child traits up to a maximum of one Trait Point per 10 points or fraction of the magus’s Creo Corpus Lab Total. Major virtues or flaws and the Gift cost 3 points; minor virtues or flaws, gender, and general features cost 1; precise features cost 3.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: The Fertility Ritual (ars-magica-magic#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to trait selection within the Lab Total-based point cap; a world could increase the cap or reduce trait costs, but would make engineered offspring more powerful.

rules.statement: A Fertility Ritual may assign a child traits appropriate to the child’s nature; its maximum Trait Points are one per 10 points of Creo Corpus Lab Total, and the vis cost equals the total points assigned. A ritual takes a season to develop and about half an hour to perform; both parents must be fertile, and the traits appear at birth nine months later.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Example: Fertility Ritual Trait Point Cost; Fertility Ritual procedure (ars-magica-magic#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a child receiving the specified traits for equal Trait Points in vis; a world can vary allowed traits or vis types, since the ritual draws on magical resources and the parents’ fertility.

rules.statement: A mother’s own ritual has a maximum of one Trait Point per 5 points, or fraction thereof, of her Creo Corpus Lab Total, but it is tied to her and cannot be used for another mother. Other parents’ traits do not constrain the child’s traits, but the ritual’s inventor must have a connection to the realm from which granted supernatural powers derive.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: The Maga's Own Child; Supernatural Traits (ars-magica-magic#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to requiring a realm connection and limiting the enhanced capacity to the mother’s own child; a world can loosen either restriction at the cost of its established magical boundaries.

rules.statement: A fertility fetish adds a Lab Total bonus equal to the maker’s Dexterity plus Craft Ability plus the supervisor’s Fertility Lore. The fertile woman must make her own fetish under supervision for a season; it holds one pawn of Creo vis, is a permanent Arcane Connection to her and children conceived using it, and can be used for multiple children.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Fertility Fetishes (ars-magica-magic#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a lasting personal connection and a Lab bonus based on both makers’ skills; a world can make the fetish more durable or more dangerous, with fertility and the invested vis as the cost.

rules.statement: A used Fertility Ritual can be repeated safely only if its original child has died. An unsafe repeat immediately gives the performer Warping Points equal to half the ritual’s Trait Point cost, rounded up, and the resulting child gains Corrupt Fertility Ritual.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Repeating a Fertility Ritual (ars-magica-magic#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a fatality prerequisite for safe repetition; a world can alter the Warping burden or resulting flaw, because reusing the ritual risks magical distortion.

rules.statement: A child with Corrupt Fertility Ritual has a sympathetic connection to prior children of the ritual, granting +2 Penetration multiplier when they use spells or magical abilities on one another. The child takes –3 on social interactions and gains one Warping Point each birthday; the flaw ends when all predecessors die, but accumulated Warping remains.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Minor Supernatural Flaw Corrupt Fertility Ritual (ars-magica-magic#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a mutual sympathetic link with recurring Warping and social costs; a world can change the bond’s benefits or end condition, reflecting the consequences of duplicated conception.

rules.statement: A Grigori Secret groups one Technique and two Forms so that their vis is interchangeable, and spells using one of the Arts may ignore requisites from the other two. Using vis through a Secret in a Divine or Infernal aura doubles the usual botch dice; a botch on a spell ignoring requisites in those auras does likewise.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: The Secrets of the Grigori (ars-magica-magic#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to interchangeable vis and ignored requisites within the Secret’s three Arts; a world can choose which Arts are linked, while Divine or Infernal influence raises the risk of failure.

rules.statement: Turning a Grigori Secret into a teachable Hermetic Legacy requires a 45-point Major Breakthrough; breaking the Limit of Vis requires a 60-point Hermetic Breakthrough. A researcher with a Secret or Legacy gains one extra breakthrough point per season, and completing the latter makes all Arts’ vis interchangeable.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: The Secrets of the Grigori (ars-magica-magic#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the stated research thresholds and bonus for practitioners; a world can set different breakthrough goals, with the consequence of changing how vis is used.

rules.statement: For one fact-based question, a magus may spend a season consulting up to Intelligence + Artes Liberales books on the relevant Ability, gaining Quality experience from each only for that question. At the season’s end, roll Intelligence plus the temporarily raised Ability against the question’s Ease Factor; failure permits more seasons, a botch gives a wrong answer, and the temporary experience is lost after more than four seasons without consultation or after other research or lab work unless preserved in notes.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Library Consultation (ars-magica-magic#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to allowing repeated seasonal research with temporary Ability boosts; a troupe can limit library access or impose a deadline, because maintaining notes costs a season and other research erases the boost.

rules.statement: A person with the Blood of the Nephilim Virtue who studies the Mount Hermon stelae in place for a season gains Baraqijal’s Secret Supernatural Virtue; studying copies does not grant it, a distinction obvious to such a person. The stelae also serve as a Magic Theory summa of Level 8 and Quality 6, and their copied inscriptions can provide Insight for integrating Grigori Secrets.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: The Legacy of the Grigori — The Stelae of the Watchers (ars-magica-magic#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to granting the Virtue only through a season of in-person study; a world can broaden or narrow eligible descendants, since the source is tied to bloodline and place.

rules.statement: Calling Shamsiel’s True Name within five paces of the Ararat obelisk transports the caller to the one-level regio, which has a Divine aura of 5. Shamsiel cannot leave his prison, while others may leave the regio freely.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: The Watchers Themselves — The Shamed Leader (ars-magica-magic#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to allowing the name-triggered entry and free exit for visitors while binding Shamsiel; a world can change the required distance or name, with the prison’s Divine constraint explaining his confinement.

rules.statement: A magus who spends a full year in Shamsiel’s regio and persuades him to teach receives Insight for Grigori integration, Shamsiel’s Gift, and the Pious Minor Personality Flaw if not already possessed. Shamsiel’s Enfolding costs 2 or 10 Might: the lesser use protects a target’s soul and mind from supernatural targeting for moments, and the 10-point use makes the target’s body invulnerable to magic, pain, harm, fatigue, wounds, and death for at most one combat round.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: The Watchers Themselves — The Shamed Leader (ars-magica-magic#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to requiring a year of instruction and accepting the associated personality cost; a world can vary the teaching term or protection duration, reflecting Shamsiel’s restricted and costly aid.

rules.statement: Shamsiel can reproduce any Hermetic or holy magical effect for 1 Might Point per 2 magnitudes, including ritual effects without vis or lengthy casting; his total expenditure is limited only by his remaining Might Pool. His Grant Secret costs 4 points and requires the target to stay with him for a full year to gain Shamsiel’s Secret.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: The Watchers Themselves — The Shamed Leader (ars-magica-magic#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to pricing copied effects by magnitude and drawing the cost from Might; a world can restrict eligible effects or add a per-use ceiling, because the stated limit is the remaining pool.

rules.statement: Mechanica can simulate Creo, Rego, Perdo, or Muto effects in Auram, Aquam, Ignem, Mentem, or Terram; ordinary devices have one effect, while awakened devices may have several. Creation takes at least a season and costs one Mythic Pound per 3 Creation Level points, with a target of 3 times the effect’s magnitudes plus modifiers; one device can be made per season, and a failed attempt loses the time and half the materials.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Major Supernatural Virtue: Mechanica of Heron (ars-magica-magic#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the listed Arts, Forms, one-effect limit, seasonal work, and Mythic Pound cost; a world can vary size or use modifiers, because compactness raises the creation target.

rules.statement: After a week of study, a Mechanician can try to change a device’s effect only to one using its original Form and Technique and no higher final level. The attempt costs one Mythic Pound and a roll against the new device’s Creation Level; failure wastes the time and money, while a botch destroys the device.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Major Supernatural Virtue: Mechanica of Heron (ars-magica-magic#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to allowing only same-Form-and-Technique changes at equal or lower level; a world can ease or tighten the roll, with time and money at risk.

rules.statement: A Mechanician can awaken a constructed animal simulacrum by exceeding a target of 9 plus the magnitude of its Magic Might, using Intelligence, Mechanica, the lower of Philosophiae or Artes Liberales, and aura. If the total is short, further seasons add a cumulative +1, but interruption ruins the device; the awakened being is sentient, receives traits based on its model, and cannot move or speak unless given suitable constant effects.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Major Supernatural Virtue: Mechanica of Heron, Continued (ars-magica-magic#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to requiring uninterrupted laboratory work and installed effects for movement or speech; a world can change the target or trait budget, with interruption risking the costly simulacrum.

rules.statement: An Awakened Device’s construction level is its Magic Might plus five times its Size; its Might also sets its Magic Resistance and the maximum pawns of vis available for instilled spell-like effects. Awakening uses a Creo + Form + Intelligence + Magic Theory + aura Lab Total, with excess points bankable across uninterrupted seasons.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Awakened Device rules (ars-magica-magic#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a device whose Might and Size govern construction and capacity; a world can raise or lower those limits, with vis and substantial construction expense as the cost.

rules.statement: Awakening requires the Vim vis needed to open an enchanted device, plus one pawn of Creo or Form-specific vis per point of Might; constructing its body also costs Mythic Pounds equal to its Material Base Points. Further enchantment is needed for movement, communication, or other abilities.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Awakened Device rules (ars-magica-magic#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to costly, separately enchanted capabilities; a world can make devices cheaper or more self-sufficient, with vis and money as the limiting costs.

rules.statement: An awakened device can use its instilled effects whenever it chooses, can gain additional powers if its material and size allow, and can learn Abilities through training or instruction. It can become a familiar only if its creator magus awakened it personally.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Awakened Device rules (ars-magica-magic#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to autonomous use and learning within material limits; a world can restrict later powers or familiar status, with creator involvement as the bond’s gate.

rules.statement: A Ptolemaic coordinate acts as a lasting Arcane Connection to a place: it can be remembered, written down, or built into an item, and does not fade. It enables comparatively swift and safe magical travel to the designated location.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: The Hesperides — Consequences (ars-magica-magic#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to durable coordinate-based access; a world can limit accuracy or destinations, with obtaining reliable location data as the cost.

rules.statement: To derive coordinates by observation, the observer must know the origin’s fixed-star pattern and succeed at Intelligence + Artes Liberales against Ease Factor 15. The process normally needs four hours of clear stargazing and four hours of calculation; specified tools and Ptolemy’s tables shorten the work.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Deriving Coordinates — Observation of the Fixed Stars (ars-magica-magic#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to observation requiring clear skies and careful work; a world can shorten the process with tools or tables, while missing origin data prevents new coordinates.

rules.statement: The origin point cannot be visited, so its stellar pattern must be reconstructed from three readings; determining the longitude adjustment requires reaching the Purple Islands’ Zero Longitude. Attempts to nominate a different western origin fail.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: The Problem of the Origin Point (ars-magica-magic#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to an immovable geographic origin; a world can make recalibration easier or harder, with the required remote journey as the cost.

rules.statement: The theater’s prediction can be used once per month on someone watching its performance, and lasts for the play, usually about an hour. Its allegorical scenes may disclose that person’s future, but their meaning can be difficult to interpret.
