locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Heron’s Theater — The Web of Mnemosyne (ars-magica-magic#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one difficult-to-interpret forecast each month; a world can change its frequency or clarity, with the audience and interpretive effort as constraints.

rules.statement: The regio entrance appears only when the Dominion aura falls below 4, and that weakness lasts only a few hours. A mechanica or signs of Serapis’ cult permit automatic entry; once the aura rises, those inside may be trapped until another ill-omened night.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Entering the Temple (ars-magica-magic#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a timed, condition-gated entrance; a world can change the aura threshold or duration, with the risk of being stranded as the cost.

rules.statement: A Guan wizard-king, invested in the role and assisted by the village, can perform the traditional community ceremonies; tested ancient formulae cannot fail or botch. Their effects include rain lasting for the ritual, weather calming, harvest blessings limited to the ruler’s community, and ancestor contact limited to eligible preserved family spirits.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Magic (ars-magica-magic#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to reliable village-assisted rituals; a setting can broaden their targets or effects, at the cost of requiring communal participation and traditional forms.

rules.statement: A speaker of a Canarian dialect can communicate across dialects as though their Ability were two points lower. Whistled speech carries about four miles, and can extend Voice Range spellcasting when treated as a booming voice.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Dialects (ars-magica-magic#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to cross-dialect communication at a two-point penalty and whistled messages at about four miles; a world can change range or spellcasting use, with distance and dialect competence as limits.

rules.statement: Weapons made with stone or volcanic glass instead of metal have their usual Damage modifier reduced by 2, to a minimum of +1.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Statistics for Guan Weapons (ars-magica-magic#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the stated two-point reduction; a world can soften or sharpen it, reflecting the tradeoff of local materials for metal.

rules.statement: The Acero monolith opens into the Garden’s regio automatically for visitors aided by the king and queen; star-measuring magi at midnight nearby, with their companions, are drawn through as well. No method permits entry while facing east.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Entering the Garden (ars-magica-magic#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the stated entry routes and east-facing prohibition; a world can change access conditions, making local knowledge or orientation the price.

rules.statement: An apple from Hera’s orchard contains one pawn of Creo vis and reduces the eater’s Apparent Age by ten years; repeated eating has cosmetic benefits. An apple harvested at the exact proper moment and by the exact proper method can make a magus immortal.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: The Garden of the Hesperides (ars-magica-magic#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one pawn and ten years per apple, with immortality reserved for the precise harvest; a world can alter availability or potency, with timing and access as costs.

rules.statement: A serpent-dryad gains one head at each annual flowering of its tree. Head-count milestones increase its Might, Soak, size, damage, attributes, and other traits; at 60 heads it gains Ladon’s power of sight.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Serpent-dryads (ars-magica-magic#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one new head per flowering and the stated milestones; a world can change growth speed or bonuses, with the tree’s survival anchoring the creature.

rules.statement: Ladon can shed his skin at sunset over an hour to heal all wounds and remove unwanted enchantments. If his body is killed, he can make a new one when the Draco constellation rises.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Ladon, Continued (ars-magica-magic#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to complete sunset renewal and constellation-linked return; a world can restrict either recovery, with time and the celestial condition as costs.

rules.statement: Only characters with The Gift or the Hyperborean Hymnist Virtue can successfully recite a Hyperborean hymn and gain its powers. A hymn is learned as a Supernatural Ability; the Virtue grants one hymn at rating 1 and 15 infused Power levels, and can be taken multiple times.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Performing the Hymns; New Virtues (ars-magica-magic#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to Gift or the Virtue as the access gate and 15 starting Power levels; a world can change eligibility or starting investment, with seasons required for further infusion.

rules.statement: Each Hymn Ability level grants 15 power levels to spend. A hymn score also adds to Soak against damage from that hymn’s principles, but this bonus does not stack with bonuses from Arts or other hymns; only the highest applies.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: New Supernatural Ability: Hyperborean Hymn (ars-magica-magic#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to 15 power levels per score point and the highest applicable Soak bonus; a world can change either rate to tune the tradition’s power and durability.

rules.statement: A character infuses a hymn Power by spending a season in focused recitation and contemplation, if Communication + Hymn Ability + modifiers + aura meets an Ease Factor of the modified Power level divided by three, rounded up. The character may then invoke it at will, without a roll, subject to a predetermined daily-use limit; raising a Hymn Ability grants another 15 levels, and vis can add one power level per pawn.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Reciting the Hymns; Gaining New Powers and Improving Existing Ones; Gaining More Levels (ars-magica-magic#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to seasonal infusion, the stated recitation test, and one vis pawn per extra level; a world can raise the vis cost or alter the season requirement because deeper power demands more sacrifice.

rules.statement: If a non-Hermetic hymn user gains more than two Warping Points at once, the user rolls Stamina + Concentration + highest Hymn score against updated Warping Score + points gained + aura and modifiers. Failure causes a fixed personal transformation into an Apollo-associated animal or separation of spirit from body for hours equal to total Warping Points; at the end, another control test can restore the human form, while failure extends the transformation for a day and applies a cumulative –1 to later attempts.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Illumination: Hyperborean Warping; Illumination: Hyperborean Warping, Continued (ars-magica-magic#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a control test after gains above two points and a transformation lasting one hour per total point; a world can adjust the trigger or recovery test to make Apollo’s influence more or less dangerous.

rules.statement: A character may voluntarily fail the Illumination control test to gain additional Warping Points equal to Warping Score + aura + modifiers, and gains an equal number of experience points for Hymn Abilities. The extra Warping increases the time spent transformed.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: The Bright Lightening (ars-magica-magic#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to exchanging voluntary loss of control for equal points of Warping and Hymn experience; a world can change that exchange rate to make the dangerous bargain more or less tempting.

rules.statement: A Power using the special 19-year Duration lasts until 19 years have passed or the stars complete their corresponding revolution, whichever comes first. It is one magnitude above Year Duration, and recognizing the stellar timing requires Artes Liberales.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: New Duration: 19 Years (ars-magica-magic#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the earlier of the 19-year limit or stellar completion; a world can change the cycle or remove the astronomical condition to set the scale of long-lasting effects.

rules.statement: A choir can perform a one-use, uninfused effect after at least a day of joint meditation. Participants add their Communication + relevant Hymn scores to the focus character’s total; each additional hymn required raises the Power level by 5, and the choir spends vis pawns equal to the final Ease Factor.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Choir Mechanics (ars-magica-magic#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to pooled recitation, a day minimum, and vis equal to Ease Factor; a world can change preparation time or the vis burden to set how accessible large-scale group magic is.

rules.statement: A hymn can enchant one Power into an item in a season without vis, using Intelligence + Hymn Ability + modifiers + aura against the total modified Power levels divided by three. Each enchanted Power takes a season, and enchanting mundane items inflicts Warping Points on the enchanter.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Hyperborean Enchantments (ars-magica-magic#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one season per Power and Warping as the cost of enchanting an ordinary object; a world can alter the duration or Warping cost to govern the availability of magical relics.

rules.statement: At night, invoking a hymn takes 15 minutes per Ease Factor point; during the day it takes about as long as a formulaic Hermetic spell. Hymn invocation requires a spoken prayer and cannot be silent, and continuous or constant effects can cause Warping.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Reciting the Hymns; Power Level Modifiers; Hyperborean Hymns and Magic Resistance (ars-magica-magic#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to spoken invocation and the stated nighttime delay; a world can shorten or remove these limits to make hymns easier to use, at the cost of their distinctive ritual burden.

rules.statement: A Hyperborean relic begins with 30 levels of Powers and gains another 30 levels for each additional purchase of the relic Virtue. Powers may fade when the owner’s Personality Traits conflict with the relic.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Sample Hyperborean Relic Powers (ars-magica-magic#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a relic holding 30 Power levels, with each extra Virtue adding 30; a world can change the allotment or fade rate, reflecting the relic’s alignment with its owner.

rules.statement: A relic permanently loses all its Powers if handled by an Infernal-aligned person or any creature with Infernal Might. An dishonorable Personality Flaw approved against by Apollo causes it to lose one Power per season in that character’s presence; damage can remove one or more Powers at the storyguide’s discretion.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Sample Hyperborean Relic Powers, Continued (ars-magica-magic#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to permanent total loss from Infernal contact and one lost Power each season of dishonorable exposure; a world can vary susceptibility or damage loss to reflect the relic’s condition and sacred allegiance.

rules.statement: Hyperborean enchantment can place any level or number of effects into any item, without shape, material, or size limits, and can include effects that would otherwise be Hermetic Rituals. The enchanter suffers 2 Warping Points per pawn of vis that opening and instilling the effects would require; opening costs this way only once per item.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: The process for creating relics (ars-magica-magic#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to unrestricted items and effects at 2 Warping Points per required vis pawn; a world can tighten eligible items or raise the personal cost, since the enchanter absorbs the sacrificed resource.

rules.statement: A Hyperborean enchanter must complete an item in one season or cannot enchant it. One effect cannot use two hymns at once, though an item can hold separate effects from multiple hymns; the method cannot make talismans or charged items, bind familiars, or create Longevity Rituals other than the named Eternal Youth of the Sun Power.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: The process for creating relics (ars-magica-magic#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a one-season deadline, one hymn per effect, and the listed exclusions; a world can relax these constraints, but they define the tradition’s limits.

rules.statement: The basilica’s Magic aura is 5 in the vale, 6 along its paved road, 7 among its buildings and in the crow copse, stream, and ponds, and 8 in most buildings. Seven days after a new moon, these auras rise by one; seven days after the waning moon, they fall by one.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: The Basilica’s Aura (ars-magica-magic#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the stated location-based aura ratings and monthly changes; a world can adjust the ratings or lunar timing to tune the site’s magical potency.

rules.statement: In the basilica’s magical aura, spells and supernatural abilities concerning the dead, future divination, disease, or spirits receive double benefit. The monastery ruins instead have Magic aura 4, the tabernacle has none, the altar has Dominion aura 1 on February 14, and the olive tree has Divine aura 1 extending to its furthest branch.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: The Basilica’s Aura (ars-magica-magic#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to doubled benefit for the four specified themes and the listed special aura pockets; a world can broaden or narrow those affinities to express the place’s lingering sacred correspondences.

rules.statement: Touching an Alexandrian altar while casting with Arcane Connection range counts as having an Arcane Connection to its linked shrines, cities, or temples with a +4 multiplier; the network links more than 70 sites.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: The Altars of Alexander the Great (ars-magica-magic#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the +4 multiplier at connected sites; a world can change the network’s reach or multiplier, with the altars serving as the costly-to-find links.

rules.statement: A ghost oracle can spend 3 Might points to possess a person or animal for at least a few minutes, provided it penetrates Magic Resistance. The victim can resist with Stamina + Concentration against Ease Factor 9; failure extends possession to a full day, after which the resistance attempt can recur daily, and Mentem effects or exorcism can end it.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: The Nekuomanteioi, Hyperborean Priests of Apollo — Possession (ars-magica-magic#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to 3 Might, penetration, and a daily resistance check at Ease Factor 9; a world can change duration or resistance difficulty, with the host’s body and the ghost’s Might as the cost.

rules.statement: The ghost oracle can examine the past or possible future of a person or place only with an Arcane Connection, receiving confused, indistinct visions. A magus using the ghost as an Arcane Connection for Intellego divination adds 4 magnitudes for the past or 5 for the hazy future, makes the spell a Ritual, and gains Warping Points equal to the spell’s total magnitude.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: The Nekuomanteioi, Hyperborean Priests of Apollo (ars-magica-magic#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to vague visions requiring an Arcane Connection and the stated ritual and Warping costs for a magus; a world can adjust clarity or costs, reflecting the danger of peering through the dead.

rules.statement: Aktióphis can answer any question truthfully for a character beside her, but only after being summoned and only if the supplicant swallows a hot coal at moonrise.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Aktióphis’s Displeasure — Augur of the Illuminated Revelation (ars-magica-magic#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a true answer gated by summoning and swallowing a hot coal at moonrise; a world can alter the price or scope, with bodily danger balancing the revelation.

rules.statement: A spirit can spend 1 Magic Might point to become physical, and may return to spiritual form at will. While physical it can be wounded or incapacitated; being killed sends it back to spiritual form, and an unmanifested spirit cannot attack or be physically attacked.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Spirit Guardians (ars-magica-magic#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to charging 1 Might for a physical body; a world can change the cost or duration because manifestation exposes spirits to physical harm.

rules.statement: Runic inscriptions hold lasting magical effects like enchanted devices, and their effects are not stopped by powers that would normally resist magic, including Parma Magica. Their active effects alter their targets so naturally that Intellego Vim cannot detect the magic; observation or intensive investigation can reveal the effect, and an active rune remains an Arcane Connection to its caster.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Chapter Nine: Rune Magic; Heirlooms and Artifacts (ars-magica-magic#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to runes making durable, resistance-bypassing changes; a world can restrict duration or bypass, since the inscrutable natural-looking result makes detection difficult.

rules.statement: Hyperborea is reached through a level 7 regio, extending to level 10 at its highest. Its fiery gates are closed to strangers: entry requires knowledge of the passwords or an invitation, and it cannot happen by accident.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Mythic Hyperborea (ars-magica-magic#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to password-or-invitation access through a bounded regio; a world can make access easier or harder because the island is deliberately protected from outsiders.

rules.statement: A dverge makes an artifact for a specific person and purpose over many seasons of calculations, recitations, and labor. Only after it is finished does the maker name a price, which cannot be negotiated; accepting may impose hidden costs such as losing the desire for one's heart's desire or surrendering 100 words or seven years of life.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: The Dvergar (ars-magica-magic#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a bespoke artifact followed by a non-negotiable, possibly hidden price; a world can make the cost literal or more alien because dvergar value things humans take for granted.

rules.statement: An inscription changes its target into a natural state matching the runes for as long as the inscription remains intact; the changed target is not itself treated as magical for resistance, although an effect directly targeting a resistant being must still penetrate.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Hermetic Integration; New Virtue: Hermetic Rune Magic (ars-magica-magic#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to lasting, natural-seeming transformations; a world can restrict which rune qualities can be applied, since the inscription’s meaning limits the change.

rules.statement: Rune Duration lasts while the runes are whole and undamaged; if carved on an object, significant damage to that object also ends the effect. This duration is equivalent to Moon and adds three magnitudes to the spell’s base level.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: New Virtue: Hermetic Rune Magic — Rune (Duration) (ars-magica-magic#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to persistence until physical damage; a world can make inscriptions more fragile, with wear or breakage as the cost of maintaining the effect.

rules.statement: Inscription Target works like Individual, but requires writing on the target or something it wears or carries. If the inscription is on a separate object, it needs an Arcane Connection to the target or must touch it; removing the object interrupts the effect without ending it while the runes remain intact.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: New Virtue: Hermetic Rune Magic — Inscription (Target) (ars-magica-magic#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to requiring a physical inscription and proximity or a connection; a world can permit remote inscription only by demanding a stronger connection.

rules.statement: The caster must physically trace the inscription as the spell is cast; magical carving cannot reach farther than Touch. Organic materials take ordinary spell-casting time, stone or metal take about two minutes, spontaneous inscriptions usually last only a few days, and durable work needs hours or up to a season for a masterpiece.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: New Virtue: Hermetic Rune Magic — Inscription (Target) (ars-magica-magic#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to brief inscriptions being quickly made but short-lived; a world can require longer craftwork for greater durability.

rules.statement: The inscription normally names the caster and describes the effect. Omitting the name imposes –5, hiding the name –2, hiding the description –5, and omitting the description –10; emphasizing runes grants +1, and extra work such as coloring or intricate design doubles casting time and grants another +1. A successful Dexterity plus suitable Craft roll against Ease Factor 15 can disguise the script without penalties; failure cancels the spell and ruins the inscribed object.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: New Virtue: Hermetic Rune Magic (ars-magica-magic#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to legible, fully identified inscriptions; a world can allow concealment, trading casting reliability or time for secrecy.

rules.statement: Runes remain an Arcane Connection to their caster, allowing another magus to target the caster by touching them; a Touch spell can use the runes as though touching the caster, and the associated Intangible Tunnel has the rune effect’s level. Each rune spell also gives its target a Warping Point, with no option to avoid that cost.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: New Virtue: Hermetic Rune Magic (ars-magica-magic#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to every rune spell leaving a traceable link and causing one Warping Point; a world can reduce exposure only by destroying the runes, which ends the benefit.

rules.statement: To create something with a rune spell, the caster writes on an Arcane Connection to it, and the target is created only if it does not already exist; the runes effectively transform the connection into the target. A healing effect substitutes for natural healing, so the inscription must remain until natural recovery would have finished; if interrupted earlier, an immediate Recovery roll determines whether the wound stays healed, reopens, or worsens.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Rune Magic and Creo Spells (ars-magica-magic#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to requiring a genuine connection for creation and natural recovery time for healing; a world can make interrupted healing riskier, with worsening injury as the cost.

rules.statement: A rune-enchanted device must be opened as usual, then takes an additional season to design the effect; its runes must be inscribed on the device, and damage to those runes stops the effect as damage to the device would. Elder Verditius Rune initiates may add their Rune Magic score instead of the usual +2 matching-wood bonus and always know a rune for their desired magical focus.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Hermetic Integration — Enchantment Runes (ars-magica-magic#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to device effects being tied to intact inscriptions and requiring an extra season; a world can allow faster crafting at the cost of fragile or less specialized devices.

rules.statement: A Gifted hedge wizard needs a master who is also Gifted and whose Gift was already opened to that tradition; opening takes one full season for both. If the apprentice has no supernatural scores, opening succeeds automatically, but existing scores require an Opening Total at least equal to twice their sum, counting Virtue-granted Minor scores as at least 2 and Major scores as at least 6, and adding 12 if the Gift was previously opened by another tradition.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Opening the Gift (ars-magica-magic#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a one-season, master-led opening; a world can raise the threshold or alter the ritual, because preexisting powers make the transition harder.

rules.statement: When the Opening Total reaches the Ease Factor but does not exceed twice it, the apprentice loses existing Supernatural Ability and Art scores, along with Virtues or Flaws attached to them. If the master lacks score 2 in any of the tradition’s relevant abilities or Arts, the apprentice gains a magic-affecting Flaw for each deficiency; an Opening Total below the Ease Factor cannot open the Gift.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Opening the Gift; Flawed Opening of The Gift (ars-magica-magic#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to losing prior powers unless the master’s total is more than double the threshold; a world can make retention easier or harder, reflecting how disruptive the opening is.

rules.statement: After a Gift has been opened, learning a new Supernatural Ability costs source quality equal to at least 15, or equal to the character’s combined Ability and Art scores if that sum is higher. If a magus opens Arts for an apprentice whose Gift was opened by a hedge tradition, add 30 to the required Intellego Vim Lab Total.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Opening the Gift; Opening the Arts (ars-magica-magic#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a growing source-quality penalty and a 30-point barrier for Hermetic opening; a world can adjust either cost to represent how resistant traditions are to cross-training.

rules.statement: A hedge wizard’s trained magical defense is either a bonus to the wizard or a penalty to an attacker: use the relevant Art score divided by 5, rounded up, or the relevant Supernatural Ability score. Defenses do not stack, do not affect Personal-range effects, apply even when the wizard is unconscious, and can also hinder friendly effects; usually they protect only the wizard, not companions.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Magic Defenses (ars-magica-magic#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one best applicable defense that works automatically; a world can make defenses selective or shareable, at the cost of reducing their dependable protection.

rules.statement: Within an Aegis, a hedge wizard’s cast effect has half the Aegis level subtracted from its Casting Total; an effect cast toward the Aegis must penetrate its level to succeed. A wizard with an Aegis token or who helped cast it is exempt; a Gifted wizard entering by mundane means feels a tingle.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Hedge Wizards and the Aegis of the Hearth (ars-magica-magic#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to an area barrier that taxes casting inside and requires penetration from outside; a world can tune its level or exempted groups, reflecting the site’s protection and access customs.

rules.statement: In the specialty of a hedge wizard’s defense, spells on the wizard expire early: Diameter effects lose rounds, Sun effects hours, Moon effects days, and Year effects weeks, by the defense bonus, with minimum remaining durations of one round, Diameter, Sun, and Moon respectively. Momentary, Concentration, and Ring spells are unaffected, and other targets retain normal duration.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Accelerated Expiry (ars-magica-magic#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to shortening ongoing effects on the defended wizard while preserving minimum durations; a world can broaden or narrow affected durations, reflecting the defense’s specialty.

rules.statement: During an effect with Concentration Duration targeting a defended hedge wizard, add the wizard’s defense bonus to the caster’s Concentration Ease Factor. If several defended wizards are included in one Group or large Target, only the highest bonus applies to the caster’s single roll.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Confounding Magics (ars-magica-magic#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one strongest bonus disrupting concentration; a world can allow cumulative disruption, making groups of defenders especially costly to maintain magic against.

rules.statement: A hedge wizard under physical or mental control in the defense’s specialty gets a resistance roll each round: Strength plus defense bonus, a simple die, minus effect magnitude, against Ease Factor 9. Failure leaves the effect active for that round, and another attempt is made next round.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Immovable Object (ars-magica-magic#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to repeated chances to resist control, even from friendly effects; a world can increase the Ease Factor or remove repeat attempts, reflecting stronger control or a more dangerous defense.

rules.statement: For each season spent studying an insight source, roll Intelligence + Magic Theory against Ease Factor 18; Inventive Genius adds 3 and a source may add modifiers. Success yields an insight, failure yields none but permits another attempt in a later season, and a botch gives a false insight revealed when the resulting effect proves wholly Hermetic or nonfunctional.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: The Integration Process (ars-magica-magic#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one seasonal research attempt; a world can alter the target or modifiers, with time and false conclusions as the costs.

rules.statement: A text or relic usually grants one fixed insight, shared by anyone studying that source. A teacher grants as many insights per associated Breakthrough as their Hedge Magic Theory score; a Gifted teacher may assist one researcher per season, and each researcher may have only one such assistant that season.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: The Integration Process (ars-magica-magic#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to fixed insights from sources and a teacher-limited supply; a world can make sources more or less generous, with scarcity and access as the costs.

rules.statement: An insight specifies exactly one effect, whose Range, Duration, Target, and other parameters cannot be varied during its invention. Successful invention requires experimentation and grants breakthrough points equal to the effect’s magnitude; others need its Lab Text to reproduce it exactly, and reproduction grants no points without the relevant insight.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Creating the Effect (ars-magica-magic#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a fixed, experimental prototype that advances research by its magnitude; a world can change how restrictive prototypes are, with experimentation and Lab Text access as costs.

rules.statement: A researcher continues gathering breakthrough points until reaching the Breakthrough threshold; integration points may be combined with original-research points. Hedge researchers generally need twice the points of equivalent Hermetic researchers, and inventing Hedge Magic Theory usually requires 60 points minus the researcher’s greatest relevant Theory score.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: The Integration Process; Hermetic Use of Hedge Theory; Original Research and Ancient Magic; Integration by Hedge Wizard Researchers (ars-magica-magic#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to cumulative research progress, with hedge researchers facing a doubled threshold; a world can alter the threshold, trading research time for broader discoveries.

rules.statement: Initiations for unGifted characters must impose an Ordeal that grants a Flaw or removes a Virtue; prior Ordeals cannot count again. An unGifted character can be Mystagogue only if they know the power being developed, and cannot initiate themselves.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: UnGifted Initiations (ars-magica-magic#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a fresh, lasting personal sacrifice for each unGifted initiation; a world can change the required sacrifice, with lost benefits or acquired flaws as the price.

rules.statement: An elementalist may spend matching Aquam, Auram, Ignem, or Terram vis to add 2 per pawn to a Summoning, Controlling, or Divining total, but not Refining; the per-effect limit is the sum of all four Form scores. Studying a Form from vis costs pawns equal to its score, while studying a Technique costs half its score rounded up in pawns of one chosen Form.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Elementalist Characters (ars-magica-magic#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to matching vis as a capped boost and study fuel; a world can alter the conversion rate, with scarce vis and limited Art capacity as costs.

rules.statement: Warping and Form scores determine elemental temperament Traits: use the Warping Score plus the associated Form score divided by 5, rounded up. Traits add to Soak against their element but penalize recovery from matching humor illnesses; at +3, +6, and +10 they respectively impose minor, major, and storyguide-controlled behavior flaws.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Elemental Warping (ars-magica-magic#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to growing mental and physical elemental influence as Warping accumulates; a world can change thresholds or benefits, with vulnerability and reduced agency as costs.

rules.statement: Summoning uses a stress die + Stamina + Summoning + the relevant Form + aura, and always costs one long-term Fatigue level. It takes minutes to hours, places a successful target within immediate reach, and the total must meet both the target’s Might and Size requirements.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Elementalist Techniques — Summoning (ars-magica-magic#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to drawing an eligible target nearby, bounded by both its Might and Size; a world can broaden targets or reduce time, with fatigue and delay as costs.

rules.statement: Summoning can use multiple elemental Forms only when the practitioner knows each one; success uses the lowest relevant Form score, while targets meeting only one of several criteria favor the higher-scored Form.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Summoning (ars-magica-magic#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the lowest relevant Form as the limiting skill; a world can permit separate attempts instead, at the cost of less reliable multi-element targeting.

rules.statement: A prepared, undisturbed boundary holds the summoned target in place; breaking or opening it releases the target. While a target remains bound, the summoner does not recover the long-term Fatigue spent to summon it, so practitioners generally bind no more than two or three targets at once.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Summoning (ars-magica-magic#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to containment lasting until the boundary is disturbed; a world can make seals easier or harder to break, with the summoner paying unrecovered fatigue while captives remain.

rules.statement: When a target summoned with the Summoning Art is held in its prepared container, later Elementalist effects against it are treated as level 0 for penetration, and the full casting total is applied to penetration; this lets the practitioner penetrate resistance only once for the later effect.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Summoning (ars-magica-magic#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the container reducing the effective level to 0; a world can remove this advantage, requiring repeated penetration against resistant targets.

rules.statement: A botched summoning can bring the being without safeguards, attract a different being such as an angel or demon, or channel excess elemental power into the summoner and cause sickness or injury.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Summoning (ars-magica-magic#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to loss of control producing a hazardous or unintended result; a world can narrow the mishap outcomes, at the cost of less dramatic backlash.

rules.statement: Medicinal Summoning requires touch and can restore or disrupt bodily humors to address disease, but does not heal wounds unrelated to deprivation, disease, or aging. A total matching the target’s Size threshold treats a Light wound or minor illness; each magnitude above that raises the affected severity by one step, through an Incapacitating wound or critical illness at three magnitudes above.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Medicinal (ars-magica-magic#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to touch and the listed severity thresholds; a world can allow remote treatment or broader healing, with greater difficulty or resource cost.

rules.statement: Theurgical elementals persist indefinitely but do not recover spent Might naturally; when their Might Pool reaches zero, they revert to their original material and leave no vis. Each pawn of vis they consume restores 5 Might points.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Theurgical; Summoning Elementals (ars-magica-magic#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to persistence until Might is exhausted, then reversion; a world can grant natural Might recovery, but should charge upkeep or another resource.

rules.statement: Controlling requires gestures, an incantation, one round, and one Fatigue level that is not long-term; the total is stress die + Presence + Controlling + relevant Form + aura. A successful effect must penetrate resistance, except that a bound summoned target is treated as level 0 for penetration.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Controlling (ars-magica-magic#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a one-round command attempt costing fatigue; a world can reduce the cost or remove the spoken-and-gestured requirement, making control easier to use.

rules.statement: Divining costs no Fatigue. It can detect an appropriate target within about 100 paces while concentrating if its total exceeds the target’s Size threshold, without penetrating resistance; touch-based understanding and communication require exceeding both Size and Might thresholds and penetrating resistance, unless the target is held in a Summoning container.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Divining (ars-magica-magic#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to short-range detection and more demanding touch-based communion; a world can widen the detection range or relax the touch requirement, at the cost of weaker certainty.

rules.statement: Refining takes a season and requires a workshop or laboratory plus cooperation from the target, unless it is held in a Summoning container. A longevity potion takes a season and costs pawns of vis equal to age divided by 5, rounded up; it adds Refining Total divided by 5 to Aging rolls until an Aging crisis, and vis spending cannot exceed the sum of the user’s Elementalist Form scores.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Refining (ars-magica-magic#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to seasonal work and a vis cost capped by Form scores; a world can make potions cheaper or quicker, with reduced duration or potency.

rules.statement: A folk witch’s Casting Total is her relevant Characteristic, Supernatural Ability, aura modifier, and a stress die; the Ability sets effect magnitude, and the equivalent spell level is five times the Ability score. A Gifted witch may spend one pawn of the appropriate vis for +1 to her Casting Score, up to the Ability score plus the effect’s vis cost; an unGifted witch cannot use vis this way.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Folk Witch Powers (ars-magica-magic#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to ability-based effects and a vis bonus only for Gifted witches; a world can change the cap or bonus to tune potency, with vis availability and Gifted status as the cost.

rules.statement: A witch must use the prescribed method for each Ability: a potion must be drunk, an incantation must be heard, or a fetish must be held. A fetish takes a season to prepare, must be made by its user, and one of several fetishes for the same Ability can serve as a spare.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Casting Methods (ars-magica-magic#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a fixed, Ability-specific access method; a world can allow more flexible methods, at the cost of weakening the tradition’s dependence on prepared items, speech, or potions.

rules.statement: On a botch, the effect usually still occurs but is uncontrolled, and the witch gains one Warping Point for each zero on the botch dice.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Botches (ars-magica-magic#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to uncontrolled effects and one Warping Point per zero; a world can soften or intensify botches, with loss of control and accumulated Warping as the cost.

rules.statement: A curse woven into a fetish requires an active Arcane Connection at the start of a season of kitchen work, and the curse must penetrate the target’s Magic Resistance throughout that season. Disease, miscarriage, and aging curses activate when the fetish is finished; other listed curses can persist until the fetish is destroyed, the connection expires, or magic cancels them.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Curse Fetish Weaving (ars-magica-magic#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a season-long, target-linked preparation with an enduring fetish; a world can shorten preparation or weaken the connection requirement, at the cost of making remote curses easier.

rules.statement: Flight requires an Ease Factor of 9. Using a flight fetish costs one Long Term Fatigue level even on a failed roll, while using a potion costs none; successful flight lasts a number of hours equal to the Ability score unless the witch touches ground, and a botch costs additional Long Term Fatigue equal to the botch count.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Flight (ars-magica-magic#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to fatigue-costing fetish flight and fatigue-free potion flight; a world can alter duration or cost, balancing mobility against exhaustion or access to potions.

rules.statement: Healing must penetrate the target’s Magic Resistance and spend Corpus vis according to the wound or fatigue level: Ease Factors 6, 9, 12, and 15 cost respectively 3–6 pawns for wounds or 1–4 for fatigue. It cannot heal the dead or restore fatigue to the unconscious, and it does not work if the required vis is unavailable.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Healing (ars-magica-magic#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to vis-funded recovery with higher costs for worse conditions; a world can change the costs or targets, with scarce vis limiting the power to restore health and stamina.

rules.statement: A folk witch can extract, in a season, Vim vis equal to one tenth of her Lab Total rounded up, with no Supernatural Ability added to that total. She can use at most twice her Folk Witch Magic Theory score in vis on laboratory projects in a season.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Vis (ars-magica-magic#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to modest seasonal extraction and a Theory-based spending cap; a world can raise either limit, with increased access to vis accelerating laboratory work.

rules.statement: In a season, a witch can improve one Arcane Connection’s lifetime by one step, with the new duration measured in units equal to her Lab Total. The work needs a kitchen and one pawn of Vim vis; the connection must be active when work begins but gains at least the season of work even if its natural duration ends sooner.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Fixing Arcane Connections (ars-magica-magic#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one connection improved per season for a pawn of Vim vis; a world can change the duration or cost, with valuable vis and kitchen time limiting the extension.

rules.statement: A character who successfully completes the Rite of Opening the Mind gains Premonitions 1 and Visions, after a season of righteous conduct and a season of sponsor instruction. The righteous-conduct season requires a Stamina roll against Ease Factor 9, adjusted by relevant Personality Traits; on failure, the character may stay another season and try again.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Rite of Opening the Mind (ars-magica-magic#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a retryable test of sustained conduct before prophecy is granted; a world can make the test harder or the ordeal longer, with time and disciplined behavior as the cost.

rules.statement: A brewed dose resolves as though its drinker had just used the relevant ability, with a total equal to the brewer’s ability Lab Total plus a stress die. The resulting success and penetration are checked normally, but neither brewer nor drinker adds a Penetration Ability bonus, and the brewing-site aura affects the Lab Total while the drinking-site aura does not affect the casting total.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Potion brewing; Potion Casting Total (ars-magica-magic#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default doses use the fixed brew total plus a stress die; a world could change the site or penetration rules, with resistance and vis limiting effectiveness.

rules.statement: A brew takes one season and yields up to a number of doses equal to Folk Witch Magic Theory; a Lab Text can add up to its level in extra doses. Each dose costs one pawn of appropriate vis, and the effect’s vis cost is paid once per batch; making fewer doses does not shorten the season, and doses last until consumed.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Potion brewing; Doses per Brew (ars-magica-magic#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default stored effects last indefinitely until drunk; a world could vary batch yield or shelf-life, while vis cost and a full season constrain production.

rules.statement: A dose can temporarily grant an ability without requiring its usual fetish or spoken incantation; for Animal Ken, Dowsing, Flight, and Second Sight, the granted score is the Brew Potency divided by 5, rounded up. Animal Ken and Second Sight last Brew Potency days, while Dowsing lasts one search and Flight one flight.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Potion Effects (ars-magica-magic#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default potions grant the listed ability score and duration; a world could adjust which abilities are potion-grantable, with a dose consumed and resistance still relevant.

rules.statement: A brewed curse is fixed for every dose in its batch. Disease, miscarriage, and aging curses trigger on drinking without remaining as ongoing magic; other curses persist until magically reversed or until a year and a day has passed, and a curse requiring an Ease Factor of 18 only works if potency plus stress die reaches that value and penetrates resistance.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Potion Effects — Cursing (ars-magica-magic#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default curses follow their defined trigger and duration; a world could alter duration or severity, with resistance and the fixed brew type limiting use.

rules.statement: A shapeshifting dose changes the drinker into the animal chosen when the batch was made, using an animal part and the witch’s matching fetish during brewing. The change lasts Brew Potency days, can be ended early by the drinker, and cannot then be resumed; at the normal end the drinker returns to natural form.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Potion Effects — Shapeshifter (ars-magica-magic#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default transformation lasts the stated days and permits early one-way release; a world could vary duration or reversion, with an animal ingredient and fetish as costs.

rules.statement: A witch can bind one animal familiar in a one-season laboratory activity if her Animal Ken Lab Total exceeds 10 plus the animal’s Size and Magic Might. If her familiar dies, she may bind another.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Familiars (ars-magica-magic#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default capacity is one living familiar and binding requires a full season and sufficient total; a world could raise the slot limit, with the binding threshold as its cost.

rules.statement: A bound familiar gains human Intelligence at −3 if it lacked it, learns the witch’s languages at her score, and can learn ordinary Abilities but not magic or Supernatural Abilities. It adds its Intelligence plus Folk Witch Magic Theory to her Lab Total as an assistant.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Familiars — Benefits of a Familiar (ars-magica-magic#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default familiar assistance adds its two scores; a world could change the bonus or learning limits, with the familiar’s capability determining its value.

rules.statement: The witch and familiar are mutual Arcane Connections and can affect one another magically without overcoming each other’s Magic Resistance. The familiar does not age to death while the witch lives, and suffers aging effects only when she does.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Familiars — Benefits of a Familiar (ars-magica-magic#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default bond bypasses mutual resistance and ties aging to the witch; a world could remove either benefit, with shared vulnerability as the bond’s consequence.

rules.statement: When Warping increases a witch’s score by 1, she immediately undergoes a Witch Moon lasting at least one month: she loses all Supernatural Abilities and suffers a disease-treated Medium Wound from fever. At each month’s end she rolls Stamina minus Warping Score plus a stress die against Ease Factor 6; failure adds a Warping Point and another month and wound, while a botch adds Warping Points equal to the botch die’s zeros.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Warping — The Witch Moon (ars-magica-magic#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default crisis suppresses abilities for a month at a time and adds wounds and Warping on failure; a world could change the recovery threshold, with escalating injury and loss of powers as the price.

rules.statement: The special Arts-opening method takes one season and lets an apprentice learn Supernatural Abilities without the usual penalty to study Source Quality from Arts scores; penalties from other Supernatural Ability scores still apply. Experimental discovery can earn 5 breakthrough points, but other experimental outcomes can damage or remove the apprentice’s Gift.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Hermetic Integration — Subtle Opening; Integration Effects (ars-magica-magic#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to removing only the Arts-based study penalty; a world can broaden or restrict the benefit, with experimental risk to the apprentice’s Gift.

rules.statement: Energy Magic permits Corpus effects to alter Fatigue: Perdo Corpus at level 5 can double short-term recovery time or remove a short-term level, at level 10 can remove a long-term level, and at level 15 can prevent recovery through rest. Creo Corpus at level 5 halves short-term recovery time, at level 10 restores a short-term level, and at level 15 restores a long-term level.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Hermetic Integration — Energy Magic; New Energy Magic Virtue & Guidelines (ars-magica-magic#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the listed Fatigue changes at their stated levels; a world can tune their availability, balancing recovery against exhaustion and spellcasting costs.

rules.statement: A Creo Corpus ritual with Momentary Duration truly restores Fatigue; with any other Duration, the restored levels return as Long-Term Fatigue when the effect ends, even if they were originally short-term.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Hermetic Integration — Energy Magic; New Creo Corpus Guidelines (ars-magica-magic#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to permanent recovery only from Momentary rituals; a world can allow temporary relief, at the cost of later Long-Term Fatigue.

rules.statement: A magus with the Ritual Items Virtue can make charged items that produce ritual effects. Each charge consumes the same pawns of vis the effect would normally require, subject to the usual seasonal vis-use limit and normal charge limits.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: New Virtue: Ritual Items (ars-magica-magic#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to ritual effects stored in charges, with vis paid per charge; a world can vary access to such items, constrained by vis supply and seasonal capacity.

rules.statement: The Sense of the Mystic Virtue lets the magus’s Intellego effects that grant a magic sense work without penetrating the sensed creature’s Magic Resistance; the effect must still penetrate the resistance of the person receiving the sense.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: New Virtue: Sense of the Mystic (ars-magica-magic#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to bypassing resistance only for the sensed creature; a world can broaden that exception, while the recipient’s resistance remains a limit.

rules.statement: An intact External Soul prevents death or incapacitating injury from physical harm and prevents dismemberment; damage that would cause those outcomes is redistributed among lesser wounds. Each such redistribution causes a Warping Point unless a Stamina + Pictish stress roll reaches 9; damage to the separate soul-object, even a scratch, kills the character.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Gruagach Virtues — External Soul (ars-magica-magic#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to physical injury being redistributed while the anchor survives; a world can change the protection, but the vulnerable soul-object is the fatal cost.

rules.statement: A character with External Soul is unaging but gains 1 Warping Point per year from the ongoing mystical effect; extraction of the soul cannot be reversed.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Gruagach Virtues — External Soul (ars-magica-magic#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to unaging with yearly Warping; a world can adjust the rate, trading longevity for accumulating mystical distortion.

rules.statement: A fetch is normally invisible, incorporeal, and unable to affect its surroundings; it can become solid to warn its master of imminent danger. A fetch granted by the Virtue has Second Sight 9 and warns of sensed danger, though its warning may be unclear or mistaken.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Gruagach Virtues — Fetch (ars-magica-magic#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a vigilant but fallible companion that can briefly interact to warn; a world can change its reliability or abilities, with ambiguity as the built-in limitation.

rules.statement: Casting requires knowledge of both the relevant Technique and Form, represented by a score of at least 0 in each. An unGifted character without an Art-specific Virtue cannot use that Art’s guidelines, regardless of other Art knowledge.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Gruagach Arts (ars-magica-magic#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.mechanism: law: art access requires both components
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to requiring both Art components; a world can loosen access for unGifted people, at the cost of making the tradition less exclusive.

rules.statement: A casting score is Technique + Form + Stamina + Aura Modifier. Formulaic total adds a die; Spontaneous total is half the casting score plus a stress die, and every Spontaneous casting costs Fatigue. Formulaic spells succeed without Fatigue if the total meets the spell level; if short by no more than 10 they succeed at a cost of one Fatigue level, and if short by more than 10 they fail and still cost one Fatigue level.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Gruagach Spells (ars-magica-magic#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to these totals and Fatigue thresholds; a world can change the reserve or thresholds, with harder casting increasing the risk of exhaustion.

rules.statement: A known Formulaic spell may vary only one of Range, Duration, Target, or size per casting, and the revised spell must be within 2 magnitudes of the original and use an available parameter. Success, Fatigue loss, and Penetration use the revised level; each full 5 points of Mastery Score adds 1 magnitude to the allowed variation.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Gruagach Spells; Flexible Casting (ars-magica-magic#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a 2-magnitude adjustment and one changed parameter; a world can widen the range through mastery, trading greater adaptability for investment in spell mastery.

rules.statement: Spells require vocalization, except a Personal-range spell may be cast silently; the tradition cannot use Quiet Magic. A caster need not sense a target if the target can hear the caster and can be described, even vaguely.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Ranges, Durations, and Targets (ars-magica-magic#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to vocal casting and voice-based identification; a world can permit silent casting more broadly, at the cost of reducing the importance of audibility and proximity.

rules.statement: Geas and Limit conditions must be fixed when cast, achievable by the target, and genuinely restrictive. For either duration, a sweeping, general, or specific prohibition adds respectively +4/+2/+1 magnitudes for Geas and +1/+2/+4 magnitudes for Limit.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Geas and Limit Durations (ars-magica-magic#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to condition-bound effects with graded casting difficulty; a world can simplify the grades, at the cost of less distinction between broad and narrow conditions.

rules.statement: A Geas spell must state aloud the prohibited action and consequences or it fails; the target need not hear, understand, or share a language with the caster. A Geas effect lasts until its condition is met or it is dispelled, and its punishment has a separate Limit condition; only the larger of their duration modifiers raises the spell level.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Geas (Condition) Duration (ars-magica-magic#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to an announced threat with a separate trigger and release condition; a world can require the target to understand the terms, at the cost of making language and communication decisive.

rules.statement: A Limit-duration blessing or curse remains until its specified condition is fulfilled; blessings and curses must use this duration. Such an effect causes Warping while active, whereas a Geas does not count as active until its prohibition is broken, so an obeying target does not Warp.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Limit (Condition) Duration; Geas and Limit Durations in Play (ars-magica-magic#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to persistent condition-based effects and Warping only for active Limit effects; a world can make all such magic Warp, charging a higher long-term cost even for compliant targets.

rules.statement: A magic tattoo is designed for one recipient, uses Personal range and Individual target, and has material score 2 multiplied by size: 1 for a tiny tattoo, 2 for palm/forehead size, 3 for a limb or scalp, and 4 for a torso. It cannot be copied from a Lab Text for another recipient; long-term mystical effects cause Warping, while creation and brief powerful effects do not.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Enchanting Tattoos (ars-magica-magic#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to recipient-specific tattoos with size-scaled capacity and long-term Warping; a world can allow transferable designs, at the cost of weakening their personal bond.

rules.statement: A curse can reduce one Ability by 1, 2, or 3 at levels 5, 10, or 15; reduce one Characteristic by 1, 2, or 3 at levels 15, 20, or 25; or inflict specified Flaws, diseases, sensory loss, or a disabled limb at the listed guideline levels. A curse must include a related prohibition or geas, and a target who passes Magic Resistance may still resist with Stamina against Ease Factor 9, modified by how fitting the punishment is.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Give Curse Guidelines (ars-magica-magic#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a related condition that lifts the curse and a Stamina resistance check at Ease Factor 9; a world can make prohibitions easier or harder to satisfy, reflecting how severe or fitting the punishment is.

rules.statement: A curse cannot impose certain social, story, or realm-related Flaws, nor Flaws that affect experience accumulation, prevent learning particular Abilities, or concern wealth. Without a prohibition, a curse is allowed only as punishment for breaking a geas; sweeping, general, and specific prohibitions differ by how easy they are to fulfill.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Give Curse Guidelines (ars-magica-magic#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to restricting curses to permitted Flaws and relevant prohibitions; a world can broaden or narrow that list, trading flexibility against the tradition's limits.

rules.statement: Every Give Curse spell must have either Geas or Limit Duration. A separate spell is needed for each specific Ability, disease, Flaw, or sense targeted; all guidelines assume Conversation range.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Give Curse Guidelines (ars-magica-magic#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one defined target and a required ending condition or duration; a world can allow broader curses, at the cost of making their scope less constrained.

rules.statement: If a Take Curse spell fails to remove a curse, the caster suffers that curse too; a botch instead gives the caster a stronger curse tailored to them. A general spell can identify a curse's terms, remove a curse the caster placed, or remove another's curse or continuing spell.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Take Curse Guidelines (ars-magica-magic#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to transferring a failed curse-removal attempt's effect to the caster and worsening it on a botch; a world can soften this danger, reducing the cost of counter-magic.

rules.statement: A general Take Curse spell reveals the caster, level, duration, and Limit of a curse when its level plus one stress die meets the curse's level; it also reveals a geas's terms. Removal requires the spell level plus one stress die to reach twice the target spell's level, except that a caster can remove their own curse by meeting its level.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Question the Cursed; Lift the Unfair Curse (ars-magica-magic#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the stated level thresholds for diagnosis and removal; a world can adjust the threshold, making curses more or less resistant to investigation and dispelling.

rules.statement: Give Shape effects require a willing recipient, who may refuse as the change begins; after accepting, the recipient cannot revoke the choice or dispel the effect before its duration ends. Shape spells also incorporate the target's carried items into the new form.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Give Shape Guidelines (ars-magica-magic#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to consent at onset and carried items transforming with the target; a world can permit later reversal or leave items behind, changing the risks of transformation.

rules.statement: Take Shape can force a target to change form, but after Magic Resistance is overcome the target may resist with Stamina against Ease Factor 9, adjusted by an appropriate Personality Trait. Returning a target to its true form is a general effect; removing another transformation generally requires a spell level plus a stress die equal to twice its level.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Take Shape Guidelines; Return the Lycanthrope to his Native Form (ars-magica-magic#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to personality-adjusted resistance and the stated removal threshold; a world can make mental disposition irrelevant or more influential, changing how hard forced changes are to resist.

rules.statement: Give Vision effects create sight or sound images, but not other sensory effects; complex illusions cost an additional magnitude and images that move or change at the caster's direction cost two additional magnitudes. Visions or Premonitions must concern a selected subject or question.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Give Vision Guidelines (ars-magica-magic#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to sight-and-sound illusions with added cost for complexity and animation; a world can expand the senses affected, at the cost of less bounded illusion-making.

rules.statement: A Vision spell botch gives twice the normal Warping Points. A gruagach who gains at least two Warping Points from one botch, or suffers another suitable powerful magical effect, may undergo transformation; at Warping Score 10 the transformation into a troll is complete and the storyguide controls the character.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Botches; Effects of Transformation (ars-magica-magic#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to escalating magical distortion, with Vision botches doubling Warping and score 10 completing troll transformation; a world can change the threshold or severity, altering the long-term cost of magic.

rules.statement: A koldun using a vision charm to sense something at a distance must gaze into water. A spell using an Arcane Connection works only if the Connection is fully submerged; casting at Arcane Connection Range adds 4 Magnitudes to the spell level.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Kolduni — Magic (ars-magica-magic#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Require water for distant sensing and connection-based spells; a world can relax the requirement, but koldun magic is tied to water.

rules.statement: A koldun's external soul returns to the body if destroyed by the wrong method; only its specific destruction method kills the koldun. The character must take Durable External Soul as an extra Major Virtue, and must repeat the External Soul initiation if the soul is destroyed the wrong way.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Kolduni — Magic (ars-magica-magic#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Let an external soul preserve its owner unless destroyed correctly; a world can make it more fragile, with the cost of losing that protection.

rules.statement: Flexible Formulaic Magic mastery permits changing one of a spell's Range, Duration, Target, or size parameters when the final level stays within one Magnitude per full 5 Mastery points. A proposed integration would raise that allowance to two Magnitudes per 5 points.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Integration of Gruagach Magic — Flexible Formulaic Magic (ars-magica-magic#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Allow one parameter to shift within the stated mastery limit; a world can increase the allowance, trading precision for greater flexibility.

rules.statement: A voice-range spell may affect a target the caster cannot sense if the target can hear the caster and the caster can describe it, even vaguely. The proposed spell increase is 3 Magnitudes, though a troupe may waive it.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Integration of Gruagach Magic — Improved Voice Range (ars-magica-magic#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Permit audible, described targets without sensing them; a world can charge 3 Magnitudes, reflecting the reach beyond ordinary targeting.

rules.statement: Mythic alchemy produces permanent, nonmagical transmutations that cannot be dispelled, but solids must remain solids and liquids liquids. Each dose costs 1 pawn of suitable vis per 5 points of final reagent level, rounded up; an alchemist handles at most twice their Mythic Alchemy score in pawns per season.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Virtues and Flaws — Mythic Alchemy (ars-magica-magic#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Make completed transmutations permanent while retaining state-of-matter and vis limits; a world can ease the limits, at the cost of rare vis and seasonal work.

rules.statement: Mythic Herbalism concoctions take days equal to one-third the effect's Ease Factor to brew. The maker rolls Intelligence plus Mythic Herbalism against that Ease Factor; failure makes the concoction useless, and a botch may poison maker or recipient. Unused preparations expire after one season.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Virtues and Flaws — Mythic Herbalism (ars-magica-magic#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Require preparation time and a success check, with botches risking harm; a world can allow reliable brewing, at the cost of longer work or scarce ingredients.

rules.statement: Herbal remedies can aid recovery for one month unless otherwise specified, while physical-bonus potions last for Sun Duration. Effects do not stack; fatigue-roll bonuses cap at +2, only one fatigue level can be ignored per day, and Soak bonuses do not stack. When a spell and poultice both aid recovery, only the larger bonus applies.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Virtues and Flaws — Mythic Herbalism (ars-magica-magic#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Use short durations and non-stacking benefits; a world can extend or stack them, at the cost of stronger preparations or greater risk.

rules.statement: Tueor protects a target against a particular kind of harm, not every danger associated with a Form; protection against common harms is harder to create than protection against rare, narrowly specified ones. Nonmagical attacks are covered by the relevant protection, but attacks that must penetrate Magic Resistance are not.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Magic of the Learned Magicians — The Arts: Tueor (ars-magica-magic#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Limit protection to a specified harm and make broad threats harder to cover; a world can broaden protection, at the cost of greater difficulty.

rules.statement: Succurro can enhance an existing quality but cannot grant an ability with no basis in the target, create something from nothing, instantly heal, or make unnatural alterations such as growing wings or seeing through walls.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Magic of the Learned Magicians — The Arts: Succurro (ars-magica-magic#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Allow improvement of existing traits but not creation of new ones; a world can loosen that boundary, at the cost of more potent and less constrained magic.

rules.statement: Vulnero effects must harm their target and cannot wholly erase an aspect; the closer an effect comes to completely destroying an aspect, the harder it is to make. It works most readily on an aspect that is already weak.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Vulnero (Vu) (ars-magica-magic#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to harmful weakening rather than complete removal; worlds can vary how difficult deeper damage becomes because destroying more of an aspect makes the charm harder to create.

rules.statement: Salutem can affect the health of any living creature, but not abstract entities. It may restore health-related loss only as far as the target's normal condition; it cannot improve a healthy target beyond normal or above-average ability.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Salutem (Sa) (ars-magica-magic#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to treating health as a living-target property with recovery capped at the target's prior normal state; worlds can broaden eligible lifeforms, but cannot use this effect to enhance ordinary capabilities.

rules.statement: A learned magician's Casting Score is Hedge Technique + Hedge Form + Communication + Aura Modifier. The Charm Total is (Casting Score + Die) / 2, or (Casting Score + Stress Die) / 5 when read from text; meeting the charm level succeeds without Fatigue, missing it by at most 10 succeeds at the cost of one Fatigue level, and missing it by more than 10 fails and costs one Fatigue level.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Charm Design (ars-magica-magic#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to these formulas and fatigue thresholds; worlds can change the effort economy, with fatigue representing the cost of a marginal or failed casting.

rules.statement: A charm read from a formulary requires an Intelligence + Language check against Ease Factor 9 to find it in 10 minutes; on failure, searching takes 10 minutes per point failed by. Reading then takes two minutes per magnitude, doubled for Language below 4 and quadrupled at 2 or less; below Language 5, add one botch die for each missing point.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Reading Charms from Text (ars-magica-magic#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to slow, language-dependent access to unlearned charms; worlds can make formularies easier or harder to search, with poor organization and limited language skill causing delay and risk.

rules.statement: An amulet is designed for one named subject and has a finite number of charges, calculated as (Lab Total minus effect level) / 5, rounded up; making it takes one season. A charta has one charge, calculated using Lab Total / 2 against the effect level, and its charge is spent as soon as it is made.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Amulet and Charta Design (ars-magica-magic#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to finite, subject-bound magical devices; worlds can adjust charge yield and preparation time, trading the creator's laboratory capacity and time for stored effects.

rules.statement: When an amulet is put on or affixed to its appropriate target, it spends one charge and runs for its designed Duration; when that Duration ends, it spends the next charge. No charge is spent while it lacks physical contact with an appropriate target; a charta instead spends its sole charge on completion and is useful only if delivered to its recipient then.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Amulet and Charta Effects (ars-magica-magic#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to automatic sequential amulet charges and immediate charta expenditure; worlds can change activation timing, with the current rule making the bearer unable to control charges and chartae vulnerable to delivery delays.

rules.statement: Entreat the Powers adds Stress Die + Presence + Realm Lore to a Casting Score or Lab Total, but its contribution cannot exceed the absolute Aura Modifier. It only offsets negative realm interaction, never supplies the initial effect total or Penetration; calling on a different realm divides the total by the hostile aura.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Mitigation of Realm Interaction Effects (ars-magica-magic#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a capped aura-offset bonus; worlds can permit broader assistance, but the invocation is limited by the hostile aura and cannot improve the magic's basic strength or penetration.

rules.statement: Fortunam affects a single target's luck, though its consequences can alter events involving others.
