A Vulnero Fortunam curse must penetrate Magic Resistance; a protective Tueor effect must penetrate an opponent's resistance in a contested roll, while a Succurro effect affecting only its target need penetrate only that target's resistance.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Fortunam (ars-magica-magic#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to indirect, chance-like changes centered on one target and apply resistance when another resistant person is affected; worlds can make luck more direct, at the cost of losing its indirect character.

rules.statement: A charm aimed at a particular kind of ongoing magic reduces its duration when its casting total is below half the charm’s level plus 4 magnitudes and a stress die; the protected-against magic must be narrower than one Hermetic Form. A separate general ward blocks creatures of one realm whose Might is below the charm’s level.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: General guidelines before Stifle the Lengthy Sickness (ars-magica-magic#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to narrow, level-limited defenses; a world can broaden the protected category or raise the Might threshold, at the cost of stronger magic.

rules.statement: Stifle the Lengthy Sickness reduces a sickness effect’s duration by one magnitude if the charm level plus a stress die and 10 reaches twice the target effect’s casting total; if duration is not magnitude-based, it is halved. A supernatural ability’s equivalent level is its score times 5; the charm does not affect Momentary effects, and each curse or spell type needs its own version.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Stifle the Lengthy Sickness (ars-magica-magic#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one duration step or half duration against a specific sickness effect; a world can allow wider cures, at the cost of requiring separate charms or stronger casting.

rules.statement: A faerie ward prevents a creature with Faerie Might no greater than the charm level from affecting the individual, but must penetrate that creature’s Magic Resistance. It does not block effects without a responsible creature that has a Might score; parallel charms are needed for other realms.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Charm of Protection Against the Faerie (ars-magica-magic#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a realm-specific, Might-capped ward; a world can extend it to other realms or effects, at the cost of separate versions and penetration.

rules.statement: Salutem protection against broad damage categories follows Greater Immunity examples, while narrow categories follow Lesser Immunity examples; such charms never protect against magical damage. Wards can only be set on a Structure or Boundary, cannot affect targets with Might, and must penetrate Magic Resistance to bar a magus from an area.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Tueor Salutem Guidelines (ars-magica-magic#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to nonmagical, category-limited protection with fixed place targets; a world can include magical harms, at the cost of using the separate Magicam approach.

rules.statement: Tueor Salutem guidelines grant +4 Soak per base level against narrow damage or +2 per base level against broad damage; other options grant +1 Stamina per base level for avoiding one disease or poison, +2 Soak per magnitude against all damage, or Defense bonuses of +4 narrow and +2 broad per magnitude. Fixed effects include animal wards at level 2, human-type wards at level 5, immunity to narrow damage at 10, immunity to broad damage at 15, and a ward against all humans at 10.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Tueor Salutem Guidelines (ars-magica-magic#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the stated category and level scaling; a world can permit broader immunity, at the cost of higher levels and stricter target limits.

rules.statement: Succurro Salutem can aid recovery but cannot permanently heal: it grants +2, +6, +12, +18, or +24 to recovery rolls at levels 1–5 respectively for one nonmagical illness, poison, or injury. It can also improve a plant’s growth at level 1 over an area up to ten paces in each direction, and has aging-crisis remedies from minor at level 10 through terminal at level 30.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Succurro Salutem Guidelines (ars-magica-magic#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to temporary support rather than permanent healing; a world can allow lasting cures, at the cost of greater power or a special exception.

rules.statement: A botch can grant one Warping Point per zero on the botch dice; gaining 2 or more Warping Points from one botch may trigger an intervention by an entity of the charm’s realm. At Warping Score 7 the entity’s direct action lasts a stress-die number of seasons, and at score 10 the abduction or loss of magic becomes permanent.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Magical Dangers: Warping and Abduction (ars-magica-magic#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to realm-linked consequences that escalate with Warping; a world can soften or intensify intervention, at the cost of changing the threat of repeated botches.

rules.statement: Mythic alchemists make powders, potions, and smoke-bearing pastilles rather than charms. Potions can be used by anyone and cost 1 pawn of vis per 5 base-effect levels, plus 1 pawn for each additional dose; pastille smoke loses effectiveness quickly in open or windy places.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Mythic Alchemists: Magic (ars-magica-magic#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to consumable, limited-use alchemical effects; a world can make doses cheaper or smoke more persistent, at the cost of vis, exposure, or environmental limits.

rules.statement: Mythic Alchemists gain Warping as learned magicians do, but at Warping Score 3 gain a Minor flaw toward secrecy and suspicion; at 6 or higher they gain a Major paranoid flaw; at 10 the player loses control of their actions because they are insane.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Passage 25, opening paragraph (ars-magica-magic#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to these escalating mental consequences at the stated scores; a setting could change the thresholds or severity, with increasing Warping as the in-world cause.

rules.statement: Quick Charged Items lets a magus make a single-charge item whose effect level is no higher than the magus’s Lab Total. Creation takes one hour per magnitude of effect, and all other charged-item restrictions still apply.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Minor Hermetic Virtue: Quick Charged Items (ars-magica-magic#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one charge and one hour per magnitude, capped by Lab Total; a world could vary the time or cap, with magical preparation as the cost.

rules.statement: During integration of single-use charged items, each device has one charge regardless of Lab Total, and the magus can create only one device per season until achieving a Breakthrough.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Single-Use Charged Items — Integration Effects (ars-magica-magic#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one single-charge device each season until the Breakthrough; a world could relax the rate limit, with research progress as the in-world constraint.

rules.statement: A nightwalker can send their spirit away while unconscious or in an altered state; the spirit can become tangible or intangible, and damage it suffers is reflected on the body. The absent body appears dead and is vulnerable.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Nightwalker; Ekstasis — The Insensate Body; Combat and the Straying Spirit (ars-magica-magic#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a separated spirit with mirrored injury and an exposed, apparently dead body; a world could change the body’s vulnerability, with separation creating the risk.

rules.statement: Straying for an hour costs one Long-Term Fatigue level, while straying for a whole night costs two. A nightwalker may change between corporeal and immaterial forms in three rounds; doing so during combat requires a Stamina + Concentration roll against Ease Factor 15.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Ekstasis — The Insensate Body; The Phantasticum (ars-magica-magic#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the stated fatigue costs and three-round change, with a difficult check in combat; a world could alter duration or fatigue, with exertion limiting use.

rules.statement: Spirit travel can cover great distances almost instantly. A Stamina + Athletics result of 3, 6, 9, 12, or 15 permits travel respectively to a place seen daily, seen in the last week, seen within the last year, previously visited with a known route, or never visited but known by route or Arcane Connection; each extra carried object adds 3 difficulty.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Ekstasis — Travel Through Straying (ars-magica-magic#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the listed familiarity thresholds and +3 per extra object; a world could adjust reach or difficulty, with route knowledge and carried burden as constraints.

rules.statement: A nightwalker’s presence makes a non-resistant person outside spirit form struggle to stay awake, requiring Concentration + Stamina against Ease Factor 3; an already sleeping target is very difficult to wake.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Combat and the Straying Spirit — Drowsiness (ars-magica-magic#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to drowsiness at Ease Factor 3 and stronger suppression of waking; a world could change the resistance threshold, with the spirit’s presence causing the effect.

rules.statement: Nightwalkers must attend their tradition’s fertility battles. Victory preserves normal food production, defeat brings poor crops or fishing until the next battle, and routing the enemy ensures a plentiful harvest.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Fertility Battles (ars-magica-magic#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to seasonal battles affecting local harvests until the next contest; a world could change the battle schedule or stakes, with compulsory attendance and defeat risking scarcity.

rules.statement: During night battles, both factions are corporeal and can be affected by magic normally; regular spells against demons also work when the opposing captain is a demon. Repeated intervention may cause the evil patron to target the magus with a supernatural-entity affliction.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Intervening in the Battles (ars-magica-magic#025)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Let magic affect both sides normally; a setting can make recurring intervention provoke retaliation, with supernatural persecution as the cost.

rules.statement: In spirit form, a nightwalker can inspect the neighborhood while invisible and incorporeal, and may use Second Sight or Sense Unholiness to notice trouble. Spiritual sampling of wine does not reduce its physical quantity, but can speed recovery of battle fatigue.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Returning Home (ars-magica-magic#025)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Allow invisible spirit-form scouting and non-depleting spiritual nourishment; a world can limit recovery to particular offerings and traditions.

rules.statement: While immaterial, nightwalkers can harm and be harmed by ghostly dead as though both were solid. They can question a particular ghost once per night: the difficulty is 3 for a yes-or-no answer, 6 for an answer of one sentence, and 9 for up to six sentences.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: The Processions of the Dead (ars-magica-magic#025)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Treat spirits in the procession as physically interactive and permit one question per ghost nightly; a setting can vary answer difficulty or add personality-based resistance.

rules.statement: A nightwalker may try to intimidate a ghost with Presence and Leadership against a difficulty of 6 plus the ghost’s Brave score. For each additional group member willing to fight, add one to the relevant side’s total.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: The Processions of the Dead (ars-magica-magic#025)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Use the ghost’s courage as a resistance threshold and let group resolve increase pressure; a world can make intimidation ineffective against fearless or protected dead.

rules.statement: If either a nightwalker or an Infernal witch breaks the taboo against discussing their night battles beyond generalities, representatives of the opposing side beat them in dreams, and the resulting injuries carry over to their waking bodies.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Battling Infernal Witches While Awake And Taboos (ars-magica-magic#025)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Enforce the silence taboo through supernatural punishment that transfers dream injuries to the body; a world can increase or reduce the severity of that cost.

rules.statement: After a benandanti feast, the Lady can restore consumed animals if their bones are placed inside their skins. Missing bones must be replaced with alder pieces, while broken bones leave the corresponding body part weak; even correctly restored cattle cannot work afterward.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Feasts of the Domina Ludi: The Lday of the Game (ars-magica-magic#025)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Permit a patron to restore spiritually consumed animals using their remains; a world can make missing or damaged bones impose lasting defects.

rules.statement: A Hound of God can pass the ability to stray to someone who toasts the werewolf’s health: the Hound blows three times over the wine bottle and speaks a formula. The former Hound loses the power after the successor is toasted.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Becoming a Hound of God (ars-magica-magic#025)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Make the ritual transfer the power and duties to one chosen recipient, ending the donor’s access; a world can restrict eligibility or make the succession harder to secure.

rules.statement: A kudlak that dies returns as a vampire unless its corpse is warded by driving in a hawthorn stake or cutting the tendons behind its knees. A kudlak’s victories can also bring temporary wealth until the next battle, with repeated victories improving social standing.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Kresniki and Kudlaki (ars-magica-magic#025)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Let death trigger return unless a specified corpse-preparation blocks it; a world can make the countermeasure culturally specific and tie repeated victories to social rewards.

rules.statement: In flame shape, a taltós uses the applicable human Abilities and gains the listed elemental-like physical traits; its Brawl attacks deal +5 fire damage. It is immune to mundane fire and wooden weapons, but if completely extinguished it dies.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Statistics and Abilities for Flame Shape (ars-magica-magic#025)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Grant a flame body with altered traits, attack damage, and defined immunities; a world can make extinguishing a lethal counter or alter the form’s vulnerabilities.

rules.statement: Rune effects can grant bonuses or penalties measured by their magnitude; for example, recovery modifiers under Berkanan equal three times magnitude, while many ability modifiers equal magnitude. Where a guideline sets a characteristic change, each further magnitude increases the change or its limit, but the score cannot exceed five points above or below the type's average.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Rune Guidelines throughout; individual rune headings (ars-magica-magic#027)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the stated magnitude-based modifier; a setting can change which rolls qualify, reflecting how closely a rune's theme applies.

rules.statement: Many effects persist only while their inscribed runes remain intact; removing or damaging the inscription can end an effect. A healing inscription that is interrupted before a Light Wound's week-long recovery period forces an immediate recovery check, which can leave the wound healed, reopen it, or worsen it to Medium.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Sample Berkanan Rune Spells (ars-magica-magic#027)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to rune integrity as the duration limit; a world can allow longer-lasting runes, at the cost of making their destruction less consequential.

rules.statement: Two applicable communication bonuses do not add together: use only the greater bonus. A persistent year-long Jera benefit can grant a Warping Point, plus another for each season when the effect is powerful.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Sample Ansuz Rune Spells; Sample Jera Rune Spells (ars-magica-magic#027)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to nonstacking duplicate bonuses and the stated persistence cost; a world can change stacking or Warping exposure, with corresponding effects on power balance.

rules.statement: Naudiz can hold a supernatural effect no higher than its own level until the runes break, or bind an active rune spell so it lasts as long as the Naudiz inscription. The held spell must be written into the combined rune effect; delayed resolution occurs when the holding runes are broken.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Naudiz Guidelines (ars-magica-magic#027)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to rune breakage as the trigger or ending condition and cap held power by level; a world can permit other triggers, balanced by stricter inscription requirements.

rules.statement: Perth dispels supernatural effects cast on its target when their level is no more than half the Perth effect's level. It can also alter the number of botch dice by its magnitude, either adding or reducing them.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Perth Guidelines (ars-magica-magic#027)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the stated half-level dispelling threshold; a world can raise or lower it, representing stronger or weaker counter-magic.

rules.statement: Several rune effects operate over a bounded radius: commonly about ten paces, with some affecting everyone in that area or a specified group. Effects that summon a target can transport it from elsewhere, and some examples require an Arcane Connection to identify the particular target.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Rune Guidelines and Sample Rune Spells (ars-magica-magic#027)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the listed range and target conditions; a world can widen the area or remove the connection requirement, at the cost of greater reach and less selectivity.

rules.statement: A Jera bonus to year-long work is received only after the full year, and its sample continuously active effect can cause Warping. Some Berkanan effects prevent wounds from healing for their duration, while sickness effects can likewise be kept from natural recovery.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Jera Guidelines; Berkanan Guidelines; Kauno Guidelines (ars-magica-magic#027)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to delayed benefits and continued harm only while the rune lasts; a world can change the duration or aftermath, trading reliability against exposure to ongoing effects.

rules.statement: The Fehu ox-summoning example restores the same dead ox to life if called by the same Arcane Connection, but not if it had Intelligence or Might; it retains no memories of earlier lives. The summoned ox remains after the spell ends, and its unusual obedience ends if the runes are destroyed.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Sample Fehu Rune Spells (ars-magica-magic#027)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to this narrow, connection-specific return with no prior memories; a world can broaden revival, but should price the lost identity or impose a stronger anchor.

rules.statement: A Thurisaz inscription is carved three times on a twisted branch; when completed, the branch becomes a venomous snake, and a Heavy Wound breaks the runes and turns it back into an ordinary branch.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Thurisaz 30, Method I (before Uruz) (ars-magica-magic#028)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a rune-marked branch becoming a snake until a Heavy Wound breaks the inscription; a world can alter the damage threshold, with the cost of changing how durable the living tool is.

rules.statement: Uruz can alter natural Strength-based Ability rolls, excluding Damage, and Encumbrance by the effect’s magnitude; its general guideline also grants immunity to mind-targeting effects below the effect’s level. At level 30 it can change Strength by one point, with further magnitudes increasing points or the cap, which remains within five points of the type’s average; its summon guidelines cover wild animals from Size −4 at level 30 up to Size +8 at level 50, in five-level steps.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Uruz Guidelines (ars-magica-magic#028)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to magnitude-based adjustments and the listed level gates; a world can change the maximum Strength shift or summon sizes, with greater power requiring higher-level effects.

rules.statement: Wunjo can change Presence-related natural Ability rolls by the effect’s magnitude, reduce Fatigue or Wound penalties by three times the magnitude, and at level 20 cause a powerful emotion. At level 30 it can remove those penalties entirely or change Presence by one point; further magnitudes raise the amount or cap, never beyond five points from the type’s average.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Wunjo Guidelines (ars-magica-magic#028)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to emotional or social effects with magnitude- and level-based limits; a world can make the emotion longer-lasting or stronger, at the cost of raising the required effect level.

rules.statement: Ihwaz can modify Intelligence by one point at level 30, with further magnitudes increasing the points or cap but never exceeding five points from the type’s average. Its other guidelines set sensing plant properties at level 15 within about ten paces, sensing corpses at level 20 within that range, corpse animation at level 25, speaking with the dead or summoning a corpse or tree at level 35, and summoning a supernatural being whose Might is at most the effect level minus 10.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Ihwaz Guidelines (ars-magica-magic#028)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the listed levels, Might ceilings, and ten-pace limits; a world can widen detection or summoning reach, with higher levels or restrictions such as avoiding consecrated ground.

rules.statement: Algiz increases or decreases Soak by the effect’s magnitude. It can also ward away appropriate supernatural beings with Might no greater than the effect level, and at level 10 ward away all things appropriate to the secondary rune.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Algiz Guidelines (ars-magica-magic#028)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a ward keyed to the secondary rune and the listed Might limit; a world can enlarge its protected area or broaden what it excludes, at the cost of stronger inscriptions.

rules.statement: The Younger Futhark has 16 runes rather than the Elder Futhark’s 24, requiring less experience to develop but opening fewer runes and offering less versatility. The Anglo-Saxon Futhorc has up to 33 runes, dividing experience across more characters and weakening each rune’s power.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Modified Runes (ars-magica-magic#028)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to fewer runes costing less experience but providing less variety; a world can expand the alphabet, trading divided training for reduced rune strength.

rules.statement: Hermetic magi can investigate rune magic as a Major Breakthrough and gain a new Rune Duration and Inscription Target; these work like Ring and Circle but need no penetration. A storyguide may grant an automatic Discovery toward this work to a magus who undergoes Odin’s Sacrifice.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Hermetic Integration (ars-magica-magic#028)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a Major Breakthrough for the new duration and target, with no penetration requirement; a world can make the discovery easier for those who make Odin’s Sacrifice.

rules.statement: For child characters, apply the age chart’s Characteristic and Size modifiers: under one year gives −10 and −3, respectively; modifiers lessen with age, reaching zero at age 14 or older. Virtues and Flaws must balance at generation, except that an apprentice may have an acquired Free House Virtue; a later Social Status change does not require rebalancing.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Chapter Two: Creating Young Characters — Aging Chart; Virtues & Flaws (ars-magica-magic#028)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the age-chart penalties and balanced Virtues and Flaws; a world can soften childhood penalties, trading a more capable child for less age-based distinction.

rules.statement: Experience-point-granting Virtues and Flaws cannot be selected by characters younger than 14. Skilled Parens and Weak Parens are unavailable when the apprentice’s instructional sources have statistics; with an unstatted parens, the Skilled Parens teaches Arts and Abilities for 12 seasons and spells for 3 seasons, while the weak version supplies Teaching Quality 8 and a Lab Total of 30.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Virtues That Grant Experience Points (ars-magica-magic#029)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: enforce the age and source-stat limits; a troupe can relax them for exceptional training histories, at the cost of departing from the stated apprenticeship assumptions.

rules.statement: Inherited Virtues and Flaws grant no benefit until they manifest, and every one must manifest by age 21. They may appear at any age, by player choice or in response to events; each has the same Minor or Major value as its ordinary version and counts during character generation.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Inherited Virtues & Flaws (ars-magica-magic#029)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: defer the effect until a chosen or story-triggered manifestation no later than 21; a world can make manifestations more tightly event-driven, trading player control for dramatic timing.

rules.statement: Child Virtues and Flaws are available to characters age 20 or younger and must be exchanged for another of equal value during a maturation transition. They must be replaced by the transition to adulthood; inherited ones must manifest before age 21.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Child Virtues & Flaws (ars-magica-magic#029)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: require equal-value replacement at the specified life stage; a world can set particular childhood traits to evolve in prescribed ways, limiting player choice.

rules.statement: From age 5 onward, a character gains 15 Ability experience points per year, or 20 with Wealthy and 10 with Poor. In the first five years, the optional infant rule instead grants 24 yearly points, of which 15 must go to a Living Language and the other 9 to a listed childhood Ability or a qualifying Supernatural Ability.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Abilities / Optional Rule: Abilities for Infants (ars-magica-magic#029)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: apply the age-based yearly allotment and infant spending restrictions; a world can vary childhood learning rates, at the cost of changing starting competence.

rules.statement: At ages 8, 15, and 21, Virtues and Flaws may be exchanged only for ones of equal value. Child traits must be changed by 21, experience-point traits cannot be replaced, and Size traits may change only if Size does not decrease; adjustments are recalculated during the first season of the new age stage.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Transitions of Maturation (ars-magica-magic#029)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: permit the listed equal-value changes at those transitions while protecting experience-point traits and preventing Size loss; a troupe can permit more flexible respecification, weakening continuity.

rules.statement: A standard Hermetic apprenticeship lasts 15 years and requires one teaching season each year. Its benchmark gives 240 experience points for Abilities and Arts and 120 spell levels; the final three years require a parens Lab Total of 40 to teach those spells.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: A Standard Apprenticeship (ars-magica-magic#029)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: use the 15-year benchmark and its stated teaching capacity; a saga can adjust the training schedule, changing the apprentice’s power at completion.

rules.statement: At childbirth, treat the mother as having a Medium Wound and make a recovery roll every two hours; birth occurs when that wound reaches unwounded. Each worsening costs the baby one Fatigue level, and losing five levels kills the baby. A midwife or physician adds the relevant Profession or Medicine score to the roll.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Birth and Blessing — Childbearing (ars-magica-magic#029)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: resolve delivery through two-hour recovery checks and the baby’s five-level limit; a world can make birth safer or harsher, changing the danger to mother and child.

rules.statement: Baptism and the described Jewish naming and Islamic purification rites cancel supernatural effects on a child that are not Divine, and drive out possessing spirits without preventing their return. They do not affect whether the child has the Gift.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Religious Rites for New Babies (ars-magica-magic#029)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: rites clear current non-Divine effects and expel possessing spirits but do not bar return; a world can narrow or broaden the rites’ authority, changing which supernatural influences are vulnerable.

rules.statement: A Gifted character who botches a stressful activity involving magic may incur Turbulence. The check succeeds only if Intelligence plus a stress die plus Aura exceeds both the storyguide’s stress die and the character’s age.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Turbulence — Incurring a Turbulence (ars-magica-magic#029)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: check on qualifying magical botches, with age acting as a threshold; a troupe can broaden triggers to supernatural places or events, increasing uncontrolled incidents.

rules.statement: When Turbulence occurs, the character controls it only if Stamina plus a stress die exceeds Warping Score plus a stress die. Success lets the player propose the effect subject to storyguide approval; failure lets the storyguide choose it, and the effect magnitude is half the difference between the totals.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Turbulence — Controlling Turbulences (ars-magica-magic#029)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: resolve control using the opposed totals and derive magnitude from their difference; a world can make uncontrolled magic more harmful or predictable, trading safety for consistency.

rules.statement: A Turbulence normally cannot penetrate Magic Resistance because its energy is spent creating the effect. If the character has Penetration, the Turbulence’s Penetration equals that score multiplied by one plus any sympathetic multiplier.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Turbulence — Effects of Turbulence (ars-magica-magic#029)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: give Turbulence no penetration unless the character has the Ability, then apply the stated multiplier; a world can let more raw power overcome resistance, at the cost of weakening protection.

rules.statement: A Gifted character can deliberately try to cause a Turbulence by spending 1 Confidence point. The player’s incurring roll must beat both the storyguide’s roll and the character’s age; if it succeeds, the character must then succeed on a separate roll to control the Turbulence. Additional Confidence points can modify either roll.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Turbulences and the Aegis of the Hearth (preceding section) (ars-magica-magic#030)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to age making forced Turbulences harder and requiring control; a world can make them easier or more common, at the cost of more frequent uncontrolled magical mishaps.

rules.statement: As a Gifted character ages, Turbulences become less frequent and harder to force; the troupe may eventually stop making incurring rolls. It may instead allow such rolls after a magical botch, meaning a botch on a Supernatural Ability or other magic roll.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Turbulences and the Aegis of the Hearth (preceding section) (ars-magica-magic#030)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to declining Turbulence rolls with age; a world can keep them available after magical botches, making magic failures carry an extra risk.

rules.statement: A Turbulence is treated like any other magical effect against the Aegis of the Hearth: participation in the Aegis spell prevents it from being hindered, while nonparticipation imposes a penalty equal to half the Aegis spell’s level on the roll to incur it.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Turbulences and the Aegis of the Hearth (ars-magica-magic#030)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the Aegis hindering nonparticipants; a world can exempt them, weakening the covenant’s magical protection.

rules.statement: For an infant who suffers a wound, a troupe may exchange wound severity for a Flaw: a Minor Flaw can reduce severity by 1 step and a Major Flaw by 3 steps. Alternatively, add the child’s age modifier penalty to wound-recovery rolls.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Character Design Notes (ars-magica-magic#030)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one of the two injury options, trading lasting character drawbacks for reduced wound severity or slower recovery; a world can omit these safeguards and make childhood injuries more dangerous.

rules.statement: A magus can spend a season searching for an apprentice and roll Perception plus a stress die against Ease Factor 12. Each assistant must also spend the season searching and roll Characteristic plus Ability against 12; a successful player-character assistant lowers the magus’s target by 3, and a successful storyguide-character assistant lowers it by 1.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Finding an Apprentice (ars-magica-magic#030)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a full season and the stated target reductions; a world can make searches easier or harder, changing the time and help needed to find a Gifted child.

rules.statement: Opening an apprentice’s Arts takes a season and legally binds the child to the magus. A magus with a score below 5 in any of the 15 Hermetic Arts causes the apprentice to gain the corresponding Deficiency, with Tribunal penalties increasing for two or at least three such Deficiencies.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Opening the Arts (ars-magica-magic#030)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the season-long procedure creating a binding apprenticeship and penalizing deficient instruction; a world can loosen the legal bond, at the cost of less secure control over the apprentice.

rules.statement: When an apprentice has non-Hermetic Supernatural Abilities, the parens needs an Intellego Vim Lab Total of at least 5 times each Ability score, plus a minimum of 10 for a Minor Virtue or 30 for a Major Virtue without a corresponding Ability; requirements stack. Meeting the required total opens the Arts but destroys those Abilities; doubling it preserves them, and a sufficiently high total can convert them into Hermetic Virtues.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Opening Arts with Supernatural Abilities (ars-magica-magic#030)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the stated Lab Total thresholds and destruction unless the total is doubled; a world can make preservation or conversion easier, reducing the cost of opening the apprentice’s Arts.

rules.statement: After the Arts are opened, the apprentice has 0 in each of the 5 Techniques and 10 Forms and can attempt spontaneous magic using those scores. The apprentice cannot cast formulaic spells without learning them.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: After the Arts Are Opened (ars-magica-magic#030)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to granting basic access to spontaneous magic but not unlearned formulaic spells; a world can delay or broaden access, changing how quickly an apprentice can use magic.

rules.statement: A Gifted child becomes legally recognized as an apprentice on the first day of the season when the master opens her Arts; this also immediately prevents the former keeper from reclaiming her as a laboratory assistant. Opening the Arts without a score of at least 5 in every Technique and Form cripples the student's magic and is generally treated as an Hermetic crime.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Teaching Schedule; Legal Issues (ars-magica-magic#031)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: opening grants apprentice status and protection immediately; a world can change the required scores or delay protection; the cost of insufficient mastery is crippled magic and legal exposure.

rules.statement: A parens must personally instruct an apprentice for one season in each year of apprenticeship. The apprentice's Arts are opened before the apprenticeship legally begins, and after fifteen years of service the master gives a readiness test, teaches Parma Magica, and releases the student from service.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Teaching Schedule; Legal Issues (ars-magica-magic#031)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: one season of personal instruction is owed yearly and release follows the test after fifteen years; a world can alter the schedule or test; neglect risks a low-crime charge.

rules.statement: To teach a Minor Hermetic Virtue, the teacher's Communication + Teaching + 3 + bonuses must reach 15; a Major Virtue requires 21. One-on-one teaching adds +6, including a Minor Hermetic Flaw the teacher possesses adds +3, and including a Major one adds +9; each Minor Virtue the student already has raises the target by 3 and each Major by 9.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Teaching Hermetic Virtues (ars-magica-magic#031)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: virtue instruction takes one season if its quality meets the adjusted target; a world can change bonuses or thresholds; added flaws ease learning at the cost of a permanent liability.

rules.statement: For seven Houses, a student earns the free Minor House Virtue after 10 seasons of one-on-one interaction with the parens. Mystery Cult House Virtues instead require a season of initiation; Ex Miscellanea's package and how it is learned are decided by the troupe.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Acquiring House Virtues (ars-magica-magic#031)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: repeated personal contact or a season's initiation grants the House gift; a world can vary the threshold or method; missing required contact means the free Virtue is not gained.

rules.statement: A Hermetic Flaw gained after character creation takes effect immediately and is permanent unless a story removes it. Teaching a Virtue can impose a Flaw to make instruction easier, and uncontrolled Temporary Twilight or opening the Arts can also produce Flaws.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Gaining Hermetic Flaws (ars-magica-magic#031)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: acquired flaws persist and affect the character at once; a world can make them temporary or removable; the tradeoff is a lasting impairment for easier learning or a magical consequence.

rules.statement: The Gift imposes –3 on social interaction totals, including teaching; Gentle Gift avoids the penalty and Blatant Gift raises it to –6. When both teacher and student have the Gift, apply –3 for each, while Parma Magica cancels the penalty if it protects the participants.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Study—Teachers (ars-magica-magic#031)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: each unprotected Gifted participant adds a –3 social penalty; a world can change the penalty or who Parma protects; teaching is harder unless protection is maintained.

rules.statement: A formulaic cantation is cast unless its casting total is at least 10 below its level; if it is less than 10 below, it succeeds but costs a Fatigue level. Under the optional learning rule, repeatedly casting the same spontaneous spell at least as many times as its level lets the character buy it as a formulaic spell for one experience point per level.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Cantations; Optional Rule: Learning Cantations in Play (ars-magica-magic#031)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: known low-level spells are reliable, while repeated use can turn a spontaneous effect into a learned spell; a world can omit the option or change the threshold; failure risk and fatigue constrain casting.

rules.statement: A character needs Artes Liberales 1 and a score of at least 4 in a book's language to gain useful insight from it. Training can teach Abilities but not Arts, and counts as a season of one-on-one instruction.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Study—Book Learning; Study—Training (ars-magica-magic#031)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: literacy and language proficiency gate useful book study, and training covers Abilities only; a world can change prerequisites or broaden training; limited access and instruction time are the costs.

rules.statement: A legal marriage requires a priest, a public announcement beforehand, and an investigation for impediments; the couple must be four steps of affinity removed. A priest can end the marriage only by annulling it as invalid from the start, and annulment is expensive and time-consuming.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Marriage (ars-magica-magic#032)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to requiring public priestly procedure and four degrees of separation; a world could relax these requirements, with the Church’s authority and the couple’s legal status at stake.

rules.statement: An apprentice assisting a magus adds the apprentice’s Intelligence + Magic Theory to the magus’s Lab Total. The apprentice cannot take over the magus’s work midway through a season; after the apprentice misses 10 days, each additional missed day reduces the apprentice’s contribution by 10 points, but never reduces the magus’s own Lab Total.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Life in the Laboratory (ars-magica-magic#032)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one assistant’s additive contribution and the 10-day grace period; a world could change the assistant limit or absence penalty, reflecting how demanding laboratory work is.

rules.statement: An uncontrolled laboratory Turbulence halves an apprentice’s assistance to the Lab Total, in addition to its normal results. A stressful season can warrant a check, including one involving experimentation, more than 10 pawns of vis, irregular hours, or a barely sufficient Lab Total.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Laboratory Turbulences (ars-magica-magic#032)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to halving the apprentice’s aid after an uncontrolled check; a world could vary which seasons trigger checks or how severe Turbulence is, reflecting laboratory instability.

rules.statement: In Bellum, players cast Ager Belli and compete to direct illusory soldiers; in a two-player match, the first to win five rounds wins. A player may instead try to disrupt an opponent’s concentration, but casting a second spell while maintaining Ager Belli requires Stamina + Concentration + a stress die against Ease Factor 15, and losing concentration ends the caster’s own spell.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Bellum (ars-magica-magic#032)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to five round wins or breaking the opponent’s concentration, with the specified risk of losing one’s own spell; a world could alter the winning threshold or casting difficulty, reflecting local game customs.

rules.statement: A player character’s apprentice loses the Gift only if the player chooses; while it is lost, the character cannot cast Hermetic spells, work magic, or use Supernatural Virtues or Abilities. If the Gift is suppressed instead, the character can still use existing Supernatural Virtues and Abilities but cannot gain new Supernatural or Hermetic Virtues; the troupe and storyguide decide whether and how it returns.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Losing the Gift (ars-magica-magic#032)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to player choice and a complete loss of magical capability, with suppression as a limited alternative; a world could make loss or recovery more rule-bound, at the cost of player control over this character-defining change.

rules.statement: A magus decides whether an apprentice has passed the Gauntlet; after three failed attempts, House Quaesitor intervenes and sets its own test. As an optional test, roll Intelligence + an appropriate Ability + a stress die against 9; failure adds another year of apprenticeship, while a botch brings a dire consequence.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Apprenticeship’s End: The Gauntlet (ars-magica-magic#032)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the master’s judgment, with Quaesitor intervention after three failures; a world could use the optional roll or impose more oversight, reflecting how much authority the Order grants individual masters.

rules.statement: An apprentice cannot invoke Parma Magica until receiving its final key instruction, normally after swearing the Oath of Hermes, regardless of the apprentice’s recorded score. Giving the key before the Oath is a High Crime.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Learning Parma Magica (ars-magica-magic#032)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to withholding the final instruction until the Oath; a world could allow earlier teaching, at the cost of committing a High Crime and exposing the secret to a non-member.

rules.statement: Ex Miscellanea has no shared Gauntlet procedure: each tradition decides when training ends and may set any kind of test. Its members still withhold the final Parma Magica instructions until the apprentice has completed 15 years of training.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: House Ex Miscellanea (ars-magica-magic#033)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to tradition-specific, story-driven completion tests; a world can standardize them, trading local identity for consistency.

rules.statement: A House Tremere apprentice passes the Gauntlet by making a respectable showing against the master in certamen, without needing to win, and presenting a birch branch as the master's sigil. The apprentice must obtain the branch beforehand; seeking a magical tree can make that task more dangerous.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: House Tremere (ars-magica-magic#033)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a non-winning but credible contest plus a branch; a world can require victory or a rarer branch, increasing the test's difficulty.

rules.statement: A House Verditius apprentice must make a finished apprentice piece for the master to pass the Gauntlet; acquiring its raw materials may itself be dangerous.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: House Verditius (ars-magica-magic#033)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a completed magical-work demonstration; a world can make component gathering hazardous, imposing adventure and material costs.

rules.statement: Gifted students generally cannot learn the Hermetic Arts in groups: those Arts must be taught individually by a magus to an apprentice. Academic and Arcane Abilities can be taught to several pupils at once.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Scholae Magicae (ars-magica-magic#033)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to individual Arts tuition; a world can allow group instruction, but must overcome the stated teaching limitation.

rules.statement: Gifted children who are not continually covered by Parma Magica tend to distrust and clash with one another; heightened anxiety makes Turbulences more likely. A powerful Aegis can reduce Turbulences, provided students receive casting tokens when they need to practice magic.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Scholae Magicae (ars-magica-magic#033)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to social friction and more frequent Turbulences without protection; a world can suppress the disruption with Parma Magica or Aegis, requiring sustained coverage and tokens.

rules.statement: A Mystery Virtue is normally kept from outsiders by secrecy and initiation: knowing general details or watching rites is insufficient to reproduce its magical effects without the Initiate's mystical understanding. Teaching such a Virtue to a non-Initiate usually needs a Minor Breakthrough.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Bonisagus and the Mysteries; Secrecy and the Mysteries (ars-magica-magic#033)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to Initiation as the access requirement; a world can permit instruction without it through a Minor Breakthrough, at research cost.

rules.statement: A candidate who accepts a cult's formal offer becomes a probationer and is sent, without disclosing plans, to a ritual site to meet a Mystagogue. If the journey requires a story, it may count as a Quest and give a later bonus to the first Initiation.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Entering a Mystery Cult (ars-magica-magic#033)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a secret journey and probation before induction; a world can waive the journey or make its story count as a Quest, changing the preparation cost or benefit.

rules.statement: Initiation rites commonly mark a symbolic passage from darkness to light or death to rebirth, and membership and magical initiation are treated as intense, life-changing events that call for a story.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Entering a Mystery Cult (ars-magica-magic#033)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a transformative rite with a dedicated story; a world can make the transition less dramatic, reducing its narrative and personal cost.

rules.statement: A successful Initiation grants the candidate a Mystery Virtue and may also impose lasting Ordeal Flaws. These changes become part of the candidate’s essential nature: magic cannot remove them, and leaving the cult does not undo them.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: The Mechanics of Initiation (ars-magica-magic#034)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to persistent gains and flaws; a world can soften or strengthen permanence, but the rite is meant to alter the initiate fundamentally.

rules.statement: The Mystagogue’s Initiation Total is Presence + (Mystery Cult) Lore + Script Bonus, with no die roll. A known Minor Virtue needs 15 and a known Major Virtue 21; if the Mystagogue does not know the Virtue, the targets are 18 and 30 respectively.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Initiation Rites (ars-magica-magic#034)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to predictable success when the total meets the target; a world can raise or lower targets to tune difficulty, reflecting how obscure or demanding its mysteries are.

rules.statement: An earlier Ordeal reduces the next three Initiation targets: respectively 3/2/1 for a Minor, 6/4/2 for a Medium, or 9/6/3 for a Major Ordeal. Only the largest applicable reduction counts, and the target cannot fall below 9.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Initiation Rites (ars-magica-magic#034)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to letting an earlier lasting cost ease later initiations; a world can change the reductions or duration, making suffering pay off more or less over time.

rules.statement: A Script adds bonuses for genuine costs, such as +3 for a Quest or Minor Ordeal, +6 for a Medium Ordeal, +9 for a Major Ordeal, and +1 for sacrificing wealth or a season of service. A component that costs nothing is invalid, and invalidating any component invalidates the entire Script; a sacrifice of great symbolic value may add +3 to +6.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: The Initiation Script (ars-magica-magic#034)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to requiring actual loss or effort for Script bonuses; a world can adjust the rewards, with the in-world rationale that power demands a meaningful price.

rules.statement: An Initiation, including its rite and preparation, occupies a full season and replaces other activities for that season. A Quest takes at least a season; if completed early, the remaining time is spent meditating, with no other study, though Lore Exposure may be awarded.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Time and Initiation (ars-magica-magic#034)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to charging a full season for initiation and quests; a world can shorten or lengthen the commitment, trading faster advancement against less reflection or greater demands.

rules.statement: The candidate needs (Mystery Cult) Lore 1 for the first Initiation; later Initiations typically require at least 3, and entry to an inner circle normally requires 6. For each month of distraction during study with the Mystagogue, reduce the Initiation Total by one-third of its original amount, rounding fractions up.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: (Mystery Cult) Lore and Degrees of Initiation; Distractions and the Initiate (ars-magica-magic#034)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to Lore gates and distraction penalties as stated; a world can vary the thresholds or penalty to make cult access more open or exacting.

rules.statement: A Mystagogue may alter one Script component per Initiation: adding a component has Ease Factor 9, changing one 12, and removing one 15. Failure makes the modified Script unusable, but leaves the original Script functional; the Virtue being granted cannot be changed this way.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Modifying the Initiation Script (ars-magica-magic#034)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one risky Script revision per rite; a world can alter the Ease Factors or allow more revisions, reflecting how stable or flexible its traditions are.

rules.statement: When inventing a Script, the Mystagogue chooses a Risk Modifier from 0 to +3. The rite is checked for experimental results and validity; the validity test is Simple Die + Risk + Intelligence + Lore against 9 + proposed bonus, or 15 + desired bonus when initiating another person. If it succeeds, the final total is Presence + Lore + revised Script bonus + Risk; the Risk bonus is not retained in the written Script.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Experimental Scripts (ars-magica-magic#034)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to uncertain outcomes and a temporary risk boost; a world can change the risk range or checks, with experimentation carrying the danger of flawed rites or failed initiation.

rules.statement: An Initiation Script sets the number of Quests and any Ordeal; it takes one season per Quest plus one season for the Initiation. Sacrificed valuable items may require additional seasons to make, and each Initiation or Quest season spent as background experience reduces that year’s 30 experience points by 10.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Chapter 2, Initiation Scripts summary (ars-magica-magic#035)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one season per Quest and one for the rite; a world can increase the sacrifice or season burden to reflect how costly cult advancement is.

rules.statement: A character who begins play as an Initiate of a Mystery Cult must take Cabal Legacy, which permits cult Virtues to be bought as ordinary character Virtues and Flaws but does not make newly acquired Flaws count as past Ordeals. The cult may rarely impose a season-long task; success improves standing, while refusal or failure earns its wrath.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Cabal Legacy — Minor Hermetic Story Flaw (ars-magica-magic#035)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to an occasional required task with status at stake; a world can make demands more or less frequent, trading personal time for cult standing.

rules.statement: Cult membership can require yearly dues; one pawn of vis is a reasonable symbolic amount, while seven or more pawns may suit Initiation into a new degree. Cult duties can also consume seasons, and voluntary service may earn access to a mystery book or teaching in Mystery Cult Lore.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Chapter 3, Responsibilities of Membership (ars-magica-magic#035)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to modest yearly dues and occasional service; a world can raise the vis or time costs to make advancement slower or cult support more substantial.

rules.statement: Art of Memory lets a character store one complex item per locus after succeeding at Stress Die + Intelligence + Art of Memory against an Ease Factor of 9 or higher. The palace has as many rooms as the Ability score, five loci per room, and stored memories may be deliberately forgotten to make room.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Chapter 4, The Art of Memory (ars-magica-magic#035)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to five memories per Ability-score room; a world can change the capacity or difficulty to make perfect recall more or less accessible.

rules.statement: A magically enhanced locus lasts only while its spell lasts unless made permanent: the caster can spend seven days meditating and succeed at Intelligence + Art of Memory against Ease Factor 9. A ritual version creates a permanent locus, and Perdo Mentem magic can destroy such loci.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Chapter 4, Enhance the Memory Palace (ars-magica-magic#035)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to temporary spell duration with a seven-day, Ease Factor 9 route to permanence; a world can make permanent memory easier or harder to obtain.

rules.statement: A container ritual must have a base level at least equal to the spell it will sustain; the sustained spell cannot be Ritual or Momentary. The container, bound spell, and a suitable disembodied spirit are required, and the spirit’s Might must be at least the spell’s level.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Chapter 4, Spell Binding (ars-magica-magic#035)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a fragile item and a matching spirit whose Might meets the spell level; a world can relax the match or raise the level threshold, changing the risk and availability of bindings.

rules.statement: If the container breaks, or either linked spell ends or fails, the sustained effect ends and the spirit is freed. If the spirit’s Might falls below the spell level, the effect fails unless its original duration has not yet expired; a command to release the spirit must exceed the container spell’s level.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Chapter 4, Spirit, Spell and Container Combined (ars-magica-magic#035)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the linked spell, item, and spirit failing together; a world can make containers sturdier or release commands easier, altering the security of stored magic.

rules.statement: Performance Magic applies to one specified qualifying Ability, replacing ordinary casting gestures and words with that Ability’s actions and/or speech, and it allows the magus to maintain a spell without Concentration rolls. In combat, Brawl or Martial Ability use requires a stress roll with three extra botch dice, with every non-botch treated as zero.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Chapter 4, Performance Magic (ars-magica-magic#035)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to concealed casting through one chosen mundane practice; a world can broaden eligible Abilities or alter the combat risk, trading discretion for danger.

rules.statement: A performer using performance-based spellcasting must genuinely carry out the relevant verbal or physical ability; it can replace only the corresponding spell components. Music can replace words, gestures, or both, but it cannot be performed silently. If ordinary components remain unreplaced, they are still required under the usual rules.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Performance Magic (ars-magica-magic#036)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to requiring an audible or visible performance in place of the components it substitutes; a world could loosen which components a performance replaces, at the cost of making casting less dependent on the performer’s actual practice.

rules.statement: When a performer casts with Voice Range, the spell reaches only as far as the song or instrument can be heard. Whether others recognize the casting depends on its visible and audible components: use a stress die + Perception + Awareness against 15 minus effect magnitude to determine the Form, with the Ease Factor adjusted by –3 for audible Hermetic words, +0 for Hermetic gestures, and +3 when both words and gestures are mundane.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Recognizing Performance Magic (ars-magica-magic#036)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to range limited by audibility and recognition depending on how much Hermetic casting is exposed; a world could make performances easier or harder to identify, affecting concealment and bystander attention.

rules.statement: Performance Duration makes a spell last only while the caster performs the chosen ability, and ends it when the performance stops. Casting requires a characteristic + Ability roll against 3; failure means the spell fails, and a botch causes a botch. No further rolls are needed to maintain the effect while performing, and formulaic spells must be designed for this duration and cannot be cast without performing.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: New Duration for Performance Magic (ars-magica-magic#036)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to sustaining the spell through continuous performance, with an initial Ease Factor 3 roll; a world could allow pauses or require continued checks, trading convenience for greater performance risk.

rules.statement: Planetary Magic can add a chosen modifier from +1 to +5 to a season’s Lab Total for creating an enchanted device, if the effect fits one planet’s influence and a horoscope roll of stress die + Intelligence + Artes Liberales (Astronomy) succeeds against three times the chosen modifier. Only one planet and modifier may apply per season; failure loses the bonus, and a roll of zero calls for botch dice equal to the desired modifier, with any botch wasting the season and vis. Missing a full laboratory day removes the bonus.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Planetary Magic — Minor Hermetic Virtue (ars-magica-magic#036)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to allowing one planetary bonus per season after horoscope work; a world could raise the bonus or reduce the danger, with the cost represented by time, failed work, or lost vis.

rules.statement: Potent Magic grants +3 to Lab Totals and Casting Scores in a narrow field, or +6 in a wide field. A Potent spell’s Potency is the sum of the selected Casting Item bonuses and adds to Casting Score, but not spell level; Potency cannot exceed Magic Theory, and casting requires touching every specified item. Only a magus with Potent Magic can design such a spell from scratch, though others can learn and cast one from a Lab Text or teacher.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Potent Magic — Minor or Major Hermetic Virtue; Potent Spells (ars-magica-magic#036)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to letting symbolic items boost a designed formula only when all are touched; a world could change the potency cap or item requirement, balancing stronger casting against access to specialized components.

rules.statement: Vulgar Alchemy experimentation can discover personal Shape or Material Bonuses while enchanting, using an Experimentation Bonus equal to a simple die plus Risk Modifier. The bonus is allocated across components, and successful tests add their discovered bonuses; known applicable bonuses succeed automatically first. The resulting Lab Total includes the bonuses, but total Shape and Material Bonuses remain capped by Magic Theory; invested devices cannot be experimented on during this process.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Vulgar Alchemy — Minor Hermetic Mystery Virtue; The Experiment; Testing the Components (ars-magica-magic#036)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to letting risky laboratory experimentation discover reusable ingredient correspondences; a world could broaden eligibility or increase the risk, trading reliable device work for discoveries or wasted seasons.

rules.statement: Withstand Casting reduces Fatigue lost from a spell by one level per Virtue level, but never below one level when the spell would normally cause Fatigue loss; it does not create a loss when none would occur. Apply Vulnerable Casting’s extra loss before Withstand Casting, and a magus cannot begin with both Virtues. Withstanding Fatigue that powers a Life-Linked effect removes the benefit of the levels withstood.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Withstand Casting — Minor Hermetic Virtue (ars-magica-magic#036)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to reducing ordinary Fatigue costs while preserving a minimum cost and any life-force fuel requirement; a world could alter the minimum, but doing so changes the balance between safety and spell power.

rules.statement: Astrological Cyclic Magic grants or penalizes magic according to sign cycles: male or female signs give magnitude 3, cardinal, fixed, or mutable signs magnitude 5, and one-element signs magnitude 6. A bonus affects Lab Totals only if it covers the whole season, while a penalty applies if it occurs at any point during the season.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Astrological Cyclic Magic — Minor Hermetic Virtue or Flaw (ars-magica-magic#036)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to varying the Virtue or Flaw by astrological timing, with stronger magnitudes for shorter cycles; a world could change the cycle-to-magnitude mapping, making the timing more or less decisive.

rules.statement: Hermetic Alchemy improves vis extraction by adding appropriate Shape and Material Bonuses to a Lab Total of Creo + Vim + Intelligence + Magic Theory + Aura Modifier. The amount of Vim vis extracted is one-tenth of that total, rounded up.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Hermetic Alchemy — Hermetic Minor Virtue; Improved Extraction of Vis (ars-magica-magic#036)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to converting an alchemical object’s correspondences into more extracted Vim vis; a world could change the conversion rate or permit Form-specific vis, affecting the value and cost of laboratory extraction.

rules.statement: Form-specific vis extraction uses a Creo + Vim (Form requisite) + Intelligence + Magic Theory + Aura + applicable Shape and Material bonuses total, but the magus cannot extract Technique vis this way. The yield is one-twentieth of the total, rounded up, and the combined bonus from a compound object cannot exceed Magic Theory.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Form-Specific Vis; Choosing Appropriate Shape and Material Factors (ars-magica-magic#037)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the one-twentieth yield and Magic Theory cap; a world can alter efficiency or the cap because the chosen material and Form govern how well the aura’s vis is drawn out.

rules.statement: Philosophic Alchemy lets the magus leave a prepared vis extraction to digest with little attention: the extraction counts as a seven-day distraction, but the magus must attend daily and cannot run a second extraction. Minor Philosophic Alchemy takes four seasons and uses the lowest season’s Lab Total; Major takes one season; more than 20 days away in any season ruins the process, and experimentation while it digests also causes failure.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Philosophic Alchemy; Automatic Extraction of Vis; Time Needed for Automatic Extraction of Vis (ars-magica-magic#037)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the stated four-season or one-season duration and spoilage limits; a world can make unattended digestion safer or riskier because the process depends on stable attention and conditions.

rules.statement: Instead of extracting vis, Philosophic Alchemy can open enchantment spaces in the prepared device; the number opened equals the Vim pawns that the same Lab Total would have extracted. The magus chooses this option at the start, and the spaces can count as extra capacity or reduce the vis needed to open the device.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Philosophic Alchemy; Ready-Opened Devices (ars-magica-magic#037)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to converting the would-be Vim yield into open spaces; a world can vary whether those spaces add capacity or lower the opening cost because they represent vis invested directly in preparation of the device.

rules.statement: A Lesser Elixir adds its Elixir Level to the base Longevity Ritual’s Aging Bonus while active, replacing that ritual’s normal modifier. Its level comes from ingredient points and cannot exceed the magus’s Magic Theory; each personally devised Vulgar Alchemy ingredient contributes double its bonus, subject to that same score as an individual-item cap.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: The Lesser Elixir; Creating the Lesser Elixir; Elixir Points (ars-magica-magic#037)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to adding the ingredient-derived level within the Magic Theory caps; a world can change ingredient values or the cap because the formula’s potency depends on the alchemist’s personal materials and expertise.

rules.statement: A successful Great Elixir permanently transforms its drinker into a magical being, grants Magic Might equal to half the invested effect level minus 20, and removes aging, Warping, and death from lesser wounds; the transformation cannot be dispelled. The test is a die roll plus Stamina, Lesser Elixir Level, and accumulated attempt bonus against age divided by 10, rounded up.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: The Great Elixir; Testing the Great Elixir; Success! Effects of the Elixir (ars-magica-magic#037)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the stated test and irreversible magical transformation; a world can alter the test or Might formula because immortality costs the drinker their humanity.

rules.statement: A Periapt Horoscope prepared at a season’s equinox or solstice acts as a temporary Lab Text for one charged-device formula that season. The Lab Total must meet the effect level, charges equal Lab Total divided by five rounded up, and effect level cannot exceed five times Astronomy; each formula needs its own horoscope.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Periapt; Creating a Periapt; Creating a Periapt Horoscope (ars-magica-magic#037)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the Lab Total and Astronomy limits; a world can change the charge yield or maximum level because celestial alignment is the source of the improved enchantment efficiency.

rules.statement: Celestial Magic can add a chosen +1 to +5 modifier to any Laboratory Total if an Astronomy roll succeeds against three times the desired bonus. Missing a full day from the laboratory removes the benefit, and a zero roll can ruin the season and any vis spent.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Celestial Magic; Improved Laboratory Horoscopes (ars-magica-magic#037)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the +1–+5 bonus and the stated roll; a world can make horoscopes more or less reliable because favorable astral timing depends on uninterrupted work.

rules.statement: Astrological spell times are usable only within about 500 paces of the measurement point, and a target extending beyond that area cannot be affected by an effect using them. Astrological Minutes, Hours, and Days define spell durations that end after the specified interval, with Astronomy rolls required to calculate them.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Astrological Durations; Limits on the Use of Astrological Time; New Duration: Minutes = Diameter; New Duration: Hours = Sun (ars-magica-magic#037)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the 500-pace bound and the specified intervals; a world can expand or shrink the area because local celestial conditions do not remain consistent over greater distances.

rules.statement: A spell may be set to last a number of Astrological Days or Signs, then end. Calculating the duration requires an Astronomy roll of die + Intelligence + Astronomy against 6 plus the desired number of time units; a Signs duration cannot exceed one year.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: New Duration: Signs = Year, Ritual (ars-magica-magic#038)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a duration ending at the calculated astrological point; a world can raise the calculation difficulty or cap durations, since miscalculation can make the effect end early or late.

rules.statement: A failed Astrological Duration calculation makes the spell last a number of units short or long, up to the amount by which the roll missed; the caster does not know the error until the effect ends. A botch makes the spell botch.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: New Duration: Signs = Year, Ritual (ars-magica-magic#038)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to an uncertain endpoint on a failed calculation and a botched spell on a botch; a world can soften or intensify the uncertainty, with the cost of less reliable timing.

rules.statement: A daily horoscope or exact astrological-time measurement each subtracts 3 from the duration-calculation Ease Factor. Specifying the exact end to the nearest Astrological Minute adds 3; an armillary sphere halves the adjusted Ease Factor after other changes.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Options: Calculating an Astrological Duration (ars-magica-magic#038)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the stated modifiers; a world can make precise timing easier or harder, trading convenience for required preparation or specialized equipment.

rules.statement: For one favorable hour per day, a caster chooses a desired spellcasting bonus from +1 to +5 and rolls Stress Die + Intelligence + Astronomy against three times that bonus. Success adds the bonus to spell casting scores during the hour; failure gives no benefit, while a botch imposes a penalty equal to the chosen bonus for the whole hour.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Favorable Hour for Spellcasting (ars-magica-magic#038)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one prepared favorable hour and a bonus purchased by increasing the target number; a world can alter the range or duration, with botching risking an equal penalty.

rules.statement: An enchantment linked to one target requires that target's Nativity Horoscope and may use an Arcane Connection. The link automatically restricts the effect to that target without the usual +3 Effect-level cost, and adds +2 for the horoscope plus any Arcane Connection bonus to the Lab Total.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Astrologically Linked Enchantments (ars-magica-magic#038)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a single-target enchanted effect with no restriction surcharge; a world can require stronger connections or additional costs, since the link narrows who can benefit.

rules.statement: A device attuned to one astrological sign or an elemental group gains a cycle adjustment equal to the maker's Astronomy score when opening it.
