The bonus applies either to Penetration or effect frequency; an opposing element receives an equal penalty, frequency below one use per day makes the effect unusable during that cycle, and frequency above ten levels gives no extra benefit.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Seasonal Enchantments (ars-magica-magic#038)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a cycle-based bonus balanced by an equal opposing-cycle penalty; a world can change the adjustment or affected cycles, at the cost of periods when the item is weakened or unusable.

rules.statement: Hermetic Divination answers a single question using the equivalent of a non-Ritual Intellego effect of any Form, range, and target except Sense targets, with Momentary duration. It cannot simulate Ritual Magic, provide senses, or speak with a target.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Divination & Augury — Major Supernatural Virtue (ars-magica-magic#038)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a momentary answer limited to information available now; a world can expand targets or duration, but should preserve limits on sensing and ritual-scale effects.

rules.statement: Hermetic Divination reports present information, not fixed future events: a question about what someone will do can reveal their current intention, which may change later. Its results therefore do not override free choice or the Limit of Time.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Divination & Augury — Major Supernatural Virtue (ars-magica-magic#038)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to present motives or conditions rather than guaranteed outcomes; a world can permit stronger prediction, but should account for changing choices and unreliable forecasts.

rules.statement: A divination answers truly when the stress die plus the relevant characteristic, Divination Ability, aura, and applicable bonuses meets or exceeds the equivalent Hermetic spell’s level. If penetration is needed, it equals the Divination Total plus Penetration Bonus minus that same Ease Factor.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Divination; Penetration (ars-magica-magic#039)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the equivalent spell level as the difficulty and subtract it again for penetration; a world can alter the available bonuses, reflecting how well its omens and connections reveal the target.

rules.statement: Casual Divination takes one round and uses Perception, with an optional omen-relevance bonus of +0 to +3, rarely +4 or +5. Ceremonial Divination takes 15 minutes per 5 Ease Factors and uses Intelligence; it can add ceremonial, sympathetic, and device bonuses.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Divination in Practice; Casual Divination; Ceremonial Divination; Divination Bonuses (ars-magica-magic#039)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to quick observation or a slower, bonus-bearing ceremony; a world can make preparations more or less valuable, with time and access to relevant omens as the cost.

rules.statement: A held Arcane Connection lets a diviner treat the target as being at Touch range, and Boundary Targets can be divined without the usual ritual requirement.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Divination (ars-magica-magic#039)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to these two exceptions to range and ritual limits; a world can restrict them, making reliable access to a connection or a Boundary question costly.

rules.statement: Dream-based ceremonial divination requires about half an hour of preparation before sleep and sleep lasting at least as long as the equivalent waking ceremony; waking the interpreter early yields no answer. Interpreting another person’s dream requires at least an hour of discussion, with 15 minutes per magnitude for each ceremonial question.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Hermetic Dream Interpreter; Divinatory Interpretation (ars-magica-magic#039)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to sleep or discussion as the required time investment; a world can shorten or lengthen the process, at the cost of lost questions or interrupted insight.

rules.statement: Dream Calling makes another person dream generally about a subject chosen by the interpreter: the interpreter touches the person as they approach sleep and speaks about the subject, then rolls Presence plus Dream Interpretation and aura against Ease Factor 6. Penetration applies if needed.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Dream Calling (ars-magica-magic#039)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a subject-directed dream at difficulty 6; a world can require stronger access or impose additional limits, with touch and a conversation before sleep as the price.

rules.statement: A spirit-powered device can perform eligible Ritual effects without making the user perform a ritual, but the bound spirit permanently loses Might Score equal to the Ritual’s vis cost, calculated as level divided by 5, rounded up. The Ritual level cannot exceed twice the spirit’s remaining Might Score.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Hermetic Empowerment; Powering Ritual Effects (ars-magica-magic#039)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to permanent spirit depletion as the fuel cost and twice-Might as the ceiling; a world can change the drain or ceiling, trading spirit suffering against device capability.

rules.statement: An Empowering Prison must have a level at least twice the bound spirit’s Might and Form requisites for every Ritual effect it is to power. When used, the spirit must still have Might at least half the Ritual’s level; otherwise neither effect works and no Might is drained.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Empowering Prison of the Declining Spirit (ars-magica-magic#039)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a permanently containing enchantment with specified Forms and a current-Might gate; a world can alter the binding threshold or add escape routes, at the cost of security or capacity.

rules.statement: The spirit familiar bonding level is the spirit’s Might plus 25, and bonding costs 1 pawn of vis per 5 levels or fraction, matched to the Technique or Form. The magus may have only one familiar, animal or spirit.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Spirit Familiar; Bonding the Ally as Spirit Familiar (ars-magica-magic#039)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one familiar slot and a Might-based bonding cost; a world can allow more slots or change the cost, at the cost of weaker bonds or additional resources.

rules.statement: Incorporating an item into the body as a talisman requires a Rego Vim effect with Muto, Corpus, and the item’s Form as requisites; its level is five times the highest bonus plus half the other bonuses’ sum, rounding up. This causes one Warping Point, or two if the effect is level 30 or higher.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Inscription on the Soul; Blending with Substance (ars-magica-magic#039)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a bonus-dependent enchantment level and Warping cost; a world can change the threshold or penalty, balancing bodily alteration against access to additional talisman bonuses.

rules.statement: A Living Ghost’s transformation limit equals its best Technique–Form combination, with a Magical Focus applicable to that combination counted twice. Its ritual must reach that limit; the Haunt’s size consumes levels from the ritual, and Might equals ritual level minus those size levels, capped by the transformation limit.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Transformation of the Living Ghost (ars-magica-magic#040)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a Might ceiling set by Arts and a tradeoff between Haunt size and Might; worlds can raise or lower the ceiling, reflecting the magus’s magical aptitude.

rules.statement: The binding ritual destroys the magus’s body and binds the spirit to a chosen area. If the Haunt ceases to exist, the Living Ghost becomes an ordinary ghost and eventually fades; a changed Boundary usually persists, while destruction of a Circle, Room, or Structure can end the binding.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Bind The Living Ghost; The Haunt (ars-magica-magic#040)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to survival while the Haunt exists and eventual fading if it ends; a world can make particular boundary types more or less durable, at the cost of security.

rules.statement: A Living Ghost can spend 1 Temporary Might per magnitude to make a spell affect the physical world. It can also permanently spend Might Score, with each point providing one pawn of raw vis.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Magic and the Living Ghost (ars-magica-magic#040)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to Might as a renewable resource for physical effects and a permanent substitute for vis; a world can change recovery or exchange rates, at the cost of potency or endurance.

rules.statement: A non-spirit familiar may join the magus’s death ordeal if the magus pays raw vis equal to the Familiar Bond Score divided by 5, rounded up; otherwise it may stay alive and lose the magus. A spirit familiar stays without extra vis.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Familiars and the Living Ghost (ars-magica-magic#040)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a vis cost proportional to the bond for a living familiar’s participation; a world can waive or increase it, reflecting how difficult the shared transition is.

rules.statement: Possess the Living Host lets a ghost enter and fully control a touched person for a Moon. The ghost can use the host’s senses but gains neither skills nor memories; an unattended host mind may resist, and the host remembers events afterward unless its memories are erased.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Possess the Living Host (ars-magica-magic#040)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to bodily control without access to the host’s knowledge, with a risk of mental resistance; worlds can alter duration or access, at the cost of stronger intrusion.

rules.statement: Names of Power add their bonuses to the relevant laboratory or casting total, but the combined bonus cannot exceed Magic Theory. Using them requires speaking firmly or loudly, so quiet or silent casting is unavailable.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Hermetic Theurgy and Names of Power (ars-magica-magic#040)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a Magic Theory cap and audible invocation; a world can raise the cap or relax the voice requirement, trading restraint for easier or subtler use.

rules.statement: An Invoke spell calls one specific named spirit; its base level is that spirit’s Might, which must equal or exceed the spell-like power’s level. After the first successful summoning and pact, the spirit answers later calls cooperatively; it performs one instructed effect, cannot botch it, and uses its Might plus aura modifier as its Casting Score.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Invoke the Spirit of (spell) (ars-magica-magic#040)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a one-spirit pact with a Might threshold and reliable single effect; a world can make pacts harder to establish or spirits less reliable, reflecting their power and autonomy.

rules.statement: An invoked spirit uses its Might plus the current aura modifier as its Casting Score, then rounds half that score up for its Casting Total; its Penetration Total is that Casting Total minus the effect’s level. It makes no roll and cannot botch, and after one instructed effect it departs.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Invoke the Spirit of (Form) (ars-magica-magic#041)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one automatic effect per summoned spirit; a world can allow longer service, but the spirit’s single-use commitment and instruction time limit it.

rules.statement: A Daimon ritual above the Daimon’s Might adds summoning points equal to ritual level minus Might each time it overcomes Magic Resistance. When accumulated points reach the Daimon’s Might, an Aspect answers; without Hermetic Theurgy, points cannot carry between castings, and a single casting must be sufficient.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Invoke the Pact of (Daimon) (ars-magica-magic#041)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to persistent summoning progress for a theurgist; a world can require a single overwhelming ritual, at the cost of losing all partial progress.

rules.statement: An Aspect lasts only while conscious and with Might remaining; it cannot appear where an Aspect of the same Daimon is present or has been within the past day, in a region at least several miles across. If an embodied Aspect’s body is slain, it returns to its parent Daimon; it cannot receive permanent changes.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: The Daimonic Aspect (ars-magica-magic#041)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a one-day, multi-mile exclusion zone and temporary bodies; a world can narrow that boundary, risking overlapping Aspects and added complexity.

rules.statement: A successful Transformation ritual contributes points equal to its level minus the Ascendant Form level. The total needed is the Ascendant Form level, plus three times the pyramid cost of negative characteristics, five times Decrepitude, and—if Flaw points exceed Virtue points—five times the Flaw points; reaching the total completes ascension.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: The Cumulative Transformation Process (ars-magica-magic#041)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to cumulative ritual progress toward a calculated threshold; a world can reduce or remove the burdens for failings, at the cost of making perfection easier.

rules.statement: A Daimon has no Fatigue levels; for magical activities that would spend Fatigue, it instead spends 5 Might per Fatigue level. If this leaves an Aspect at 0 Might or less, that Aspect fades and returns to its parent.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: The Daimonic Magus (ars-magica-magic#041)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to converting each Fatigue cost into 5 Might; a world can lower the conversion, but risks making spirit magic much less costly.

rules.statement: A pact invocation grants Daimon Points equal to its spell level divided by 5, rounded up, once invocation points reach the Daimon’s Might and it appears. Points can preserve one study experience point or one spell magnitude for 1 point, raise Might by 1 for 5 points, or raise a Characteristic by spending 10 times its purchase cost.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Learning and Improving as a Daimonic Spirit (ars-magica-magic#041)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to reward points only when the Daimon answers the call; a world can grant them on every casting, at the cost of easier spirit advancement.

rules.statement: A Hermetic Synthemata spell adds its level to Penetration against one named being for an immediate spell; its Diameter version adds its level minus 5 until the duration ends. The target becomes aware of the threat when the effect is used in its presence.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Hermetic Synthemata (ars-magica-magic#041)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to target-specific Penetration with an awareness tell; a world can hide that tell, but loses the target’s opportunity to react or bargain.

rules.statement: With Synthemata Magia, a magus present with a being can attempt to intuit its synthemata using Perception plus Realm Lore against Might plus name hiding, with both sides adjusted by their local auras. Failure bars another attempt until the magus’s relevant ability improves; a botch alerts the being, and multiple zeroes can create a temporary channel through the magus’s Magic Resistance.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Intuit Synthemata (ars-magica-magic#041)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one failed attempt until the researcher improves; a world can permit retries, but risks turning a guarded identity into routine knowledge.

rules.statement: A Rote is designed up to one-fifth of its Rote Lab Total, rounded up; the total adds Technique, Form, Intelligence, Magic Theory, arithmetic, book bonus, and aura modifier, with arithmetic limited by Magic Theory. It is invoked without a die roll or fatigue, succeeds when its Casting Total (Casting Score divided by two, rounded up) meets its level, and benefits as if it had Quiet Casting and Still Casting.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Rotes (ars-magica-magic#042)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to quiet, fatigue-free formulae with a one-fifth design limit; a world can lower the limit or require a casting roll, reflecting how reliable numerological training is.

rules.statement: A lesser Numerologist’s Book costs 8 pawns of vis and requires Magic Theory 4, granting +4; a greater one costs 16 pawns and requires Magic Theory 8, granting +8. The bonus is capped by the user’s arithmetic score, applies to specified numerological work, and benefits only the attuned magus consulting one carried book at a time; consulting before a Rote adds an extra round.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: The Numerologist’s Book / Creating the Numerologist’s Book (ars-magica-magic#042)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one attuned book granting a capped bonus in exchange for vis, carrying it, and time; a world can adjust the bonus or costs to set how accessible prepared insight is.

rules.statement: Tracing a circle or line for a spell gives +3 to Casting Score; a regular geometric figure can also support ceremonial casting for another +3, cumulative where applicable. A perfect circle drawn freehand requires Dexterity plus Scribe against 15, or against 6 with posts and string; circle or ring casting still requires tracing at no more than ten paces per round and a successful Intelligence plus Concentration check against 6 each round.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Hermetic Geometry — Drawing a Perfect Shape / Bonus for Circles, Rings, and Lines / Ceremonial Figures (ars-magica-magic#042)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to bonuses for carefully traced geometry, with skill and concentration gates; a world can change the bonuses or difficulty to make precision more or less powerful.

rules.statement: Line range can reach as far as Sight without seeing the target, but the caster must sense it and calculate its location with Intelligence plus Artes Liberales (geometry) against an Ease Factor equal to Distance Level, minimum 9. The calculation takes one round per three Ease Factor points, rounded up; failure misplaces the target by the Ease Factor times the shortfall, while a botch also botches the spell.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: New Range: Line (ars-magica-magic#042)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to sensed but unseen targeting gated by a slow, error-prone calculation; a world can alter the minimum difficulty or the error distance to control remote precision.

rules.statement: Arcane Circle and Arcane Ring let a caster trace a perfect circle nearby to affect a remote circle of the same size, whose center is calculated as for Line range. The remote magical circle ends if either circle is broken; Arcane Ring has the duration equivalent of Moon and adds one magnitude.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: New Target: Arcane Circle / New Duration: Arcane Ring (ars-magica-magic#042)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to remote circle effects that persist only while both linked circles remain intact; a world can change the duration or vulnerability to breaking, reflecting the stability of sympathetic links.

rules.statement: Hermetic Architecture uses a number of identical component devices equal to the structure’s Size multiplier, placed in a geometrically calculated pattern; placement uses Intelligence plus geometry against 6 plus that multiplier. A Mystery ritual then binds the devices, requiring a base level of at least 5 plus the highest invested effect level, with extra magnitude for structures larger than Group; removing any component suspends the effect until it is returned.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Hermetic Architecture — Compound Component Devices / Completing and Binding the Enchantment / Breaking the Device (ars-magica-magic#042)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a multi-device structure that works only while all pieces are correctly placed and bound; a world can change the number of components or binding threshold to scale construction burden.

rules.statement: Structural enchantments can raise a Magical aura by one step up to the guideline’s stated maximum, with Creo Vim levels from 35 for a maximum of 1 through 75 for a maximum of 9. They can also alter aura or regio size, and Rego Vim can connect levels of a single regio; these guidelines apply only to Hermetic Architecture structural enchantments.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Boosting Magical Auras / New Aura Magic Guidelines (ars-magica-magic#042)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to aura and regio changes only through costly structural enchantment; a world can change the maximum aura or permitted size shifts to set how much architecture can reshape magical places.

rules.statement: Shrinking a regio interface halves its size per step; reducing a 100-pace diameter to less than one pace takes seven steps and a base level 35 effect. Shrinking only the interface adds one magnitude, and the effect also needs a Perdo requisite and increased magnitude.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Passage 44, regio interface enchantment (ars-magica-magic#043)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: an interface can be sealed by shrinking it below one pace; dial the starting size and magnitude cost; the inhabitants pay for closing access.

rules.statement: Spiritual dream travel leaves the traveler's body in a trance. Physical disturbance requires a Concentration roll to remain in the dream; failure wakes the traveler, and waking of the dreamer also ejects travelers unless they have left through a portal.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Spiritual Dream Travel (ars-magica-magic#043)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: spiritual travelers remain in dreams only while the dream continues; dial the difficulty of bodily disturbance; risk of waking limits exploration.

rules.statement: Inside dreams, a spiritual traveler's magic uses Imaginem for its Form, including magic resistance. Dream duration follows dream time; real-world vis can sustain effects by real-world time, while dream vis has no effect outside dreams.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Magic in Dream; Dream Vis (ars-magica-magic#043)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: dream magic uses Imaginem and dream vis stays dream-bound; dial whether real-world vis is accessible; lasting effects consume real resources.

rules.statement: A Dream target affects one sleeper's actual dream, regardless of size, and applies only to Mentem spells. A higher guideline can include up to ten spirits at level 30, multiplying that number by ten for each added magnitude.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: New Target: Dream; New Spell Guidelines (ars-magica-magic#043)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: one dream and one sleeper are affected; dial the number of spirits by adding magnitudes; broader access requires greater magical effort.

rules.statement: A dreamer who notices travelers may reshape the dream by succeeding at Intelligence against Ease Factor 9. The dreamer's roll gains +3 for being a magus, +3 for Dream Magic, +3 for Hermetic Dream Interpreter, and +1 per other relevant supernatural ability, to a maximum +3.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: The Dreamer in Control (Lucid Dreaming) (ars-magica-magic#043)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: dream control requires awareness and a successful roll; dial the dreamer's bonuses; travelers risk losing control of their surroundings.

rules.statement: A spiritual traveler who takes a dream wound rolls Stamina against an Ease Factor equal to the total wound penalty; failure wakes the traveler. An Incapacitating wound uses Ease Factor 9, and wounds accumulate during combat, making later checks harder.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Fatigue and Wounds (ars-magica-magic#043)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: dream wounds threaten to eject spiritual travelers but are not bodily injuries; dial the shock threshold; repeated wounds increase the risk.

rules.statement: Giving a dream object reality requires a Momentary Ritual and real-world vis; dream vis cannot sustain it outside the dream. To make an enchanted object real, the effect must also account for its enchantment levels and Vim and relevant Art requisites, or it becomes mundane.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: The Greater Dream Grimoire; New Guidelines (ars-magica-magic#043)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: only real-world vis makes dream objects persist outside dreams; dial the size or enchantment strength; the costly vis and added magic limit extraction.

rules.statement: Dream magic cannot create a soul: attempts to give living substance to dream people have not succeeded, though beasts have been made real.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: New Guidelines, Creo (Form) (ars-magica-magic#043)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: dream-made people cannot gain souls; dial whether this limit is absolute; the setting treats soul creation as beyond Hermetic power.

rules.statement: A traveler who enters a dreamer’s constructed memory palace can inspect its memory locations and read the memories there. While inside the dream, the traveler can rearrange memories, making them harder to recall or easier to retrieve; dream magic can strengthen memories or make them solid, and removing a solid memory into the waking world erases it from the dreamer’s mind.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Passage 45, memory palace discussion (ars-magica-magic#044)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to allowing dream intrusions to inspect and rearrange memory; a world can restrict solidification or removal, since stolen memories are permanently lost to the dreamer.

rules.statement: Dream travelers may use portals to reach a wider dreamscape or other dreams, but physical travelers, waking-world objects, and real-world vis cannot cross into the dreamscape. Dream bodies can be recreated with Imaginem after dream-wound death, but dream-Mentem or Might attacks that destroy the traveler’s spirit cause actual death, with no direct route back to waking life.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: The Dreamscape (ars-magica-magic#044)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to spiritual travel only, with dream-body loss recoverable; a world can make spirit destruction final because waking escape is unavailable.

rules.statement: While a traveler’s spirit is in the dreamscape, the entranced body cannot be awakened and the traveler does not perceive changes to it, including injury or death. Dream-time outside combat can heal even incapacitating wounds to the dream body.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: The Dreamscape (ars-magica-magic#044)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to disconnecting the traveler’s awareness from the entranced body; a world can make body death more dangerous by allowing the spirit to discover it only upon return.

rules.statement: Dream forms and dream vis can serve most purposes in the dreamscape, but they cannot make permanent changes real there. A portal from the dreamscape into another dream does not let a traveler bring real-world vis to make lasting changes in that remote dream.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Dreamscape — Dream or Reality? (ars-magica-magic#044)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to preventing dream effects from producing permanent waking-world change; a world can relax this limit, at the cost of blurring dream and reality.

rules.statement: A Road spell can reach a sensed target on the caster’s same path, at the same spell-level range as Voice. Road Network can reach a sensed target across an unbroken connected path network, at the Arcane Connection range level and only with ritual magic; bridges and fords interrupt that connection.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Neo-Mercurian Road Magic: New Ranges and Targets (ars-magica-magic#044)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to requiring a sensed target and continuous paths; a world can let bridges or fords count as connected, making road magic more reliable.

rules.statement: Road as a spell target covers the road and its occupants, normally 100 paces long and up to ten paces wide, and uses Room-level calculation. Road Network covers the connected roads and their occupants, normally 10,000 paces long and up to ten paces wide, and uses Boundary-level calculation and ritual magic; extra width requires increased Size or reduced length.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Neo-Mercurian Road Magic: New Ranges and Targets (ars-magica-magic#044)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the stated standard dimensions and scale costs; a world can enlarge coverage, with greater Size or shorter reach as the tradeoff.

rules.statement: For a similar spell, a caster may apply the mastery score and its associated special abilities from a mastered spell. If more than one mastered spell applies, the caster chooses one mastery score and only the abilities attached to that choice.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Cult of Mercury and Neo-Mercurian Spell Mastery Special Abilities — Adaptive Casting (ars-magica-magic#044)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to borrowing one similar spell’s mastery package at a time; a world can allow combining packages, increasing the benefit of broad mastery.

rules.statement: A satisfactory, pure animal offered on a deity’s altar can replace 1 to 6 pawns of vis used for a ritual spell that summons that deity; rarity and nobility determine value, from 1 pawn for an unblemished lamb to 6 for a pure lion. Magically created or altered animals do not qualify, and forceful spirit magic spoils the altar for later use.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Hermetic Sacrifice — Minor Hermetic Mystery Virtue (ars-magica-magic#044)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to substituting 1–6 vis according to the offering’s value; a world can demand greater sacrifice, while coercing the spirit risks permanently spoiling the altar.

rules.statement: A Raven’s initiation imposes a magical oath that adds the minor Dutybound flaw tied to the Legion; afterward, higher ranks may summon the initiate at any time when the Order faces a crisis.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: First Rank: Ravens (ars-magica-magic#045)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: The engine can default to an enforceable duty that triggers call-up on crisis; a world can vary the oath’s scope and penalties, with service and reduced freedom as the cost.

rules.statement: A Raven’s training in Strong-Willed takes an entire season. A Soldier’s third season of training teaches either Reserves of Strength or Enduring Constitution.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: First Rank: Ravens; Third Rank: Soldiers (ars-magica-magic#045)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: The engine can default to training that grants the specified trait after a season; worlds can alter the duration, with time and other seasonal activity as the cost.

rules.statement: A Persian’s initiation usually requires sacrificing the magus’s existing talisman so that a silver sickle can be enchanted as its replacement.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Fifth Rank: Persian (ars-magica-magic#045)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: The engine can default to transferring the talisman’s role to the sickle only after the old talisman is sacrificed; worlds can change what must be relinquished, with the existing enchanted item as the cost.

rules.statement: The final ascension sought by the Philosophers requires support from many magi; continued devotion and invocation after success help the new Daimon grow stronger, and it can reward its supporters.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: The Structure of the Philosophers of Rome (ars-magica-magic#045)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: The engine can default to ascension needing a collective of supporters and ongoing worship to build the Daimon’s strength; worlds can set the number and duties, with continued service as the cost.

rules.statement: A new Child of Hermes studies the cult’s Lore for a season, receives a Mystery initiation and its script, and then owes at least two pawns of vis each year. The initiate is also expected to recruit others and collect the same dues from them.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Structure of the Children of Hermes (ars-magica-magic#045)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: The engine can default to annual dues of at least two pawns plus recruitment duties; worlds can change the payment and collection rules, with vis and ongoing obligations as the cost.

rules.statement: The Inner Circle can take lore and initiation material obtained from other cults, assimilate it into the Children’s teachings, and circulate modified scripts; this adaptation is conducted by the Inner Circle.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Structure of the Children of Hermes (ars-magica-magic#045)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: The engine can default to learned cult lore being adapted for the Children after Inner Circle review; worlds can limit what transfers, with access to another cult’s knowledge and the risk of betrayal as the cost.

rules.statement: An Electus’s hair is kept as a permanent Arcane Connection, while the Initiators also record the initiate’s birth name and signature and retain the natal horoscope. Together these give a user a spellcasting Penetration bonus equal to eight times the Penetration score against that initiate.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Electus (ars-magica-magic#045)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: The engine can default to the retained personal links multiplying Penetration by eight against their subject; worlds can change the multiplier or required links, with enduring vulnerability to targeted magic as the cost.

rules.statement: The Fraternity’s Electus initiation requires a natal chart and leaves the Initiators holding a lock of the initiate’s hair as a permanent Arcane Connection; this combination is an initiation Ordeal.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Electus (ars-magica-magic#045)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: The engine can default to initiation creating lasting personal links held by the group; worlds can change which records or remains are kept, with lasting exposure to hostile magic as the cost.

rules.statement: Mathematikoi must abstain from meat and green beans, teach new initiates, and provide visiting initiates with food and lodging for as long as needed.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: The Inner Order: Mathematikoi (ars-magica-magic#045)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: The engine can default to membership imposing dietary, teaching, and hospitality duties; worlds can vary their strictness, with ongoing restrictions and resource use as the cost.

rules.statement: A being with Might belongs to a supernatural realm and can be targeted by Warding spells; against other spells it may resist with either its Might score or Form + five times Parma Magica, but cannot add those defenses together.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Appendix A: Immortal Magi (ars-magica-magic#046)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to choosing one of the two defenses; a world can change which defense is available, reflecting the being’s realm or training.

rules.statement: Immortals do not age, make Aging rolls, or suffer Warping or Twilight, and need not eat, drink, or breathe. A bodily immortal can still be slain, while one without a body can be destroyed by magic that destroys its spirit.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Appendix A: Immortal Magi (ars-magica-magic#046)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to immunity to aging and ordinary bodily needs, while leaving destruction possible; a world can make particular immortal forms harder to destroy at the cost of additional requirements.

rules.statement: An immortal naturally returns to its basic state: unmaintained magical and mental changes fade, wounds heal, and study does not remain learned without magical reinforcement. Changes whose magical duration exceeds Momentary begin fading only after the effect ends, and any unbound temporary change fades completely within a season.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Immortal and Unchanging (ars-magica-magic#046)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to complete reversion within a season; a world can lengthen or shorten the recovery window to reflect how strongly immortality resists change.

rules.statement: An immortal may preserve study by binding it into a talisman in a laboratory; the enchantment needs an already opened space and must be completed within one season. Its level is 10 times the XP retained, and if the full amount cannot be invested that season, only the XP covered is retained and the rest fades.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Learning Arts or Abilities; Binding the Immortal Memory (ars-magica-magic#046)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to preserving only the XP paid for by a completed talisman effect; a world can alter the level-per-XP rate, with talisman capacity and laboratory time as the cost.

rules.statement: An immortal can retain a learned spell by investing an always-active talisman effect at the spell’s level, completed in one season; the effect stores knowledge rather than casting the spell, so the magus casts it normally. The stored spell is lost if its talisman is destroyed.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Learning Spells; The Immortal’s Grimoire (ars-magica-magic#046)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to requiring one level of enchantment per spell level and a season to finish; a world can change the rate, with opened talisman spaces and the device’s vulnerability as costs.

rules.statement: To build a high-level spell’s talisman foundation across multiple seasons, the immortal alternates a season of investment with relearning the spell, matching the prior partial investment with an Intelligence + Magic Theory roll against 6 + the spell’s magnitude. Failure reveals the mismatch and permits abandoning that cycle; a botch goes unnoticed, ruins the investment, and risks altering an existing talisman effect.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Binding High-Level Spells (ars-magica-magic#046)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the stated matching test and botch risk; a world can ease or intensify the target, reflecting how reliably a spell can be reconstructed.

rules.statement: A mortal magus can bring a familiar along into an immortal transformation by adding raw vis equal to the Familiar Bond Score divided by 5, rounded up. Without that extra vis the familiar remains mortal, is severed from the transformed magus, and soon dies; a spirit familiar needs no extra vis.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Becoming Immortal with a Familiar (ars-magica-magic#046)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to charging rounded-up vis based on bond strength; a world can waive or change the cost, reflecting the nature of the familiar and transformation.

rules.statement: A bodily immortal’s wounds do not worsen: make a simple recovery roll weekly for ordinary wounds, improving Light, Medium, and Heavy wounds at totals of 10, 12, and 15 respectively; stable wounds gain +3 on later rolls. For Incapacitating wounds, roll at sunrise and sunset and improve them to Heavy on 9+, while wounds and scars otherwise fade within a season; a sufficiently severe wound can still kill the immortal.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Immortal and Unchanging (ars-magica-magic#046)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to gradual recovery and complete healing by season’s end without worsening; a world can change the thresholds or healing window, trading resilience against the possibility of death.

rules.statement: A spirit can maintain calm weather throughout a harbor for a season; spells that would disrupt the weather must overcome its Magic Resistance of 60.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Portunes, Spirit of Safe Harbor — Safe Harbor (ars-magica-magic#047)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to season-long protection over one harbor; a world could widen the area or duration, at the cost of stronger resistance or greater power expenditure.

rules.statement: Portunes can remove a magical lock if its level is below 40.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Portunes, Spirit of Safe Harbor — Opening Enchanted Locks (ars-magica-magic#047)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to ending locks below level 40; a world could raise the threshold, balanced by higher cost or stricter access.

rules.statement: Honos can immediately impart 17 experience points in Leadership, up to score 6, but the recipient must spend a season studying and reflecting before gaining the increase.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Honos — Instill Leadership (ars-magica-magic#047)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a limited, delayed ability increase; a world could allow faster gains, at the cost of removing the required season of study.

rules.statement: Honos creates enough food for 100 people, which lasts one hour. Dutybound people who eat it are cured of Light and Medium Wounds and receive +10 on their next recovery checks; these benefits persist after the food vanishes.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Honos — Centurions' Feast (ars-magica-magic#047)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a short-lived meal with lasting benefits for a restricted group; a world could expand eligibility or healing, at greater power cost.

rules.statement: Pukis can become invisible and inaudible for as long as it chooses, ending the concealment if it touches a person or animal.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Pukis, Dragon of the Hearth — Invisibility (ars-magica-magic#047)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to indefinite concealment with contact as the limit; a world could remove that trigger, balanced by a duration or power-cost limit.

rules.statement: Pukis can ignite anything slightly flammable with a glance.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Pukis, Dragon of the Hearth — Mischievous Flame (ars-magica-magic#047)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to igniting only slightly flammable targets; a world could permit less flammable materials, at increased cost or with closer range.

rules.statement: By touching an object weighing less than three pounds, Pukis sends it instantly to its home, where it appears beside its master's hearth.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Pukis, Dragon of the Hearth — Sneak Thief (ars-magica-magic#047)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a touch-triggered transfer limited to objects under three pounds and one fixed destination; a world could lift either limit, at greater cost.

rules.statement: While Pukis lives in a hearth kept hot throughout the year, its ashes yield one pawn of Ignem vis per season.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Pukis, Dragon of the Hearth — Sacred Fire (ars-magica-magic#047)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one pawn per season under continuous upkeep; a world could increase the yield, requiring more maintenance or a larger sacrifice.

rules.statement: Dietrich can permanently raise one person's Perception, Presence, or Communication by one point, once per person, to a maximum of +3 in the chosen characteristic.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Dietrich von Bern — Sacred Kingship (ars-magica-magic#047)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one permanent point per recipient, with a +3 ceiling; a world could raise the ceiling, at the cost of stricter eligibility or a rarer grant.

rules.statement: Dietrich's dragon-blooded sword cannot be deflected, harmed, or controlled by magical spells of level 40 or lower. A wound it inflicts burns for an additional 5 damage per round, which armor does not soak, until an alchemist, herbalist, or healer cures it.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Magic books and Mysteries: Dietrich von Bern — Combat (ars-magica-magic#047)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to immunity against spells up to level 40 and recurring, armor-bypassing damage until treated; a world could raise the immunity threshold or intensify the burn, requiring harder cures.

rules.statement: On an aura-strengthening result of 10, spontaneous magical effects appear and targeted people gain 1 Warping Point; spontaneous casting gets up to +3. Results of 11 and 15–20 raise the aura by 1 temporarily for a season or permanently, respectively; other results can produce vis, localized changes, or expansion, and a result of 21+ is rolled twice more as 20.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Aura Strengthening Table (ars-magica-realms#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Use the listed table outcomes as the default; a world can make aura change more or less disruptive, because rapid change risks Warping and regio formation.

rules.statement: On an aura-weakening result of 10, spontaneous casting receives up to a −3 penalty; results of 11 and 15–20 lower the aura by 1 for a season or permanently, respectively. A result of 12 wastes 1–3 pawns of vis permanently, while 21+ is rolled twice more as 20; unless specified otherwise, effects last at most a year.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Aura Weakening Table (ars-magica-realms#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Use the table and its one-year limit by default; a world can make aura decline more persistent or localized, with lost vis and diminished magic as the cost.

rules.statement: A botch during aura variation can remove a regio level, or create one if none exists; a newly formed regio has a mundane level and a top level at the overall aura strength. With an existing regio, a new intermediate level is added instead; everyone present gains 3 Warping Points, doubled on a double botch or worse, and no regio may have more levels than the aura score plus 1.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Magic Regiones (ars-magica-realms#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Treat botches as the default trigger for fractured levels; a world can make regio formation more controllable, but the cost here is Warping and potentially dangerous displacement.

rules.statement: When a regio’s aura score falls, the top level usually weakens; if another level already matches the new score, the top level vanishes instead. Its inhabitants drop to the next lower level and each gain 3 Warping Points; an increase usually strengthens the top level but does not create a new one, though a dormant matching level may return.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Magic Regiones (ars-magica-realms#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Use strength changes to alter or release levels as described; a world can let vanished levels remain accessible, but the default risks stranding inhabitants and possessions.

rules.statement: After a few minutes in an emotion-aligned aura, a character without a Magic-derived supernatural ability gains or modifies a non-essential Personality Trait by +1 at aura levels 1–3, +2 at 4–6, or +3 at 7–10, if the character has a trait the aura supports or opposes. The change fades within minutes of leaving, but any permanent Warping remains.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Auras that Enhance Emotions / Aura Effect Table (ars-magica-realms#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Apply temporary trait adjustment as the default; a world can make emotional influence more lasting, but enduring Warping is the lasting cost.

rules.statement: An Art-aligned aura adds its level to the Casting Score and appropriate Lab Total for work using that Art, effectively counting the aura modifier twice. A creature with matching Might spends 1 less than usual to use a Power when its normal cost is positive; opposed Arts receive no penalty.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Auras Aligned with Arts (ars-magica-realms#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Grant the listed bonuses without opposed-Art penalties; a world can restrict which activities benefit, because the advantage depends on the aura’s alignment.

rules.statement: For each point an aura’s score increases, one inhabitant may unwittingly gain a new Supernatural Virtue, or someone with a Supernatural Ability may gain 20 experience points in it. Weakening can reverse this by removing 20 experience points, and an ability reduced to zero cannot be used.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Symptoms of Aura Variation / Signs and Supernatural Abilities (ars-magica-realms#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Use one affected inhabitant per aura point by default; a world can make the change deliberate or selective, while involuntary power loss or acquisition is the consequence.

rules.statement: In a cosm, changes to the cosm usually affect its connected worlds; within these places, ordinary natural rules—especially geography and downward falling—may not apply. A microcosm may be contained in something small, while a macrocosm may encompass a greater whole represented by its parts.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Magic Perspectives / Worlds Within Worlds (ars-magica-realms#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Treat cosm changes as reflected in their connected worlds; a world can narrow or sever that correspondence, because travel and alteration otherwise risk consequences beyond the cosm.

rules.statement: While in the Magic Realm, a character gains no experience; instead, each full season produces pawns of one chosen vis type equal to the experience the character would have earned. For a season split between realms, divide the experience-equivalent between vis for Magic Realm time and experience for mundane time.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Rules of the Realm (ars-magica-realms#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to converting the season’s usual experience yield into vis; a world can change the rate or type, with magical knowledge serving as the in-world source.

rules.statement: Characters do not age by aging rolls in the Magic Realm, but their actual age still increases as years pass; they heal wounds and recover Might and Fatigue normally. Diameter, Sun, and Moon effects last until the current season ends, while Year effects persist as long as their targets remain there.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Rules of the Realm (ars-magica-realms#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to suspended aging and season-bounded shorter durations; a world can set different duration rules, because the Realm's timeless quality alters how time passes.

rules.statement: Arcane Connections to things outside the Magic Realm are interrupted while brought inside and resume when returned; connections do not decay there unless carried through boundaries or vestiges. Things touched in the Realm remain connected to the toucher while they stay in the same area.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Rules of the Realm (ars-magica-realms#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to suspending external connections inside the Realm and preserving local ones; a world can change which connections persist, with passage across Realm boundaries risking their loss.

rules.statement: A boundary has a level from 0 to 10, adding that many points to magical activities on top of the constant Magic aura of 10; effects of its aligned Form double the boundary contribution. Rolls benefiting from the aura gain botch dice equal to the boundary level, and the boundary produces pawns each season equal to the modified aura divided by 10, rounded up, which fade after a season if unharvested.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Boundaries and Vestiges (ars-magica-realms#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to stronger aligned magic, greater botch risk, and seasonal vis equal to the aura scale; a world can tune level and yield, with dangerous concentrated magic as the cost.

rules.statement: A vestige is a sensory-complete but insubstantial impression, passable with resistance roughly proportional to how hard its mundane counterpart would be to move. It cannot suffocate or drown travelers, but changing a vestige can alter its mundane counterpart when the two are connected.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Boundaries and Vestiges (ars-magica-realms#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to allowing vestige changes to affect the linked mundane thing; a world can limit which links respond, with uncertain correspondence making the consequences hard to predict.

rules.statement: To travel through a boundary or vestige, roll a stress die plus Perception, an appropriate Ability, and any applicable Form bonus against three times 10 minus its level, reduced by the best Familiarity modifier. Success sets an initial speed from the amount the result exceeds the target; the destination must be connected or have level at least 1.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Magical Travel (ars-magica-realms#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to level and familiarity determining passage difficulty and travel speed; a world can adjust thresholds, with unknown destinations and weak connections making travel harder.

rules.statement: In the Twilight Void, the leader's initial speed determines a fixed maximum travel time; concentrating can improve the group's speed while the leader does nothing else. A botch reduces speed one step per botch, and a speed below zero strands the group; supernatural effects expire on entering or leaving, and Arcane Connections degrade one duration category on entry.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Magical Travel (ars-magica-realms#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to fixed passage time, concentration-based acceleration, and costly botches; a world can change speed and degradation, with lost effects and connections making transit hazardous.

rules.statement: In the Twilight Void, travelers do not age, need food, drink, or breath, or suffer natural wound changes or long-term Fatigue recovery; they gain neither experience nor vis. A Comprehension roll can yield a beneficial or harmful Essential Trait change, twice a simple die in experience for an Art or Ability, and Warping Points for a character without Might; each botch slows travel one chart step.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: The Twilight Void (ars-magica-realms#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to suspending bodily needs and ordinary advancement while allowing comprehension to change traits and grant learning; a world can alter rewards, with failed understanding carrying harmful effects and delay.

rules.statement: Hermetic magic normally cannot affect Magic Realm boundaries or vestiges. A single Minor Breakthrough costing 30 Breakthrough points unlocks the guidelines, but research cannot begin until the magus has visited the Realm and dealt with a boundary or vestige; a magus may instead learn a guideline through a qualifying Lab Text or gain an Insight by converting vis, with each pawn producing one magnitude of effect and no more than one Insight gained per season.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Magic Realm Magic (ars-magica-realms#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default access is closed until the magus has experienced the Realm; a world can make research, vis conversion, or scarce Lab Texts the route in, reflecting the difficulty of understanding Realm-specific magic.

rules.statement: Magic Realm effects draw on the Realm’s special properties and work there or through a link to it; a being with Magic Might has a link of the Form matching its Might. In the Realm, environmental Durations shorter than Year last a season, while Year is effectively permanent; outside the Realm, durations revert to normal and an expired effect ends immediately.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Magic Realm Magic (ars-magica-realms#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default effects work only in the Realm or through a qualifying link and use its altered duration scale; a world can broaden access or normalize duration, at the cost of reducing the Realm’s distinctiveness.

rules.statement: Magic Might gives innate Magic Resistance equal to the Might Score, but it does not stack with other base resistance; a magus who has Might may add Form bonuses but must use either Parma or Might as the base. Magic characters spend Might Points to activate powers and recover them steadily over 24 hours, with a character of Might 12 recovering one point every two hours; vis of the matching Form restores 5 points per pawn, other vis restores 2, and consumed vis adds +2 Penetration for a matching power.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Chapter Four: Magic Characters (ars-magica-realms#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default Might supplies both resistance and a spendable power reserve; a world can tune recovery and vis replenishment, with faster recovery making powerful beings harder to exhaust.

rules.statement: If an effect reduces a magic character’s Might Score to 0 or less, the character is destroyed, with the form of destruction depending on its nature. A character with Might 0 can also be destroyed by an effect designed to reduce Might if that effect penetrates its resistance.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Chapter Four: Magic Characters (ars-magica-realms#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default destruction occurs at zero Might; a world can make the result banishment, inertness, mundane restoration, or death, determining what can be recovered afterward.

rules.statement: Magic characters need no food, drink, sleep, shelter, or breath, and do not age, but conditions that would cause deprivation or exposure prevent them from recovering Might or Fatigue and give their wounds an immediate chance of worsening. A character cannot spend more pawns of vis on one activity than its Might Score.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Chapter Four: Magic Characters (ars-magica-realms#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default deprivation blocks recovery and risks worsening wounds despite the lack of ordinary needs; a world can remove or intensify this constraint, trading survival convenience against vulnerability.

rules.statement: A magic thing’s Might depends on its Size: the listed minimum sizes range from –21 for Might 0 to 0 for Might 15, with each additional 5 Might requiring 3 more Size. Its power falls immediately if it is separated from the larger entity or matter supporting its increased size; injuries reduce its Might Pool and appear as vis, and it recovers spent Might slowly.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Magic Things (ars-magica-realms#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default power is tied to size and continued physical or metaphorical contact; a world can loosen that dependency, at the cost of removing a distinctive vulnerability.

rules.statement: Magic spirits are generally imperceptible and unaffected except by magic characters of the same Form; without a power to manifest, they are invisible and pass through solid objects. When they interact with other spirits, they can be harmed as though they had flesh, and if their true form is destroyed or banished they cease to exist as that character.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Magic Spirits (ars-magica-realms#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default spirits are intangible to ordinary beings but vulnerable among their own kind; a world can let mundane beings sense or affect them, weakening their separation from the physical world.

rules.statement: A magic animal’s Might Score is reduced by its Size, or increased by the absolute value of a negative Size; this adjustment does not change the number of Magic Qualities it receives. A magic human’s monstrous appearance imposes –6 on social interactions with mundane humans or animals.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Magic Animals; Magic Humans (ars-magica-realms#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default animal Might trades off against size, while supernatural human appearance impairs social dealings; a world can alter either penalty to favor imposing stature or easier social integration.

rules.statement: Subtract a magic character’s Might Score from every Advancement Total, including exposure and adventure totals. The character also receives the same number of points to spend on Magic Qualities; Minor Qualities cost 1 point and Major ones cost 3, while Inferiorities can add points.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Magic Might Score (ars-magica-realms#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to subtracting all Might from advancement and granting equal Quality points; a saga can adjust starting Might and thereby tune both development and supernatural advantages.

rules.statement: A character’s asterisked true-form Personality Trait is essential: the character cannot act against it, and magic cannot force such behavior.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Finishing Touches (ars-magica-realms#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to making true form an absolute behavioral boundary; a world can loosen the boundary, at the cost of weakening the character’s defining nature.

rules.statement: A power’s Penetration is Might Score minus five times its Might Point cost, plus its Penetration bonus. At Might Pool zero, only zero-cost powers can be activated; powers already running continue until their duration ends.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Magic Powers (ars-magica-realms#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the stated cost-sensitive Penetration and zero-pool restriction; a world can change the cost penalty or permit borrowing, with consequences for resistance and depletion.

rules.statement: A Greater, Lesser, or Personal Power may be made constant if designed with Sun duration and one extra magnitude. It activates at sunrise and sunset, paying its Might cost each time; insufficient Might interrupts it, and a Confidence Point can prevent a triggering activation.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Magic Powers (ars-magica-realms#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to two daily activations paid from the Might Pool; a world can alter the trigger schedule or substitute another cost, changing reliability and resource demand.

rules.statement: An incapacitated magic character cannot spend Might Points, though it can activate zero-cost powers. A costly constant effect ends at the next sunrise or sunset and cannot restart until the character is no longer incapacitated.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Magic Powers (ars-magica-realms#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to disabling Might expenditure during incapacitation; a world can allow limited expenditure, at the cost of making injury less effective at shutting down powers.

rules.statement: Ritual Powers cost Might Pool points and also reduce permanent Might Score by one per cost point when used. Instead, the user may spend one Confidence Point per cost point; lost Might Score may recover slowly at the storyguide’s discretion.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Ritual Power (ars-magica-realms#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to permanent Might loss or a Confidence expenditure for exceptional effects; a world can make recovery easier or harder, adjusting the long-term price of ritual power.

rules.statement: A permanent power that imposes a Virtue or Flaw costs from both the user’s Might Score and Might Pool; a temporary one ties up its spent Might Points until the effect is withdrawn.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Common Magic Powers — Grant (Virtue or Flaw) (ars-magica-realms#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to paying permanently for permanent changes and locking points for temporary ones; a world can change the recovery condition, shifting the cost of altering another being.

rules.statement: A sworn oath takes effect only if all participants consent and the power penetrates each participant’s Magic Resistance. A participant who knowingly acts against it becomes aware of the breach and, if proceeding, gains a Minor Flaw; the Flaw can be removed by renewing the oath before the original participants.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Common Magic Powers — Oath-Swearing (ars-magica-realms#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to consent, penetration, and a breach-triggered Flaw; a world can change the enforcer or penalty, with the oath’s force and risk changing accordingly.

rules.statement: A wounded magical being loses Might Points equal to the wound penalty: 1 for Light, 3 for Medium, 5 for Heavy, and 5 when incapacitated. As accumulated wound penalties reach each additional 5 points, a pawn of vis is separated from its body; the number is the total wound penalty divided by 5, minus pawns already lost.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Minor Magic Inferiorities (preceding section) (ars-magica-realms#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Track Might loss and bodily vis release by wound severity; a world can change the conversion rate, because injury costs magical substance as well as strength.

rules.statement: A power gained through Focus Power, Greater Power, Lesser Power, or Personal Power costs fatigue levels equal to its Might Point cost divided by 5, rounded up. Focus Power instead uses a 25-point design pool, with each effect-level increase costing 2 points and each Penetration point costing 1; powers without a Might Score otherwise have zero Penetration unless points or levels are spent on it.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Focus Power; Greater Power; Lesser Power; Personal Power (ars-magica-realms#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Charge rounded-up fatigue for activations; a setting can raise or lower the fatigue conversion, because power users have no Might reserve to spend.

rules.statement: A Ritual Power costs rounded-up fatigue at one level per 5 Might Points, plus Confidence Points equal to the power's Might Point cost. Mastery points can reduce the Might Point cost, while power levels may be traded for Penetration.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Ritual Power (ars-magica-realms#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Require both fatigue and confidence for a ritual activation; a world can tune either payment, reflecting how taxing such effects are to the user.

rules.statement: The Atlantean Water-way range can affect a target connected to the same river, canal, lake, or sea as the caster, provided the caster touches the water and the target touches or floats on it. The target need not be seen, but must be sensed unless the spell is an Intellego effect that detects presence; its spell-level range is equivalent to Sight.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Atlantean Magic — Water-way (ars-magica-realms#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Permit targeting only along a shared waterway with physical contact and sensing; a world can define waterway boundaries more broadly or narrowly, because geography determines magical reach.

rules.statement: Storm duration requires casting during a storm and ends when that storm ends; it is available only for Aquam or Auram forms and is rated like Concentration. A natural storm's remaining hours can be estimated by a stress die divided by 2; a botch means it dissipates in minutes.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Atlantean Magic — Storm (ars-magica-realms#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Tie spell duration to the storm's natural lifetime; a world can lengthen or shorten storms, since the environment supplies the effect's limit.

rules.statement: A Body-of-water target affects an entire lake, river, or sea, with boundaries judged as for waterways; it is rated like Structure and very large bodies require increased spell magnitude.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Atlantean Magic — Body-of-water (ars-magica-realms#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Allow whole-water-body targeting at Structure scale; a world can set larger magnitude surcharges, since the target's size limits coverage.

rules.statement: A Composer of Power teaches songs that reproduce one power the composer knows. Each performance consumes vis of the appropriate Form equal to 1 plus that power's Might Point cost; in a season the composer may teach one song to as many students as their Leadership score, and each student's knowledge lasts one year.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Composer of Power (ars-magica-realms#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Let taught songs reproduce known effects for a per-use vis payment; a world can change student capacity or retention, because musical power is both teachable and consumable.

rules.statement: An Imbued with the Spirit of a Form magus may replace vis of that Form with long-term fatigue levels, one fatigue level per pawn. The loss follows spellcasting and lasts through the laboratory process when used there; it cannot replace vis for studying vis.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Imbued with the Spirit of (Form) (ars-magica-realms#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Allow bodily exhaustion to substitute for matching vis, with long recovery and activity limits; a world can vary the exchange rate, because the user is paying with vitality.

rules.statement: A power may require a special ceremony before it can be used, or it may work only on a specified kind of target or in specified circumstances; this restriction may be taken separately for each power.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Opening passage, preceding Servant of the (Land) (ars-magica-realms#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to powers working without ceremony or narrow conditions; a setting can restrict them by ritual, target, or circumstance to express their origin or instability.

rules.statement: A character who owes a task to a powerful magical creature must spend at least one complete season each year working on it. While the task remains unfinished, failure to do so brings a curse; the associated prohibition does not count against the character’s Virtue and Flaw limit.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Servant of the (Land) (ars-magica-realms#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one season of required service per year; a world can make the task or curse more demanding to reflect the patron’s power and displeasure.

rules.statement: One of a character’s powers takes an additional round of preparation to activate. This restriction can apply to different powers, but not more than once to the same power.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Slow Power (ars-magica-realms#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to ordinary activation time; increase preparation time to make a power less responsive without changing its effect.

rules.statement: A wanderlust-driven character cannot stay in one place longer than a season and may spend only two nonconsecutive seasons each year in the same Magic aura. If prevented from traveling, the character may be unable to spend or regain Confidence or restore Might until it leaves.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Wanderlust (ars-magica-realms#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the stated travel limit and possible recovery denial; a setting can intensify the discomfort or its consequences to make the compulsion more costly.

rules.statement: Sensitive or weak senses impose a –2 penalty on activities under the relevant conditions. Extreme cold or heat also causes one Fatigue level of loss per hour when the character is at least two chart steps beyond its accustomed temperature range.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Warped Senses (ars-magica-realms#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the listed penalties and hourly Fatigue loss; a world can vary which environments trigger them to reflect a character’s magical adaptation.

rules.statement: A magic character regains Might while concentrating in a Magic aura at a rate of 1 Might Point per aura level per ten minutes, and can prevent Acclimation at twice the normal rate. Disturbance calls for a concentration check using this Ability, and failure wastes that period’s effort.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Magical Meditation (ars-magica-realms#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the aura-level recovery rate and doubled protection rate; a world can make concentration harder to maintain to balance rapid magical replenishment.

rules.statement: At each year’s end, a magic character permanently loses either one Magic Quality or 1 point of Might unless it has met a protection condition during the year; if neither loss is possible, it ceases to be magical. Protection can come from a sufficiently strong Magic aura, magical effects linking it to another being, or consuming vis equal to half its Might in pawns.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Acclimation (ars-magica-realms#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to annual magical decline unless one of the listed protections is satisfied; a world can alter the protection thresholds to determine how costly it is to remain magical.

rules.statement: Transformation improves a magic character only in ways consistent with its essential nature. Study can add or change Qualities and Inferiorities for the listed experience costs, from 0 to 30 points; alternatively, spending vis equal to the character’s Might yields a stress-die result plus aura bonus in experience, with botch dice based on one per 5 pawns consumed.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Transformation (ars-magica-realms#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the listed experience or vis costs and require changes to fit the character’s nature; a world can permit broader transformations at the cost of greater risk or altered identity.

rules.statement: Magic characters’ Essential Traits define enduring aspects of their nature, and magical effects that would force conduct against those traits fail. A Character Trait modifies its associated Characteristic by taking the more extreme value when trait and score are both beneficial or both detrimental, and otherwise adding the trait value.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Essential Traits (ars-magica-realms#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to Essential Traits being unchangeable and protective; a world can make the traits more specific or more restrictive to make magical identity a stronger limit.

rules.statement: A power may affect creatures that hear its sound, but Magic Resistance can prevent the effect. The Cockerel’s crow drives eligible night-active spirits away until the next sunrise or sunset.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Cockerel of Virtue — Scourge the Spirits of the Night (ars-magica-realms#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default the effect to flee-inducing sound that lasts until dawn or dusk; a world can narrow which spirits count as nocturnal, because the power relies on their night-bound nature.

rules.statement: The Cockerel’s comb can be made into a worn item that grants Second Sight at Ability 3; making it requires an amber bead, consecrated ground, and at least 12 Sundays of preparation.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Cockerel of Virtue — Vis and Enrichment (ars-magica-realms#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default the finished comb to grant Second Sight 3 when worn; a world can vary the preparation time, with consecration and the 12-Sunday wait as the cost.

rules.statement: The Stallion senses ground movement within one mile and can determine direction, distance, weight, number, and manner of movement. Its constant sensing costs 2 points.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Great Stallion of the Camargue — Sense the Feet that Tread the Earth (ars-magica-realms#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default the sense to report the listed details within one mile; a world can reduce its range or detail, because maintaining constant awareness draws on the Stallion’s power.
