rules.statement: The Stallion can cover one league in one Diameter when unencumbered; each Burden level adds one Diameter to the travel time. It can also cross open water and chasms at a trot, but not at full speed.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Great Stallion of the Camargue — Sprint of the Zephyr; The Unimpeded Traveler (ars-magica-realms#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default the speed to one league per Diameter without burden and 30 miles per day over difficult terrain; a world can change the rate, with burden and trotting across gaps as limits.

rules.statement: The Lion’s circle prevents mundane beasts from crossing it, and the effect can be used to trap prey. The ring ends when its duration expires.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Pentele, a Lion of Virtue — Circle of Beast Warding (ars-magica-realms#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default the circle to bar mundane beasts while it holds; a world can change the duration or eligible creatures, with the boundary limiting who can cross.

rules.statement: The Panther’s scent entrances humans and beasts unless they succeed on a Stamina roll against Ease Factor 9. Its breath travels up to 100 paces in ideal wind, and seeing its face breaks the effect; dragons are unaffected.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Panther of Virtue — Pleasing Breath (ars-magica-realms#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default the scent to lure susceptible targets toward the Panther within 100 paces; a world can alter range or resistance, with the Stamina test and dragons’ immunity limiting it.

rules.statement: The Salamander’s touch extinguishes any fire, though a very large fire is put out only within three paces of it. Its body is unharmed by heat and flame even without using this power.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Salamander of Virtue — Devouring the Heat of the Fire (ars-magica-realms#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default a touch to extinguish fire, capped at a three-pace radius for very large blazes; a world can adjust the affected area, because the Salamander’s reach limits the effect.

rules.statement: The Stag can heal one of its own Heavy or lesser wounds only after eating dittany. It can also delay poison’s effects in its body until the next sunrise or sunset, then neutralize poison already inside it permanently by drinking water.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Stag of Virtue — Healing; Delay the Serpent’s Venom; Alleviate the Serpent’s Bite (ars-magica-realms#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default healing to one Heavy-or-lighter wound with dittany, poison delay to the next dawn or dusk, and permanent neutralization with water; a world can change the requirements, which are the cost.

rules.statement: The White Stag’s presence makes a group of deer fight as a trained unit and adds +2 to their defense rolls. Its trackless effect leaves no earth tracks except when it stops.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: White Stag of the Wood — Defense of the Herd; Trackless Step (ars-magica-realms#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default the herd bonus to +2 while the Stag is present and tracks to vanish while it moves; a world can alter the bonus or tracking medium, with presence and stopping as limits.

rules.statement: A cat’s Greater or Lesser power has a listed character-creation cost in spell levels and a Penetration Score equal to its Might plus its Penetration Bonus. The Might-point cost shown is for a Lesser power; a Greater version costs half as much, rounded up.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Cats’ Greater or Lesser Magical Powers (ars-magica-realms#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Use the listed cost and penetration formula by default; a world can change the power tier or penetration bonus, with greater effects requiring a larger share of the creature’s power.

rules.statement: A Lesser cat power’s Initiative Bonus is Quickness minus twice its Magnitude; for a Greater power, subtract half the Magnitude instead.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Cats’ Greater or Lesser Magical Powers (ars-magica-realms#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Apply the tier-specific initiative formula by default; a world can alter the tier, trading stronger effects against slower activation.

rules.statement: A cat chooses one magical power for each purchase of Greater or Lesser Magical Power, and either quality can be bought more than once. The personal powers use an Initiative bonus of Quickness minus half their Magnitude.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Magical Powers / Personal Magical Powers for Cats (ars-magica-realms#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Grant one power per quality purchase by default; a world can cap repeated purchases, limiting how many distinct powers a cat can acquire.

rules.statement: A Bird of Nephelococcygia can command up to 100 birds for Sun duration; they follow understandable, non-suicidal orders, and the effect must penetrate any target bird’s Magic Resistance. Without further orders, birds summoned by Call the Flock disperse over the following few hours.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Powers of the Birds of Nephelococcygia (ars-magica-realms#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Allow commands to bind a group for the stated duration by default; a world can reduce group size or duration, limiting control over living creatures.

rules.statement: Call the Flock brings 10 mundane birds per round for the next Diameter when used in open air. They gather around the caller and attack obstructing characters, but the power itself does not let the caller command them.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Powers of the Birds of Nephelococcygia (ars-magica-realms#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Use the stated arrival rate and duration by default; a world can reduce the flock or make arrival depend on local bird availability.

rules.statement: The Crow’s Song adds 5 to the target’s next Aging Roll when the target next sleeps, even if the target is normally too young to roll; it must penetrate Magic Resistance. A cat’s shared warding ritual adds cats’ Penetration Scores, with the highest-level effect applying, but too many participants make a fatal botch more likely.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Powers of the Birds of Nephelococcygia / Warder’s Walk (ars-magica-realms#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Use the stated aging penalty and cooperative warding by default; a world can increase the penalty or participation risk, making the effect more dangerous.

rules.statement: The Nephelococcygia regio entrance moves with the wind. After finding it, a character who succeeds at Intelligence + Magic Lore against Ease Factor 9 can predict its path for the next season; entry requires flight or a flying carrier, and is normally guided by a bird that knows the way.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Birds of Nephelococcygia (ars-magica-realms#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Make the entrance mobile and require flight and guidance by default; a world can make its route harder to predict, increasing the cost of reaching the regio.

rules.statement: The city’s constant birdcalls impose a –3 penalty on Concentration rolls. In winter, all resident birds must attend the Assembly or be ostracised; preparing and studying songs occupies a full season.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Birds of Nephelococcygia (ars-magica-realms#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Apply the noise penalty and seasonal obligation by default; a world can intensify the penalty or social consequence, making the city harder to work in and resist.

rules.statement: A dragon can constrict only a victim smaller than itself. While maintaining the grapple, it deprives the victim of air, who must make a Stamina check every 30 seconds (five rounds) or suffer the usual effects of deprivation.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Option: Constriction Attacks (ars-magica-realms#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to allowing constriction only against smaller targets and checking every five rounds; a world can shorten or lengthen that interval to make the slow suffocation more or less dangerous.

rules.statement: After successfully grappling and beginning constriction, a dragon can keep constricting while attacking with claws or bite on later rounds; it may target the grappled victim or someone else.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Option: Constriction Attacks (ars-magica-realms#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to permitting one constriction and a separate claw or bite attack in subsequent rounds; a world can limit those additional attacks to make holding a victim more demanding.

rules.statement: Arkliss can spend 1 point to surprise a person with eye contact and impose one understood verbal command lasting a Moon; the target carries it out as best they can.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Arkliss, a Dragon of the Fens — Powers: Domination (ars-magica-realms#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one command that lasts a Moon and requires surprise, eye contact, and comprehension; a world can alter duration or remove the surprise requirement, changing how readily the power controls people.

rules.statement: Arkliss can spend 1 point to exhale a mist reaching everyone within five paces; each exposed victim must beat Ease Factor 9 with a Stamina roll or suffer a Medium wound from disease.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Arkliss, a Dragon of the Fens — Powers: Pestilential Breath (ars-magica-realms#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a five-pace group effect, with a Stamina check against 9 and a Medium wound on failure; a world can change the reach or severity to tune the danger of the breath.

rules.statement: Polymathes can alter the appearance of an object he touches with an Imaginem effect of up to fifth magnitude, paying 1 Might point per magnitude.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Polymathes, the Draconic Librarian — Powers: Master of Illusion (ars-magica-realms#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to touch range, a fifth-magnitude ceiling, and a cost of one point per magnitude; a world can raise the ceiling or lower the cost, making substantial illusions easier to produce.

rules.statement: Polymathes's blood remains poisonous for nine days after it is spilled. If a character wounds him and later botches in the battle, blood has reached the character's skin, who must succeed at a Stamina roll of 12 or die immediately.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Polymathes, the Draconic Librarian — Powers: Poisonous Blood (ars-magica-realms#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to nine-day potency and a Stamina target of 12 for instant death after the specified botch; a world can shorten the potency or replace death with a lesser consequence.

rules.statement: Animals gain Warping as people do: at score 1 they gain a Minor Flaw, at 3 another Minor Flaw, and at 5 a Minor Virtue; further increases give Major Flaws. At score 5, an animal stops gaining Warping merely from continued exposure to the same kind of aura.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Transformed Animals — Warping (ars-magica-realms#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the stated thresholds and to ending repeat-aura accumulation at score 5; a world can change the thresholds or remove that stopping point to make magical exposure transform animals faster or more persistently.

rules.statement: Activating a cage of change gives a captive animal of up to Size +1 five Warping points. This normally brings a previously unwarped animal to score 1 and a Minor Flaw, but the particular Flaw is not guaranteed; a magus caught by a version with Penetration may instead enter Wizard's Twilight.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Intentionally Warping an Animal — Cage of Change (ars-magica-realms#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a once-daily touch effect that grants five Warping points, with uncertain resulting Flaw; a world can adjust the points or make the result more predictable, at the cost of making the device less hazardous or less reliable.

rules.statement: A three-point Size difference represents about a tenfold mass difference. As an optional combat rule, a giant gains a defensive bonus equal to twice its Size difference from a smaller opponent against scuffling, grappling, and disarming, but not ordinary melee or missile attacks.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Giants in Combat (ars-magica-realms#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the doubled Size-gap defense for close-contact maneuvers; a world can instead make such attempts automatically ineffective, reflecting the giant's mass advantage.

rules.statement: A giant of Size +4 or more must bend over double to reach a Size 0 human with its hands, so it will usually kick or use a weapon instead.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Giants in Combat (ars-magica-realms#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to requiring a kick or weapon at this size gap; a world can allow hand attacks when circumstances permit, at the cost of awkward reach.

rules.statement: Giants have the Gigantic Quality, which increases Strength and reduces Quickness; apply those changes after purchasing Characteristics. Giants above Size +2 should take the Quality more than once, and need enough Might to support the resulting Qualities.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Might and Qualities (ars-magica-realms#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to applying Gigantic after Characteristics are set; a world can permit exceptions to size and Might requirements, at the cost of less consistent creature balance.

rules.statement: Corpus spells generally use a base Individual that covers a person of Size +1 or less, so most such spells are not designed to affect giants larger than that.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Giants in Combat (ars-magica-realms#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the stated Corpus target limit; a world can extend spells to larger bodies, at the cost of needing a suitable higher-scale effect.

rules.statement: A spirit pact lets its servant spend a Confidence Point and roll Presence + Magic Lore + a stress die to acquire a Might Pool. The amount is always below the spirit's current Might points; a botch removes all the servant's Confidence points.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: New Virtue: Spiritual Pact (ars-magica-realms#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the roll-based pool with Confidence as its price; a world can make the gift more predictable, at the cost of weakening the pact's uncertainty and risk.

rules.statement: A pact servant spends the acquired pool on the spirit's powers but gains no Might score, Magic Resistance, or vis on death. The pool does not replenish; using the last point ends the power and all effects whose durations remain active, while invoking the pact again replaces any points still held.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: New Virtue: Spiritual Pact (ars-magica-realms#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a non-replenishing, replace-not-add pool whose exhaustion ends ongoing effects; a world can allow residual effects to persist, at the cost of weakening the pact's finite-resource limit.

rules.statement: A Flame Dancer can spend 1 point to feel unwounded and free of fatigue until sunrise or sunset. The benefit lasts only until that boundary.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Endurance of the Flame Dancer (ars-magica-realms#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to suppressing wound and fatigue sensations until the next sunrise or sunset; a world can let actual harm accumulate normally, at the cost of the power's protective effect being temporary.

rules.statement: A Flame Dancer can spend 0 points to set a slightly inflammable target on fire, up to the size of a house; the power has a listed +20 Penetration.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Let the Bonfire Burn (ars-magica-realms#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to igniting only slightly inflammable targets within the stated size limit; a world can broaden the eligible materials, at the cost of making fire powers more potent.

rules.statement: A Loamwalker can move instantly from one visible tree to another within 50 paces. Another listed power changes the user into a tree until sunset.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Loamwalker Stats: From Hill to Hollow; Stance of the Patient Tree (ars-magica-realms#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to limiting tree-to-tree movement to visible trees within 50 paces and tree form to sunset; a world can extend the range or duration, at the cost of loosening those boundaries.

rules.statement: Simulacrum Form lets its user continuously reshape into a watery imitation of a touched target, but contact must be maintained for one round. The imitation stays visibly watery, gains no target abilities, keeps the user’s characteristics, and must be within one Size category of the user.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Men of the Lake — Simulacrum Form (ars-magica-realms#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a one-round, touch-dependent cosmetic transformation; a world could broaden eligible forms, at the cost of making disguise more effective.

rules.statement: Memory of Water reveals a mental image of a touched volume’s past for as long as the user concentrates. A memory no more than a Diameter old costs 2 Might Points, Sun old 3, Moon old 4, or Year old 5; older memories cannot be reached.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Men of the Lake — Memory of Water (ars-magica-realms#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to limited, increasingly costly historical impressions; a world could extend the time window, at the cost of greater power expenditure.

rules.statement: Seal the Wounds of Impetuous Youth permanently heals one Light wound and costs 3 points to use.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Lost Children — Seal the Wounds of Impetuous Youth (ars-magica-realms#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one permanently healed Light wound per use; a world could allow more serious healing, at the cost of more points or stricter limits.

rules.statement: A character using Sail the Wind concentrates to create winds that lift and carry them through the air. Multiple users can lift and steer a small boat, or a ship if at least three cooperate.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: People of the Clouds — Sail the Wind (ars-magica-realms#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to personal flight, with craft requiring cooperation; a world could allow a single user to lift a ship, at the cost of exceptional power.

rules.statement: A revenant is immune to fatigue and pain, can ignore injuries fatal to a living person, and cannot be incapacitated by ordinary wounds: such wounds count as Heavy. Destroying its body does not destroy its animating spirit, which normally cannot return to that corpse or possess another without a specific ability.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Revenants, the Walking Dead — Fighting the Walking Dead (ars-magica-realms#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.mechanism: law: corpse and spirit are separate
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a resilient corpse whose spirit survives bodily destruction but cannot re-enter without a special power; a world could make bodily destruction final, at the cost of the revenant’s supernatural persistence.

rules.statement: A person seeking transformation through drowning must contact a magical water entity with Might greater than 35, negotiate its aid and any required task or sacrifice, then surrender to the water without protective magic. If rescued, the person becomes a transformed magical being; the bargain may allow the task to be completed afterward.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Drowned Men — Planning for Drowning (ars-magica-realms#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to transformation only after a negotiated bargain and genuine surrender to drowning; a world could waive the bargain, at the cost of removing the entity’s leverage and the character’s obligation.

rules.statement: A spirit cannot affect matter without a supernatural power, and a material being cannot sense or interact with one without magical assistance. Spirits ignore physical damage and deprivation, pass through air and solid objects, and do not age or contract disease.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Spirits as Characters (ars-magica-realms#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to mutual inaccessibility between spirits and the material world unless powers intervene; a world could make spirits routinely tangible, at the cost of their protection from physical hazards.

rules.statement: At the storyguide’s discretion, a magus entering Final Twilight may become a magical creature or spirit with Might generally around 20–40, or set by five times a relevant Ability or by a relevant Art score. The transformed magus loses the ability to use Hermetic magic.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Magi in Final Twilight (ars-magica-realms#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a 20–40 Might transformation that ends Hermetic spellcasting; a world could preserve spellcasting, at the cost of weakening the transformation’s defining tradeoff.

rules.statement: A spirit usually has 1–5 supernatural powers. An effect that targets another being must penetrate that being’s Magic Resistance; a power comparable to a Ritual spell permanently reduces both the spirit’s Might score and Might pool, and the score can be restored only by the method given in Chapter 4.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Spirits, introductory paragraph (ars-magica-realms#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Require penetration for effects on protected beings and charge permanent Might for Ritual-scale effects; a world can ease either limit, but spirits otherwise expend lasting power to force major changes.

rules.statement: A spirit’s immaterial body usually holds 1 pawn of appropriate vis per Might magnitude, but a spirit below Might 5 has too little for even 1 pawn. Destroying Might reduces the vis proportionally; destroying all Might leaves none. A slain corporeal body contains material vis, while Presence can yield (Might/10) pawns each year without harming the spirit.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Spirits as a Source of Vis (ars-magica-realms#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Treat vis as conserved in the spirit unless its Might is destroyed; a world can make immaterial vis easier to harvest, at the cost of weakening the link between spirit and resource.

rules.statement: A spirit controlling a human can issue commands, but the target may try to break control whenever a request is complex, dangerous, or against their nature. The target rolls Intelligence against 9 + the spirit’s Might magnitude, modified by the most applicable Personality Trait; each failure gives +1 cumulatively to the next attempt.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Control Human (ars-magica-realms#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Allow resistance checks at each significant test of control, with growing odds of escape; a world can make control harder or more absolute, trading dramatic agency for stronger domination.

rules.statement: Donning the Corporeal Veil makes a spirit one physical body, with its own physical statistics and maximum Size +1; each further 3 points of Size requires another magnitude and another power quality. The body lasts until slain or dissolved, suffers aging, disease, and deprivation but not fatigue, and its death destroys the spirit or Aspect.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Donning the Corporeal Veil (ars-magica-realms#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Give spirits one vulnerable, maintainable body at a time; a world can permit larger or safer forms, but the standard body exposes the spirit to ordinary bodily hazards.

rules.statement: Ghost Touch moves unattended, unsecured objects: 1 Might point moves up to 5 pounds, and each additional point doubles that limit. A hurled object deals +5 damage per point spent; the spirit needs Thrown Weapons to hurl it, and the effect lasts until it releases the object.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Ghost Touch (ars-magica-realms#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Scale lifting capacity exponentially with Might spent and keep control only while held; a world can raise the damage or weight, but doing so consumes the spirit’s reserve.

rules.statement: Manifestation gives touched plants or animals a Might score equal to the points spent and controls them; it costs 4 points for a pace-wide plant or 5 for a Size +1 animal. An extra 2 points controls ten standard targets, each further 2 multiplies the controlled mass by ten, and spending cannot exceed the spirit’s Might magnitude; it cannot control humans or other sentient beings.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Manifestation (ars-magica-realms#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Limit control by target scale and the spirit’s Might magnitude, while excluding sentient beings; a world can permit broader targets, but control then risks overriding meaningful agency.

rules.statement: Material Anchor creates an Arcane Connection between a spirit and a person or place, or makes an object an Arcane Connection to the spirit. It costs 1 point for hours or days, 2 for weeks or months, 3 for years or decades, and 4 for an indefinite connection; the spirit must be at the object and penetrate Magic Resistance as usual.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Material Anchor (ars-magica-realms#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Let duration determine the Might cost and require physical presence at the object; a world can make anchors cheaper or longer-lived, but persistent links grant lasting access to the spirit.

rules.statement: Presence makes a spirit aware of everything in its chosen domain and doubles its Might for Tether Strength. Its area is a Room at Might 5–10, a Structure at 15–25, or a standard Boundary at 30+; Daimons gain one size modifier per 5 Might above 30, while Airy Spirits and anima remain limited to a standard Boundary. The domain yields (Might/10) pawns of appropriate vis each year without eroding the spirit’s Might.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Presence (ars-magica-realms#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Tie perception and renewable vis to a bounded domain and Might; a world can expand domain size, but doing so grants the spirit broader awareness and resource production.

rules.statement: Summoning, perceiving, or controlling a spirit must overcome its Magic Might. A Hermetic summoning of an Airy Spirit requires an Arcane Connection; summoning itself uses Momentary duration.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: New Spirit Spells and Spell Guidelines; Spirits and Hermetic Magic (ars-magica-realms#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to requiring both a connection and penetration past Might; a world can ease either limit when spirits are familiar or accessible, at the cost of weaker safeguards against summoning them.

rules.statement: A non-theurgist Hermetic magus needs a known laboratory text or teacher to summon a specific Daimon's Aspect, and the ritual's base level must be at least twice the Daimon's Might. A theurgist may invent the spell without that source and can repeat a lower-level ritual to succeed through persistence.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Spirits and Hermetic Magic (ars-magica-realms#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the higher level and prior instruction requirements; a world can allow repeated weaker attempts for specialists, trading time and persistence for lower initial power.

rules.statement: A worldly representation of an Airy Spirit, a genius loci's physical location, or an Airy Spirit's name can serve as an Arcane Connection; the name lasts indefinitely. A Daimon's name does not suffice, and Daimons rarely produce such connections except through powers such as Material Anchor.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Arcane Connections, True Names, and Synthemata (ars-magica-realms#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to allowing connections only through listed representations and names; a world can make Daimons easier to reach, at the cost of weakening their resistance to magical targeting.

rules.statement: A True Name is an indefinite-duration Arcane Connection and a learnable spelllike ability that costs 5 experience points; learning it also grants 1 experience point in the relevant Realm Lore. Synthemata are required for theurgy but grant no power by themselves, and knowing a being's True Name adds 5 to lab totals for researching its synthemata.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Arcane Connections, True Names, and Synthemata (ars-magica-realms#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to making True Names costly but reliable connections; a world can make them cheaper or less durable, shifting the cost between research effort and access to the target.

rules.statement: Goetic Summoning can be aligned with Magic, Faerie, or Infernal spirits; Ablating, Binding, and Commanding are Infernal-aligned and taint work using them. They respectively call spirits, steal their power, force them into objects or beings, and demand obedience.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Spirits and Non-Hermetic Magic (ars-magica-realms#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to giving each art its stated function and taint; a world can reduce the taint or broaden the alignments, at the cost of weakening the arts' defining danger or restriction.

rules.statement: A magical ghost remains tied to the world by an overwhelming emotion or unresolved personal need; resolving that connection makes the ghost pass away permanently. Apparitions usually retain their life memories, shades have emotion-dominated thought and incomplete memories, and spectres repeat an occupation or role.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Ghosts (ars-magica-realms#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to making unresolved ties sustain a ghost and their resolution release it; a world can allow ghosts to persist after resolution, at the cost of removing a clear means to lay them to rest.

rules.statement: Adranus can save 15 Might points by remaining inactive for a year, spending no other Might during that time; those points are added to his pool for the first year after awakening, allowing the pool to exceed his permanent Might of 50.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Adranus, the Spirit of Mount Etna (ars-magica-realms#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to allowing only this stated one-year accumulation; a world can change the storage period or cap, balancing a more powerful awakening against prolonged inactivity.

rules.statement: The Rhine spirit can sense along the river's full length but can exercise its full power only at the waterfall where it is pinned. It longs to be released from that location-bound restriction.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: The Rhinefalls (ars-magica-realms#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to restricting full effects to the waterfall while preserving remote sensing; a world can widen the spirit's active domain, at the cost of loosening its confinement.

rules.statement: Special vis loses its exceptional effect if moved into a different physical form. Lesser-enchantment vis normally remains available for ordinary magical use and its special effect does not consume it, but spell-like vis is depleted when its effect finishes.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Extraordinary Vis; Lesser Enchantment Vis; Spell-like Vis (ars-magica-realms#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.mechanism: law: native form preserves vis effects
rules.default_dial_reason: Preserve a special vis power only in its native form; a world can relax transfer loss, but doing so makes rare magic easier to transport and trade.

rules.statement: A single dedicated-vis pawn counts as two for an applicable Technique-and-Form combination: it gives a +4 vis boost per pawn when powering a matching spell, counts double for matching ritual or enchantment use, and counts double in botch rolls. It cannot be separated into ordinary pawns, and changing its form destroys the bonus.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Dedicated Vis — Spell Use (ars-magica-realms#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Apply the doubled benefit only to the vis's fixed Arts; a world can broaden the matching combinations, with the cost of making specialized vis more versatile.

rules.statement: When dedicated vis is studied, each pawn counts as two toward the minimum needed for the relevant Art total, but the Source Quality is a stress die plus aura bonus divided by 2. A double botch causes Wizard's Twilight, with botch dice equal to twice the pawns studied; mixing normal and dedicated vis requires at least one dedicated pawn per normal pawn and halves the resulting Source Quality.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Dedicated Vis — Study (ars-magica-realms#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Treat dedicated vis as a two-Art study resource at half Source Quality; a world can remove the divided quality, at the cost of faster advancement.

rules.statement: Storing a large amount of vis of one Art may cause spontaneous nearby effects within Voice range. The minimum might be 10–20 pawns in a low-vis saga or 100 in a high-vis saga; reaching the minimum yields first-magnitude effects, and each further multiple adds a magnitude.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Vis Storage (ars-magica-realms#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Let concentrated vis generate Art-appropriate effects once a saga-specific threshold is reached; a world can raise that threshold, reducing the hazards of storing valuable resources.

rules.statement: Enrichment takes a season of uninterrupted magical work and requires an Enrichment Total of at least 9, calculated from Intelligence, Magic Lore, and aura. It uses the object's vis so that the vis can no longer be extracted or used normally; a carrier gains its granted Virtue only while the object is intact and the carrier has no Magic Resistance.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Enriching a Thing of Virtue (ars-magica-realms#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Require a season and threshold 9 to turn eligible vis-bearing things into wearable Virtues; a world can lower the threshold, at the cost of making rare abilities commonplace.

rules.statement: An enriched Herb usually fades after one year per pawn of its original vis, while other enriched Things generally persist unless damaged. A Major Virtue also brings a Minor Flaw, some Minor Virtues bring a Flaw, and the bearer receives Warping from a constant low-power effect.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Enriching a Thing of Virtue (ars-magica-realms#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Make the benefit conditional on a durable, intact object and pair stronger gifts with drawbacks and Warping; a world can remove those costs, weakening the setting's risk around magical gifts.

rules.statement: An enriched Opal of Virtue grants Sure Traveler but also imposes a minor Personality Flaw selected by the storyguide; the gem contains 2 pawns of Terram vis before enrichment.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Opal of Virtue (ars-magica-realms#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to granting travel competence with a storyguide-chosen social irritation; a world can change the flaw’s severity to reflect the item’s cost.

rules.statement: An enriched Clam Shell grants Tough only while its owner wears or carries it; before enrichment it contains 1 pawn of Terram vis.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Clam Shell (ars-magica-realms#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a carried item supplying its virtue; a world can make the benefit contingent on wearing it or merely keeping it nearby.

rules.statement: An enriched Emerald grants Animal Ken for serpents only; it contains 2 pawns of Animal vis before enrichment.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Emerald (ars-magica-realms#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a bounded animal-sense gift limited to snakes; a world can broaden the eligible creatures at the cost of a weaker gift or harder enrichment.

rules.statement: An enriched Jet grants Puissant Stealth, but loses that benefit if anyone other than its owner sees the stone; before enrichment it contains 1 pawn of Perdo vis.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Jet (ars-magica-realms#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to stealth aid that depends on the gem staying unseen; a world can relax the secrecy condition by making the virtue weaker or temporary.

rules.statement: A Clach Crubain carried close to the body grants Lesser Immunity to arthritis when enriched; it holds 1 pawn of Perdo vis beforehand.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Formed Stones — Clach Crubain (ars-magica-realms#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to immunity while the stone is carried; a world can widen the protected condition at the cost of a more demanding enrichment.

rules.statement: An enriched Thunderbolt held in the hand wards away air demons with Might 10 or less; its Auram power is continuous and the stone contains 1 pawn of Auram vis beforehand.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Formed Stones — Thunderbolt (ars-magica-realms#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a hand-held ward with a Might ceiling of 10; a world can raise the ceiling by increasing the power’s cost or limiting its duration.

rules.statement: An enriched Glossopetrae can neutralize liquid poison after being placed in the suspected liquid for at least two Diameters; the victim takes a Fatigue loss instead of a wound. It has 1 pawn of Aquam vis before enrichment.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Formed Stones — Glossopetrae (ars-magica-realms#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to poison mitigation after a waiting period, converting injury to fatigue loss; a world can shorten the wait by making the remedy less effective.

rules.statement: Awakened trees in a Magic aura become more alert and active as the aura strengthens; at level 6 or higher they see and hear roughly as well as humans. They grow lethargic as the aura weakens.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Awakened Trees (ars-magica-realms#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to aura strength setting tree awareness and activity; a world can alter the threshold, with stronger activity drawing more attention to the forest.

rules.statement: A spell-animated tree normally has no Might, while one animated through Manifestation temporarily gains Might equal to that power’s activation cost. Trees can uproot and shuffle only if the effect allows it.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Awakened Trees — Animated Trees (ars-magica-realms#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to animation without Might unless a spirit inhabits the tree; a world can grant additional mobility or resilience through a stronger animating effect.

rules.statement: Enriching a Tree of Virtue or harvesting its vis depletes its inherent magical properties; it may recover over time only if the storyguide determines that it is renewable.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Trees of Virtue (ars-magica-realms#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a harvest that consumes the tree’s magic unless it is explicitly renewable; a world can allow regrowth by making recovery slow or uncertain.

rules.statement: Each of the 13 enriched Blackthorn thorns can curse a target once, using a wax likeness and an Arcane Connection; both restrictions limit the power.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Trees of Virtue — Blackthorn (ars-magica-realms#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a one-use curse requiring a sympathetic link and a likeness; a world can remove one restriction by reducing the number of thorns or the curse’s strength.

rules.statement: A Rowan amulet wards its bearer against creatures of one chosen supernatural Realm, with a Level 10 effect and Penetration 10; it expires after seven years. The maker chooses Magic, Infernal, or Faerie, but not Divine.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Trees of Virtue — Rowan (ars-magica-realms#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one bearer and one selected Realm for seven years; a world can extend the term or protection scope by raising the enrichment cost.

rules.statement: An enriched mandrake root moves at one foot per minute and its motions can provide Premonitions 3, but it must be fed blood to use the divinatory ability.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Character Guide: A Mandrake Root of Virtue (ars-magica-realms#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to slow movement and blood-fed omen reading; a world can improve its speed or foresight by demanding more frequent or costly feeding.

rules.statement: Elementals form through rarefication of raw elemental matter; ordinarily one forms, with maximum size limited by available matter. Once formed, they do not age, need food, or succumb to disease, and persist until destroyed.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Elementals (ars-magica-realms#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one durable elemental whose size depends on raw matter; a world can make formation more likely or rarer by changing the magical conditions.

rules.statement: Elemental combat reduces the Might Pool as well as inflicting the equivalent wound penalty in Might loss; an incapacitating wound removes 5 Might points, while the Might score and Size remain unchanged.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Elemental Combat (ars-magica-realms#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to damage draining expendable Might without changing size; a world can make wounds more costly by increasing the pool loss.

rules.statement: When an elemental's Might pool reaches 0, it becomes inanimate and cannot move; after it regenerates 1 Might point it can move again. Because elementals have a temporary Might-recovery drawback, suitable vis may be needed to revive one that has lain dormant for years.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Elemental discussion, before Elemental Powers (ars-magica-realms#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: zero Might makes an elemental dormant until it recovers 1 point; a world can change the recovery delay or required vis, reflecting how hard it is to restore its animating force.

rules.statement: Matter broken off an elemental in physical combat contains vis that can be collected and spent to power spells, even before the elemental is destroyed. The elemental may reabsorb that matter to replenish its Might; if its matter is destroyed, including by certain magic or an opposing element, its vis is destroyed too.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Elemental discussion, before Elemental Powers (ars-magica-realms#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: detached matter is recoverable vis, but the elemental may reclaim it; a world can adjust how easily it is collected or destroyed, with the elemental's regeneration at stake.

rules.statement: Every elemental has one power based on its bodily element and one describing its natural attack. Magic Resistance can stop the elemental from touching its opponent, but these attacks cost no Might points; most elementals also have at least one additional, type-related power.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Elemental Powers (ars-magica-realms#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the elemental's basic attack is free but contact can be resisted; a world can make attacks consume Might, trading repeated use for finite reserves.

rules.statement: An elemental's Size depends on its chosen Might rather than being bought with Magical Qualities or Inferiorities; its typical Characteristics also follow its Might. The table gives examples from Might 1 (Size –18) through Might 50 (Size +21), with the listed Characteristics at each step.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Size, Might, and Characteristics of Elementals (ars-magica-realms#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: Might sets the elemental's typical Size and Characteristics; a world can use a different progression, changing how much physical scale a given reserve represents.

rules.statement: Mundane beasts use Cunning for rolls that would otherwise use Intelligence. They cannot learn new Abilities unless trained by an intelligent being, though they may improve Abilities already found in their species.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Beast Statistics (ars-magica-realms#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: beasts have limited problem-solving and cannot independently learn new Abilities; a world can permit broader learning, at the cost of reducing the distinction between animal and human minds.

rules.statement: For each point of Size added to a beast, increase Strength by 2 and reduce Quickness by 1; for each point removed, reduce Strength by 2 and increase Quickness by 1. Recalculate combat statistics after changing those Characteristics.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Modifying Beast Sizes (ars-magica-realms#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: changing Size exchanges agility for Strength at a 2-to-1 Strength rate; a world can use another exchange rate to make large animals less or more cumbersome.

rules.statement: A beast with Ferocity receives 3 Confidence points, usable only in a described circumstance that triggers its natural ferocity, such as defending its den or fighting a natural enemy.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: New Virtues for Beasts: Ferocity (ars-magica-realms#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: three Confidence points are limited to the beast's stated trigger; a world can widen or narrow that trigger, changing how reliably instinct can fuel decisive action.

rules.statement: A beast can make only one weapon attack in a round, even if it has several natural weapons; its best weapon is listed first and other weapons may be used when appropriate. Beasts without cooperative fighting instincts use the untrained group rules.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Beasts in Combat (ars-magica-realms#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: one attack per round prevents stacking natural weapons; a world can allow multiple attacks, increasing damage potential at the cost of greater combat danger.

rules.statement: A faerie must obey the rules of its role; if it stops fulfilling that role, it fades away or withdraws to Arcadia until it returns in another form. Participating in stories lets faeries draw vitality from human participants, even when the faerie is only incidental to the events.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Chapter One: Nature of Faerie — Glamour: Rules Instead of a Soul (ars-magica-realms#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to enforcing each faerie’s role rules and granting vitality from story participation; a world can loosen either rule, at the cost of weakening the story-based logic that sustains faeries.

rules.statement: Faeries need human vitality to feel, grow, learn, and age, and they seek it instinctively. Their awareness of how they obtain it varies: some do not understand the source, some understand only one way to harvest it, and highly cognizant faeries can use human interactions to change roles and develop powers.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Chapter One: Nature of Faerie — Cognizance: Understanding the Need for Humans (ars-magica-realms#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to requiring vitality for faerie activity and change; a world can make particular faeries less dependent or more aware, with reduced access to human vitality as the balancing cost.

rules.statement: A faerie’s body is assembled from nearby matter with symbolic ties to its role and held together by glamour drawn from a spiritual anchor. If the body is catastrophically disrupted before the glamour can be recovered, the anchor may remain as vis; some well-maintained anchors also help the faerie rebuild more quickly.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Chapter One: Nature of Faerie — Bodies: Incidental Matter (ars-magica-realms#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to requiring a symbolic anchor for a faerie’s body and allowing catastrophic disruption to strand its glamour; a world can make anchors safer or faster to use, at the cost of making them more accessible targets.

rules.statement: A faerie’s response to bodily damage depends on its cognizance: an incognizant faerie feels pain, a narrowly cognizant one must act as if it does, and a highly cognizant one feels pain only if it chooses. Incognizant faeries that form replacement bodies do not remember earlier incarnations, while narrowly cognizant faeries retain their memories.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Chapter One: Nature of Faerie — Cognizance: Understanding the Need for Humans; Bodies: Incidental Matter (ars-magica-realms#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to tying pain and memory persistence to cognizance; a world can make recovery more consistent across faerie types, at the cost of erasing this distinction in how they experience bodies.

rules.statement: Glamour-generated possessions remain with a faerie unless it permits a transfer or a story changes ownership. If a faerie withdraws its glamour from an unwillingly taken item, the item becomes incidental matter and any vis in it vanishes; generated possessions are Arcane Connections to the faerie until its role changes.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Chapter One: Nature of Faerie — Ownership (ars-magica-realms#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to making faerie-made goods dependent on the maker’s glamour and consent; a world can allow ordinary theft to work, at the cost of removing the story and connection-based limits on ownership.

rules.statement: Dogs commanded as a trained group use their human Master of the Pack’s Animal Handling score, rather than Leadership, to determine how many dogs can be commanded. A wolf pack can fight as a trained group when its leader is present.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Hound (Canis); Wolf (Lupus) (ars-magica-realms#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to requiring a present leader and using Animal Handling for a human-led dog group; a world can permit larger or leaderless formations, at the cost of reducing the importance of training and command.

rules.statement: Dogs receive +3 on endurance-related rolls from the Long-Winded Virtue, and all dogs receive +3 on rolls related to smell; the bloodhound’s especially keen smell also grants +3 on related rolls. Deer receive +3 on running- or jumping-related rolls, and lions receive +3 on jumping-related rolls.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Hound (Canis); Lion (Leo); Stag (Cervus) (ars-magica-realms#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to applying the listed +3 bonuses only to their specified activities; a world can broaden or narrow the covered rolls, at the cost of changing the animals’ specialized advantages.

rules.statement: When a stag sheds its antlers in spring, it must fight with its hooves until its antlers return in autumn. The autumn and winter antlers have weapon statistics of Init +2, Attack +3, Defense +2, Damage +3; its spring hooves have Init +2, Attack +2, Defense +2, Damage +1.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Stag (Cervus) — Natural Weapons (ars-magica-realms#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to seasonal changes in a stag’s available natural weapon; a world can make antlers available year-round, at the cost of removing the seasonal combat limitation.

rules.statement: Faeries can imitate human Abilities with Pretenses without spending Might or maintaining Concentration. They use the ordinary Ability rules, but improve their Pretense scores by copying better human examples rather than learning through experience.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Pretenses (ars-magica-realms#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to effortless imitation with no Might or Concentration cost; a setting could require effort or expenditure to limit it, because glamour is the source of the imitation.

rules.statement: A character with an Ability score of at least 6 may recognize a faerie's subtle magical imitation by succeeding at Perception + Awareness against 12 minus the Ability score being mimicked. Deliberately using a Pretense to do something impossible for a human is immediately noticed by anyone who has mastered that Ability.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Pretenses (ars-magica-realms#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the stated threshold and automatic detection of impossible feats; a world could make detection harder or easier, reflecting how familiar people are with glamour.

rules.statement: Speaking with a faerie creates an Arcane Connection to it with a Penetration multiplier of 2, lasting until the conversation ends. Eating its food makes the human its guest and servant, prevents departure without permission, and creates a multiplier-2 connection to the glamour carried inside until permission to leave is granted.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: The Open Body is Vulnerable to Glamour (ars-magica-realms#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to speech and shared food creating binding links with the stated durations; a world could weaken or strengthen the obligations, with hospitality and faerie custom determining the cost.

rules.statement: A faerie that claims territory with Extend Glamour creates an aura equal to its Might divided by 5. If two powerful faeries contest an area, their combined glamour instead gives an aura of 2 plus the higher Might divided by 5, capped at 9; only the claimant or contenders contribute, not their retainers.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Faerie Presence (ars-magica-realms#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to Might-based aura strength and the stated contest formula; a world could alter the cap or contribution rules, reflecting how fiercely faeries compete for territory.

rules.statement: If a magus extracts vis from a faerie aura and the faerie cannot stop it, the aura falls by 1 around the extraction site, usually within 300 paces, and further extractions can drive the faerie out. The faerie can restore control by taking something it considers equally valuable, or can agree beforehand to an exchange that avoids damaging the aura.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Auras Rise and Fall (ars-magica-realms#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a one-point local aura loss per unopposed extraction and negotiated symbolic repayment; a world could vary the affected area or price, depending on the faerie's sense of value.

rules.statement: A faerie entering an area ruled by another Realm must keep its glamour within its body unless it has gained admittance by a recognized right, invitation, behavioral code, payment, or contest. Without permission it cannot use powers at ranges beyond Touch, except against targets to which it has Arcane Connections.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Aura Conflicts (ars-magica-realms#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the range restriction until a stated admission condition is met; a world could demand stricter or cheaper entry terms, with local custom and rival powers setting the price.

rules.statement: A character with Faerie Sight, Second Sight, or Magic Sensitivity can try to read the action that opens the next regio level with Perception + Awareness against an Ease Factor of 5 plus twice the difference between the current aura and the next level. A character who knows the symbolic action can perform it; a Faerie Lore guess instead uses Intelligence + Faerie Lore against 15, reduced when the story narrows the options.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Finding a Regio Entrance (ars-magica-realms#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the stated aura-based discovery difficulty and symbolic entry action; a world could make entrances more or less apparent, reflecting whether its faeries want visitors.

rules.statement: When characters enter a faerie regio and affront its principal glamour, the principal faerie determines when their departure is appropriate to its motif; killing that faerie does not restore control over time, because a successor takes over. People who stay so long that they die of old age may persist as glamour-held bodies, which fall apart if they leave.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Time in Faerie Regiones (ars-magica-realms#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to motif-governed return times and succession of control, with bodily decay only after subjective old age; a world could make the time distortion milder or harsher, reflecting the regio's story.

rules.statement: A faerie's glamour binds it to its anchor and role. If the anchor breaks a taboo represented by a Ward Flaw, the role ends, the faerie fades from the mortal world, and the anchor becomes accrued vis.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Passage 20 — opening paragraphs (ars-magica-realms#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: taboo-breaking severs the role-anchor link; a world can vary which taboos count, with loss of the faerie's mortal presence as the cost.

rules.statement: Giving dormant vis vitality can awaken it into a faerie; the required vitality varies, and some vis may awaken spontaneously. Abstract vis instead creates only glamour-based imitations in a faerie's demesne and cannot be used for concrete tasks such as making magic items.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Sleeping Vis; Abstract Vis (ars-magica-realms#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: vitality can animate dormant glamour, while abstract vis produces only local imitations; a world can set the awakening trigger and price, from simple acts to vis or a life.

rules.statement: To enter Faerie, a traveler must accumulate Threshold points equal to (13 − aura modifier) × 3. Apply Realm interaction to the aura modifier; in a Faerie regio, add its Faerie aura modifier to any underlying Faerie aura modifier, while ignoring other underlying auras.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Getting to Faerie (ars-magica-realms#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: crossing requires meeting the aura-based point threshold; a world can adjust how strongly local realms affect it, with travel access as the consequence.

rules.statement: Only one entry attempt is allowed for a given set of circumstances. After a failed attempt, a knowing traveler must change one contributing element and wait until at least the next moonrise before trying again.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Sources of Threshold Points (ars-magica-realms#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: each unchanged situation supports one attempt; a world can loosen the retry interval, with the cost of making repeated crossings easier.

rules.statement: A faerie using Spirit Away can add Threshold points to a mortal who already has some, paying 1 Might point per added point; it cannot supply the only points. It can also send characters out of Faerie for 3 Might points per person.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: New Power: Spirit Away (ars-magica-realms#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: supernatural help adds to an existing crossing effort and costs Might; a world can change the rate or allow solo assistance, at the cost of making entry or escape easier.

rules.statement: A traveler reaches Faerie only after passing the Guardian, who presents a choice between proceeding and returning. A Guardian has Faerie Might at least equal to the group's Threshold total, but the encounter need not be resolved by combat.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: The Guardian of the Threshold (ars-magica-realms#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a guardian gates completion of the crossing and is scaled to the group's threshold; a world can make the challenge more or less permissive, with passage at stake.

rules.statement: In Faerie, a character may spend one fable point to add a bonus equal to current fable score to one roll. Raising the score costs points equal to the current score plus one; on leaving Faerie, all fable points and score disappear.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Vitality and Fable in Faerie (ars-magica-realms#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: story participation fuels temporary influence, with increasing cost to raise the score; a world can change the bonus or growth rate, at the cost of stronger story control.

rules.statement: A human in Faerie can exchange Virtues for faerie-appropriate ones in a quantity equal to fable score; Major Virtues count as three. The Faerie version applies only there, and the character's normal Virtues return outside, while the exchanges reapply on a later visit.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Becoming Faerie Through Fable (ars-magica-realms#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: accumulated fable temporarily reshapes the character's traits within Faerie; a world can vary the exchange limit and eligible traits, with altered identity as the cost.

rules.statement: A character with unspent fable points can learn from a faerie to reproduce one of its powers or Virtues as an appropriate Lesser or Greater Benediction. Teaching takes minutes to several days, and the donor often loses the ability being taught; the learner may take a Lesser or Greater Charm as the exchange Flaw.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Passage 21, before “Creativity in the Faerie Realm” (ars-magica-realms#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to transferring a faerie ability through instruction and often removing it from the teacher; a world can make instruction harder or preserve the donor’s ability, at the cost of less consequential bargains.

rules.statement: To change Faerie through a creative offer, a character spends one fable point and one Long Term Fatigue Level, and promises a service that supplies vitality. The cost applies even if the offer is rejected, but the character is not bound by the promise if the faerie did not comprehend the offer.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Crafting an Offer (ars-magica-realms#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to charging the offer’s cost whether accepted or not and enforcing a comprehended promise; a world can soften the cost or require more service, trading dramatic stakes against accessibility.

rules.statement: The offer Ease Factor depends on the threat the proposed change helps overcome, not on the size of the change: 6 for trivial, 9 for minor, 12 for serious, 15 for major, and 18 for overwhelming threats.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Crafting an Offer (ars-magica-realms#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to mapping the obstacle’s danger to the listed Ease Factor; a world can shift the scale, making bargains easier or harder according to how much vitality the story would otherwise demand.

rules.statement: Offer modifiers include +1 for minor mortal goods, +2 for creative mortal crafts, and +3 for Free Expression or especially desirable goods. Changes in Elysium take a –6 penalty, except efforts to restore a derailed Elysian story, which reduce all Ease Factors by 3.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Offer Modifiers (ars-magica-realms#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the listed bonuses and Elysium penalty, with restoration as an exception; a world can increase or reduce the influence of creativity to reflect how rigidly its stories are preserved.

rules.statement: A promise to overcome a threat through mundane action gives a –6 modifier; simple symbolic evasion gives –3; a conventional story solution gives 0; and a cunning plan with a high chance of failure gives +3. Larger promises improve the offer, but reneging has consequences.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: The Promise of Service (ars-magica-realms#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to rewarding greater service with a better offer while making the promise binding; a world can be more forgiving or exacting, changing the danger of breaking a bargain.

rules.statement: Creative changes can alter an environmental object for +3, or give the characters substantial environmental advantage for 0. Changing a faerie’s intentions or motif for a substantial advantage gives –3, while a comprehensive change gives –6; attitude changes usually last only for one transaction and concern one person.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Changes in Environment; Changes in Attitude; Changes in Symbolism (ars-magica-realms#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to pricing broader or deeper alterations more harshly and keeping attitude changes brief; a world can widen the scope or duration, at the cost of requiring greater vitality or more consequential service.

rules.statement: A Merinita initiated into Arcadian Travel can leave Faerie before the story ends and choose a destination by reaching an Arcadian Travel Total of (13 minus the destination aura modifier) × 3. An Arcane Connection reduces the Ease Factor by 6; the maga can take additional travelers equal to her Faerie Magic score.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Leaving by Using Merinita Mysteries (ars-magica-realms#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to requiring the stated total and limiting companions by Faerie Magic; a world can ease travel or increase the passenger limit, reducing the mystery’s exclusivity.

rules.statement: A completed Faerie story returns its participants to the mundane world when they pass the Guardian of the Threshold. The Guardian may change to reflect the story’s outcome, and the return is usually to the place from which they departed, unless the Mother Road takes them elsewhere.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Leaving Faerie (ars-magica-realms#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to releasing characters at story’s end through the Guardian, usually at their entry point; a world can make the destination less predictable to emphasize Faerie’s influence.

rules.statement: At departure, each Warping point taken reduces effective fable score by 1. The resulting score sets mortal-world time per Faerie day: scores 0–7+ correspond to 1 hour, 12 hours, 1 day, 3 days, 1 week, 1 month, 1 season, and 1 year; companions leaving together use the lowest effective score, and others take enough Warping to match it.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Warping and the Passage of Time (ars-magica-realms#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the score-based time dilation and allow Warping to reduce it, with groups synchronized to the slowest effective score; a world can alter the conversion or make the cost less avoidable.

rules.statement: To enter Elysium deliberately, align Threshold sources with the chosen tale; unsuitable sources subtract points rather than adding them. The character must name the hero after passing the Guardian, spend 1 Confidence point, and thereby gains 1 fable point and a fable score of 1.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: The Road of Destiny; Identification as the Hero (ars-magica-realms#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to requiring a deliberate, story-aligned Threshold and a 1-Confidence payment; a world can loosen alignment or cost, with the in-world price being weaker entry or diminished commitment to the tale.

rules.statement: When several characters identify as the hero, each spends 1 Confidence point, but only the character holding the agreed token is treated as the hero at a given time. Others can take the role by possessing the token, even in view of faeries; attentive faeries may notice and resist the switch. Assistance from companions in a single-hero journey is credited as the hero's action, but prevents him from claiming total victory for that scene.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Identification as the Hero; following Hermetic Legends (ars-magica-realms#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one active hero selected by a transferable token; a world can permit multiple simultaneous heroes, at the cost of weakening the story's focus.

rules.statement: The Elysian quest's success is measured by fable points earned while acting as hero: 0–3 is failure, 4–6 mediocre success, 7–9 accomplished success, and 10 or more unmitigated success. The reward increases with the tier, from a small clue or +1 bonus, through partial information or +2, to a substantial answer or +3; leaving Elysium returns the earned knowledge, object, or bonus-token.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: The Measure of Success (ars-magica-realms#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to these four reward bands; a world can shift thresholds or reward scale, with greater rewards requiring closer reenactment of the tale.

rules.statement: Elysian story events must ultimately resolve in a way that restores the underlying legend, even if the characters' actions derail it; correcting the tale can earn fable points. A reenactment creates a variant but does not replace the established legend, and conflicting tellings may each be true in Elysium.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Running Elysian Stories; The Measure of Success (ars-magica-realms#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the original tale exerting narrative pressure; a world can let variants supplant it, at the cost of the old tale's accumulated potency.

rules.statement: A Eudokian story is built from dilemmas, usually one per intended Story Experience point; each element cannot be left until a choice is made, and only one choice aligns with the story's theme. Success requires more than half of the correct choices; reaching that threshold early ends the journey and sends the characters home, otherwise it ends after all elements.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Planning Eudokian Stories (ars-magica-realms#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a majority-of-choices test and mandatory decisions; a world can change the proportion or allow abandonment, with the cost being a less decisive transformation.

rules.statement: After a Eudokian journey, the character's Personality Trait shifts by one point according to whether the experience was overall positive or negative. More correct than incorrect choices grant a Virtue, Major if every choice was correct and otherwise Minor, balanced by a corresponding Charm Flaw; more incorrect choices grant a Flaw, Major if all choices were incorrect and otherwise Minor, lasting as long as the time spent in Faerie.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Faerie Boons (ars-magica-realms#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to choices shaping a trait and granting a paired Virtue/Charm Flaw or temporary Flaw; a world can make these permanent or fading, with the Charm or time spent in Faerie setting the cost.

rules.statement: A character who fails the ibis Guardian's purity test loses their heart and cannot experience emotions while in Faerie. The heart is not returned by the test.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Typical Elysian Guardians of the Threshold (ars-magica-realms#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to lasting emotional loss for failing the test; a world can make the loss temporary or recoverable, at the cost of reducing the Guardian's severity.

rules.statement: The swan cloak changes its owner's form into a swan, and stealing it lets another wearer transform in the same way.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: The Swan Cloak (ars-magica-realms#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the garment enabling animal transformation while worn; a world can require a particular trigger or limit duration, with the cloak's possession governing access.

rules.statement: Mjollnir has a short handle that gives –2 to Attack and Defense scores; a successful hit adds 30 lightning damage to normal weapon damage. Lightning penetration equals the wielder's Might, or the magus's Auram score.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Mjollnir (ars-magica-realms#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a weapon with a –2 handling penalty and a +30 lightning strike using the stated penetration; a world can tune damage or penetration, with the hammer's awkward grip as its cost.

rules.statement: A faerie’s Might score equals its innate Magic Resistance and its pool of spendable Might points; these points normally refill completely over 24 hours, and this resistance does not stack with other resistance.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Faerie Might Score (ars-magica-realms#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a Might-sized reserve and resistance with a 24-hour refill; a world can change the reserve or recovery rate, because faerie power depends on spiritual strength.

rules.statement: Faeries may recover Might faster through specific conditions: one Virtue restores the full pool in six hours, another returns 5 points from traditional offerings once per day, and another returns 2 after the faerie drains a human’s long-term fatigue or causes at least a Medium Wound.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Virtues That Affect Might (ars-magica-realms#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the listed recovery triggers and amounts; a world can change the payment or frequency, because offerings and stolen vitality fuel the faerie.

rules.statement: A faerie whose Might is restricted by a condition immediately ends its ongoing supernatural effects when that condition begins, except effects that constantly affect itself; while restricted, it can neither spend nor recover Might. Major restrictions apply at least a quarter of the time, while minor ones are uncommon.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Restricted Might (ars-magica-realms#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to ending external ongoing effects and freezing the pool during the restriction; a world can choose how often the trigger applies, because vulnerability is the cost of the limitation.

rules.statement: A faerie’s traditional props are glamour-made extensions of its body, do not cause Encumbrance, and can be reconstituted nearby in one round at no Might cost if lost.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Equipment Without Encumbrance (ars-magica-realms#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to free recovery of role-related props in one round; a world can restrict which props qualify, because they are part of the faerie’s constructed body.

rules.statement: Faeries can regenerate according to their story: after a scene, narrowly or highly cognizant faeries can repair all but cosmetic damage, while an incognizant one heals quickly unless its role requires illness. If humans kill or witness the destruction of a faerie, rebuilding takes the faster of its Might score in months or its Might divided by the adjusted Aura in months.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Regeneration (ars-magica-realms#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to role-sensitive healing and the stated rebuilding time; a world can make recovery faster or slower, because the faerie’s story determines how its body returns.

rules.statement: A faerie is permanently destroyed if its Might is destroyed, if a miracle or Infernal agent destroys it, or if the vis in its anchor is used. Destroying an external anchor also makes its distant body disintegrate, though the faerie can later form a new body unless the anchor’s vis is consumed.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Permanent Death; External Vis (ars-magica-realms#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a recoverable body-loss state tied to an anchor and permanent death when its vis is spent; a world can add other permanent-kill methods, because the anchor preserves the faerie’s essence.

rules.statement: An immaterial faerie is invisible without magical aid and can pass through solid objects, but cannot move objects until it takes on matter; while material, it cannot pass through objects, and destroying that body leaves its spirit attached to the matter as vis.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Glamorous, Immaterial Forms (ars-magica-realms#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to intangible movement with no physical manipulation, switching to material form to affect objects; a world can change what magical aid reveals it, because taking matter binds the spirit to that body.

rules.statement: Faerie bodies and their glamour-made props are not stopped by ordinary Magic Resistance, but spells aimed at their material substance or spiritual nature can affect them; most faerie powers with a Might cost and a range beyond Personal are opposed by Magic Resistance.
