locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Magic Resistance Against Faeries (ars-magica-realms#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to physical attacks bypassing resistance while ranged Might-cost powers face it; a world can broaden or narrow those exceptions, because body-making is intrinsic to faeries.

rules.statement: A faerie with a ward is uncomfortable around it, cannot touch its bearer directly or through equipment or powers, is burned by contact, and cannot regenerate Might while the ward is present.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Quick Start Guideline (ars-magica-realms#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a ward that blocks contact and recovery and burns on contact; a world can choose the ward’s form, because the faerie is antithetical to it.

rules.statement: Faerie social interaction traits affect dealings with humans and replace human social-status traits; around other faeries, a character is generally treated according to the human group it accompanies. Appearance can impose a −6 penalty, while a disturbing reputation imposes −3 on social rolls.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Social Interaction Virtues and Flaws (ars-magica-realms#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to these modifiers only in human-facing interactions; a setting can broaden or narrow them according to how faeries are regarded.

rules.statement: A faerie’s cognizance limits how it can develop: an incognizant faerie cannot consciously seek improvement, a narrowly cognizant one develops along traditional lines, and a highly cognizant one can actively pursue human-caused change. Incognizant faeries may still gain Pretenses by assisting humans in stories.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Virtues and Flaws Concerning Cognizance (ars-magica-realms#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to development constrained by cognizance; a world can make faerie change more or less accessible, with human assistance or initiative as the cost.

rules.statement: A minor traditional ward prevents a faerie from touching the protected thing and stops it regenerating Might nearby; forced or prolonged contact damages and can ultimately destroy its body. An incapacitating wound from such an item also prevents Might expenditure, and nonzero-cost constant powers expire at the next sunrise or sunset and cannot be restarted until recovery.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Traditional Ward (ars-magica-realms#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to wards that constrain contact and recovery, with sustained exposure causing bodily breakdown; a setting can turn up their severity or ease of escape.

rules.statement: A sovereign ward prevents a faerie from harming anything it protects, compels the faerie to flee, and destroys its body instantly on contact. A faerie with this weakness cannot use indirect means to harm the protected target.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Sovereign Ward (ars-magica-realms#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a broad, direct prohibition enforced by the ward; a world can define what counts as harm more narrowly or broadly.

rules.statement: Each faerie power use costs Might, and that expenditure grants one use; penetration equals Might Score minus five times the cost, plus any penetration bonus. At zero Might, a faerie cannot activate powers with a cost, though already-active effects continue until their durations end.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: An Exemplary Catalog of Faerie Powers (ars-magica-realms#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to Might as both fuel and a constraint on penetration; a world can make powers cheaper or dearer, trading resource use against efficacy.

rules.statement: An intricacy point spent on a non-Focus power either raises its Initiative by one or reduces its Might cost by one; for a Focus power it can raise Initiative but not reduce cost. A Focus power can also spend one point to raise its maximum effect level by five, even above the faerie’s Might Score, without increasing Might or Magic Resistance.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Intricacy Points (ars-magica-realms#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to points improving speed, efficiency, or Focus limits; a world can make intricacy more or less available through virtues or leftover power-design levels.

rules.statement: A ritual power costs Might Points equal to its magnitude and also reduces the faerie’s Might Score by that amount when activated; lost Might Score may return slowly at the storyguide’s discretion. Ritual powers are at least level 20 and are required for effects above level 50 or other specified exceptional effects.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Ritual Power (ars-magica-realms#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to rituals imposing both an immediate resource cost and a slower-recovering loss of capacity; a world can make the capacity loss recover faster or slower.

rules.statement: A faerie in an area dominated by another Realm cannot use powers at ranges beyond Touch without an Arcane Connection to the target or an invitation. A power with Until duration ends when its stated event occurs; when paired with another duration, it ends at whichever limit comes first.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: An Exemplary Catalog of Faerie Powers; Odd Targets and Durations (ars-magica-realms#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to foreign-Realm territory limiting reach and event-bound durations ending at the first applicable limit; a world can relax access with invitations or connections.

rules.statement: A focus power costs Might points equal to the magnitude of the effect used; its Initiative is Quickness minus the focus’s maximum magnitude, and its associated Forms determine Magic Resistance interactions.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Focus Powers (ars-magica-realms#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to charging by actual effect magnitude and setting Initiative from maximum magnitude; a world can broaden or narrow approved themes, with troupe agreement limiting overly flexible motifs.

rules.statement: A domestic-work faerie can move up to five pounds for 1 Might point, doubling the weight for each additional point. Blunt thrown objects deal +5 damage per point spent; attacks must penetrate Magic Resistance, and the effect lasts until the faerie releases the object.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Focus Powers — Domestic Work (ars-magica-realms#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to doubling moved weight and adding damage per point; a world can restrict available objects, with held or fastened objects outside the power’s reach.

rules.statement: Father of Serpents and Smithying reproduce eligible non-Ritual spells within their specified Forms and motifs, at 1 Might point per magnitude. Manifestation controls suitable animals or plants within the faerie’s glamour using eligible effects of at most 25 spell levels.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Focus Powers — Father of Serpents; Manifestation; Smithying (ars-magica-realms#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the stated spell families, targets, motif limits, and costs; a world can widen the motif, with troupe approval preserving a meaningful thematic boundary.

rules.statement: Miser’s Midas turns a touched living thing other than its user to stone; turning a human to stone for longer than a few minutes is level 35 (Base 20, Touch +1, Sun +2).
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Focus Powers — Miser’s Midas (ars-magica-realms#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to touch and the listed level for a lasting combat-useful effect; a world can change duration or targets, with greater reach or persistence raising the level cost.

rules.statement: Extended Glamour makes a faerie aware throughout a chosen domain; its Might supports a Room at 5–10, a Structure at 15–25, or a standard Boundary at 30 or more. The domain yields yearly vis equal to Might divided by 10, and bargained-for removal does not harm the faerie.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Personal Powers — Extended Glamour (ars-magica-realms#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to domain-sized awareness and the stated yearly harvest; a world can limit the domain or yield, while taking the vis without agreement risks harming the faerie.

rules.statement: Faeries gain Pretense experience by closely participating in a selected person’s momentous experience for a season, but only up to that person’s Ability level; adventure experience can likewise copy an Ability raised by a participant or adversary if it is at least as high as the Pretense. They cannot advance through study, training, or practice.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Increasing Pretense (ars-magica-realms#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to story-linked experience with an Ability-level ceiling; a world can let a Virtue increase advancement frequency, at the cost of making the faerie unusually engaged with human stories.

rules.statement: A faerie’s advancement consumes stored Pretense points and requires a creative human collaborator to open and alter its glamour. The table sets costs from 0 + Might at Ease Factor 6 to 30 + Might at Ease Factor 24, with each result permitting specified Virtue or Flaw changes; failure wastes the stored vitality and bars that human from altering the faerie again.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Faerie Advancement Through Change — Vitality; Creativity (ars-magica-realms#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the table’s paired cost and change limits; a world can reduce the Ease Factor by 3 when a change restores local folklore, while failure consumes vitality and ends that collaborator’s future access.

rules.statement: Once a faerie opens its glamour, it must accept the human’s changes. A suitably experienced collaborator aware of this control may secretly add one change to motif, attitude, or memory, rolling against the requested change’s Ease Factor minus 6.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Faerie Advancement Through Change — Creativity (ars-magica-realms#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to faerie consent to the resulting changes but allow the specified hidden extra alteration; a world can make servants notice major changes, creating political or social costs.

rules.statement: Some faeries can exchange an Ability with a human and store the acquired Ability for later transfer; others possess ordinary human Abilities and can train humans conventionally. An Ability advanced as a Pretense cannot thereafter be trained into humans beyond its level at conversion.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Pretense: Faerie Abilities — Faerie Instructor; Faerie Trainer (ars-magica-realms#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to exchange for an existing Ability or conventional instruction by a trainer; a world can let a faerie reclaim a lent Ability through its prop or bargain, limiting the human’s lasting benefit.

rules.statement: A faerie’s power may move a child who has met its gaze up to 50 paces into a sack. A separate power keeps children inside unconscious until they are removed or sunrise arrives, whichever comes first.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: The Man in Black with a Sack on His Back — Powers (ars-magica-realms#025)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: limit the abduction to a child who met the faerie’s gaze and to 50 paces; a world could extend the range, at the cost of greater power, while sleep ends upon removal or sunrise.

rules.statement: The gorgon can turn a person or animal she meets eye-to-eye into stone. The victim returns to life if the gorgon dies or loses all her Might.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Gorgon — Powers (ars-magica-realms#025)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the gaze petrifies until the gorgon dies or loses Might; a world could make the change permanent, at the cost of removing this release condition.

rules.statement: If Mormo’s possession takes hold, she directly controls the victim. Making the victim perform an action against their nature costs Might based on a personality roll; using the host’s supernatural power costs 1 Might per magnitude, and both costs apply when both conditions hold.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Mormo — Possession (ars-magica-realms#025)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: control and compelled actions spend Might; a world could reduce those costs, but should make possession easier to sustain or harder to resist.

rules.statement: A possessed host gains Mormo’s Magic Resistance while Mormo directly controls them, and is then affected by wards that exclude her. A host acting freely gains no such resistance, but may pass through those wards.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Mormo — Possession (ars-magica-realms#025)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: resistance and ward vulnerability follow who controls the host; a world could decouple them, at the cost of making possession’s protective consequences less predictable.

rules.statement: A changeling can use illusion to appear to be the stolen child; the mother’s care restores its youth and form. Some faeries leave a stick or statue that imitates the child’s death and can sever the family’s longing that might otherwise help reunite them.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Child Stealers; Faeries that Prey on New Mothers (ars-magica-realms#025)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: illusion disguises the replacement while the family’s attachment may still help find the child; a world could make the decoy sever that connection, at the cost of a potent means of reunion.

rules.statement: A glanconer’s draining power works at Arcane Connection range, causes only a light wound, and can be used repeatedly over successive days. Its connection must come from a love token knowingly given by the victim, not a stolen token or one connected to an enemy.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Glanconer — Powers (ars-magica-realms#025)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: require a willingly gifted love token and repeated exposure; a world could permit any connection, at the cost of removing the victim’s meaningful consent condition.

rules.statement: Some faerie spouses are trapped in human form when someone steals the prized item that lets them change shape, such as a selkie’s skin or a bird-woman’s feather cloak. Finding the item or breaking a taboo can let the faerie leave.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Faerie Spouses Trapped by a Trinket (ars-magica-realms#025)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the stolen token binds the spouse until recovered or a taboo is broken; a world could make the binding permanent, at the cost of removing either route to release.

rules.statement: Faeries expected to die in combat gain vitality from being killed, but must wait long enough before repeating the same role for it to count as a new story. A faerie may instead return in a different role or tell the story elsewhere.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Creatures Designed to Die in Combat (ars-magica-realms#025)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: permit recurring deaths only after enough time or a changed role or place; a world could allow immediate repetition, at the cost of diminishing the story’s novelty and vitality.

rules.statement: The fachan’s constant appearance-based effect forces each viewer to pass a Bravery check against difficulty 9; on a failure, each round inflicts a fresh Light wound from heart cramping until the viewer succeeds on the check.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Fachan, Lurching heart (ars-magica-realms#026)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one check per affected person, with recurring Light wounds until success; a setting can change the difficulty or wound severity, because the creature’s fear is its source of harm.

rules.statement: The fachan’s weapons carry poison with difficulty 9; the passage gives no further poison outcome or duration.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Fachan, Poisoned Weapons (ars-magica-realms#026)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to poison that requires overcoming difficulty 9; a setting can adjust its potency, with greater danger paid for by greater lethality.

rules.statement: The knight’s magical horse is made from the knight’s glamor, flies whenever the knight flies, and shares the knight’s Magic Resistance.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Knight (Minor), Equipment (ars-magica-realms#026)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a mount that remains an extension of its maker and shares its protection; a world could allow it to act independently, at the cost of that shared nature.

rules.statement: A barking beast’s Spirit Away power has variable cost and lets it serve as a threshold guardian; the chase may also lead hunters and their retainers into distant places, though the passage leaves open whether this is actual travel or glamour-induced misdirection.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: The Barking Beast, Powers and Appearance (ars-magica-realms#026)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a guardian effect with variable expenditure, while treating distant journeys as uncertain; a setting can make the travel literal or illusory, with glamour as the alternative explanation.

rules.statement: A Valkyrie’s visions reveal where and when worthy men are likely to die, and she chooses worthy dead for transformation into spiritual warriors awaiting Ragnarok.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Death, Psychopomps, Valkyrie (ars-magica-realms#026)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to visions that identify likely deaths and a chooser who selects among the dead; a setting can make the forecast more or less certain, with worthiness as the selection limit.

rules.statement: The White Lady’s water-focused power can produce effects such as drowning, torrents, and whirling water, at a cost of up to 10 points; separate powers can transform her into a current or wave, or a victim into a seagull, crab, or salmon.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Faerie Monarchs, White Lady (Dame Blanche), Powers (ars-magica-realms#026)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to water effects bounded by the stated power budget and listed transformation forms; a setting can broaden the focus, at the cost of loosening its thematic restriction.

rules.statement: The Privy Counselor can take coin form to spy, use illusion to maintain an apparent home, and steal money through shapeshifting and enthrallment; its restricted Might applies around honest people.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Faerie Noble: The Privy Counselor (ars-magica-realms#026)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to covert role-based deception constrained by honesty-related weakness; a setting can strengthen its unrestricted operation, at the cost of reducing that vulnerability.

rules.statement: Sprites can cause sickness with an arrow: strokes have difficulty 6 and inflict a Heavy wound, while this court’s fever effect has difficulty 9 and inflicts a Light wound.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Lesser Courtly Faeries, Sprites, Powers (ars-magica-realms#026)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the court’s fever version, which is harder to inflict but less severe; a world can choose the stroke version, trading ease for heavier injury.

rules.statement: A seasonal guardian can hold power over a season or land until summer, when that power passes to a rival; in some versions the guardian keeps summer captive instead. The Cailleach Bheur’s glamour reaches across much of the land and lets her know about many important events in distant places.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Passage 28, opening section (ars-magica-realms#027)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to broad, important-event awareness within the guardian’s land; a world can narrow its range or precision because the glamour is tied to that territory.

rules.statement: Południca’s fatigue power removes one long-term fatigue level by causing heatstroke. Her whirlwind transformation costs 3 points, while shifting between human appearances costs 1 point and can vary Presence from +3 to –3.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Południca — Powers (ars-magica-realms#027)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the listed costs and the stated Presence range; a world can make transformation cheaper or costlier by changing intricacy, reflecting how much power the faerie has invested.

rules.statement: For faerie hounds, 50 spell levels can be spent on Greater Powers; each complete 5 levels traded away buys an intricacy point that reduces either a power’s use cost or its Initiative penalty by 1. A damaging bite effect adds +5 damage when present.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Roads — Faerie Hounds, Powers (ars-magica-realms#027)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the stated 5-level exchange and +5 damage; a world can change the exchange rate or damage bonus, with stronger effects consuming more of the faerie’s power budget.

rules.statement: A kelpie’s Adhere power makes a rider stick to its back; it can then plunge into water with the rider held fast. The Aufhocker variant’s grip also adds 6 to its victim’s combat Load.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Roads — Kelpie (Water Horse) (ars-magica-realms#027)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a successful grip preventing the rider from dismounting; a world can let targets resist or escape, because the faerie’s grip is a supernatural expenditure rather than ordinary adhesion.

rules.statement: A merfolk net reduces an opponent’s Attack score by half the net wielder’s Thrown Weapon Pretense; the passage notes this special rule does not apply when humans use nets. Some merfolk can also ask questions of their local sea, and the effect lasts for Concentration.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Waterways — Tritons (ars-magica-realms#027)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the stated merfolk-only net rule and local-sea questioning; a world can extend the net rule to humans or widen the area of answers, with broader effects requiring greater power.

rules.statement: Selkie blood spilled into the sea produces a rain-and-thunder effect; a group shedding blood together can create a much greater storm. This is used to retaliate for mass seal slaughter or the death of other selkies.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Waterways — Selkie King, Powers (ars-magica-realms#027)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to blood on the sea producing a storm, with group participation increasing its scale; a world can require more blood or participants for stronger weather because the blood is the price and fuel.

rules.statement: A faun’s music can grant listeners +3 to Weapon Skills and Brave totals for the rest of the scene. Its other music can make listeners more riotous by increasing traits such as Reckless, Lustful, and Impulsive for that same duration.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Forest — Fauns, Powers (ars-magica-realms#027)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the listed bonuses or trait changes lasting one scene; a world can narrow the audience or duration, as the faun’s performance supplies the emotional stimulus.

rules.statement: Kallikantzaroi can reach the surface from Christmas until the Epiphany on January 6; when they return underground, the World Tree has regenerated and their labor begins again. A person can divert one by dropping a colander or spilling grain, forcing it to stop and count.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Christmas — Kallikantzaroi (ars-magica-realms#027)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the annual Christmas-to-January-6 release and the counting distraction; a world can alter the dates or what objects trigger counting, reflecting local seasonal belief and custom.

rules.statement: A positive Sympathy Trait can replace an ordinary specialization bonus on a relevant Ability check, adding its full value, but only the highest applicable positive Trait counts. Using one requires a stress die, and a botch gives Warping Points. A negative Trait instead subtracts its strongest applicable value from relevant Abilities and adds that many botch dice to botch checks.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Sympathy Traits (ars-magica-realms#028)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to applying the strongest relevant Trait as a bonus or penalty; a world can change the Trait range or botch risk, since faerie resonance is volatile and can bring Warping.

rules.statement: A Sympathy Trait normally cannot be raised above the character’s Warping Score. Practice for a season grants 5 experience points; improving a negative Trait costs 10 experience to go from –1 to 0, 15 from –2 to –1, 20 from –3 to –2, and so on, and requires Warping Score greater than its absolute value. A roll of 1 while using a Trait grants 1 experience to each applicable Trait, while each botch removes 1; these fluctuations ignore the Warping limit, and the gains and losses reverse for negative Traits.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Increasing Sympathy Traits (ars-magica-realms#028)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to Warping-limited growth and roll-driven fluctuations; a world can alter training awards or the cap, because repeated faerie exposure may strengthen or destabilize a person’s connection.

rules.statement: Faerie Rank equals the highest positive Sympathy Trait modified by the lowest negative Trait; for example, +4 and –2 yield Rank 2, while +1 and –5 yield –4. Sympathetic influence may temporarily grant a Trait: a brief ceremony takes about 10 minutes, needs a leader with Faerie Lore 1+, costs each participant a Confidence Point, and lasts perhaps a week; practical influence takes a season and lasts up to a year. Participants need a suitable Personality Trait or Flaw, and temporary Traits do not affect Faerie Rank or grow through experience.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Faerie Rank; Sympathetic Influence (ars-magica-realms#028)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to these durations, eligibility requirements, and Confidence cost; a world can change the method or persistence, because sustained association or ritual commitment shapes sympathy.

rules.statement: Tinting an aura gives everyone inside temporary Personality Traits that draw them toward the tint and repel them from its opposite, with strength limited by both the influencer’s Sympathy Trait and the aura level. A stress-die roll with Presence and Concentration sets the strength; ceremonial tints fade by 1 each day and practical tints by 1 each season, while multiple tints can conflict.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Tinted Auras (ars-magica-realms#028)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to an aura-wide temporary influence that decays at the stated rate; a world can adjust the maximum strength or decay, since lingering faerie resonance shapes everyone present.

rules.statement: A charm-based Virtue normally works without affecting its operation, but if another person learns the actual activation method, the power is lost. A Lesser Charm must then be made again, while a Greater Charm must be recovered; even a private written record of the method violates the secrecy requirement.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Charms (ars-magica-realms#029)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to ending a charm power when its activation becomes known; a world can relax or tighten what counts as disclosure, because secrecy fuels the magic.

rules.statement: A Virtue can use a charm only if it is not Social Status or background-based, does not affect experience points, changes what the character can do rather than fundamental statistics, and is not Hermetic or among the excluded Magical, Divine, Infernal, or Mystery categories.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Charms (ars-magica-realms#029)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to permitting only capability-granting, non-excluded Virtues; a world can widen the list, at the cost of weakening the distinction between personal charm magic and other sources.

rules.statement: A character with Faerie Lore and a Sympathy Trait can craft a folk charm using ordinary craft time. It stops an appropriate faerie effect if applied to its target or original caster and the user’s stress die + Intelligence + Faerie Lore + aura modifier beats the effect’s level; the charm fails if taken away or damaged.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Sympathetic Magic — Folk Charms (ars-magica-realms#029)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to requiring an appropriate crafted focus and a successful level contest; a world can make charms more robust or easier to use, trading away their dependence on personal sympathetic links.

rules.statement: Using a folk charm costs one Fatigue level and causes one Warping point. A user who cannot take Fatigue or is immune to Warping cannot activate it; against Magic Resistance the charm must penetrate, though an applicable Sympathy Trait adds its value to Penetration.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Sympathetic Magic — Folk Charms (ars-magica-realms#029)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to charging fatigue and warping for each activation; a world can lower either cost, but should account for the reduced danger of repeatedly ending faerie effects.

rules.statement: A magus can use applicable Sympathy Traits as specializations for Abilities used in Hermetic magic, including Penetration and Magic Theory. For laboratory Abilities, the magus must experiment to receive the bonus and automatically experiments when an applicable negative Sympathy Trait is involved.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Sympathetic Magic — Hermetic Charms (ars-magica-realms#029)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to allowing relevant positive or negative sympathetic modifiers, with laboratory benefits tied to experimentation; a world can remove that risk, but then sympathetic lab work loses a meaningful cost.

rules.statement: When enchanting a device, a magus may add relevant Sympathy Trait values to the Lab Total, limited by Magic Theory, and may attune a talisman to a relevant trait. A device designed as a charm can add traits appropriate to its effect, but stops working if it is not activated in secret.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Sympathetic Magic — Hermetic Charms (ars-magica-realms#029)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to making sympathetic bonuses depend on the maker’s current trait and keeping charm devices secret; a world can make attunements permanent, sacrificing that personal and changeable connection.

rules.statement: A human with Faerie Blood may use powers granted by the listed faerie Virtues by paying one Fatigue level for each 5 points or fraction of their normal Might cost. For Penetration calculations, treat the user as having Might 0; regular Faerie Blood permits only Minor Virtues, while Strong Faerie Blood also permits Major ones.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Faerie Powers for the Faerie Blooded (ars-magica-realms#029)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to converting power cost into fatigue and using zero Might for Penetration; a world can permit stronger powers or reduce the fatigue burden, but should preserve a compensating limit.

rules.statement: Faerie Blood can appear through faerie influence or be inherited, and its strength need not fade with generations: it may skip generations and reappear at a similar strength. Faerie Legacy replaces the usual blood benefit with an enhanced version rather than adding to it.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Faerie Blood — Varieties of Faerie Blood (ars-magica-realms#029)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to allowing traits to reappear unchanged across generations and making Legacy a replacement benefit; a world can make inheritance more predictable, at the cost of reducing faerie blood’s capriciousness.

rules.statement: A Faerie rite’s level is a stress die plus the relevant Characteristic, Method, Power, and Faerie aura modifier, capped at five times the total applicable Sympathy Trait scores. Negative Traits count by their absolute value toward the cap; a roll of 1 gives experience in applicable Traits, while a botch removes experience from them.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Chapter Six: Faerie Wizardry — Performing Faerie Rites (ars-magica-realms#030)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Use the listed formula and Sympathy cap by default; a world can raise or lower the cap, making stronger effects depend on how closely the caster is tied to the target.

rules.statement: Faerie rites at ritual level take 15 minutes per magnitude and need no vis, but cannot make permanent effects. A Momentary rite ends at once; lasting change is possible only when it results from a natural or supernatural process.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Chapter Six: Faerie Wizardry — Performing Faerie Rites (ars-magica-realms#030)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Treat rite effects as temporary unless they set a process in motion; a world can permit lasting direct effects at added cost, though the passage gives no such default cost.

rules.statement: A ceremony’s group modifier is the participants’ Ceremony scores added together minus the number of participants. Participants also add their relevant Characteristic and Ability or Method scores to the focus character’s total; if they lack that Ability or Method, they add only the Characteristic.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Faerie Abilities — Ceremony (ars-magica-realms#030)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Use the stated group arithmetic, which can yield a negative modifier; a world can require or reward particular group sizes, with coordination as the in-world burden.

rules.statement: Curse-Throwing transfers a harmful disease, curse, spell, power, or supernatural ability from an afflicted target to a recipient, who must be present or represented by an Arcane Connection. The caster performs a ritual, typically an hour per 5 Ease Factor points or fraction, and must meet the listed Ease Factor; Magic Resistance must be penetrated, and a botch transfers the effect to the caster.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Faerie Abilities — Curse-Throwing (ars-magica-realms#030)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Transfer harmful effects rather than erase them; a world can make the transfer more difficult across species or weaker Arcane Connections, shifting the burden onto someone else.

rules.statement: A Lesser Charm requires a brief ritual to activate its owner’s Virtue; if the charm is stolen or its secrecy is exposed, it stops working and must be remade, usually in less than a day. A Greater Charm has only one copy, and stealing it transfers the Virtue to the thief until the original charm is recovered or destroyed.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: New and Modified Flaws — Lesser Charm; Greater Charm (ars-magica-realms#030)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Require possession and secrecy for charm-bound powers; a world can make charms easier to duplicate or harder to reclaim, trading security against portability.

rules.statement: At Warping Score 1, a character may gain a hindering Reputation instead of the usual Flaw; it rises by 1 whenever Warping Score rises. At score 3, glamour holders must act in keeping with that Reputation to avoid Deprivation, with the interval shortening to a month at score 4, a week at 5, and a day at 6 or more; later thresholds can also grant Sympathy Traits or supernatural Virtues and Flaws.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Faerie Warping (ars-magica-realms#030)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Use the listed Warping thresholds and increasingly frequent need; a world can change the required behavior or penalty, making the character’s public story a growing personal cost.

rules.statement: A Faerie-aligned character who gains at least 2 Warping Points at once undergoes Faerie Calling and is dazed until the scene is addressed. Complex action requires a Perception + Awareness roll against three times the sum of Warping Score and Warping Points gained; resolving the dream can raise or lower a Sympathy Trait by 1, and at Faerie Rank of at least +10 or at most −10 the character may disappear permanently after the corresponding positive or negative outcome.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Faerie Calling (ars-magica-realms#030)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Trigger the Calling at 2 simultaneous Warping Points and use the stated thresholds; a world can alter the trigger or Rank needed for permanent departure, with the Faerie realm claiming the character as the cost.

rules.statement: A homunculus wizard must secretly feed the homunculus some of his blood once each day and protect it from harm and human sight. If it is harmed or seen by another human, it dies immediately; until another is bound, the wizard cannot use or improve powers that are not Faerie-associated or that require The Gift.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Homunculi Wizards (ars-magica-realms#030)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Treat the homunculus as a maintained external source with a daily blood cost and a severe secrecy vulnerability; a world can change the upkeep or failure consequence.

rules.statement: A Symbol duration lasts as long as the physical symbol made during casting remains intact and applicable. Damage ends the effect; a target ceasing to match the symbol suspends it until the match returns, and the effect can outlast its caster. It is at Year level, requires a ritual, and needs at least 3 applicable Sympathy Trait points for each Symbol parameter; combining Range, Duration, and Target as Symbol therefore needs at least 9.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Symbol (Duration) (ars-magica-realms#031)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to an effect sustained by an intact, applicable object; a world can raise or lower the required Sympathy points, reflecting how demanding symbolic links are.

rules.statement: A Medium target carries an effect until an applicable target enters range, at which point the effect transfers to that target. Removing the target interrupts the effect, but the medium can pass it to another target while duration remains; the caster needs applicable Sympathy Traits for both medium and target, and the medium must be in range at casting.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Medium (Target) (ars-magica-realms#031)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to repeatable transfer while the duration lasts; a world can restrict the medium to one transfer, making suitable sympathetic links scarce.

rules.statement: Passion affects only people inclined toward the emotion or desire built into the rite: each person in the area rolls a simple die and adjusts for relevant Personality Traits, and totals of 6 or more are affected. It uses Group-level targeting and scales with area size.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Passion (Target) (ars-magica-realms#031)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the stated individual threshold within an area; a world can change the threshold or area scaling, reflecting how strongly passions resist supernatural influence.

rules.statement: A Symbol target includes all targets represented by a symbol within range; it uses Boundary-level calculation, with modifiers for target-group size, and requires a ritual. It needs at least 3 applicable Sympathy Trait points per Symbol parameter, or 9 when Range, Duration, and Target all use Symbol.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Symbol (Target) (ars-magica-realms#031)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to affecting represented targets within range; a world can increase the Sympathy requirement, reflecting the difficulty of reaching many symbolic matches.

rules.statement: Faerie Methods are learned or gained as abilities, improve on the Ability scale, and can only be used with a Faerie Power; any Method can accompany any Power. Each tradition defines a rite characteristic, usually a cost, and a situational advantage.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Faerie Methods (ars-magica-realms#031)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to requiring both a Method and a Power; a world can change learning sources or method costs, reflecting how a tradition draws on Faerie.

rules.statement: Evocation costs either a Warping Point or a Confidence Point. It can spend vis to add 2 to the Rite Casting Total per pawn, capped at the character's Evocation score plus the associated Power score; non-Faerie vis also adds one botch die per pawn when the casting roll is 0.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Evocation (ars-magica-realms#031)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the stated personal cost and vis cap; a world can adjust the cap or botch risk, reflecting how safely its practitioners can channel borrowed power.

rules.statement: Enchantment requires an Ability performance roll against an Ease Factor of three times the intended effect magnitude. Success allows casting next round at that magnitude, or another performance to raise the intended magnitude by one; excess over the Ease Factor adds to the next roll, while failure loses the accumulated bonus and requires starting over. Its performance conceals where the rite begins from ordinary observers, and it permits a simple casting die that avoids botching but forfeits the benefit of a 1.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Enchantment (ars-magica-realms#031)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to accumulated performance bonuses and restart on failure; a world can make observers more perceptive or alter the botch tradeoff, reflecting how exposed performance magic is.

rules.statement: Empathy costs a Fatigue level and usually takes about an hour; if the caster cannot lose Fatigue or would become unconscious, the cost is a Light Wound instead. The disorientation lasts for the effect and prevents Fatigue recovery. Each additional Fatigue level doubles applicable Rite Casting bonuses and resets the Confidence or vis spending limit; it also doubles the Sympathy Trait value used for maximum effect level, so 3 Trait points can support level 30 with two Fatigue levels or level 45 with three.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Empathy (ars-magica-realms#031)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to increasing output through escalating exhaustion; a world can alter the fatigue-to-power exchange, reflecting how much bodily strain Faerie rites impose.

rules.statement: Each Faerie Power has a chosen uncommon vulnerability, such as iron, running water, salt, Dominion, or its user's name spoken three times. Applying it to the target or caster dispels all effects associated with that Power on that subject.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Faerie Powers (ars-magica-realms#031)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a chosen vulnerability that ends associated effects; a world can broaden or narrow the trigger, reflecting how readily a power can be disrupted.

rules.statement: Summoning costs one Fatigue level after a few minutes of mental preparation. The summoner’s applicable Sympathy Trait scores are added, treating negative scores as positive, and the result times 5 sets the maximum Might he can attempt; a faerie appears even if the roll fails or botches.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Faerie Bargaining — Summoning (ars-magica-realms#032)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to an appearance on every attempt, bounded by Sympathy and Fatigue; a world can make botches harsher because a hostile or mistaken visitor can result.

rules.statement: If the Summoning Total meets or exceeds the faerie’s Might and the summoner penetrates its resistance, the faerie must attend and listen, and the summoner is protected from its attacks and powers. Either party can end this hold at any time, whereupon the faerie returns to its origin; without both checks, the faerie is unbound and cannot be sent away by the summoner.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Faerie Bargaining — Summoning (ars-magica-realms#032)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a temporary, mutually terminable hold only when both checks succeed; a world can make the hold more reliable by relaxing either threshold, at the cost of less bargaining risk.

rules.statement: After a summoning, making a bargain grants the summoner 1 experience point in an appropriate Sympathy Trait, while failing to agree costs 1 point. Breaking the bargain immediately gives the summoner a –3 appropriate Sympathy Trait, and the faerie remains bound to its agreement even if the summoner fails to keep his side.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Faerie Bargaining — Summoning (ars-magica-realms#032)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to enforceable bargains with a substantial penalty for reneging; a world can soften enforcement or penalties, trading away the faeries’ leverage and the cost of bad faith.

rules.statement: Bonding costs one Fatigue level, requires the faerie to be within voice range when the bond is formed, and must exceed its Might and penetrate its resistance. The bond creates an Arcane Connection and grants one chosen benefit; a character can benefit from only one bond, and forming another destroys the first.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Faerie Bargaining — Bonding (ars-magica-realms#032)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one active bond and one selected benefit, with Fatigue and resistance limiting access; a world can allow multiple bonds by increasing upkeep or other costs.

rules.statement: Captivating costs one Fatigue level and, if its total exceeds the faerie’s Might and penetrates resistance, exchanges control of the two bodies for the duration without exchanging memories, Personality Traits, Confidence, Faith Points, or the summoner’s Sympathy Traits. Either can try to end the exchange; resisting an attempted ending is settled by comparing a stress die plus an appropriate Personality Trait, with the summoner adding applicable Sympathy Traits, and the effect causes the summoner’s body 1 Warping Point each season and another each year.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Faerie Bargaining — Captivating (ars-magica-realms#032)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to reciprocal body control, a contest over release, and accumulating Warping; a world can reduce the lasting cost, but the exchange then becomes a safer route to prolonged life.

rules.statement: Dismissing costs one Fatigue level and requires speech with the being; its reach is capped at five times the applicable Sympathy Trait total. It can cancel a being’s power effect, end an effect targeting a being with Might, or release a being from a supernaturally enforced agreement, provided the relevant total and resistance checks succeed.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Faerie Bargaining — Dismissing (ars-magica-realms#032)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to spoken, Fatigue-costing cancellation and release with a Sympathy-based cap; a world can make release easier, at the cost of weakening supernatural agreements.

rules.statement: When using any of the four bargaining arts, a stress-die result of 1 grants 1 experience point in an applicable Sympathy Trait used against the faerie, while a botch removes 1 experience point.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Faerie Bargaining — opening passage on Bonding, Captivating, and Dismissing (ars-magica-realms#032)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to Sympathy improving or worsening through risky use; a world can remove this feedback, but then repeated bargaining no longer changes the summoner’s connection to faeries.

rules.statement: A Dominion aura spreads outward from a worshipping community’s sacred center and weakens with distance; at night its rating drops by 1, while on holy days it rises by 1. Where it meets an equally strong aura from another realm, Dominion prevails, but a stronger opposing aura overcomes it.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Dominion Power; Conflicting Auras (ars-magica-realms#034)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a worship-centered field whose strength varies with distance and calendar; a world can change its reach or schedule, with faithful gatherings and holy observances sustaining its force.

rules.statement: Creating a Dominion requires two successful rites: first to consecrate a site, then to let the Dominion enter it. Each needs a celebrant with a suitable religious role and Theology or Dominion Lore 2+, at least ten believers, and a stress roll adding Communication and the relevant Ability against Ease Factor 6; the resulting aura starts at 3 and endures while worship continues regularly.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Creating a Dominion Aura (ars-magica-realms#034)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a congregation and two successful rites as the entry cost; a world can adjust the group size or rite difficulty, with regular worship required to maintain the aura.

rules.statement: A Dominion created by regular weekly worship rises to rating 4 after a year and may reach 5 after a decade if the congregation is large and the site significant. Once worship stops, its rating fades steadily over a period matching the duration of regular worship; relics with more than 5 Faith Points can raise a rating above 5 by 1 per excess point.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Creating a Dominion Aura (ars-magica-realms#034)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to gradual growth and decay tied to the history of worship; a world can accelerate or cap these changes, with sustained devotion or powerful relics providing the in-world support.

rules.statement: A consecrated Eucharistic Host radiates a Dominion aura of 5 until the next Good Friday, falling by 1 for every five paces from it. Profaning it in any way ends the aura.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Holy of Holies (ars-magica-realms#034)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a potent, localized sacred effect that expires on a calendar date or through profanation; a world can alter its duration or radius, with preservation of the Host as the limiting condition.

rules.statement: A miracle above magnitude 50 can create a static Empyreal aura: magnitude 50 gives rating 1, and each additional 5 levels adds 1 rating. It lasts while the miracle remains present or influential, and its sphere extends as far as the miracle’s effect.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Empyreal Aura Power (ars-magica-realms#034)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a fixed field scaled to miracle magnitude and effect area; a world can change the threshold or scaling, with the miracle’s continuing influence sustaining it.

rules.statement: A divine creature with Might 20 or more can spend 10 Might to make a one-level regio of rating 1; each further 10 Might adds a level or rating. The regio lasts one year, then disappears unless its creator or another divine creature spends monthly the amount used to create it.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Creating Divine Regiones: Divine Creatures (ars-magica-realms#034)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to Might expenditure for creation and ongoing upkeep; a world can change the price or duration, with divine power paid both initially and after the first year.

rules.statement: In a celestial regio, a mortal must pass a stress roll of Stamina plus Dominion Lore against three times the regio rating to act normally; a higher Parma Magica or similar protection Ability may replace Dominion Lore. Spending 1 Faith Point avoids this disorientation, while failure imposes a penalty equal to three times the rating until departure.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Inside Celestial Regiones (ars-magica-realms#034)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to an entry hazard scaled to the regio’s rating, with Faith or protection as ways around it; a world can change the check or penalty, while stronger heavens impose greater strain.

rules.statement: After hours equal to Stamina plus Parma Magica or similar protection Ability plus 3, an ordinary human in a celestial regio loses 1 Fatigue level per hour. Once unconscious, the character gains Warping Points equal to the regio level each hour; characters with True Faith measure these periods in days instead.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Inside Celestial Regiones (ars-magica-realms#034)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to escalating bodily and supernatural harm from prolonged exposure; a world can change the safe interval or rate, while spiritual resilience extends the time before consequences begin.

rules.statement: An angel can spend 2 Might to take a physical-seeming form that behaves like mortal flesh and is subject to natural laws. If this form is killed, the angel returns to spiritual form and may manifest again immediately if it chooses and can pay the cost.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Angelic Powers (ars-magica-realms#035)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to allowing temporary physical forms for 2 Might; a world can restrict re-manifestation, with the cost being the angel's limited Might reserve.

rules.statement: For 2 Might, an angel can shield a target's soul and mind from all supernatural targeting for a few moments. For 10 Might, it can instead make a person's body invulnerable to magic, pain, harm, fatigue, wounds, and death for no more than one combat round.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Angelic Powers (ars-magica-realms#035)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to brief, complete protection at the stated costs; a world can extend its duration, but should increase the Might cost or narrow what it protects against.

rules.statement: An angel may send a divine message through a target's dream for 1 Might or while the target is awake for 5 Might. Either version can reach a target at any distance.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Angelic Powers (ars-magica-realms#035)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to dream messages costing less than waking visions; a world can limit the waking form by distance or reliability, with the extra Might representing its greater impact.

rules.statement: A being's True Name functions as an indefinite Arcane Connection and gives a caster a +5 multiplier bonus to Penetration. The name may also enable other magical effects.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Angelic True Names (ars-magica-realms#035)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a True Name providing a persistent connection and the stated bonus; a world can make names harder to discover, with secrecy protecting the named being from magical leverage.

rules.statement: In spiritual form, an angel can be affected only by Mentem or Vim, has no Wounds or Fatigue, and is immune to magic that would make it violate its nature or Personality Traits. Reducing its Divine Might below zero destroys it permanently.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Angels and Magic (ars-magica-realms#035)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to spiritual immunity with destruction only when Might falls below zero; a world can broaden the forms that affect angels, at the cost of making them more vulnerable.

rules.statement: Angels move instantaneously without occupying the space between their starting point and destination. While using a physical Mantle, they may instead choose to move normally.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Angelic Movement (ars-magica-realms#035)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to instantaneous movement for spiritual angels; a world can require ordinary travel, trading supernatural reach for more predictable positioning.

rules.statement: Angelic illumination conveys a message directly to a recipient's soul, but its Penetration is zero unless modified by the angel's Penetration Ability. Angels use spoken human languages when that direct communication cannot get through.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Angelic Language (ars-magica-realms#035)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to direct communication with zero Penetration; a world can let it bypass resistance, but should make that a stronger capability than ordinary illumination.

rules.statement: Four Cherubim can each spend 30 Might to bring a direct Divine manifestation around a target. It removes all Warping, Decrepitude, and Aging Points, raises any lower Intelligence, Perception, Presence, and Communication scores to +3, or increases True Faith by 1.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Cherubim (ars-magica-realms#035)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to requiring four Cherubim and 30 Might apiece for this extensive restoration; a world can narrow the benefits or require greater piety, preserving the exceptional cost.

rules.statement: A Principality can spend Might to banish non-Divine creatures from its domain from sunrise to sunrise: 5 for a family, 10 for a village, 15 for a town, 20 for a duchy, 30 for a kingdom, or 40 for an empire. Its Penetration is doubled against Infernal creatures.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Principalities (ars-magica-realms#035)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a one-day banishment with cost scaling by territory; a world can permit longer protection, but should raise the cost or make the area harder to defend.

rules.statement: A Watcher cast to Earth is permanently confined to its Angelic Mantle. If slain, it dies permanently unless it has enough Divine Might to make another Mantle immediately.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Grigori, the Watchers (ars-magica-realms#036)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to permanent death when the Mantle is destroyed; a world could allow replacement with sufficient Might, at the cost of that reserve.

rules.statement: Angels in human disguise behave entirely mundanely and avoid revealing their nature unless dire need forces them to act. Their divine powers are generally withheld when guidance can lead mortals to act for themselves.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Storyguiding Angels — As Characters; Portraying Angels (ars-magica-realms#036)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to an effective mundane disguise; a world could make extraordinary events pierce it, risking exposure.

rules.statement: An angel in spirit form cannot affect physical things and cannot be affected by physical forces. Some angels can instead take a cloud or fiery form, with the specific immunities and nearby damage described for those powers.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Example Angels — Azrael; Kolazonta (ars-magica-realms#036)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to physical immunity paired with inability to act physically; a world could vary which forms retain contact, at the cost of narrower powers.

rules.statement: Angelic Holy Magic can reproduce Hermetic or holy magical effects for 1 Might Point per 2 magnitudes; it can also reproduce rituals without vis or lengthy casting, limited by the angel’s remaining Might.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Example Angels — Eiael, Aid to the Wise (ars-magica-realms#036)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one Might per two magnitudes, with no per-effect cap beyond remaining Might; a world could raise the rate to limit powerful effects.

rules.statement: Gabriel can implant Knowledge by spending 1 Might Point per experience point granted, but cannot raise a recipient’s Ability above 15 this way.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Example Angels — Gabriel, the Archangel of Prophecy (ars-magica-realms#036)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one Might per experience point and a score ceiling of 15; a world could change the ceiling, with greater knowledge demanding more power.

rules.statement: A person with angelic blood ages slowly: after age 150, they roll for aging once per decade and receive –5 on those rolls. They gain no benefit from aging-slowing effects; after their first Decrepitude Point, subtract age divided by 10 from Advancement Totals, to a minimum of 1 per season.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: New Virtues — Blood of the Nephilim (ars-magica-realms#036)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the stated slower aging and learning penalty; a world could ease the penalty, while preserving the bloodline’s unusual longevity.

rules.statement: A Nephilim-blooded character must eat as much as three ordinary people daily. Going without food for a day causes supernatural sleep; without food equal to the character’s body weight, they starve after 2 plus their Divine Might days, then lose one Long Term Fatigue Level per unfed day on waking.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: New Virtues — Blood of the Nephilim (ars-magica-realms#036)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the listed food burden, sleep, starvation deadline, and fatigue loss; a world could soften the costs, at the expense of the heritage’s bodily burden.

rules.statement: A Powerful Relic has Faith 3 and one agreed power, but stops working if its owner acts impiously, until suitable penance is performed. An ordinary Relic has True Faith 1 and no additional power.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: New Virtues — Powerful Relic; Relic (ars-magica-realms#036)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to suspending the powerful relic’s use after impiety until penance; a world could make the suspension shorter or stricter.

rules.statement: Strong Angelic Heritage grants Divine Might equal to age divided by 20, corresponding Magic Resistance, and Corpus vis equal to Might divided by 10 with a minimum of one pawn; the vis can be extracted only after death, and the character is immune to Warping.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: New Virtues — Strong Angelic Heritage (ars-magica-realms#036)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to age-scaled Might and locked vis that can be harvested only from a corpse; a world could alter the scale, with greater power increasing the body’s value.

rules.statement: A character can invoke up to 30 levels of holy-power effects by spending Might; each effect costs half its magnitude in Might, rounded as specified by the rules, with a minimum cost of 1. Each additional purchase of this power adds 30 usable levels but does not increase Divine Might.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Passage 38, holy powers (ars-magica-realms#037)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a 30-level pool with a minimum 1-point cost; a world can raise the pool by allowing repeated purchases, but those purchases do not increase Might.

rules.statement: For a leader-led Ceremony, the leader's score limits how many participants contribute; without a leader, add everyone's Ceremony scores and subtract the number of participants to get a group modifier. Participants also add their relevant characteristic-and-ability or characteristic-and-method totals to the focus character's total; anyone lacking the relevant ability or method contributes only the characteristic.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: New Abilities, Ceremony (ars-magica-realms#037)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to pooling participant contributions under these formulas; a world can require a leader or allow leaderless groups, with spiritual authority determining who may lead.

rules.statement: Invocation requires a loud spoken prayer or a written one, adds Communication to the roll, and costs one Confidence or Faith point. A user may choose a stress die instead of a simple die when calling a holy effect.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: New Abilities, Invocation (ars-magica-realms#037)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to requiring a point and an audible or written prayer; a world can permit stress-die attempts, accepting the greater risk of offending the divine.

rules.statement: A successful holy influence roll sets a new temporary Personality trait: a result of 9, 15, or 24 gives it a value of +1, +2, or +3 respectively. Personal influence can last about a year, while ceremonial influence usually fades within a week; the subject must be willing to consider the holy character's advice and within that character's spiritual authority.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Holy Influence (ars-magica-realms#037)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a temporary trait capped at +3 and limited to willing people under the influencer's authority; a world can change persistence, with continued conduct reinforcing the change.

rules.statement: An invoked temper adds its value to rolls aligned with its virtue and subtracts it from opposing rolls within the aura. Ceremonial tempering loses one point of value each day, personal tempering loses one each season, and one character cannot maintain more than one temper at once.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Tempers (ars-magica-realms#037)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one fading virtuous trait that shifts aligned and opposed rolls; a world can vary the decay interval, while conflicting authorities may create opposing influences.

rules.statement: Invoking God's aid costs one Confidence or Faith point and grants a scene bonus of +1, +2, or at most +3 on a total of 9, 15, or 24. The bonus applies only to rolls clearly serving the requested objective and ends at the first failed roll or the scene's end; a zero on the stress die calls for at least three botch dice.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Invoking God's Aid (ars-magica-realms#037)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a capped, objective-bound bonus that ends on failure or scene end; a world can make botches harsher, reflecting divine displeasure.

rules.statement: An invested ruler gains Magic Resistance and a Soak bonus equal to one fifth of that resistance, plus a voice-range commanding aura with no Penetration. A relic's resistance adds to the ruler's own resistance but does not increase the Soak bonus or aura; accepted excommunication or other valid sanctions remove these benefits until penance.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: The Commanding Aura (ars-magica-realms#037)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to rank-conferring protection and an aura sustained by divine favor; a world can withdraw the benefits for accepted sanctions or direct divine displeasure.

rules.statement: A leader may confer a commanding aura only with authorization from superiors, cannot grant greater resistance or Soak than they possess, and must spend a Confidence or Faith point during the investiture. Without that expenditure the ceremony has no effect.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: The Commanding Aura, Player Characters and the Commanding Aura (ars-magica-realms#037)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a hierarchy-limited grant requiring a point from the conferrer; a world can vary the investiture ceremony, but not the authorization or power ceiling.

rules.statement: Holy relics can serve as foci of divine power and can bind oaths; they may also be humiliated in hopes of prompting a saint to act or encouraging people to change their behavior. A successful theft or transfer may be understood as the saint's approval, while counterfeit relics have no power.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Relics (ars-magica-realms#037)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to relics as potent objects that can witness binding oaths; a world can make their authenticity or a saint's response uncertain.

rules.statement: A relic’s Divine Might equals its highest applicable Faith score multiplied by 10; its Might limits use of its powers, resists effects aimed directly at it, and is restored at sunrise. Faith points can provide the bearer with Magic Resistance or be spent as Confidence.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: The Powers of Relics (ars-magica-realms#038)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to relic power use bounded by Might and restored at sunrise; a world can change the reserve or refresh schedule to suit its theology, since divine power is finite between renewals.

rules.statement: A relic’s hostile aura extends a number of feet equal to its Divine Might. Infernal creatures whose Might does not exceed the relic’s cannot enter; those that do take damage equal to its Might each round until they leave, while merely affiliated beings are unaffected.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: The Powers of Relics (ars-magica-realms#038)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to an aura that bars weaker Infernal beings and harms intruders; a world can vary its range or threshold, because the relic’s Might expresses its reach and strength.

rules.statement: A relic’s powers work only for its eligible faith group and cease when its bearer behaves impiously; a suitable act of contrition restores use. A stationary relic can likewise stop benefiting a community that offends the Divine.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: The Powers of Relics (ars-magica-realms#038)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to faith eligibility and suspended use after impiety, restored by contrition; a world can make the restriction stricter or more permissive, since divine favor depends on conduct.

rules.statement: To produce a miraculous effect, a character needs scores in both its Method and Power, performs the Method’s activity, then adds a simple die, the linked Characteristic, both Ability scores, and any aura bonus. The effect happens if the total reaches its level; otherwise there is no effect and hubris may cause retribution.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Miraculous Effects (ars-magica-realms#038)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the stated additive test and hubris risk on failure; a world can adjust the target or consequence, because miracles demand both practiced means and divine power.

rules.statement: A character with True Faith may use Faith score times 10 instead of the rolled effect total when checking whether a failed attempt causes hubris. Hubris can impose listed ability loss, flaws, wounds, botch dice, Warping, Decrepitude, possession, or regional disaster, with severity based on the failure margin.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Tragedies of Hubris (ars-magica-realms#038)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to Faith cushioning hubris and escalating consequences by failure margin; a world can change which consequences are permanent, since the Divine response reflects the transgression.

rules.statement: Invocation calls on divine aid and requires Confidence; Meditation uses inward concentration; Purity forgoes bodily needs and usually costs long-term Fatigue. Each Method works only with its listed Powers.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Methods and Traditions (ars-magica-realms#038)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to distinct activation practices, with Purity costing long-term Fatigue and Invocation requiring Confidence; a world can change these costs because each tradition approaches miracles differently.

rules.statement: A holy effect that would need an Arcane Connection uses a holy connection instead. Hermetic limits on Duration and Target do not apply, but the effect’s level increases by 20; Boundary, Year, and permanent effects are generally treated as four magnitudes more difficult for comparison.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Powers and Effects (ars-magica-realms#038)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to holy connections and the stated +20 level adjustment; a world can alter the adjustment or connection requirements to balance the unusual freedom from Hermetic limits.

rules.statement: A tradition may favor at most four Abilities. A character with True Faith studying a favored Ability avoids the usual study penalty from total Supernatural Ability scores, but can receive this benefit from only one tradition; other members without True Faith cannot learn that tradition’s favored Abilities.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Learning Methods and Powers (ars-magica-realms#038)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one favored tradition and a four-Ability ceiling; a world can change access or the ceiling, since traditions guard and teach distinct practices.

rules.statement: While concentrating on a general Transcendence effect, the character cannot be targeted by spells or powers below the effect level plus 5. Transcendence can also grant specific protections, such as raising Soak by the effect magnitude plus 3 or resisting all physical damage at level 30.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Transcendence Guidelines (ars-magica-realms#039)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to blocking supernatural targeting below the level threshold; a world can narrow protection to particular effects, since broad protection is costly in effect level.

rules.statement: Transcendence can project perception to another location at level 5 and permit travel to any place within range in an instant at level 40. Spending too long in this state may cause Warping and related effects, while departure can leave the body apparently dead or comatose and usually erases memories of the journey.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Transcendence (ars-magica-realms#039)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to allowing spiritual departure and return; a world can increase the duration risk, with Warping or bodily harm as the price.

rules.statement: Understanding visions become less focused as a character pursues a subject further, and repeating questions tends to cause confusion rather than clarity. Its revelations may mislead, omit mundane or sinful possibilities, or overwhelm the mortal mind.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Understanding (ars-magica-realms#039)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to imperfect, increasingly diffuse insight; a world can make repeated inquiry more dangerous, risking confusion or mental harm.

rules.statement: A character with the True Faith Virtue begins with Score 1 and one Faith Point; a character's Magic Resistance equals Score times 10. At dawn, Faith Points recover up to the Score, but points above that threshold do not replenish.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Taking the True Faith Virtue (ars-magica-realms#039)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to daily recovery capped by the Faith Score; a world can raise the score for stronger resistance, at the rare cost of additional Major Virtues.

rules.statement: A test of faith can suspend use of Faith Points and Holy Virtues until a specified condition is met or a period such as a month or year passes. During a crisis of faith, the character loses Faith Points and holy powers stop working, with no fixed recovery time or guaranteed task that restores them.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Tests of Faith; Crises of Faith (ars-magica-realms#039)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to temporarily disabling holy benefits during a spiritual trial; a world can set a longer or condition-based test, paid for by the character's loss of supernatural support.

rules.statement: To pray for a miracle, spend a Faith Point and roll True Faith Score plus Concentration plus Aura against the chosen holy effect's level; each extra Faith Point spent adds 3. A successful miracle has infinite Penetration and cannot be resisted, reversed, or changed by supernatural powers.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Praying for Miracles (ars-magica-realms#039)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a powerful but costly divine effect that consumes Faith; a world can make a request harder through its timeliness and need modifiers, with divine intervention remaining beyond opposition.

rules.statement: A miracle's level is adjusted for when it arrives and how justified the request is: immediacy adds 10, while a generation-long delay subtracts 20; need ranges from a 15-point reduction for calamitous need to a 20-point increase for an impious request. A botched prayer removes all Faith Points for a number of weeks equal to botches, or bars unanswered prayers for that many months if the character has no points.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Miraculous Special Effects; Botching (ars-magica-realms#039)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to making urgent or selfish requests harder and botches costly; a world can shift these modifiers, trading speed or righteousness for a higher level.

rules.statement: Only living people can have True Faith; on death, a faithful character enters Heaven, gains Divine Might equal to Score times 10, and gives up True Faith. True Faith itself cannot be targeted, detected, suppressed, or altered by supernatural powers.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: True Faith (ars-magica-realms#039)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to an inviolable living bond with the Divine that converts to Divine Might at death; a world can change the afterlife reward, but not manipulate the bond directly.
