rules.statement: At True Faith 2, a character gains Premonitions and can spend 1 Faith Point to dispel any supernatural illusion or Faerie glamour, regardless of its level. At True Faith 3, spending a Faith Point as Confidence adds 6 instead of 3, and Magic Resistance against Mentem effects is doubled.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Hope: True Faith 3; preceding True Faith Score 2 paragraph (ars-magica-realms#040)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the stated thresholds and benefits; a setting can alter Faith-point potency or dispelling scope, reflecting how strongly divine conviction contests supernatural influence.

rules.statement: At True Faith 5, a character radiates a Divine Empyreal aura rated at the True Faith Score minus 4, extending to Voice range. It interacts with other auras and supernatural powers like a normal Divine aura, can overwhelm weaker auras or be overwhelmed by stronger ones, and may be tempered by the character.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Charity: True Faith 5 (ars-magica-realms#040)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to an aura rating of Faith minus 4 and Voice range; a world can change its reach or strength, with the aura's influence on nearby powers and places as the consequence.

rules.statement: A character present when a miracle of level 30 or higher occurs gains 1 Warping Point, except when directly affected by a miracle intended for that character or when praying for its benefit. Continuous miracles do not cause Warping through constant exposure; each zero on a botch die while using a holy power or divine supernatural ability adds 1 Warping Point.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Causes of Divine Warping: Miracles; Botches (ars-magica-realms#040)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the level-30 threshold, the stated exemptions, and one point per botch zero; a setting can shift the threshold or exposure rules, trading supernatural intensity against lasting change.

rules.statement: A holy character with a Holy Power or Miraculous Ability who gains at least 2 Warping Points from one event checks for Divine Ascent. Roll Presence + Concentration or Meditation + a stress die against Warping Score + Warping Points gained + True Faith Score + local aura + a stress die; on failure, the character ascends and gains additional Warping Points equal to the failure margin, which do not trigger another check.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: The Divine Ascent: Ascension (ars-magica-realms#040)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the two-point trigger, opposed totals, and margin-based extra Warping; a world can change the trigger or destination, making ascent more or less likely and costly.

rules.statement: An ascent lasts Warping Score plus all Warping Points gained in days, at least 1 day; True Faith subtracts its score from the duration. At Warping Score 6 or higher, the base duration is in months instead of days. The body either remains in the mundane world, immune to supernatural powers, illness, deprivation, and wounds, or vanishes and returns to its former location when the ascent ends.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: The Divine Ascent: Experiencing the Ascent (ars-magica-realms#040)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the score-based duration and either protected-body or vanished-body option; a world can change the time unit or bodily risk, with separation from mundane life as the cost.

rules.statement: During Divine Gloom, each Warping Point gained also grants the same number of Experience Points for Dominion Lore, Holy Power Abilities, or Ability Scores of holy-source Virtues, while the same number of Experience Points must be removed from mundane-focused Abilities. The character also attracts beings from the Invisible World.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Divine Gloom: Game Effects (ars-magica-realms#040)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to equal experience gained and lost, plus attracting supernatural beings; a world can change the exchange or attraction, balancing sacred insight against mundane loss and danger.

rules.statement: Divine Form gives Magic Resistance equal to Warping Score, stacking with True Faith resistance but not other sources; Penetration equals Warping Score plus five times Faith Score. For a required roll tied to an impious act, add three botch dice per Warping Score; venial sin causes an unsoakable light wound and mortal sin an unsoakable medium wound, healable naturally or by miracle only.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Divine Form: Game Effects (ars-magica-realms#040)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the listed resistance, penetration, botch, and wound formulas; a world can change the penalties for impiety, making holiness mechanically powerful but costly to violate.

rules.statement: In Divine Unity, choose a virtue; the character adds Warping Score to its associated Personality Trait. People in regular company for a season or more are affected by Holy Influence using that virtue, and an aura occupied for a season or more takes a temper suited to it, possibly causing Schism.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Divine Unity: Game Effects (ars-magica-realms#040)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to season-long exposure and a Warping-score trait bonus; a world can change the duration or whether the aura shifts, allowing a person's exemplified virtue to reshape others and places.

rules.statement: Sacraments affect only participants who willingly accept them. Once accepted, supernatural resistance cannot prevent the sacrament’s effect; many grant Faith Points, but a character can hold only one unspent point from any particular sacrament.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: The Sacraments (ars-magica-realms#041)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to willing acceptance and unresistible effects; a world can restrict which rites grant Faith Points, since their blessing depends on the participant’s acceptance.

rules.statement: Excommunication removes the character’s sacramental benefits and any Confidence or Faith Points gained, and treats the character as never baptized. Repentance followed by penance can restore the connection to the Church.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Excommunication (ars-magica-realms#041)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to immediate loss of Church benefits; a world can make restoration harder or easier, with repentance and penance as the stated route back.

rules.statement: An interdict lowers the Dominion aura across the affected realm by 1 each year until the interdict is lifted; local church auras can nearly disappear while churches remain empty.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Interdiction (ars-magica-realms#041)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a one-level yearly decline; a world can vary the affected territory or duration, with closed churches and withheld sacraments driving the decline.

rules.statement: A first baptism expels possessing spirits and cancels nonpermanent supernatural effects on the subject unless they belong to the Divine realm. The baptismal name is protected from use as a magical True Name.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: The Sacraments — Baptism (ars-magica-realms#041)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to cleansing only at the subject’s first baptism; a world can change which influences are removed, while Divine effects remain outside the rite’s reach.

rules.statement: After Extreme Unction, the deceased cannot be affected by other supernatural powers for three days. Christian burial then prevents necromancy or magic from affecting the spirit, although the body can be affected if physically removed from the churchyard.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: The Sacraments — Extreme Unction (ars-magica-realms#041)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to three days of protection followed by protection of the buried spirit; a world can change the duration or burial condition, with removal of the body as the stated vulnerability.

rules.statement: The Dominion tends to weaken substantially on the eve of major holy days. During the twelve days from Christmas through Epiphany, supernatural boundaries blur, and storyguides may let suitable Faerie and Magic powers ignore Dominion penalties.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Church Calendar (ars-magica-realms#041)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a seasonal weakening and reduced penalties during the Christmas period; a world can change which holidays or powers are affected, as supernatural boundaries loosen.

rules.statement: A Christian’s mortal sin removes the state of grace; penance and absolution are needed to avoid damnation. Venial sins instead add to the time the soul is expected to spend in Purgatory.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Beliefs — sin and penance (ars-magica-realms#041)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to mortal sin breaking grace and venial sin adding Purgatory time; a world can adjust the severity of particular acts, with penance and absolution as remedies.

rules.statement: Marriage gives each spouse a Faith Point to use against temptation or adversity, but that benefit is lost if the marriage is annulled or a spouse sins against the other. The blessing is also believed to aid childbirth and healthy offspring if the marriage lasts until a child is born.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: The Sacraments — Marriage (ars-magica-realms#041)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one Faith Point per spouse with the stated loss conditions; a world can change the blessing’s benefits, which depend on the marriage continuing.

rules.statement: In these ordeals, the accused performs a public ritual test and the court treats its outcome as divine judgment: failure to show the prescribed sign of innocence results in presumed guilt and execution. In the combat ordeal, the loser is charged with making a false claim if he survives.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Ordeals (ars-magica-realms#042)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the stated test outcome deciding guilt; a world can turn how reliably divine intervention produces the sign, because people trust the ordeal to reveal innocence.

rules.statement: A relic’s Faith score sets its Faith points and Divine Might at ten times that score. Ordinary finger-bone and True Cross fragments each have 1 Faith point and Divine Might 10; St Martin’s bones have 4 of each and can provide suitable healing miracles to a truly pious petitioner, but cannot do so again until dawn once their Might is spent.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Christian Relics (ars-magica-realms#042)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to relic Faith determining its reserve and the relic supplying its listed miracle; a world can turn the piety requirement or recovery, with access limited by spent Might and dawn.

rules.statement: The Mantle of Nerius lets its wearer go without food while it is worn; activating this effect costs 4 Might points. The mantle has Faith 3, 3 Faith points, and Divine Might 30.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: The Mantle of Nerius (ars-magica-realms#042)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the garment sustaining only its current wearer while worn; a world can turn the activation cost, paid from its limited Might reserve.

rules.statement: The Holy Lance can invoke Celestial Immunity on the nearest 10 people, at an increased cost of 15 Might. It has Faith 7, 7 Faith points, and Divine Might 70.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: The Holy Lance (ars-magica-realms#042)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to protecting the nearest ten targets; a world can turn the target cap or cost, with the relic’s Might paying for the protection.

rules.statement: Christian exorcism either lets a possessed person roll to resist an infernal effect that permits resistance, or petitions for a miracle when it does not. Performing the rite properly costs the exorcist one Confidence or Faith point; holy water and a crucifix each add +1 to the subject’s total, and extra Faith points spent by the exorcist also add to it.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Exorcism (ars-magica-realms#042)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to an attempt to free the victim, using a resistance roll when possible; a world can turn the rite’s bonuses or prerequisites, while the exorcist pays a Confidence or Faith point.

rules.statement: If both the Eastern patriarch and the pope exert holy influence over the same aura and temper it, the Dominion becomes conflicted and great confusion results in the East.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Two Churches (ars-magica-realms#042)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to conflicting authority making the shared aura confused; a world can turn whether both influences can be applied, since each institution claims spiritual authority there.

rules.statement: A person may petition a saint once per day without a special Ability or Virtue. Roll Communication + Charm + modifiers + a simple die against 15 plus a hidden simple die; success gets the requested aid if it is within that saint’s powers, while failure gives no aid until another petition the next day. Recent miracles and an unfamiliar or non-patron saint impose –20 and –15 respectively.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Invoking a Saint; Invocation Modifiers (ars-magica-realms#043)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one petition per day with a secret divine difficulty; a setting can alter access or modifiers to reflect how familiar, favored, or recently helped the petitioner is.

rules.statement: After a failed petition, a person may force a specific miracle attempt by rolling Presence + Leadership + modifiers + a stress die against 9 plus one fifth of the saint’s Divine Might; Confidence may be spent, but Faith Points may not. Success immediately grants a miracle in the saint’s repertoire; failure bars petitions for a month, a result at least 10 below the target also brings a minor curse and a season without aid, and a botch brings the saint’s curse.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Threatening a Saint (ars-magica-realms#043)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to escalating penalties as the threat roll worsens; a world can make coercion more or less dangerous, with the saint’s displeasure and loss of future aid as the cost.

rules.statement: Saints have no independent miracle power: God supplies the power they channel, and saints cannot forgive sins. A saint’s available powers are generally limited to a total use cost no greater than one fifth of Divine Might, though this is only a guideline.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Saints’ Miracles; Designing Saints (ars-magica-realms#043)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to miracles being delegated divine effects and cap a saint’s listed power costs at one fifth of Might; a setting can loosen that guideline to represent exceptional divine favor.

rules.statement: A saint’s spirits have no corporeal form and cannot be harmed by physical means. Apparition can make a physical-seeming manifestation, but weapons and objects pass through it without causing harm.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Designing Saints; Powers (ars-magica-realms#043)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to saints being intangible and physically invulnerable, even when visible; a world can allow a more embodied manifestation at the cost of changing the nature of the spirit.

rules.statement: Celestial Immunity prevents all physical injury while an imminent threat remains, then ends when that danger has passed. The Incombustible Shroud instead protects its target from fire damage regardless of the fire’s scale or strength.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Saints’ Miracles — Powers (ars-magica-realms#043)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to protection ending when its stated danger ends, or being limited to a named harm; a setting can broaden its coverage, trading specificity for greater protection.

rules.statement: Raising the dead restores a corpse only if its soul has not been accepted into Heaven; souls in Purgatory or Hell can still be raised. This miracle costs 7 points.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Saints’ Miracles — Powers (ars-magica-realms#043)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to revival being possible only while the soul remains outside Heaven; a world can change the soul-state boundary, making the afterlife’s judgment the limiting cost.

rules.statement: A saint’s invocation roll receives circumstance modifiers: being at the tomb or touching a relic gives +1, the feast day +3, a recent pilgrimage +2, imminent peril +2, and a donation +1 to +3. True Faith adds +1 per Faith Score; a recent unchristian act penalizes –1 to –3, and no donation in a year penalizes –3.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Invocation Modifiers (ars-magica-realms#043)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to devotion, proximity, and peril improving the chance of aid, while misconduct and neglect reduce it; a world can tune the importance of each sign of devotion.

rules.statement: The Neriusian Portal creates a minor, level-1, single-layer terrestrial regio around its caster for Sun duration. The enclosed area is hidden from the mundane world and is accessible by regio rules, but the caster may enter or leave at will; the rite uses Purity and Intervention for ceremonial casting.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: The Neriusian Portal (CrVi65) (ars-magica-realms#043)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a temporary hidden regio accessible under the usual regio rules, with the caster exempted; a setting can alter duration, layer, or access at the cost of greater ritual power.

rules.statement: Holy Music works through a devotional song: roll Presence + Music against an Ease Factor set by circumstances, then use Presence to determine the effect. Distraction requires a Concentration roll to maintain focus; the Holy Music Ability is described as working like Meditation to gain divine insight.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Abilities — Holy Music (ars-magica-realms#043)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to focused devotional music producing an insight effect after a successful performance roll; a world can vary the effect or the difficulty according to circumstances and distraction.

rules.statement: Only a Christian Gifted reader can learn the Notory Art, and initially it must be learned from the original text. Reading it accurately requires scores of at least 4 in Latin, Greek, Hebrew, and Chaldean, plus Artes Liberales 4; translating the text destroys its magic.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Studying the Text (ars-magica-realms#044)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Require the four languages and the stated minimum scores; a setting can relax the literacy barrier, but doing so risks altering or losing the text’s sacred power.

rules.statement: A ring succeeds when Intelligence + Ars Notoria + modifiers + a stress die meets its Ease Factor. A first recitation uses EF 6 + 3 times the ring level + 1 per season of desired duration; later recitations of that ring use EF 3 + 3 times its level + 1 per season.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: The Rings of Solomon (ars-magica-realms#044)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Use the listed thresholds and let prior mastery reduce difficulty; a world can make devotion more or less decisive, with impiety and sin imposing the stated penalties.

rules.statement: Fasting grants +1 to the recitation score per season, but each season requires a Stamina + stress die roll against EF 6, increasing the EF by 1 for every consecutive season. Failure ends the fast; a botch permanently lowers Stamina by 1 through aging.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Ars Notoria Modifiers (ars-magica-realms#044)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Apply the fasting bonus and escalating endurance test; a world can make fasting safer or harsher, trading greater recitation power for bodily risk.

rules.statement: The first recitation of a ring takes a full season. A later recitation takes 10 days minus the practitioner’s Ars Notoria score, but never less than one day.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: The Rings of Solomon (ars-magica-realms#044)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Use the stated time reduction with a one-day minimum; a world can lengthen the observance, costing more time to renew a benefit.

rules.statement: Rings must first be successfully learned in order from the first through the seventh. Afterward, known rings can be recited in any order; repeating an active ring extends its duration rather than stacking its benefits.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: The Rings of Solomon (ars-magica-realms#044)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Enforce ordered mastery and non-stacking; a world can permit overlapping blessings, but that would make repeated recitations substantially more powerful.

rules.statement: While any ring is active, the practitioner gains no Warping Points from a Divine aura. The practitioner may also reduce the Divine-aura penalty on other magic by 3 for each Ars Notoria point.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Beneficial Side-Effects (ars-magica-realms#044)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Apply both protections as written; a world can cap the penalty reduction, preserving some interference from the Divine realm.

rules.statement: A successful fifth-ring recitation lets the practitioner identify a being’s affiliated realm with Perception + Ars Notoria against EF 6 + one-fifth of the target’s Magic Resistance, without penetrating that resistance. Beating its Magic Resistance by 5 reveals its weakest power, and each further 5 reveals another; a botch gives false information.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: The Fifth Ring of Solomon (ars-magica-realms#044)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Use the listed test and information thresholds; a world can make some beings harder to read, at the cost of less reliable identification.

rules.statement: The seventh ring replaces simple die rolls with stress rolls and prevents the practitioner from botching. The patron angel can end this benefit if it judges the practitioner to be abusing it through pride.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: The Seventh Ring of Solomon (ars-magica-realms#044)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Grant immunity to botches while the blessing lasts, with the angel as enforcer; a world can make the angel stricter, risking early loss of the boon.

rules.statement: Invoking a particular holy figure for baraka requires being at a shrine associated with that figure; the Qur'an may be invoked anywhere. Invocation rolls use the listed situational modifiers, including +3 on the figure’s feast day, +2 for a pilgrimage to the shrine, and −5 for requesting a specific miracle rather than general aid.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Muslim Invocation Modifiers Table; Sample Muslim Holy Figures (ars-magica-realms#045)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default invocation is limited to the relevant holy place and modified by the table; a setting can broaden access or alter modifiers, with remoteness and unfamiliarity explaining the difficulty.

rules.statement: Muslims may not threaten their holy forbears. Attempting this is treated as blasphemous.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Muslim Invocation Modifiers Table (preceding text) (ars-magica-realms#045)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default forbids threats to holy forbears; a setting could relax the prohibition, at the cost of religious and social consequences.

rules.statement: A Muslim Dominion aura gains 1 point while ritual salat is underway and 1 point during Ramadan or a Muslim holiday. These bonuses stack, so prayer during a holiday raises the aura by 2; after prayer ends, only the holiday bonus remains, and after the holiday the aura returns to normal.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: 2. Salat; 4. Sawm; The Muslim Calendar (ars-magica-realms#045)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default aura increases are temporary and cumulative; a setting could change their size or duration, reflecting how strongly communal observance affects the place.

rules.statement: A creature of the Infernal realm that hears the shahada spoken aloud suffers momentary discomfort; rare creatures suffer actual pain. An Infernal creature that handles goods being directly paid as zakat suffers excruciating pain, but the effect ends once another person or creature has touched the goods.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: 1. Shahada; 3. Zakat (ars-magica-realms#045)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default effects distress Infernal creatures under the specified conditions; a setting can vary which creatures are vulnerable and the severity, according to their nature.

rules.statement: Completing the hajj grants Pious +3 and 3 Faith Points. Repeating the pilgrimage can restore these benefits, but Pious cannot exceed +3 through this means.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: 5. Hajj (ars-magica-realms#045)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default pilgrimage grants the stated trait and points, with the trait capped at +3; a setting can change the reward or cap to reflect the significance of the journey.

rules.statement: A Muslim funeral makes the deceased wait in the grave until the Last Judgment, so most properly buried Muslim ghosts will not answer magical summons. Prophets and martyrs have already passed to Paradise and cannot be summoned regardless of funeral rites; only Muslim ghosts without the prescribed funeral may be summoned.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Death and Inheritance (ars-magica-realms#045)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default funeral observance blocks summoning for ordinary Muslim dead, while prophets and martyrs are always unavailable; a setting could alter the rite’s force or the afterlife’s rules.

rules.statement: The birth rites make a Muslim child’s name unusable as a True Name in supernatural activities, in the same way baptism does for a Christian child.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Birth (ars-magica-realms#045)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default birth rites prevent supernatural use of the child’s name as a True Name; a setting could vary which rites provide this protection and what names remain usable.

rules.statement: The holy ritual boosts the next spell cast immediately afterward by the ritual’s level minus 15, but the bonus cannot exceed ten times the caster’s score in the associated Personality trait. The spell must use only the listed Form or Forms, and receives no bonus if it has other requisites.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: (Immortal)’s Blessing (ars-magica-realms#046)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default the bonus to the ritual level minus 15, capped by ten times the relevant trait; a world could change the cap or eligible Forms, with the Immortals’ associations explaining the restriction.

rules.statement: Saoshyant’s Elixir takes a season to prepare and requires the caster to endure molten metal over the body for three days, survive, and sacrifice a holy animal for the spell’s vis. While the drinker follows Zoroastrianism, aging rolls are skipped and fatal wounds cause incapacitation instead of death, but the drinker gains a Warping point each year, on gaining Aging or Decrepitude points by other means, and when a lethal wound or blow would kill them; the ritual cannot be cast on another and makes any Longevity Ritual ineffective for its duration.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Saoshyant’s Elixir (ars-magica-realms#046)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default the elixir to prevent aging deaths and convert fatal injuries into incapacitation while adding Warping; a world could change the ordeal, sacrifice, or ongoing faith requirement, with survival and spiritual purity as the price.

rules.statement: A Sufi automatically has the Mentor Minor Story Flaw, which gives no points toward buying Virtues. The tariqa supports the Sufi in need, while the shaykh expects commitment to the leader and fellow members.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Virtues — Sufi (ars-magica-realms#046)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default the Sufi’s group support alongside a mandatory mentor obligation; a world could alter the support or the mentor’s demands, with mutual service as the cost.

rules.statement: A non-Muslim adult male under Muslim rule must pay the jizya head tax, usually no more than one dinar per year; all dhimmis must follow social restrictions in return for tolerance and protection from the authorities.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Flaws — Dhimmi (ars-magica-realms#046)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the stated tax and restrictions in exchange for official protection; a world could vary the levy or restrictions, with legal status and social limits as the cost.

rules.statement: A Sufi group’s dhikr or sama’ gradually builds fervor toward an ecstatic state that may bring mystical insight. A shaykh with Ceremony can synchronize participants’ efforts for greater understanding, and non-Sufis find it harder to gain the full benefits.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Traditions — Holy Tradition: Sufis (ars-magica-realms#046)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default group ritual to build fervor and insight, with Ceremony improving coordination; a world could vary the required participation or degree of insight, with access limited by permission and Sufi affiliation.

rules.statement: A person with spiritual authority over a community or place can temper the aura there. A rabbi’s authority covers the community served by his synagogue or school, a chief rabbi’s can cover his city, and the Exilarch’s can reach communities he visits or sends an authorized deputy to.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Holy Influence (ars-magica-realms#047)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default the authority’s reach to their community; a world can widen it to a city or distant communities when office and recognized authority justify the cost.

rules.statement: A Torah scroll made according to ritual custom counts as a relic with one Faith Point. Tefillin ordinarily have no innate power, but those once owned by a hidden righteous one count as a relic with one Faith Point.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Holy Books and Artifacts; A Jewish Library — The Torah (ars-magica-realms#047)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default these objects to no independent effect beyond the stated Faith Point; a world can make provenance grant relic status, at the cost of requiring a qualifying owner or ritual preparation.

rules.statement: A shofar used on a holy day or in a Jewish exorcism rite counts as a relic with one Faith Point; when silent or sounded on another day, it has no power.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Holy Books and Artifacts (ars-magica-realms#047)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default the horn’s power to require the specified occasion; a world can allow broader use only by changing the ritual restriction.

rules.statement: During kapparah, a chicken is circled around a person’s head three times, transferring that person’s sins to the bird; the bird is then killed and given to the poor.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Observances (ars-magica-realms#047)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default the rite to move sins onto the bird; a world can make the transfer literal or symbolic, with the animal’s death and the rite’s disputed standing as costs.

rules.statement: An eruv marks an area as private for Shabbat, allowing essential work inside it despite the general prohibition on work in the public domain.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Observances (ars-magica-realms#047)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default the boundary to reclassify only the enclosed area; a world can vary its size, with the need to establish and maintain the boundary as the limit.

rules.statement: At Rosh ha-Shanah, the living are judged: those granted another year have their names entered in the Book of Names, while those omitted are said to die during that year. At Yom Kippur, their fates are sealed.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Observances (ars-magica-realms#047)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default this as a yearly fate-setting event rather than a usable prediction; a world can make the record accessible, at the cost of exposing a person’s allotted fate.

rules.statement: A target who notices a magus use magic may perform a folk ritual and gain Magic Resistance equal to five times their Magic Lore score against that magus’s magic; without Magic Lore, the resistance is 0. A person with Magic Lore can also try to break a lasting enchantment with an Intelligence + Magic Lore roll against an Ease Factor of 9 plus the spell’s magnitude.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: New Flaw: Vulnerable to Folk Tradition (ars-magica-realms#048)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to allowing an immediate folk countermeasure and a later, harder attempt to undo lasting magic; a world can make such remedies rarer or stronger based on local tradition.

rules.statement: A protective charm made by a Ba'al Shem or a character with Craft Amulets grants resistance equal to five times its maker’s Magic Lore; the charm need not itself be magical. For Jewish magi, touching such a charm protects against the described vulnerability to folk tradition.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: New Flaw: Vulnerable to Folk Tradition (ars-magica-realms#048)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a nonmagical charm providing a maker-scaled defense; a world can limit its effectiveness by requiring a skilled maker or a specific protective purpose.

rules.statement: The Evil Eye causes each character making stress rolls in the afflicted person’s presence to take one additional botch die. An amulet or troupe-defined ritual, or Magic Resistance of 0 or more, prevents this effect.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: The Evil Eye (ars-magica-realms#048)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a passive harmful aura checked by simple folk protection or any positive resistance; a world can make the danger more severe or less common according to the bearer’s control.

rules.statement: Cherem excludes a person from Jewish society until amends are made or the sanction otherwise ends; its restrictions include mourning dress, uncut hair, no shoes, and exclusion from the community count and formal funeral rites. Nezifah is a housebound sanction from business and pleasure, usually lasting no more than a day; karet is a spiritual death that may be lifted by open repentance.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Cherem and Karet (ars-magica-realms#048)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to sanctions that impose defined social or spiritual consequences until lifted by repentance; a world can vary their duration and severity through the authority of its court.

rules.statement: The City of Luz bars the Angel of Death; people inside its level 7 regio age but do not die, and may leave at any time. After a stay longer than a year, leaving forces an immediate aging roll using true age and a penalty of −1 for every five years spent there.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: The City of Luz (ars-magica-realms#048)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to death being prevented inside the city while aging continues, with accumulated time charged upon departure; a world can adjust the grace or the aging penalty.

rules.statement: The City of Luz is reached through an opening in an almond tree in the Holy Land, or by a divinely granted vision of that tree that acts as a route. Summoning a pathway to the gates requires a base 35 Purity or Merkavah miraculous effect and a Holy Connection to the city or tree.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: The City of Luz (ars-magica-realms#048)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a specific, connection-dependent route into a layered place; a world can make the gateway easier to find or require the full miraculous procedure.

rules.statement: Jewish amulets have Touch range and Worn duration, equivalent to Sun, and can target an Individual, Room, Structure, or Boundary. They remain active until broken or removed; a Boundary-targeted amulet adds 20 to the effect level, and non-Individual targets require the amulet to touch or be buried beneath them.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Craft Amulets (ars-magica-realms#048)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to an effect carried by an amulet that lasts while it stays in place; a world can broaden target size or reduce the extra cost for Boundary coverage.

rules.statement: Amulet shapes, materials, and colors can add bonuses to crafting totals, but their combined bonus cannot exceed the maker’s Craft Amulets score. Some specified designs grant +10 to a particular effect, such as copper name-plates buried at the four compass points to locate a named person; an amulet’s prescribed wearing or burial ritual must be followed for it to work.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Shape and Material Bonuses (ars-magica-realms#048)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to capped bonuses from suitable materials and exact ritual placement; a world can allow other correspondences while retaining the Craft Amulets score as the cost ceiling.

rules.statement: A Karaite magus must design all magic, including spells, enchantments, and longevity rituals, using Holy Magic rather than Magic Theory, and cannot accept healing or other magical effects from non-Karaites. Divination, astrology, and spirit use are restricted; performing them, or receiving non-Karaite magic, makes the target ritually unclean and risks Holy Magic failing until cleansing.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Karaite Magic (ars-magica-realms#048)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a faith-bound magic system with prohibited practices and a cleansing requirement after violations; a world can make the failure risk more or less immediate.

rules.statement: A Minor amulet is made for one specific target, takes (12 minus the crafter’s Craft Amulets score, minimum 1) hours, and requires a Craft Amulets Total at least twice the effect’s level. Its effect usually lasts days or weeks according to construction quality.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Amulets (ars-magica-realms#049)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to single-target amulets with short, quality-dependent duration; a world can lengthen their life at the cost of better construction.

rules.statement: A Major amulet requires consecutive seasons of work: each point by which the Craft Amulets Total exceeds the effect level adds one progress point, and the effect level must be reached. A maker can work on only one Major amulet per season.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Amulets (ars-magica-realms#049)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one long project at a time; a world can permit parallel work by relaxing the crafter’s seasonal commitment.

rules.statement: Amulets begin with penetration 0. A designed-in effect can gain 2 penetration for each effect level spent; Holy or Arcane Connections provide penetration based on their base multiplier, while sympathetic connections modify connection-based penetration but not designed-in penetration.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Amulets (ars-magica-realms#049)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to no penetration unless resources or effect levels are committed; a world can make amulets more penetrating by increasing their crafting cost.

rules.statement: Dream divination requires a prepared night’s sleep and (6 minus Dream Interpretation, minimum 1) hours of reflection, then an Intelligence plus Dream Interpretation roll; Premonitions adds its score. Its difficulty matches an equivalent Momentary, non-ritual Intellego spell, with an Arcane Connection treated as Touch and Boundary needing no ritual.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Dream Interpretation (ars-magica-realms#049)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to dream answers limited by an equivalent spell’s difficulty; a world can make access easier or harder by changing preparation and the question’s effective range.

rules.statement: Changing a true name through Shinnui Shem takes a season, severs existing Arcane Connections to the person, and grants a bonus to Aging Rolls equal to (Simple Die + Intelligence + Gematria + Understanding + Book Quality + Dominion Aura) divided by 5. The benefit ends when the person next gains an Aging Point, cannot stack with other supernatural aging bonuses, and each person can undergo the change only once.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Jewish Mysticism — Shinnui Shem (ars-magica-realms#049)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a one-time seasonal rite that temporarily protects against aging and breaks existing links; a world can extend the benefit by making the rite repeatable or cumulative.

rules.statement: To awaken a golem, the first season forms and inscribes its clay body; later seasons build progress, with each point above Ease Factor 30 adding one Might point. Final Might adds a Stress Die, is capped at five times the lead kabbalist’s Kabbalah score, and botch dice equal the number of participants.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Golems — Creating Golems (ars-magica-realms#049)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a multi-season creation process with a score-based Might cap; a world can allow stronger golems by raising the cap or lowering the creation difficulty.

rules.statement: A golem can hold powers whose total magnitudes do not exceed its Divine Might. Each power costs its magnitude in Might to use, acts at the golem’s Quickness, and its Might pool refreshes at sunset; removing an existing power adds its level to the Empower Golem Total when designing a replacement.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Golems — Empowering Golems; Altering the Golem’s Powers (ars-magica-realms#049)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a Might-limited power capacity and daily renewal; a world can allow more frequent use by speeding recovery, at the cost of weakening the resource limit.

rules.statement: A golem can be sent into torpor by a member of its protected community if its Trusting trait is positive. In torpor it needs no food, drink, or air and does not age, and it can be set to awaken on command or when a specified event occurs.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Golems — Destroying a Golem (ars-magica-realms#049)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to community members being able to place a trusting golem into event-triggered stasis; a world can restrict who may command this, trading convenience for security.

rules.statement: Infernal aura strength ranges from 1 to 10. At 1–2 it encourages irritability and paranoia or depression; at 3–5 it also stunts plants and fouls the surroundings; at 6–8 it can make the landscape hazardous and support dangerous beasts and demonic delusions; at 9–10 it subjects lingering people to intense hallucinations, obsessions, and risk of serious harm.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Infernal Auras (ars-magica-realms#050)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: aura strength determines escalating environmental and mental harm; a world can tune the tier effects, because local evil manifests differently.

rules.statement: An Infernal aura spreads outward from a focus but follows mundane barriers such as walls and doors; its strength may vary near the focus or remain uniform. Its footprint is independent of its strength, and it gains 1 strength at night and additional strength on unholy nights, never exceeding 10.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Infernal Auras in Play (ars-magica-realms#050)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: aura follows barriers and gains strength at night; a world can alter its reach or calendar, because corruption follows local geography and observance.

rules.statement: In a community where everyone observes Shabbat, an Infernal aura falls by 1 from Friday sunset to Saturday sunset; one violation cancels this effect. In Christian lands it rises by 1 on the Wednesday before Easter and remains elevated through Good Friday, then falls to 0 at dusk until Easter Monday; it recovers evenly over the following week. In Islamic lands it falls to 0 until dawn on the Night of Destiny, then stays 2 below its earlier strength until Ramadan ends. An Interdict raises it by 1.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Infernal Auras in Play (ars-magica-realms#050)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: religious observances temporarily change aura strength as specified; a world can choose which calendar applies, because local faith and holy days shape the effect.

rules.statement: A weaker Infernal aura inside a stronger supernatural aura is normally dormant and loses 1 strength for each number of years equal to its current strength. It does not erode while equal to the dominant aura, when it becomes dominant at night, when manifested evil actively maintains it, or after a successful maintenance corruption roll resets its erosion period.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Infernal Auras in Play (ars-magica-realms#050)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a stronger aura wears down a weaker, neglected Infernal one on a strength-based schedule; a world can change the schedule or what counts as upkeep, because active evil sustains corruption.

rules.statement: After a major sin that imperils the sinner’s soul, roll a stress die plus temporary Infernal aura strength. Exceeding 3 plus the dominant aura strength maintains a weaker aura by resetting its erosion period; exceeding 6 plus that strength creates an aura of 1 or increases an existing one by 1, replacing the dominant aura if it becomes strongest. Aura strength cannot exceed 10.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: The Formation of an Infernal Aura (ars-magica-realms#050)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: major sin can create or strengthen an aura when the roll beats the stated thresholds; a world can adjust the thresholds, because existing supernatural influence resists corruption.

rules.statement: A corruption rite formalizes a mortal sin so a corruption roll can be made, but its ritual trappings do not affect the roll. The practitioner may spend Confidence Points to influence the outcome, a sacrifice grants its specified bonus, and the rite cannot succeed more than once per season.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: The Formation of an Infernal Aura (ars-magica-realms#050)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the rite enables an aura-forming roll, with Confidence or sacrifice as optional leverage and a seasonal limit; a world can change the limit or price, because Hell is not freely summoned.

rules.statement: Only a permanent Infernal aura that dominates its locality imposes supernatural effects on residents; temporary Infernal auras cannot acquire tarnish or corruption. Permanent Infernal auras modify supernatural-power use and penalize recovery from wounds, diseases, or deprivation by the aura strength; diseases treated there cannot improve, and at least one recovery roll remains penalized after leaving.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Effects of an Infernal Aura (ars-magica-realms#051)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a persistent local field with strength-based penalties; vary whether an aura dominates its area, reflecting the locality’s concentrated evil.

rules.statement: A tarnish assigns a sinful Personality Trait to an aura, and everyone within it shifts that trait by the aura strength, including an equal shift in the opposite direction for its opposing trait. Indulging in a matching sin while affected counts as ritualized sin, giving a Warping Point and a Confidence Point.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Tarnished Auras (ars-magica-realms#051)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a subtle, strength-scaled emotional influence; a world can vary the tarnish, with moral compromise costing a Warping Point.

rules.statement: A corrupted aura is permanently tarnished, cannot have its tarnish changed by an Infernalist, and has strength of at least 3. Its special features may impose further effects that encourage sin.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Corrupted Auras (ars-magica-realms#051)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a lasting field with fixed character and strength of at least 3; allow stronger custom effects at the cost of entrenched corruption.

rules.statement: In a Debauched aura, Confidence Points cannot be spent. Example features can require an opposed Personality roll at Ease Factor 3 plus aura strength to leave, a roll at 6 plus aura strength to resist returning after sinning there, permanently shift a related trait by 1, or cost a Fatigue level for each resistance roll.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Debauched Auras (ars-magica-realms#051)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to temptation that drains resolve and may entrench a trait; tune the roll difficulties and fatigue cost to the aura’s strength.

rules.statement: Malevolent auras may add their strength to Damage totals, add that many botch dice to physical activities, corrupt creatures that dwell there, and reopen old wounds inflicted by Infernal entities. A former Incapacitating Wound returns as Medium, a former Heavy Wound as Light, and lesser wounds as cuts or scratches.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Malevolent Auras (ars-magica-realms#051)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to escalating physical danger based on aura strength; worlds can choose which listed harms apply, at the cost of injury and corruption.

rules.statement: In an Abyssal regio, all eight Characteristics are reduced by the aura strength while a character remains there. Each day, an Intelligence roll against the aura strength is required; failure gives a listed mental Flaw that fades after that many weeks, unless the roll botches, in which case it is permanent.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Abyssal Regiones (ars-magica-realms#051)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to an ongoing strength-scaled suppression plus daily risk of mental damage; adjust the aura strength to set the severity and duration.

rules.statement: In a Tartaran regio, Fatigue suffered counts as long-term and cannot be recovered until departure. Direct contact with its fire deals +5 to +35 damage, and heat or fire damage gains an additional amount equal to the victim’s sinful Personality Trait scores, counting negative scores in sinless traits as sinful.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Tartaran Regiones (ars-magica-realms#051)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a hazardous environmental field whose fire and fatigue effects persist until escape; vary damage with exposure and the victim’s sins.

rules.statement: Infernal vis risks depend on its variety: vis infesta adds one botch die per pawn and worsens botches; vis sordida adds three botch dice per pawn, with at least one per pawn, and gives non-Infernal users +5 to casting totals per pawn; vis prava forces a zero and a botch check with two extra botch dice per pawn and at least one per pawn. Infernal-aligned users avoid these disadvantages; vis prava instead gives them +5 to casting totals per pawn.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Infernal Vis (ars-magica-realms#051)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to graded consumable vis with increasing botch risk and special benefits for Infernal users; tune the risk by vis type and alignment.

rules.statement: A demon spends 1 Might point per 10 Might, or fraction, to form its one specified solid body; forming it takes one round per point of Infernal Might. It can dissolve the body in one uninterrupted round of concentration, and its statistics do not change, though spiritual form cannot use physical Characteristics.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Coagulation (ars-magica-realms#053)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one fixed physical shape with a Might-scaled formation time; a setting can vary what matter supports the body, because the power gathers ambient substance.

rules.statement: When a mortal indulges a venial sin, a demon can spend 1–3 Might points to impose its matching Obsession Trait, provided the effect penetrates Magic Resistance. At the next opportunity to indulge, resistance can prevent the effect; failure permanently adds or raises the trait by 1.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Obsession (ars-magica-realms#053)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to requiring a sinful opening and a successful resistance test; a setting can make corruption easier or harder, because the imposed impulse exploits existing vice.

rules.statement: A demon can enter a sleeper’s dream for 1 Might point, or impose a waking vision for 5; the waking vision may stun for a round, and extreme terror requires a Brave roll against Ease Factor 9 to avoid a severe reaction. A spiritual demon can use this power as its sole means of communicating with mortals.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Envisioning (ars-magica-realms#053)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to gradual dream distortion but immediate waking hallucinations; a setting can raise the cost or severity, because waking visions overwhelm the target’s ordinary perception.

rules.statement: A demon transfers any chosen number of Might points into a host as a separate pool, which does not regenerate until possession ends at zero. Spending more points enables greater action but weakens Penetration; use of the host’s supernatural abilities costs points according to their magnitude or ability score, and forcing actions against the host’s nature also costs points.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Possession (ars-magica-realms#053)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a finite, nonrenewing possession pool; a world can alter the expenditure rates, because the demon’s power is invested in the host until released.

rules.statement: Hermetic magic cannot reveal demonic deceptions or sense a demon’s Infernal nature. Second Sight normally detects naturally invisible things at Ease Factor 9, but a non-Divine source cannot pierce demonic illusions; Divine Second Sight uses Ease Factor 6 plus the demon’s Might magnitude.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Demons and Magic (ars-magica-realms#053)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to Hermetic detection failing against demonic concealment; a setting can allow other senses to pierce it, because Divine perception is treated differently.

rules.statement: A demon normally restores its full Might in 24 hours, at Infernal Might divided by 24 points per hour. In an Infernal aura of rating A, it restores its full pool in 24 − 2A hours; in a Divine aura it restores none.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Demons, Auras, and Regiones (ars-magica-realms#053)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to ordinary recovery outside Infernal auras and no recovery in Divine ones; a world can adjust the aura rate, because ambient supernatural influence changes replenishment.

rules.statement: A relic radiates a holy area whose radius in feet equals its Divine Might; a demon may enter only if its Infernal Might exceeds that score, and while inside it takes damage equal to the relic’s Divine Might each round, soakable normally.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Demonic Weaknesses (ars-magica-realms#053)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a Might-scaled exclusion and damage zone; a setting can alter the area or harm, because holiness actively opposes Infernal presence.

rules.statement: A demon’s True Name is an enduring Arcane Connection that adds +5 to the Penetration Multiplier against an Infernal creature. Learning one costs 5 Infernal Lore experience points, and grants 1 additional experience point in that Ability.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: True Names (ars-magica-realms#053)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a durable name-based connection with a fixed penetration bonus; a setting can change access or bonus, because the name links to the creature’s spiritual essence.

rules.statement: A Deluder spends 1 Might point for an illusion affecting an Individual amount of material or 5 points for an illusion filling a room; every illusion has some flaw. A Deluder can also reproduce a non-Ritual Hermetic spell matching one of its available Techniques for 1 Might point per magnitude, but the spell’s level cannot exceed its Infernal Might.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Deluders — Powers (ars-magica-realms#054)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to flawed illusions and Might-paid spell imitation; a world can vary the flaw or cost because deception is the demon’s specialty and its reserve limits output.

rules.statement: An Aerial Power spends 1 Might point per magnitude to create a Creo, Muto, or Rego effect in its chosen elemental Form; the effect cannot exceed its Infernal Might or duplicate a Ritual. Attempts to control rather than destroy one treat its Might as 1.5 times its actual value, or raise the relevant Ease Factor by 50%.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Aerial Powers — Powers (ars-magica-realms#054)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one calamity-linked elemental Form and heightened resistance to control; a world can adjust the resistance because these demons are especially difficult to restrain.

rules.statement: A Fury can force a victim’s passion to overcome reason; the victim rolls against Ease Factor 9, adjusted by relevant Personality Traits. It can also grant the Berserk Virtue for 1 point, lasting until the target calms down.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Furies — Powers (ars-magica-realms#054)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to trait-adjusted resistance and a rage state that ends on calming; a world can change the emotional trigger or duration because emotional excess defines the effect.

rules.statement: An Accuser’s heart-search reveals one fact per use that the target would never admit, though a truly holy person without secrets may be immune. Its anxiety effect lasts one month and ties the victim’s distress to hidden wrongdoing.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Accusers — Powers (ars-magica-realms#054)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one concealed fact revealed per use and a month of linked anxiety; a world can broaden immunity or shorten duration because holy purity and exposure of guilt are central costs.

rules.statement: A demon can spend a Confidence Point to imitate a virtue for one situation, and the imitation lasts only while that situation continues. Demons otherwise lack virtues and cannot reliably act against their defining vices.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: A Life Lacking in Virtue (ars-magica-realms#054)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one-situation virtue simulation for a Confidence Point; a world can allow more or less simulation because demons’ moral incapacity is a defining limitation.

rules.statement: Demons remain loyal only while effectively controlled, and demons of equal rank do not cooperate by choice; force can make them assist, but their minions remain unreliable. Demons also commonly repeat mistakes because they fail to connect remembered experience to decision-making.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Without Faith; Without Charity; Without Prudence (ars-magica-realms#054)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to coerced, unstable cooperation and poor learning from experience; a world can relax either limit because demonic selfishness and lack of prudence explain the friction.

rules.statement: Aerial Powers have control of one particular natural calamity, and their elemental effects are bounded by that chosen Form and their Infernal Might. Their destructive effects are indiscriminate and they are notoriously hard to control.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Aerial Powers (ars-magica-realms#054)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one calamity and one matching Form per demon; a world can broaden the domain because the chosen natural disaster is the source and limit of its power.

rules.statement: The Deluders’ listed Infernal Might is no more than 25; Aerial Powers also cap at 25, while Furies, Accusers, and Tempters and Evil Spirits cap at 20. Effects whose rules specify a Might ceiling cannot exceed the demon’s Infernal Might.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Deluders; Aerial Powers; Furies; Accusers; Tempters & Evil Spirits (ars-magica-realms#054)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the stated order-specific ceilings and effect-level cap; a world can change the ceilings because Might bounds both a demon’s standing and its supernatural output.

rules.statement: A decanus may possess a body as possession does, but the victim develops that decanus’s disease; medical or magical treatment cannot cure it while possession continues. Each week the victim rolls Stamina against Ease Factor 9 or suffers a Light Wound, and recovery uses Stamina alone.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Decani (ars-magica-realms#055)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to persistent disease while possession lasts; a setting can vary its severity or duration, with exorcism as the stated means of release.

rules.statement: A famulus can lend its sight or hearing to a being it physically touches; the effect lasts indefinitely, but immediately ends if the borrowed sense encounters religious sentiment such as a cross, sacred name, or prayer call.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Famuli (ars-magica-realms#055)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to indefinite borrowed senses while contact and the taboo condition hold; a world can broaden the religious trigger, making sanctity the price of continued spying.

rules.statement: A ruach makes chance favor the target’s opponent and applies –2 to rolls in matters where luck outweighs skill or judgment. The effect lasts until the imp becomes bored or is driven away.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Ruchin (ars-magica-realms#055)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the fixed –2 penalty and adverse chance until departure; a world can change the penalty or duration, reflecting how persistent the spirit is.

rules.statement: A person ridden by an incubus or succubus remains conscious but cannot move until dawn, loses one long-term Fatigue level, and cannot recover other Fatigue levels during that night. Repeated nights cause additional long-term Fatigue loss.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Incubi & Succubae (ars-magica-realms#055)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one night of immobility and fatigue loss; a world can make stronger demons inflict wounds or death, at the cost of escalating danger.

rules.statement: A shedim’s chosen victim cannot directly attack it without a major effort of will, renewed whenever the victim wants to attack again. Once the victim recognizes the manipulation and spends a Confidence or Faith point to reject it, the demon is left powerless.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Shedim (ars-magica-realms#055)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a recurring will barrier and a one-point rejection cost; a world can alter the price of resistance, tying liberation to its spiritual economy.

rules.statement: A hand of glory has five charges, one per finger. When lit in a building with nobody awake, it renders most occupants other than its holder unconscious until sunrise or until extinguished; brave or pious people with a relevant Trait of +3 or more, and people carrying relics, are unaffected. It cannot be put out with water, but milk or the lighter’s breath extinguishes it; a failed lighting attempt spends no charge.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: The Hand of Glory (ars-magica-realms#055)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to five attempts and building-wide sleep ending at sunrise or extinguishing; a world can change the charge count or protected groups, balancing theft against reliable use.

rules.statement: A demon’s boast-triggered talent can grant a nearby person an Ability or Power that contradicts the boast and make them use it immediately; the effect must penetrate Magic Resistance and lasts 1–10 rounds. A physical alteration instead lasts until the boaster and target can no longer see one another, and the demon spends all its Might points to do this.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Bomburkhan (ars-magica-realms#055)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the stated duration and full-reserve expenditure; a world can change the duration or price, making boast-puncturing more or less costly.

rules.statement: A demon’s secret-binding effect prevents one thief from revealing a specified secret; if the thief tries, the tongue will not move and the demon is alerted. A separate theft aid grants +3 to one roll for an actual act of stealing, but not for breaking in or picking a lock.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Valefar, the Thief's Demon (ars-magica-realms#055)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one specified secret or one theft roll per use; a world can broaden the protected secret or eligible thefts, increasing the scope of infernal assistance.

rules.statement: A demon can spend at least 1 Might Point to enhance a mortal’s spell, adding +2 to the caster’s Casting Total per point spent; it must penetrate the caster’s Magic Resistance. The resulting spell must follow the limits for similar spells and cannot exceed the original spell’s level plus the Might spent, but the demon may alter one aspect, including its target or concentration; a zero on the caster’s player roll also adds a botch die.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Enervators — Deceiver’s Boost (ars-magica-realms#056)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to +2 Casting Total per Might Point; worlds can vary how much spell control the demon receives, with the cost being the demon’s Might and possible interference.

rules.statement: Forcas can make a visible person truly invisible until the next Sunday or until he ends the effect; Hermetic magic cannot reveal the target. He can also retrieve an object he has an Arcane or sympathetic connection to, making it appear near him, but must penetrate the Magic Resistance of anyone holding or wearing it.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Forcas — Powers (ars-magica-realms#056)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to invisibility lasting through the next Sunday and retrieval requiring a connection; a world can change duration or connection requirements, trading certainty for stronger limits.

rules.statement: A pure-hearted character cannot be harmed by an Infernal Dragon; qualifying requires True Faith or at least two noble Personality Traits at +3 or higher, and no un-absolved sins. Its venom causes a bitten victim to make a Stamina roll against Ease Factor 9 or suffer a Medium Wound, even if bite damage was fully Soaked; contact with wood or softer organic matter destroys it in one round.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Infernal Dragons — Powers (ars-magica-realms#056)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the stated moral qualification and fixed Ease Factor; worlds can broaden the protected group or alter the test, making purity a consequential safeguard.

rules.statement: The Miser’s Pot can reshape its inner surface around an object within its lip, making an unbreakable grip; it can include a rich person’s hand and drag that person away. Its silent suggestion to store valuables can be resisted with a Personality Trait roll against Ease Factor 9, with circumstances such as already owning a strongbox potentially granting a +3 bonus.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Miser’s Pot, Bane of the Hoarder — Powers (ars-magica-realms#056)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to an unbreakable grip and an Ease Factor 9 suggestion; worlds can change the grip’s strength or resistance bonus, with the risk of capture or temptation as the cost.

rules.statement: The Seven Spirits can impose one of seven named curses, each treated as a Lesser Malediction: they affect truthfulness, quarrelsomeness, others’ hostility or envy, ambition, understanding earnest speech, or a victim’s worst trait. A curse lasts indefinitely unless the spirits retract it or Divine agency removes it.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Spirits of Solomon — The Worst You Can Be (ars-magica-realms#056)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a lasting curse removable only by retraction or Divine agency; worlds can loosen removal conditions, with the consequence that the curse can persist beyond the caster’s control.

rules.statement: A Watcher who teaches an Ability for a season can taint the knowledge with a Corrupted Ability Flaw, but only if the pupil’s score increases because of that teaching. Affected pupils learn that selfish or sinful use of the Ability brings greater rewards.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Watchers — Corrupted Knowledge (ars-magica-realms#056)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one season of teaching and require an actual score increase; worlds can make corruption arise from shorter or longer instruction, with compromised learning as the price.

rules.statement: Architectus can summon swarms of lesser creatures that work with extraordinary speed, building complicated structures in a single evening and taking other assigned tasks. He must fulfill any agreement he makes.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Architectus, Demon Builder — Powers and Weakness (ars-magica-realms#056)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the stated rapid construction and binding obligation; worlds can limit the swarm’s tasks or speed, with the demon’s agreement serving as the cost.

rules.statement: A Fifth Trump demon with footprints or an Arcane Connection can track prey without being fooled by ordinary trail tricks. It loses the trail while the prey is in a Church, near a relic with at least 2 Faith Points, or inside a magical ward whose strength exceeds its Might.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Demons of the Fifth Trump — Inescapable (ars-magica-realms#056)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to reliable tracking except at the listed sacred or warded barriers; worlds can alter which sanctuaries block pursuit, making safe refuge a limited resource.

rules.statement: Lucifuges can use their fire-control ability only to affect light, never fire or heat, and cannot create light. Their touch drains blood: a Stamina roll against Ease Factor 3 avoids losing a Fatigue level; failure instead causes a Light Wound.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Lucifuges — Powers (ars-magica-realms#057)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to light-only manipulation and a touch that causes fatigue or injury; a world could widen the elements affected, at the cost of weakening the demon's defining limitation.

rules.statement: A lucifuge can remove one fact, memory, or desire from a target's mind, but can use this ability on each target only once. The stolen thought is permanently lost, although a desire can return naturally and facts can be learned again.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Lucifuges — Powers (ars-magica-realms#057)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one irreversible mental removal per target; a world could allow repeat uses, with the risk of stripping away more of the victim's identity.

rules.statement: Each maggot possessing a person causes a different Delusion, and the host can experience waking dreams without the demon spending Might. Several maggots can possess one victim at once, but each must be exorcised separately.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Maggots — Powers (ars-magica-realms#057)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one distinct delusion per possessing demon, with separate removal for each; a world could limit simultaneous occupants, reducing the danger of compounded madness.

rules.statement: A mazzik's wilderness-fear effect costs 2 points and can affect one victim, or up to ten people who can see the demon. Each affected person who fails a Brave stress roll against Ease Factor 7 runs until exhausted, or collapses until sunrise if unable to flee.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Mazzikim — Powers (ars-magica-realms#057)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to fear that drives flight or paralysis, with visibility setting a cap of ten targets; a world could change the cap or duration, making the power either subtler or more overwhelming.

rules.statement: A Merry Devil's mind-clouding ability costs 1 point per use, and each use makes one real object or person appear different to a victim. The illusion can encourage mistaken recognition or misinterpretation, such as seeing urine as beer.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Merry Devils — Powers (ars-magica-realms#057)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one altered perception for one victim per point; a world could let one use affect multiple perceptions, at the cost of greater power expenditure.

rules.statement: Naonhaithya can summon a storm from existing clouds that fills the visible sky and directs its rain, hail, wind, thunder, and lightning. Its swarm power can attack up to ten targets, each of whom must make a Stamina roll against Ease Factor 9 each round to avoid a Medium Wound; the attacks prevent concentration.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Naonhaithya — Powers (ars-magica-realms#057)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to weather requiring pre-existing clouds and a swarm capped at ten targets; a world could remove those limits, with the cost of making the powers more difficult to resist or control.

rules.statement: Sabaoth can divide into as many as twenty ravens, each holding at least 1 Might and acting independently at any distance while instantly sharing awareness. A dead raven permanently costs the demon the Might invested in it, and all surviving birds must reunite before the demon can return to its natural discorporate state.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Sabaoth — Powers (ars-magica-realms#057)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a maximum of twenty bodies that divide a finite Might supply and share awareness; a world could make lost Might recoverable, reducing the lasting price of a destroyed raven.

rules.statement: A character with Might cannot take Virtues tied to another realm; Magic Resistance from multiple sources does not add, and only the highest total applies. Such characters ignore Warping and realm-specific supernatural backlash, but can spend 1 Might Pool point to use an Ability or Power that would normally cause Warping; other failed-roll consequences still apply.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Characters with Might Scores (ars-magica-realms#058)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to realm exclusivity, highest-only resistance, and immunity to Warping; a setting can loosen these limits, trading away the distinction and protection that Might provides.

rules.statement: Infernal Powers granted by Demonic Blood cost Might equal to half the Power’s magnitude, rounded as specified by the rules but never below 1. Constant effects reduce the character’s Might Pool by their cost and cannot be switched off; the character has up to 30 Power levels from this Virtue, while Demonic Powers adds 20 levels each time it is taken.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Demonic Blood; Demonic Powers (ars-magica-realms#058)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a fixed level budget and Might-paid activations, with constant effects permanently reserving their cost; worlds can alter the budget or price to change how freely demonic gifts can be used.

rules.statement: Infernal Blessing grants 60 levels of effects for a Minor Virtue, capped at level 40 per effect, or 120 levels for a Major Virtue, capped at level 60. It can be taken repeatedly, with a limit of five instances (ten for a Mythic Companion); each instance also gives 3 Warping Points and 1 experience point in an appropriate Infernal Reputation.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: Infernal Blessing (ars-magica-realms#058)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a finite effects budget, per-effect ceiling, and five-instance cap; a world can change these dials to make demonic sponsorship broader or more restrained, with Warping and reputation marking the price.

rules.statement: A group performing an Infernal ceremony must have 13 participants, including a focus character who has the needed Ability. Without a leader, add all Ceremony scores and subtract 13 for the group modifier; participants also add their relevant Characteristic plus Ability or Method to the focus character’s total, using only the Characteristic if they lack the relevant skill.
locators: Ars Magica 5e Realms of Power: New Abilities — Ceremony (ars-magica-realms#058)
rules.speaker: rulebook
